Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-6101
Investigation Summary: Cost-price discrepancies were investigated in BUS UAT for test products MC395379T1 and ML351505. MC395379T1 had a manually updated cost price in Bus Price Master Staging that differed from Realtime Staging Master. ML351505 had a NULL Price Group, causing its Realtime Staging Master Cost Price to remain aligned with Bus Price Master Staging; the Price Group was updated and the record reprocessed.
Important Findings: ['For product MC395379T1, the cost price in Bus Price Master Staging was manually updated for testing and differed from Realtime Staging Master.', 'For product ML351505 in BUS UAT, the Price Group was NULL.', 'The NULL Price Group caused the Cost Price in Realtime Staging Master for ML351505 to remain the same as the value in Bus Price Master Staging.', 'The Bus Price Master Staging cost price for MC395379T1 was corrected and the record was reprocessed.', 'The Price Group for ML351505 was updated and the Bus Price Master Staging record was reprocessed.']
Root Cause: Manual cost-price modification in Bus Price Master Staging for MC395379T1 and a NULL Price Group for ML351505 in BUS UAT.
Resolution: Corrected the cost price for MC395379T1 in Bus Price Master Staging and reprocessed the record; updated the Price Group for ML351505 and reprocessed its Bus Price Master Staging record.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-6091
Investigation Summary: Users could not select model codes while creating quotes, stopping quotation operations. Investigation confirmed that the Catalog File was not imported and that the Model Code and Catalog files were not executed in the correct order. This left model codes unassociated with the Body Type selected in the quote, preventing their display; recovery was completed and models became selectable.
Important Findings: ['Model codes on the quotation screen are displayed based on the Body Type selected in the quote.', 'The Catalog File was not imported into the system.', 'The Model Code and Catalog files were not executed in the correct order.', 'Because of the incorrect execution order, model codes were not configured with the Body Type selected in the quote.', 'The issue was caused by a work error during the file-loading process.', 'Recovery was completed and models became available for selection.']
Root Cause: The Catalog File was not imported and the Model Code and Catalog files were executed in the wrong order, leaving model codes unassociated with the selected Body Type.
Resolution: Completed recovery by correcting the file-loading/execution process so that models became available for selection; planned automation and streamlining of catalog-file imports as a preventive measure.

According to the SAP team, the current approach relies on S User credentials and may be vulnerable to future issues such as password expiration, account lockout, or S User lifecycle changes.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-6075
Investigation Summary: The latest Sales Quote revision was not reflected in the Sales Order because quote synchronization stopped during processing. The Sales Order had synchronized successfully through Sales Quote Revision 4, but a concurrent manual update to Line Number 30 (Additional Body) caused a Siebel record-concurrency error. The affected data was recovered, and normal operation was confirmed in UAT; no system modification was required.
Important Findings: ['Sales Order synchronization completed successfully through Sales Quote Revision 4.', 'The Sync Sales Order step failed in EAI Siebel Adapter > Synchronize while writing MF RF Order Entry - Line Items / MF Order Item record 30.', 'The backend logged SBL-DAT-00523, indicating the selected record was modified by another user after retrieval, along with SBL-BPR-00162 and SBL-EAI-04451.', 'All line items except Line Number 30 (Additional Body) were updated at the same time by Siebel Script, confirming normal synchronization for those items.', 'Line Number 30 (Additional Body) had a different Last Updated Source and Last Updated timestamp, showing an application-user update; it was also recorded in CX_EAI_LOGS.', 'Recovery of the affected record was completed, and the process operated normally in UAT.']
Root Cause: A user manually updated Sales Order Line Number 30 (Additional Body) while the latest Sales Quote synchronization was in progress. Siebel detected the concurrent record change and stopped synchronization with SBL-DAT-00523.
Resolution: Recovered the affected record. No system fix was implemented because the issue was identified as a rare concurrent-user-operation scenario and normal operation was confirmed in UAT.
Technical Entities: ['Sales Order', 'Sales Quote Revision 4', 'Sync Sales Order', 'EAI Siebel Adapter', 'Synchronize', 'SBL-BPR-00162', 'MF RF Order Entry - Line Items', 'MF Order Item', 'WriteRecord', 'SBL-DAT-00523', 'SBL-EAI-04451', 'Line Number 30', 'Additional Body', 'Siebel Script', 'CX_EAI_LOGS', 'UAT']

Comment: Thank you for your support.
We would like to share the analysis details for the incident MFTBCFFR-6075, related to latest quote revision not reflected in SO.
Please find the summary below:
|Incident number|MFTBCFFR-6075|
|Event|The latest estimate revision is not reflected in the order. |
|RCA|After investigation, we have confirmed that orders are successfully synchronized up to Sales Quote Revision 4.
During the subsequent synchronization process with the latest revision, a user updated the order, which caused the synchronization process to stop.
At that time, the following error was output on the backend.
"An error occurred while executing service 'EAI Siebel Adapter', method 'Synchronize' in step 'Sync Sales Order'. (SBL-BPR-00162) In method 'WriteRecord' of business component 'MF RF Order Entry - Line Items' (integration component 'MF Order Item'), a record with search condition ' = "30"' returned the following error: "The selected data was modified by another user after it was retrieved. Please continue. (SBL-DAT-00523)"(SBL-EAI-04451)"
When we checked the database, we confirmed that all items except item 30 (Additional Body) were updated at the same time using the Siebel script, and that the synchronization process was executed correctly.
 
On the other hand, for item 30 (Additional Body), the last update source and last update date were different from the other items, and the update source was the application user rather than the Siebel script. This detail was also recorded in the backend CX_EAI_LOGS.
 
Based on the above, we believe that the cause was that the user manually updated the details of the additional bodywork during the synchronization process, and Siebel detected the update by another user and stopped the synchronization process.
 
As a result, the latest estimate revision was not reflected in the order.
 
|
|Recovery status|Recovery of the target data has been completed.
 
We apologize for the inconvenience, but please check. |
|Fix Plan|We have confirmed from the backend logs that the cause was that the user updated the same record during the synchronization process.
 
This is an extremely rare case that occurs only when the user performs multiple operations at the same time.
 
Currently, the system is operating normally, and we have confirmed that it operates normally in the UAT environment. Therefore, we have determined that system modification is not necessary. |
(English)
|Incident Number|MFTBCFFR-6075|
|Description|Latest quote revision not reflected in SO|
|Root Cause (RCA)|We investigated this issue and observed that the Sales Order was last successfully synced with the Sales Quote Revision number 4. The sync process for the latest quote revision stopped because the Sales Order was modified while the quote synchronization was in progress.
As a result, the following error was logged at the backend:
"An error occurred while executing service 'EAI Siebel Adapter', method 'Synchronize' in step 'Sync Sales Order'. (SBL-BPR-00162)
In method 'WriteRecord' of business component 'MF RF Order Entry - Line Items' (integration component 'MF Order Item'), records with search criteria ' = "30"' returned the following error: "The selected data has been modified by another user since it was retrieved. Please continue. (SBL-DAT-00523)"(SBL-EAI-04451)
From the database, we observed that all line items except *Line Number 30 (Additional Body)* were updated by the*Siebel Script* as part of the normal quote synchronization process. The*Last Updated* timestamp for these line items is also the same, confirming that the synchronization completed successfully for them.
However, for *Line Number 30 (Additional Body)*, both the *Last Updated Source* and the *Last Updated* timestamp are different from the other line items. Instead of showing the*Siebel Script* , it shows the application user who manually updated the record. The same line item is also referenced in the *CX_EAI_LOGS* backend error log.
This confirms that the Additional Body line item was manually modified by the user while the quote synchronization was in progress. Since the same record was updated during synchronization, Siebel detected that the record had been modified by another user and stopped the synchronization process, resulting in the*SBL-DAT-00523* error. Therefore, the latest quote revision was not reflected in the Sales Order.
\\
|
|Recovery status|The recovery has been completed for the affected record. Kindly verify.|
|Fix Plan|Our backend error logging clearly mentions that record was simultaneously modified by another user. It is a very rare occurrence where user performs two operations at the same time.
Currently the process is working fine, which can be tested on UAT as well. No fix required.|

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-6062
Investigation Summary: Job Cards were assigning incorrect labor price lists for their creation branch. In BUS UAT, Branch Price List selection depends on the Billing Type and a non-blank Discount Classification from the Vehicle/Chassis; otherwise the system defaults to an SC Price List such as FDP B Price List. The price list setup was corrected, and newly created Job Cards correctly selected the applicable Branch Price List; existing Job Cards retained the previously stamped Branch Labor Price List Id.
Important Findings: ['Branch Price List is selected only when Billing Type is an eligible inspection-related value and Discount Classification is populated.', 'Discount Classification is sourced from the Vehicle/Chassis record.', 'When the selection conditions are not met, the system defaults to the SC Price List, including FDP Price List/FDP B Price List.', 'Job Card I050000511 used a Vehicle/Chassis with blank Discount Classification, causing FDP B Price List to be selected.', 'Existing Job Cards created before the price list setup correction retain the old Branch Labor Price List Id, including for newly added labor line items.', 'A newly created Job Card correctly selected Branch GY Price List after the setup update.']
Root Cause: The price list setup contained an incorrect Branch Labor Price List configuration; Job Cards created before the correction had the old/wrong Branch Labor Price List Id stamped on them. Additionally, blank Discount Classification causes the expected fallback to the SC/FDP Price List rather than a Branch Price List.
Resolution: Updated the price list setup and validated that newly created Job Cards select the correct branch-specific price list, including Branch GY Price List. Existing Job Cards must be replaced with newly created Job Cards to use the corrected stamped price list.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-6062
Timestamp: 2026-07-16T11:11:00
Comment: HelloThank you for your support.
As per your concern, please find our analysis below.
In the BUS UAT environment, we have two types of labor price lists:
# *SC Price List* — for example, *FDP B Price List*
# *Branch Price List* — specific to individual branches
The price list is picked while creating line items in the Work Order based on the below conditions.
The *Branch Price List* will be picked only when both of the following conditions are satisfied:
# *Billing Type* should be one of the below values:
{noformat}Shaken
3mon Inspection
6mon Inspection
12mon Inspection
24mon Inspection
Completion inspection fee
Shaken Agency fee
MPC Shaken
PDF Shaken
MPC+PDF Shaken
Spare Tire-Toolbox
OBD Inspection{noformat}
# *Discount Classification* should not be blank, as shown in the attached screenshot. 
The Discount Classification value comes from the Vehicle/Chassis record. Therefore, kindly create the Job Card for a Vehicle/Chassis where Discount Classification is available.
If above conditions are not true, the system will always pick the *SC Price List* as default, that is, the *FDP Price List*, instead of the Branch Price List.
The Job Card *I050000511* that you were testing was created against a Chassis/Vehicle where *Discount Classification* is blank. Because of this, the system picked the *SC Price List* by default, that is, the *FDP Price List*, instead of the *Branch Price List*.
Kindly validate the above and let us know if you have any further concerns or queries.

We would like to report the results of our investigation regarding this matter.

The address information ID was incorrectly migrated during this re-patch, which resulted in the address mismatch that we are currently seeing.
[Recovery]: We have completed recovery for all target records that have been shared so far.
Additionally, we have confirmed that similar events have not occurred in other production environments.
[Permanent countermeasure]: In the future, we will strengthen verification during data migration work and strive to prevent similar data inconsistencies from occurring again.
We have determined that this is not a code-related issue and that no system modification is necessary.
Therefore, we would like to close this incident and would appreciate your approval.
 
If you have any questions or need additional information, please let us know.
Thank you for your understanding.

Thank you for your support and cooperation.

During the migration activity, most of the records were imported successfully. However, due to an issue with a few records, they had to be re-patched approximately 20 days after the initial migration.
This re-patching caused this issue and in the IDs of the address entries was migrated incorrectly, which is the reason for the address mismatches that we are observing.
*Recovery:* We have completed the recovery for all the records that were previously shared. In addition, we thoroughly checked all other production environments and found no similar issues.
*Countermeasure:* Going forward, we will perform additional verification for all data migration activities to ensure that such inconsistencies do not occur again.
Since this is not a code-related issue and no system fix is required, we would like to request your approval to close this incident.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-6047
Investigation Summary: The blank expense calculation sheet behavior was investigated and determined to be expected system configuration, not a defect. The implemented logic generates expense calculation sheet data from an Invoice only when the associated Order Amount is greater than 0. The behavior was replicated in FDP UAT using UV Sales Orders with zero and positive amounts.
Important Findings: ['Expense calculation sheet generation from Invoice requires Order Amount to be greater than 0 for report data to be populated.', 'An Order Amount of 0 generates a blank expense calculation sheet.', 'The behavior was replicated in FDP UAT.', 'UV Sales Order E001305081 had Amount = 0.', 'UV Sales Order E001302483 had Amount > 0.']
Root Cause: Configured logic only populates the expense calculation sheet when the Invoice's associated Order Amount is greater than 0; zero-value orders produce a blank report.
Resolution: No code fix was required; the incident was classified as system configuration/expected behavior and proposed for rejection.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-6038
Investigation Summary: The vehicle inspection certificate import error was resolved by correcting a parameter configuration in OCI setup. The reported customer code in the User-Customer Code Pick Applet was identified as an Account Receivable (AR) code rather than a missing customer-master account. The pick applet is designed to display both Account and corresponding AR codes, consistent across Bus Force, SC Force, and SC Production; Japanese character display was also corrected.
Important Findings: ['The vehicle inspection certificate import error was caused by an OCI setup parameter configuration issue.', 'Customer code "0009381071" was identified as an AR code of an account.', 'User-Customer Code Pick Applet displays both Account codes and Account Receivable(Customer) codes.', 'When an AR code differs from its Parent Account code, it cannot be directly searched in Accounts master; the Parent Account can be identified by customer name.', 'The behavior in Bus Force was confirmed to match SC Force and SC Production.', 'Japanese characters were subsequently displayed correctly.']
Root Cause: The vehicle inspection certificate import issue was caused by an incorrect parameter configuration in OCI setup. The apparently unmigrated customer shown in the pick applet was an expected Account Receivable (AR) code displayed alongside its Parent Account, not a missing customer-master record.
Resolution: Corrected the OCI setup parameter configuration, restoring vehicle inspection certificate import processing. Confirmed that the User-Customer Code Pick Applet intentionally shows both Account and corresponding AR codes, and corrected Japanese character display.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-6030
Investigation Summary: SC Price Lists header records were created in Bus Force solely to support transactional data migration; price list items were not migrated. Root Cause: Price list header records cannot be deleted after migration because they are referenced by migrated transactional data, including service line items.
Resolution: Retain the migrated SC Price Lists header records after transactional data migration.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-6022
Investigation Summary: The latest Sales Quote revisions were not reflected in the Sales Order after the original quote line was deleted and replaced with a new line using a different Model Code. Deleting the original line removed the line-number reference required by the quote-to-Sales Order synchronization. The new quote line's line number was updated to match the original line, and the Sales Order then synchronized successfully with the latest quote revision.
Important Findings: ["The initial quote used Model Code 'FBAV0B22S00G-4', and the Sales Order was created from that quote.", "In quote revision 2, the original line item was deleted and replaced with a new line using Model Code 'FBAV0B22S00G-4-G830'.", 'Deleting the original quote line caused the original line-number reference to be lost, preventing Sales Quote synchronization with the Sales Order.', 'The Sales Order remained synchronized only through revision 1 despite subsequent quote revisions up to revision 5.', "Updating the replacement quote line's line number to match the original line restored synchronization with the latest quote revision.", 'Users should update the Model Code on an existing quote line instead of deleting and recreating the line.']
Root Cause: User deleted the original quote line item and created a replacement line with a different Model Code, which removed the line-number reference required to synchronize the Sales Quote with the Sales Order.
Resolution: Updated the line number of the quote line with Model Code 'FBAV0B22S00G-4-G830' to match the previously created quote line; the Sales Order then synchronized with the latest quote revision. No system fix was required.
Technical Entities: ['ESC', 'China', 'Sales Quote', 'Sales Order', "Model Code 'FBAV0B22S00G-4'", "Model Code 'FBAV0B22S00G-4-G830'", 'quote line item', 'quote items', 'quote revision 1', 'quote revision 2', 'quote revision 5']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-6022
Timestamp: 2026-07-13T14:08:00
Comment: Dear Shiromoto san
Thank you for your support.
We would like to share the analysis details for the incident MFTBCFFR-6022, related to latest quote revision not reflected in Sales Order.
Please find the summary below:
|Incident Number |MFTBCFFR-6022|
|Description|The latest quote revision is not reflected in Sales Order.|
|Root Cause (RCA)|We have investigated this issue and observed that the user created the first quote revision using model code 'FBAV0B22S00G-4'. After completing the quote, user proceeded to create the corresponding sales order from this quote.
After that user revised the sales quote and in second revision, the user deleted the line item having model code as 'FBAV0B22S00G-4' and created a new quote line item in quote items using a different Model Code 'FBAV0B22S00G-4-G830'.
When user completed the sales quote revision 2 and attempted to synchronize the sales quote with the Sales Order, the line number reference for original quote line item had been lost and the synchronization process could not be completed.
However the user continued to revise the quote upto revision number 5, but the sales order remained in synchronized only with revision 1. 
For the recovery, we updated the line number of the new created quote line item with Model Code as 'FBAV0B22S00G-4-G830' to match the line number of the previously created item. After this update, the Sales Order was successfully synchronized with the latest quote revision.
To avoid this issue, users are advised to update the Model Code on the existing quote line item instead of deleting the entire line item and creating a new one. This preserves the line number reference required for successful synchronization.
Since this is a case of user misoperation, no fix is required.|
|Recovery status|Recovery has been completed.|
|Fix Plan|Since this issue occurred due to user misoperation, no system fix is required.|
If you require further clarification or assistance, please feel free to reach out.
Regards
Sunaina Gill

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-6006
Investigation Summary: Migration validation identified mismatched record counts and non-bus data in Bus Force/BUS UAT across NV Opportunities, NV Quotes, NV Sales orders, Chassis Orders, and Body Orders. The migration logic included NV Opportunities when at least one related entity had a bus product class, which could include associated truck data. A confirmed mapping defect caused SC name and Branch Name values to be reversed or displayed incorrectly; Branch Mapping and SC-level mapping were corrected, while several other migration defects remained under investigation.
Important Findings: ['Bus migration criteria included records where NV Opportunity, NV Quote, Vehicle, or Model Code contained a bus product class: HB, MB, LB, 320, 330, or 340.', 'The migration criteria could include truck-associated data when a related entity contained bus information, resulting in records considered unnecessary for Bus Force validation.', 'For Daisuke Higuchi records created before 2026/06/01, Bus UAT and SC showed matching counts of 148 NV Opportunities and 318 NV Quote records when equivalent filters were applied.', 'For Chassis Orders created before 2026/06/01 with product class HB, MB, or LB, SC Force had 9,107 records and Bus Force had 9,051 records; 56 records were not migrated for documented reasons.', 'The SC name/Branch Name reversal was caused by missing SC-level mapping, preventing correct mapping.', 'NV Sales order Branch Name information was updated using the revised Branch Mapping; competitor data for new car deals was migrated to BUS UAT.']
Technical Entities: ['SC Force', 'Bus Force', 'BUS UAT', 'SC Production', 'UAT', 'Production', 'NV Opportunities', 'NV Opportunity', 'NV Quote', 'NV Sales order', 'Chassis Order', 'Body Order', 'Vehicle', 'Model Code', 'Sales Team', 'Daisuke Higuchi', 'HB', 'MB', 'LB', '320', '330', '340', 'Branch Name', 'SC name', 'Headquarters Location', 'FUSO BUS', 'Branch Mapping', 'SC-level mapping', 'Cubastion Mapping', 'FDP version', 'Planned Pool Cost - Shipment', 'Recycling Fee', 'Eligible business registration number', 'Non-IBOS', 'Quotation approval']

Root Cause: Manual setting of the quote to "Customer Approved" in MFTBCFFR-5819 caused the JCO creator to be "Siebel Administrator", resulting in a blank workshop code and blank Department Code(CSJS200) and Department Code(CSJS300), which prevented JV linkage to KB.
Resolution: Recovery was completed; the JVs for JC I050809872 and I050809889 were to be linked to KB that night. No logic fix was required.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5995
Investigation Summary: Multiple New/Used Vehicles/NVUV master-data migration and configuration discrepancies were identified during UAT and Production environment validation, including incorrect model-code relationships, mismatched master records, and options not displayed in VC. Investigation showed that several migrated masters and configurations were not aligned with the SC version or contained additional/incorrect values. The affected master data was corrected, required Campaign model codes were added, and VC option display was fixed; final confirmation was received from Mr. Tsunoda.
Important Findings: ['Campaign Master data received from the business initially lacked model information, resulting in incorrect or missing target model codes.', 'Recommended Model Master/Substitute&Recommend contained additional records with relation type Campaign under model codes that were not applicable.', 'Registration&Deliveryrequestdeadlinemaster was corrected to retain only records for the 11SC organization, matching the SC version.', 'RecycleFeeMaster contained an unknown selection value "AB", which was removed.', 'Option Category Master/Optcategory and Option Information Master/Optinformation could not be validated because options were not displayed in VC; the fix restored option and corresponding price display.', 'KitMaster had not been migrated during the Chugoku migration and was subsequently migrated from SC, using 5SCB for the 5SC ID in Bus Force.']
Root Cause: Master-data migration and configuration were not consistently aligned with the SC version, causing incorrect model-code relationships, extra or invalid master values, missing migration data, and VC option-display issues.
Resolution: Corrected the affected master data and configurations to align with SC, removed invalid RecycleFeeMaster value "AB", added all required model codes to Campaign, migrated KitMaster from SC, and fixed VC so all options and corresponding prices display correctly. Final validation was confirmed by Mr. Tsunoda.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5979
Investigation Summary: Job Card I000471957 was initially closed on 23/06/2026, later re-edited, and closed again on 30/06/2026. Re-Edit Journal vouchers were not created if the re-edit occurred before the issue was fixed on 24/06/2026. Recovery covered impacted Job Cards closed on or before 27/06/2026, so this later re-closed Job Card was not captured; ongoing functionality was confirmed as working.
Important Findings: ['Job Card I000471957 was closed on 23/06/2026, re-edited, and closed again on 30/06/2026.', 'The Re-Edit Journal voucher creation issue was resolved on 24/06/2026.', 'Recovery was performed for impacted Job Cards closed on or before 27/06/2026.', 'I000471957 may have been re-edited before 24/06/2026, when Re-Edit JVs were not created, but was re-closed after the recovery cutoff.', 'The incident was considered an uncatchable historical event; no issue was identified in ongoing functionality.']
Root Cause: Job Card I000471957 was likely re-edited before the 24/06/2026 fix, when Re-Edit Journal vouchers were not created, but its subsequent closure on 30/06/2026 caused it to fall outside the recovery scope for Job Cards closed on or before 27/06/2026.
Resolution: The Re-Edit Journal voucher creation defect was fixed on 24/06/2026 and recoveries were completed for impacted Job Cards closed on or before 27/06/2026. No additional action was taken for I000471957 because it was identified as an uncatchable historical case and ongoing functionality was working.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5976
Investigation Summary: Goodwill quote approvals created by the Branch Service Manager failed to update the header status when the "SV FDP_MGW Goodwill Approval Manager" approval flow was generated. The issue was replicated on FDP-UAT1 and traced to a missing LOV required by that approval flow. A corresponding LOV was created and verified on FDP-UAT1; deployment to FDP-Shikoku-PROD was approved.
Important Findings: ['The issue was replicated on FDP-UAT1 for JC#: I001305186 and Quote#: 1-8H5UAJ.', 'The issue occurred when approval was generated for the Branch Head using the "SV FDP_MGW Goodwill Approval Manager" approval flow.', 'Quotes containing Goodwill line items created by the Branch Service Manager generated the "SV FDP_MGW Goodwill Approval Manager" approval flow.', 'The required LOV for the "SV FDP_MGW Goodwill Approval Manager" approval flow was missing.', 'The missing LOV caused an approval-process error and prevented the header status from being updated correctly.', 'After creating the corresponding LOV on FDP-UAT1, header status updates were verified for JC#: I001305215 and Quote#: 1-8H3NSR.']
Root Cause: The LOV required by the "SV FDP_MGW Goodwill Approval Manager" approval flow was missing, causing the approval process to error and preventing the quote header status from updating.
Resolution: Created the corresponding LOV for the "SV FDP_MGW Goodwill Approval Manager" approval flow on FDP-UAT1, verified correct header-status updates, and received approval to deploy the change to FDP-Shikoku-PROD.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5966
Investigation Summary: The Recycle Fee Order was not displayed in the corresponding Chassis Order because the D21F file was received and processed before the corresponding D21A file from TOB. At D21F processing time, the Chassis Order and vehicle record did not exist, so the Recycle Fee Order could not be created. Recovery was completed by re-executing D21F after D21A completed; however, the requested permanent problem resolution was not accepted, and Jira closure was rejected.
Important Findings: ['D21F was received and processed before the corresponding D21A file, as confirmed by the attached file timestamps.', 'The Chassis Order and vehicle record had not been created when D21F was processed, preventing creation of the Recycle Fee Order.', 'Processing D21A later created the Chassis Order, but did not automatically recreate the already missed Recycle Fee Order.', 'Re-executing D21F after successful D21A processing created the Recycle Fee Order and made it visible in the Chassis Order.', 'The incident was attributed to TOB file processing sequence rather than a Siebel system defect.', 'Email monitoring was implemented for FDP Production, but it was characterized as supporting recovery rather than resolving the underlying ordering issue.']
Root Cause: The TOB D21F file was processed before the corresponding D21A file, so the required Chassis Order and vehicle record did not exist when the Recycle Fee Order creation process ran.
Resolution: The affected record was recovered by re-executing the D21F process after successful completion of the D21A process.

|Description|Recycle Fee Order is not displayed in corresponding Chassis Order.|
|Root Cause (RCA)|We investigated this issue and observed that the D21F file for the creation of the Recycle Fee Order was received from the TOB side before the D21A file for the corresponding Chassis Order. As a result, the D21F file was processed before the D21A file.
Since the corresponding Chassis Order (and therefore the vehicle record) had not yet been created when the D21F file was executed, the system was unable to create the Recycle Fee Order.
Later, when the D21A file was received and processed, the corresponding Chassis Order was created successfully. However, because the D21F file had already been processed, the Recycle Fee Order was not created for this Chassis Order.

|

|Fix Plan|To prevent this issue from occurring again, we will implement a monitoring mechanism that sends an email notification whenever a D21F file is processed before the corresponding vehicle has been created. Upon receiving the notification, we will perform the necessary recovery procedure and inform you the same.
This monitoring mechanism is already implemented and functioning in the SC Production environment. We will apply the same solution to the FDP Production environment as well.|

Comment: Dear Tsunoda San, 
Thanks for your support. 
Please find below the analysis details for incident *MFTBCFFR: 5966* regarding the issue where the recycle order was not displayed in the Chugoku Production environment.
*Root Cause Analysis (RCA):*
The *D21F* file was received and processed before the *D21A* file. Since the chassis record had not yet been created during the D21A file execution, the recycle fee order could not be created during the D21F execution.
*Recovery Action:*
As part of the recovery, the *D21F* process was re-executed after the successful completion of the *D21A* process. This resulted in the successful creation of the recycle fee order. 
*Countermeasure:*
As this issue was caused by the sequence of *TOB* file processing and is *not related to the Siebel system*, we are unable to provide a Siebel-side countermeasure for this scenario.
 *Monitoring:*
To avoid such errors, Cubastion has configured email notifications to alert the team whenever any file execution fails. This enables us to promptly identify unprocessed or failed files and take timely recovery actions whenever required.
Since this issue was caused by the TOB file processing sequence and is not related to the Siebel system, we would like to proceed with closing this Jira ticket.
Best Regards,
Deepika Raheja

We would like to report the results of our investigation regarding **incident MFTBCFFR-5966 (recycling fee order not displayed on chassis order in production environment in China)**.
 
■ Cause (RCA)
 
After investigation, we confirmed that the D21F file was received and processed before the D21A file.
 
At the time of D21F processing, a recycling fee order could not be created because the chassis order (vehicle information) by D21A had not yet been created.
 
■ Recovery support
 
We have confirmed that re-running the D21F process after completing the D21A process will successfully create a recycling fee order.
 
■ Measures to prevent recurrence
 
This event is caused by the TOB file processing order and is not a problem with the Siebel system, so there is no system modification that can be done on the Siebel side.
 
Additionally, in order to detect similar events at an early stage, Cubastion has introduced a monitoring function that sends email notifications when file processing fails.
 
This allows us to quickly detect processing failures and unprocessed files, and promptly implement recovery measures if necessary.
 
We have confirmed that this issue is caused by the TOB file processing order and is not a problem with the Siebel system, so we would like to close this JIRA.
 
If you have any questions, please feel free to contact us.
 
Thank you for your support.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5957
Investigation Summary: Delivery completion approval history was not created when a rejected Delivery Approval Request was regenerated. After rejection, the Sales Order status changed to "Rejected" and the user could trigger "Generate Approval" again; the status then changed to "Delivery Pending Approval" without generating approval history. The affected record was recovered, and corrected approval flows were implemented in FDP UAT-1 and deployed to Production on June 30 after business hours.
Important Findings: ['The issue occurred after a Delivery Approval Request was rejected and "Generate Approval" was triggered again.', 'After rejection, the Sales Order status changed to "Rejected" and the "Generate Approval" button became active again.', 'On the second "Generate Approval" action, the Sales Order status changed to "Delivery Pending Approval", but no approval history was generated.', 'The configured approval flow for this scenario was not functioning as expected.', 'Recovery for the affected record was completed and its approval history was generated successfully.', 'Corrected approval flows were implemented in FDP UAT-1, validated with reference record UV SO#: E001305061, and deployed to Production.']
Root Cause: The approval flow configured for regenerating a Delivery Approval Request after rejection was not functioning as expected, so the approval flow did not execute and approval history was not generated.
Resolution: Recovered the affected record and implemented corrected approval flows in FDP UAT-1, then deployed the corrected approval flows to Production on June 30 after business hours.
Technical Entities: ['Delivery Approval Request', 'Generate Approval', 'Sales Order', 'Rejected', 'Delivery Pending Approval', 'approval history', 'approval flow', 'FDP UAT-1', 'Production', 'UV SO#: E001305061']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5943
Investigation Summary: The user could not create a Body Building purchase order in UV SO for body building line item Row ID 1-3Z76YI. Investigation confirmed that PO# F000601618 had already been created for this line item. The subsequent manual update of the Body Building Unit Price from ¥16,000 to ¥17,600 did not allow creation of another PO; existing functionality permits only one PO per line item.
Important Findings: ['PO# F000601618 was already associated with body building line item Row ID 1-3Z76YI.', 'The Body Building Unit Price in the existing Body Building Purchase Order was manually changed from ¥16,000 to ¥17,600.', 'Existing functionality prevents creation of a second Purchase Order for the same line item after a PO has been created.', 'The behavior was reproduced in UAT-1 using UV SO# E001305053 and PO# F001305055 after changing the Body Building Unit Price from ¥22,000 to ¥27,900.']
Root Cause: A Purchase Order, PO# F000601618, already existed for body building line item Row ID 1-3Z76YI; the system does not allow a second PO for the same line item, regardless of a subsequent Body Building Unit Price update.
Resolution: No recovery or fix was required because the observed behavior is existing functionality.
Technical Entities: ['UV SO', 'Body Building purchase order', 'Body Building Purchase Order', 'Purchase Order', 'Row ID: 1-3Z76YI', 'PO# F000601618', 'UAT-1', 'UV SO# E001305053', 'PO# F001305055', 'Body Building Unit Price']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5943
Timestamp: 2026-06-26T06:26:00
Comment: Dear Shiromoto san
Thank you for your support.
We would like to share the analysis details for the incident MFTBCFFR-5943, related to the issue where user is unable to create a Body Building purchase order in UV SO.
Please find the summary below:
|Incident Number |MFTBCFFR-5943|
|Description|The user is unable to create a Body Building purchase order in UV SO.|
|Root Cause (RCA)|We checked the issue and observed that the user is not able to create purchase order for body building line item (Row ID: 1-3Z76YI) because the Purchase Order for this particular line item has already been created PO# F000601618.
Please note that the PO# F000601618 is associated with body building line item having Row ID: 1-3Z76YI, however the user has manually updated Body Building Unit Price in Body Building Purchase Order from ¥16,000 to ¥17,600.
Once the Purchase Order is created for a line item, the user can not create a second PO for the same line item as per the existing functionality.
For your reference kindly check this functionality on UAT-1 test record : UV SO# E001305053, PO# F001305055. Similar to the production record, PO was created for a body building line item and the Body Building Unit Price in Body Building Purchase Order from ¥22,000 to ¥27,900. Now second PO can not be created for the same line item.|
|Recovery status|As the Purchase Order has already been created for the mentioned line item so no recovery required.|
|Fix Plan|NA|
We hope this resolves your query.
Regards
Sunaina Gill

Investigation Summary: Users could not create a Body Building Purchase Order from a UV Sales Order because the 'Create Purchase Order' button was inactive when the Delivery Completion Request was Rejected. Root Cause: The existing UV Sales Order logic did not enable the 'Create Purchase Order' button when the Delivery Completion Request was Rejected.
Resolution: Updated the logic so users can create a Body Building Purchase Order in UV Sales Order when the Delivery Completion Request is Rejected; deployed to FDP UAT-1 and released to production on 09 July.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5931
Investigation Summary: Journal vouchers (JVs) were not created for Parts Sales Return Order M000486052 because its base amount was negative. The JV creation logic was updated to support negative base amounts for all JV types of Parts Sales Return Order, and missing JVs were manually recovered. The fix was validated in UAT-1 and deployed to production in the regular release on 2026-07-09.
Important Findings: ['JV creation for Parts Sales return types previously occurred only when the base amount was greater than 0.', 'Order M000486052 had a negative amount, preventing JV creation.', 'Missing JVs for the affected order were manually created and scheduled to link to KB through the regular batch.', 'The updated logic allows JV creation for all JV types of Parts Sales Return Order when the base amount is negative.', 'The fix was tested using UAT-1 Test Record M001305079 and approved for production release.']
Root Cause: The JV creation logic excluded Parts Sales Return Orders with negative base amounts because it only allowed creation when the base amount was greater than 0.
Resolution: Manually created the missing JVs for order M000486052 and deployed an updated JV creation logic that supports negative base amounts for all JV types of Parts Sales Return Order to production on 2026-07-09.
Technical Entities: ['JV', 'Parts Sales Return Order', 'M000486052', 'KB', 'regular batch', 'UAT-1', 'M001305079', 'Prod', 'FDP']

Recovery:

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5920
Investigation Summary: In FDP, a Quote's Required Quantity could be changed from 3 to 1 after a Sales Order and three child Sales Orders had been created. Although the child Sales Orders were cancelled, the backend retained their linkage to the parent Sales Order, causing Sales Posting to fail. The recommended remediation was to align FDP with SC Production by making Required Quantity read-only after Sales Order creation; PROD deployment was requested, but completion is not documented.
Important Findings: ['A Required Quantity of 3 created three child Sales Orders during Sales Order approval.', 'After a Quote revision changed Required Quantity from 3 to 1, added options were synchronized to all existing child Sales Orders.', 'Cancelling all child Sales Orders did not remove their backend association with the parent Sales Order, so Sales Posting failed.', 'FDP allowed Required Quantity changes after Sales Order creation, enabling the failing scenario.', 'The proposed FDP behavior is to make Required Quantity read-only after Sales Order creation, matching SC Production.', 'For post-order quantity increases, the proposed process requires cancelling the current Sales Order and creating a new Quote and Sales Order.']
Root Cause: FDP allowed Required Quantity to be reduced after Sales Order creation, but the backend logic did not automatically unlink existing child Sales Orders from the parent Sales Order when Required Quantity became 1.

Author: Shubham Agarwal
Comment: Dear Tsunoda San,
 
Thank you for your continued support.
 
We would like to report the results of our investigation and the details of our response regarding this matter.
 
■ Cause
When revising the estimate for the first time, we set the number of units discussed to 3 and created an order.
After the order was approved, three branch orders were created depending on the number of units negotiated.
After that, we revised the estimate again, changed the number of units discussed from 3 to 1, and added options.
At the time of order synchronization, the added options were reflected in all three branch orders.
Since the number of units negotiated became 1, the user canceled all branch orders and recorded sales for the parent order.
However, the sales recording failed because the system still linked it to the branch order.
■ Expected behavior
 
If the number of units negotiated is changed from 2 or more to 1, the linkage with the branch order will be automatically canceled and the parent order will be able to record sales normally.
 
■ Current operation
 
With the current backend logic, even if the number of sales negotiations is changed to 1, the link with the branch number order is not released.
As a result, the parent order was treated as an order with a branch order, and sales failed to be recorded.
 
■ Correspondence details (modifications)
 
We have corrected the backend logic so that when the number of sales reaches 1, the link with the branch number order will be automatically canceled.
This will enable you to successfully record sales for parent orders without any manual action.
 
■ Test data
UAT-1:NV SO:A001305145
 
If you have any questions, please feel free to contact us.
 
Thank you for your support.
 
(English)
Thank you for your constant support
Root Cause:
During the first quote revision, the user set the Required Quantity to 3 and created the order.
During order approval, 3 child sales orders were created, as expected.
Later, the user revised the quote again and changed the Required Quantity from 3 to 1, while also adding additional options.
During order synchronization, the newly added options were synchronized to all existing child sales orders.
Since the required quantity was now 1, the user canceled all three child sales orders and attempted to complete the sales posting for the parent sales order.
The sales posting failed because the system still considered the parent sales order to have linked child sales orders.
Expected Behavior:
When the required quantity is reduced from a value greater than 1 to 1, all child sales orders should automatically be unlinked from the parent sales order. This allows the parent sales order to proceed through the normal sales posting process.
Actual behavior:
The existing backend logic did not automatically unlink the child sales orders after the required quantity was reduced to 1. As a result, the parent sales order continued to be treated as a parent with child orders, causing the sales posting process to fail.
Resolution/Fix:
The backend logic will be updated so that whenever the Required Quantity becomes 1, all linked child sales orders are automatically unlinked from the parent sales order. This will ensure the parent sales order can complete the sales posting successfully without requiring manual intervention.
 
Test Data:
UAT-1: NV SO: A001305145

Comment: Dear Tsunoda-San,
 
Thank you very much for your continued support.
 
We would like to share with you the results of our investigation into this matter and our countermeasures.
As a result of our investigation, we have confirmed that this issue occurs because FDP has a specification that allows you to change the *number of units negotiated* in the estimate even after an order is created.
 
In this event, three branch orders were created with the number of units negotiated as ``3'' when the order was created, and then the number of units negotiated was changed to ``1'' due to the estimate revision. After that, when I canceled all the branch orders and recorded the sales using the parent order, the backend determined that the branch orders were related, so the sales recording failed.
 
In the SC production environment, such an event will not occur because the number of units negotiated cannot be edited after an order is created. On the other hand, with FDP, it is possible to change the number of units negotiated, so business scenarios that do not occur with SC can be executed.
 
We are considering the following two options as ways to deal with this issue.
*Plan 1*
This is a method of adding logic that automatically releases the association between the parent order and branch order on the backend when the number of sales orders is changed to "1".
This method allows you to maintain the current FDP business flow.
*Plan 2*
This is a method of changing the FDP to the same specifications as the SC production environment and making it impossible to edit the number of units negotiated after an order is created.
If you wish to change the number of units negotiated, you will need to create a new quotation and order.
 
We recommend *Plan 2* because similar data inconsistencies can be prevented by unifying the specifications to the same as the SC production environment.
In order to decide on the implementation policy, could you please confirm whether there is any problem with operating FDP in the same way as in the SC production environment *by disabling the number of units for negotiation after an order is created?

Thank you for your continued support.
We would like to share the investigation results and the proposed solution for this issue.
Our investigation confirmed that this issue occurs because FDP currently allows users to modify the *Required Quantity* on the Quote even after a Sales Order has been created.
In the reported case, a Sales Order was initially created with a *Required Quantity of 3*, and the system correctly generated three child Sales Orders. Later, the Quote was revised, and the *Required Quantity was changed from 3 to 1*. After all child Sales Orders were canceled, the user attempted to perform Sales Posting using the parent Sales Order. However, Sales Posting failed because the backend still recognized the parent Sales Order as being associated with child Sales Orders.
In the SC Production environment, this scenario cannot occur because the *Required Quantity* becomes read-only once a Sales Order has been created. In contrast, FDP currently allows the Required Quantity to be modified after Sales Order creation, enabling a business scenario that is not supported in SC.
We have considered the following two approaches to address this issue.
*Option 1*
Update the backend logic so that when the Required Quantity is changed to *1*, the relationship between the parent Sales Order and its child Sales Orders is automatically removed.
This approach allows the current FDP business process to continue without any operational changes.
*Option 2*
Modify FDP to follow the same behavior as SC Production.
Once a Sales Order has been created:
* The *Required Quantity* becomes read-only.
* Users cannot modify the Required Quantity through Quote revisions.
* If a quantity change is required, users must create a new Quote and a new Sales Order.
Since this approach prevents data inconsistencies and aligns FDP with the standard SC business process, *we recommend Option 2*.

Root Cause: An invalid Planned Delivery Date of 2007/03/30 in the NV Sales Quote caused the Tax Rate for NV Sales Order SO# A000497806 to remain blank, resulting in NV Sales Order Sheet BIP Report generation failure.
Resolution: A corrected Planned Delivery Date validation fix for NV Sales Quote was tested in FDP UAT-1 and released to all FDP-PRODs on July 10 to prevent invalid date input and resulting blank Tax Rate values.

Regarding this matter, we have shared RCA via email, but we will also share it with JIRA.
BI Publisher restart support]
An issue occurred where the BI Publisher service could not be started normally when performing periodic service restart tasks.
As a result of our investigation, we confirmed that there was a permission setting issue in some BI Publisher-related directories, causing log files to not be output correctly. As a result, the BI Publisher service startup process was not completed successfully, causing intermittent failures.
We determined that directory permission mismatches were the primary cause of service startup failures and system instability.
On June 21st, we corrected the ownership and access permissions of the affected directories, and the BI Publisher service was restored to normal operation.
Monitoring results after the fix have confirmed that system stability has been improved and the number of BI Publisher-related failures has decreased significantly.
Additionally, as part of our permanent response, we conducted a planned restart of BI Publisher after 21:00 on June 22nd. The purpose of this work is to confirm that the modified permission settings are reflected correctly, clear the application cache, and eliminate any remaining abnormal processes.
The restart process was completed without any problems, and we confirmed that the cache was cleared and all BI Publisher services started correctly.
Furthermore, during operational monitoring on June 23, we confirmed that there were no startup failures due to privileges, and the system was operating stably.
This issue was a server-side issue, not logic. Correspondence has already been completed.
If there is no problem, may I close this matter?
Thank you for your support.
Manisha

Comment: Mr. Tsunoda
Thank you for your continued support.
Regarding this incident *MFTBCFFR-5910*, we would like to share the analysis results regarding the phenomenon in which users were unable to generate *NV purchase order BIP report*.
Please see the summary below.
|Incident #|MFTBCFFR-5910|
|Details|An issue has occurred where users are unable to generate the NV Purchase Order BIP report. |
|Cause Adjustment|I initially thought it was a server-side issue because other trucks were experiencing similar BIP printing issues.
However, after further investigation at the code level, it was discovered that in the affected SO number: A000497806 (Shikoku production environment), the tax rate field of the NV sales order was not set (blank), so the BIP report was not generated.
Tax rates are calculated based on the estimated delivery date entered on the applicable NV Order Quote.
For the affected records, "2007/03/30" was entered in the expected delivery date field of the NV order estimate.
As a result, the system was unable to derive a valid tax rate and failed to generate the BIP report.
Please note that a validation message is displayed for NV opportunities, and users are prevented from entering a date earlier than the current date.
On the other hand, since similar validation does not exist for NV order quotation, it is possible to enter extremely old dates, including dates and times in the past than the current date.
|
|Recovery Status|The BIP report has already been shared in the previous comment. |
|Correction Plan|As a result of investigating this matter, we found that an invalid "P delivery date" was entered in the NV order estimate, resulting in the Tax Rate not being set, which caused the BIP report generation to fail.
As a countermeasure to this issue, a validation message will be added to the scheduled delivery date field of the NV order estimate to prevent incorrect date input. |
If you have any other questions, please contact us.
Thank you for your support.
Manisha

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5897
Investigation Summary: The incident involved a Vehicle Master Model Difference where a vehicle's Model Code differed from the expected value. Recovery for the affected record was completed. |Description|Vehicle Master Model Difference|
|Root Cause (RCA)|We investigated the issue and observed that the Model Code field is editable from the Administration - Vehicle screen. From this screen if user drilldown on the vehicle number and navigates to the detail view, the Model Code field remains editable to the user.

Kindly confirm if this fix plan is correct and for which users the screen should have read-only access.|

Sunaina Gill

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5858
Investigation Summary: The Sales Order synchronized successfully through NV Quote revision 8, but synchronization from revision 8 to revision 9 stopped. Concurrent invoice creation for the same NV Sale Order caused simultaneous modification of the Recycle Fee line item, triggering Siebel exclusive-control errors. Recovery was completed for the affected record; no program fix was required.
Important Findings: ['The affected Sales Order was synchronized through quote revision 8; synchronization stopped when processing NV Quote revision 9.', 'Invoice C000105274 was created for the same NV Sale Order while the Rev.9 Sales Order synchronization was running.', 'The concurrent operations modified the same Recycle Fee line item, Line Number = 47, Part# YN5Z.', 'The Sync Sales Order step failed in EAI Siebel Adapter Synchronize with SBL-BPR-00162, SBL-DAT-00523, and SBL-EAI-04451.', 'Recovery was completed for the affected record, and the process subsequently operated normally, including in UAT.']
Root Cause: Concurrent quote-to-Sales Order synchronization and invoice creation updated the same Recycle Fee line item (Line Number = 47, Part# YN5Z), causing Siebel exclusive control to reject the synchronization update.
Resolution: Recovered the affected record. No program correction was required because the incident was a rare concurrent-update scenario and the process was functioning normally afterward.
Technical Entities: ['NV Quote', 'NV Sale Order', 'Sales Order', 'Invoice#: C000105274', 'Sync Sales Order', 'EAI Siebel Adapter', 'Synchronize', 'MF RF Order Entry - Line Items', 'MF Order Item', 'WriteRecord', 'Line Number = 47', 'Recycle Fee', 'Part# YN5Z', 'SBL-BPR-00162', 'SBL-DAT-00523', 'SBL-EAI-04451', 'Siebel', 'UAT']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5858
Timestamp: 2026-06-09T12:15:00
Comment: Thank you for your support.
We would like to share the analysis details for the incident MFTBCFFR-5858, related to latest quote revision not reflected in SO.
Please find the summary below:
|Incident Number |MFTBCFFR-5858|
|Description|Latest quote revision not reflected in SO|
|Root Cause (RCA)|We have investigated this issue and observed that the Sales Order was last synced with quote revision 8. Sync process for further quote revision stopped due to Multi browser activity. At the time of sync of NV Quote from rev 8 to rev 9, the user was creating an invoice in the NV Sale Order (Invoice#: C000105274).
As a result, the error was logged at the backend.
"An error occurred while executing service 'EAI Siebel Adapter', method 'Synchronize' in step 'Sync Sales Order'. (SBL-BPR-00162)
--
In method 'WriteRecord' of business component 'MF RF Order Entry - Line Items' (integration component 'MF Order Item'), a record with filter ' = "47"' returned the following error: "The selected data has been modified by another user since it was retrieved. Please continue. (SBL-DAT-00523)"(SBL-EAI-04451)"
\\
The line item corresponding to = "47" is a Recycle Fee line item having Part# 'YN5Z'. While user tried to sync quote revision 9 with SO, the invoice was created in SO at that same time. Please note that this Recycle Fee line item is also used in Invoice. Due to this multi session activity for same line item the sync process was stopped.|
|Recovery status|The recovery has been completed for the affected record. Kindly verify.|
|Fix Plan|Our backend error logging clearly mentions that record was simultaneously modified by another user. It is a very rare occurrence where user performs two operations at the same time.
Currently the process is working fine, which can be tested on UAT as well. No fix required. |

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5858
Timestamp: 2026-06-09T13:22:00
Comment: Dear Tsunoda-San
Thank you for your continued support.
We would like to report the results of our investigation regarding the issue of the latest revised estimate not being reflected in orders (MFTBCFFR-5858).
 
|Incident number|MFTBCFFR-5858|
|Event details|The latest revised version of the quotation is not reflected in the order|
|RCA|As a result of our investigation, we have confirmed that the affected orders were successfully synchronized up to quotation revision version 8, but the synchronization process had stopped for subsequent revisions.
At the time of synchronizing the NV quotation from Rev.8 to Rev.9, a user was creating an invoice (Invoice#: C000105274) for the same order.
As a result, the following error occurred on the backend and the synchronization process stopped.
"An error occurred while executing service 'EAI Siebel Adapter', method 'Synchronize' in step 'Sync Sales Order'. (SBL-BPR-00162)
--
In method 'WriteRecord' of business component 'MF RF Order Entry - Line Items' (integration component 'MF Order Item'), records with search criteria '= "47"' returned the following error: "The selected data has been modified by another user since it was retrieved. Please continue. (SBL-DAT-00523)"(SBL-EAI-04451)"
 
The item corresponding to "Line Number = 47" in the error message is the recycling fee item for part number "YN5Z".
When the estimate Rev. 9 synchronization process and the invoice creation process were executed at the same time, this recycling charge detail was also used in the invoice creation process, resulting in simultaneous updates to the same record.
As a result, we have determined that the synchronization process has stopped due to Siebel's exclusive control. |
|Recovery Status|Recovery has been completed for the target record. |
|Fix Plan|The backend logs clearly record that "the record was updated by other users at the same time."
This event is an extremely rare case that occurs due to multiple processes being executed simultaneously on the same record.
It is currently working properly, and the same operation can be confirmed in the UAT environment.
Since this is not a system defect, we have determined that no program correction is necessary at this time. |
That's all.
If you have any questions, please let us know.
 
Thank you for your support.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5846
Investigation Summary: Recycle Invoice DT27 processing created incorrect Journal Voucher values, initially affecting Segment2 Code fields and later Posting Date and client-code fields. The investigation identified chassis-number derivation/mapping issues, DT27 file formatting sensitivity, and UAT8 mapping differences from Chugoku prod and other FDP UATs. The corrected UAT logic was verified with test data, and the fix was scheduled for the 2026-07-23 FDP release.
Important Findings: ['The calculation and reconciliation process formed the chassis number using "Stamp Code-C#", rather than the chassis-number position highlighted in the DT27 file.', 'Incorrect Segment2 Code(CSJS210) and Segment2 Code(CSJS310) values were initially associated with data received from TOB, including "********************" values in the DT27 Recycle Invoice file.', 'An extra space in the DT27 file caused amount value 80 to be treated as 8 during JV creation.', 'Client Code(CSJS208) and Client Code(CSJS308) mappings in UAT-8 differed from Chugoku prod and other FDP UATs, resulting in incorrect Recycle Invoice JV data.', 'UAT8 master data also caused client-code issues and was updated to match Chugoku prod.', 'After mapping updates, test data verified that JVs were created correctly with the correct Posting Date(CSJS005) and client-code values.']
Root Cause: UAT-8 mappings for Client Code(CSJS208) and Client Code(CSJS308) differed from Chugoku prod and other FDP UATs, causing incorrect Recycle Invoice Journal Voucher data. DT27 input formatting, including an extra space that converted 80 to 8, also caused an incorrect JV amount during testing.
Resolution: Updated UAT-8 mappings and master data based on Chugoku prod and other FDP UATs, corrected DT27 test-file formatting, and verified correct Journal Voucher creation with new test data. The approved fix was scheduled for the 2026-07-23 FDP release.
Technical Entities: ['DT27', 'Recycle Invoice file', 'TOB', 'Siebel', 'Segment2 Code', 'CSJS210', 'CSJS310', 'JV', 'Journal Voucher', 'Chassis number', 'Stamp Code-C#', 'UAT', 'UAT8', 'UAT-8', 'Posting Date', 'CSJS005', 'Client Code', 'CSJS208', 'CSJS308', 'Chugoku prod', 'FDP UATs', 'FDP release', 'PROD']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5842
Investigation Summary: Vehicle Certificate Correction failed because two vehicles with vehicle key 'FBA00-610330' existed after migration from SC to FDP Chugoku. The duplicate key caused the error during the correction process. Recovery was performed by changing the key of the old vehicle in status "Before Stock-In" to 'FBA00-610330_dummy', allowing the user to continue the Vehicle Correction Process.
Important Findings: ["Two vehicles with vehicle key 'FBA00-610330' existed after migration from SC to FDP Chugoku.", 'The duplicate vehicle key caused an error during the Vehicle Certificate Correction process.', 'The old vehicle with status "Before Stock-In" had its key changed to \'FBA00-610330_dummy\'.', 'A UAT fix and an error-message change were being considered, but no completed implementation was confirmed.', 'Affected records with similar issues were still under analysis.']
Root Cause: Duplicate vehicle key 'FBA00-610330' for two vehicles migrated from SC to FDP Chugoku.
Resolution: Changed the vehicle key of the old vehicle with status "Before Stock-In" from 'FBA00-610330' to 'FBA00-610330_dummy' and instructed the user to proceed with the Vehicle Correction Process.
Technical Entities: ['Vehicle Certificate Correction process', 'Vehicle Correction Process', 'SC', 'FDP Chugoku', 'UAT', 'vehicle key', 'FBA00-610330', 'FBA00-610330_dummy', 'Before Stock-In', 'vehicle master', 'chassis number']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5838
Investigation Summary: The backend logic initially updated Activity Status to "Work Completed" when JC Status changed to "Delivery Completed", as confirmed in UAT-1 with JC Number I001304693. Important Findings: ['Existing backend logic updated Activity Status to "Work Completed" when JC Status changed to "Delivery Completed".', 'The initial behavior was reproduced and verified in UAT-1 using JC Number I001304693.', 'The expected behavior was for Activity Status and Journal Vector updates to occur when JC Status becomes "Closed".', 'The fix was validated in FDP UAT-1, where Activity Status was updated when the JC was closed.', 'The corrected logic was deployed to FDP-PROD in the regular release on the 23rd.']
Root Cause: The backend logic triggered the Activity Status update at JC Status "Delivery Completed" instead of at JC Status "Closed", contrary to the required workflow.
Resolution: Updated the logic so that the Activity Status update occurs when the JC is closed; validated in FDP UAT-1 and deployed to FDP-PROD.

Regarding this issue, we analyzed the BIP logic and found the following:

* If *Billable Flag = N*, the BIP uses the *Ship To Finance Account Code* field. In this case, the value is also *0000805629*.
Therefore, even after updating the Billable Flag, the account code displayed in the BIP remained unchanged because both fields currently contain the same value (*0000805629*).
These fields are visible on the Job Card screen as:
* *Ship To Finance Account Code*
* *Bill To Finance Account Code*

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5829
Investigation Summary: Price Master creation failed for newly received materials in Wakayama and Okinawa - PROD because the Price Master job could start before batch product release completed. Materials arrived through the D2S_MATERIAL_MASTER file, and high material volumes extended the product-release processing time. Realtime job schedules were shifted by 30 minutes on all FDP environments, and successful price uploads were verified in all FDP-PROD environments.
Important Findings: ['Materials were received through the D2S_MATERIAL_MASTER file.', 'A batch job scheduled at 02:50 AM releases products after Material Master updates.', 'High volumes of received materials can delay completion of the product-release process.', 'The Price Master creation job was scheduled at 04:30 AM and could overlap with incomplete product release.', 'The error "Issue While Updating/Inserting Price Master with Product Name: MK718834" occurred when the material had no existing Price Master record.', 'Realtime jobs were delayed by 30 minutes, and price uploads subsequently succeeded on all FDP-PROD environments.']
Root Cause: The Price Master creation job started before the batch product-release process completed for high-volume Material Master updates, causing Price Master insert/update errors for materials without existing price records.
Resolution: Increased scheduled timings of the Realtime jobs by 30 minutes on all FDP environments, shifting Price Master creation and related batch jobs to prevent overlap; verified successful price uploads on all FDP-PROD environments.
Technical Entities: ['Wakayama', 'Okinawa - PROD', 'D2S_MATERIAL_MASTER', 'Material Master', 'Price Master', '"Issue While Updating/Inserting Price Master with Product Name: MK718834"', 'Realtime jobs', 'FDP environments', 'FDP-PROD environments', 'MK718834']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5829
Timestamp: 2026-06-10T18:29:00
Author: Soham Modi
Comment: Dear Hata san,
Thank you for your support.
As per our analysis, we found that these materials were received through the D2S_MATERIAL_MASTER file. Whenever a material is updated through the material master, the corresponding product is released by a batch job scheduled at 02:50 AM. In cases where a high count of materials is received, the product release process may take longer than usual to complete. Since the Price Master creation job is scheduled at 04:30 AM, there can be instances where the price creation process starts before the product release has been completed. This overlap results in an error similar to the one observed in this case: "Issue While Updating/Inserting Price Master with Product Name: MK718834". The issue occurs specifically when the material does not have any existing price record in the Price Master.
To prevent this timing overlap, we plan to reschedule the Price Master creation job from 04:30 AM to 05:00 AM. The subsequent related batch jobs will also be shifted by 30 minutes to maintain the existing processing sequence and synchronization between the price creation processes.
After the fix is implemented, we'll closely monitor the package for sometime so as to ensure the correct functioning of the package.
Meanwhile, please let me know in case of any queries.
Best regards,
Soham Modi

Author: Ayaz Farooqui   !image-20260528-121049.png|width=569,alt="image-20260528-121049.png"!
Comment: Thank you for your support.
This is regarding MFTBCFFR-5819.
After checking the issue, we found that the “Internal Order Number” field is blank in both JCs. Please find the attached screenshot for reference.
 If we update the Quote and Work Order status directly from our side, then some normal system processes, such as new JCO creation, will not happen correctly.
 Previously, we handled a similar case with Yoshihara San, and the following recovery steps were used successfully:
＜Recovery Steps＞
Step-1: Update Internal Order Number field in JC Header
Blank → E003112596 (Any Order Number)  (By Cubastion)
Step-2: Change Quote Status
Approved → Customer Approved  (By User)
Step-3: Recover Internal Order Number field in JC Header
E003112596 → Blank  (By Cubastion)
Step-4: Check Work Order  (By User)
 
Could you please confirm if you are okay with these recovery steps so that we can proceed?
Meanwhile, please let us know if you have any queries.
 
Regards,
Ayaz Farooqui

Root Cause: POs for Body line items added through an NV Quotation revision were not created before Sales Posting. When the remaining POs were created after Sales Posting, the system did not create “Sales Posting Body Non IBOS GI” JVs because those JVs are generated only at Sales Order Sales Posting.
Resolution: Recovery was completed for the affected orders listed in the Jira using recovery JV data linked to KB in the nightly daily batch. A permanent post-Sales-Posting Body GI JV enhancement remains pending and requires PJ-CR.

Comment: Thank you for your support.
I have checked this issue and found that “Sales Posting Body Non IBOS“ and “Sales Posting Body Non IBOS GI“ JVs were not created for above mentioned Body orders due to following reasons:
1. Before Sales Posting of Sales Order, NV quote was revised and Body Line Line Items were added and synced to SO but PO was not created for all line items from 'Body' tab in Line Items of SO.
2. Once these line items were synced, invoicing and sales posting was done. After sales posting completion, “*Sales Posting*”* JVs were created for the Sales Order and POs mapped to it.
3. After Sales Posting, PO was created from body of line details for remaining body items.
Since Sales Posting was already completed , that is why GI JV was not created for these line items. As per current functionality, once Sales Posting is completed, then PO is created then JV is created for delta values with Journal event type like *“Revise Sales Posting*“*.
*UAT1 Test Record:* A001304611, B001304616
*Fix Plan:* We can add validation on sales posting to create PO for all body line items present in current sakes order before proceeding with Sales Posting of the Sales Order.
*Recovery Plan:* Recovery for Orders mentioned in the description of this Jira has already been completed. We are working on finding affected records for other FDPs as well and will share it with you by {{2026-05-26}} end of the day.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5803
Timestamp: 2026-05-26T05:07:00
Comment: thank you always.
As a result of confirming this matter, the reasons why the JV of "Sales Posting Body Non IBOS" and "Sales Posting Body Non IBOS GI" were not created for the bodywork order above are as follows.
1. The NV Quotation was revised before sales of the sales order, Body Details were added and synchronized to SO, but POs were not created for all Lines from the Body tab within Lines in SO.
2. Billing and sales were then performed with the corresponding line items synchronized to SO. After the sale was completed, a 'Sales*' JV was created for the sales order and the associated PO.
3. After the sale was completed, a PO was created for the remaining bodywork details.
Since the sale has already been completed, no GI JV was created for the item.
According to the current specifications, when a PO is created after a sale is completed, a JV is created for the delta values ​​using the Journal Event Type of "Revise Sales Posting*".

Root Cause: The initiating user's manager was configured with Manager Active Flag = 'N' (Inactive), so the approval workflow could not resolve the reporting-manager hierarchy and did not generate the approval request.
Resolution: No system fix was required. Update the respective manager/user Manager Active Flag to 'Y' (Active) and retry the approval generation process.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5780
Timestamp: 2026-05-20T19:07:00
Author: Atul Yadav
Comment: Dear Shiromoto-San,
Thank you for your support.
*Root Cause:*
We investigated this issue and found that, for Cancellation Requests, the approval flow *"UV Purchase Order Cancel UV Mgr Approval Request"* is triggered. In this approval flow, only *SCHQ-Sales-UV-Mgr* is configured as the approver position.
We could not find any user in Wakayama assigned to this position. As a result, when *Generate Approval* is clicked, the *Approvers* field remains blank in the Approval History. Therefore, according to the CR-4196 change, when the Approver field is blank, validation is triggered and the history record gets deleted.
We checked all Cancellation Requests in the Wakayama production environment and found that the Approver is null for all requests. We also tried to replicate this issue in UAT, and it is working correctly there.
Therefore, this is not a bug, but an issue caused by the absence of a user assigned to the *SCHQ-Sales-UV-Mgr* position.
*Recovery Plan:*
# Assign the *SCHQ-Sales-UV-Mgr* position to a user and ask the user to click *Generate Approval* again.
# Since the status in the Cancellation Request is editable, the user can proceed by changing the status to *"Approved"* manually.
# We can retrigger the process from the backend and approve the request.
Please let us know which recovery method you would like us to proceed with. Kindly let us know if you have any questions.
Regards,
Atul Yadav

Investigation Summary: An order remained in Pending Approval and was manually recovered by updating its status to Approved. Engineering reviewed the complete flow, logs, and database entries and assessed the incident as a rare multi-user case. Reproduction attempts in UAT using multiple user sessions and Approved, Rejected, and Completed actions did not reproduce the issue; no product fix was required.
Important Findings: ['The affected order was recovered and its status was updated to Approved.', 'Logs, database entries, and the complete processing flow were reviewed.', 'The incident was assessed as a potential multi-user case.', 'UAT testing with multiple user sessions and Approved, Rejected, and Completed actions always updated the final status according to the latest action.', 'The issue could not be reproduced and no similar recurring cases were identified.', 'No fix was required; the incident was requested for closure.']
Resolution: The affected order was manually recovered by updating its status to Approved; no product fix was required.
Technical Entities: ['Approved', 'Rejected', 'Completed', 'Pending Approval', 'UAT']

Timestamp: 2026-05-20T05:26:00
Author: Shubham
Comment: Thank you for your constant support.
We have checked the complete flow, reviewed the logs and verified the database entries. Based on our findings, this looks like a multi-user case.
We have tried many times to replicate the issue in the UAT environment using different scenarios and combinations from multiple user sessions, including Approved, Rejected and Completed actions. In all cases, the system updated the final status correctly based on the latest action and we were not able to reproduce the issue where the status remained in Pending Approval.
At this point, the issue looks irreproducible and also appears to be a very rare occurrence, as no similar recurring cases have been found.
Regards,
Shubham
