investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5757
Investigation Summary: The incident concerned Chassis GI JV records not being created despite GR JV creation for selected orders. Initial analysis attributed missing GI JVs for several chassis orders to absent Model Code pricing in the Price Master/Price List, but the issue was subsequently addressed in UAT by updating the GI JV filter condition. After the change, Chassis GI JV creation was confirmed for test records A001304859 and B001258096.
Important Findings: ['GI JV was not created for orders B000121443, B000062227, B000062228, B000062229, and B000001569, while other reviewed records were reported as correct.', 'For B000062227, B000062228, B000062229, and B000001569, the Model Code had no price in the Price Master/Price List when the Chassis Orders were created.', 'Without Model Code pricing, GR JV included only priced items such as Options and Colors; the Model Code amount was excluded.', 'A GI JV filter condition was updated in UAT, after which Chassis GI JV was created correctly for test records A001304859 and B001258096.', 'The reported concern was that GI was not created despite GR being present.']
Root Cause: The GI JV filter condition required correction; updating this condition in UAT enabled Chassis GI JV creation.
Resolution: Updated the filter condition in GI JV in UAT and verified correct Chassis GI JV creation using test records A001304859 and B001258096.
Technical Entities: ['GI JV', 'GR JV', 'Chassis Orders', 'Sales Orders', 'Model Code', 'Price Master', 'Price List', 'Options', 'Colors', 'Sales Posting', 'Siebel', 'UAT', 'KB data', 'journal entries', 'B000121443', 'B000062227', 'B000062228', 'B000062229', 'B000001569', 'A001304859', 'B001258096']

Comment: Dear Tsunoda-San,
Thank you for your continued support. 
We would like to report the results of our investigation regarding the chassis orders for which GI JV was not created (B000062227, B000062228, B000062229, B000001569). 
As a result of our investigation, we have confirmed that the reason the GI JV was not created was because the price of the "Model Code" was not registered.
At the time the target chassis order was created, price information for the corresponding model code did not exist in the price master (Price List). Therefore, when creating the GR JV, only details with registered prices such as options and colors were considered, and the price of the model code was not included. 
Sales posting was then carried out, but the GI JV was not created because no price was set in the model code. 
[Cause]
This is because the price information for the target model code was not registered in the price master when creating the chassis order. 
[Response policy]
This issue is not a problem with Siebel, and the system is operating normally. Therefore, we have determined that system modification is not necessary. 
Please let us know if you have any questions. 
Thank you for your support.
(English)
Thank you for your continued support and cooperation.
We would like to share the results of our investigation regarding the affected Chassis Orders (B000062227, B000062228, B000062229, and B000001569) for which the GI JV was not created.
Our analysis confirmed that the GI JV was not generated because the corresponding Model Code did not have a valid price maintained in the Price Master at the time the Chassis Orders were created.
When these Chassis Orders were created, the Price List did not contain pricing information for the affected Model Code. As a result, during GR JV creation, only the amounts for line items with valid prices, such as Options and Colors, were included. The Model Code amount was not included in the GR JV calculation.
Subsequently, when Sales Posting was performed for the related Sales Orders, the GI JV could not be created because the Model Code line item still did not have a valid price.
Root Cause
The required pricing information for the affected Model Code was not maintained in the Price Master List at the time the Chassis Orders were created.
Fix Plan
This is not a Siebel system defect. The system is functioning as designed, and therefore no system modification is required for this case.
Should you have any questions or require further clarification, please feel free to contact us.
Best regards,

Once a Parts Return Order is created/completed, the return amount does not automatically sync with the existing Quote and JCO.

In the reported case, after creating the Return Order, a new Quote was not created and approved by the user. Due to this, the updated return amount was not synced, which resulted in a price mismatch between the Quote and the JCO.
Based on the current observations and system behavior, the issue appears to be related to the operation flow executed at the user end.

Comment: Thank you very much for your continued support.
Thank you for sharing your scenario and UAT test data.
 
As a result of reconfirming the entire processing flow on our side, we have confirmed that the current system specifications operate as follows.
After a parts return order is created/completed, the updated return amount will not be automatically synced to the existing JCO.
In order to correctly reflect the updated return amount in JCO, you need to create a new quotation and then perform "Customer Approved".
After Customer Approved, the latest amount will be synchronized between the estimate and JCO.
Additionally, if you do not create and approve a new quotation after implementing a return order, an error message "Please synchronize the quote first" will be displayed when JC is closed.
Regarding this behavior, we have confirmed similar behavior during reproduction verification in the UAT environment.
However, in the event you reported this time, the process was performed without displaying the synchronization check/error that should have occurred, and we were unable to reproduce the same event in our environment.
Although we conducted UAT verification, log confirmation, and database confirmation using multiple scenarios, we were unable to consistently reproduce the incident you reported.
Based on the current investigation results, we believe that this issue is more likely to be an extremely rare operational special case than a reproducible product defect.
Since this is a rare case, may we close this matter?
 
If you have any questions, please contact us.
 
Thank you for your understanding.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5748
Investigation Summary: The "Order Date" field on Chassis Orders displayed the Sales Order creation date when a Chassis Order was synchronized or mapped to a Sales Order. The behavior was confirmed as existing system logic, including in the SC environment. Based on the confirmed requirement, the logic was changed so that "Order Date" displays the Chassis Order creation date, and the fix was deployed to Production in the 11 June FDP release.
Important Findings: ['Existing logic populated the Chassis Order "Order Date" field with the Sales Order creation date during Chassis Order and Sales Order synchronization.', 'The same behavior was confirmed in the SC environment.', 'The required value for "Order Date" was confirmed as the Chassis Order creation date.', 'The field is editable in the UI.', 'The change was validated in UAT-1 using Chassis Order B001248284 and in UAT-6 using Chassis Order B000007110.', 'The Production fix was deployed as part of the 11 June FDP release.']
Root Cause: Existing system logic set the Chassis Order "Order Date" field to the Sales Order creation date when the Chassis Order was synchronized or mapped to a Sales Order, rather than using the Chassis Order creation date.
Resolution: Modified the "Order Date" logic to display the Chassis Order creation date; validated in UAT and deployed to Production in the 11 June FDP release.
Technical Entities: ['Order Date', 'Chassis Order', 'Sales Order', 'SC environment', 'UAT', 'UAT-1', 'UAT-6', 'B001248284', 'B000007110', 'Production', '11 June FDP release']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5739
Investigation Summary: A delivery approval error occurred in UV Sales Order because an Activity was marked Closed while its mapped Job Card had been canceled. During delivery approval, the system validates that an active Job Card is linked to the Activity; no valid active Job Card was found. Recovery was completed by updating the Activity status to Work Completed, and no product fix was required.
Important Findings: ['An Activity in UV Sales Order is considered completed when its status is Work Completed or Closed.', 'Closing the Job Card normally sets the related Activity status to Work Completed.', 'The issue was replicated in FDP UAT-1 by canceling a Job Card and then manually changing the related Activity from Open to Closed.', 'Delivery approval validates that the Activity has a valid active linked Job Card.', 'A canceled mapped Job Card caused the validation failure because the Activity was Closed without an active Job Card.', 'When a Job Card is canceled, the linked Activity must be manually set to Cancel Request.']
Root Cause: The linked Job Card was canceled, but the related UV Sales Order Activity was manually set to Closed instead of Cancel Request, causing delivery approval validation to fail because no valid active Job Card was linked.
Resolution: Recovery was completed by setting the Activity status to Work Completed. No fix was required; for canceled Job Cards, users must manually set the linked Activity status to Cancel Request.
Technical Entities: ['UV Sales Order', 'Activity', 'Job Card', 'delivery approval', 'FDP UAT-1', 'Work Completed', 'Closed', 'Open', 'Canceled', 'Cancel Request']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5739
Timestamp: 2026-05-13T11:16:00
Comment: Thank you for your support.
We would like to share the analysis details for the incident MFTBCFFR-5739, related to delivery approval error in UV SO due to incomplete Activity.
Please find the summary below:
{color:#ffffff}__{color}
|Incident Number |MFTBCFFR-5739|
|Description|delivery approval error in UV SO due to incomplete Activity|
|Root Cause (RCA)|Please note that the Activity status in UV Sales Order is set to 'Work Completed' when Job Card is closed. After that user can manually set the status of Activity to 'Closed'. In both these cases where Activity status is 'Work Completed' or 'Closed', the Activity is considered to be completed.
So, the status of Activity being set as 'Closed' is not the issue in this case.
We have replicated this issue on FDP UAT-1 environment. Please find below the user steps:
1.) User created a Activity in UV Sales Order and created a Job Card for this Activity.
2.) User then set the status of Job Card to 'Canceled'.
3.) The Activity for this Job Card remained in UV Sales Order with status as 'Open'. User manually updated the status of this Activity to 'Closed'.
While completing the delivery approval request, the system check for he valid active Job Card linked to the Activity. In the affected record, since the Activity status is 'Closed' but the mapped JC was already cancelled, the system could not find a valid active JC. Due to this validation failure error message was displayed.
In this case user should manually update the status of this Activity to 'Cancel Request'.|
|Recovery status|Recovery has been completed.|
|Fix Plan|No fix required. When user Cancel the Job Card, the status of the Activity linked to this Job Card should be manually set to 'Cancel Request'.|
If you require further clarification or assistance, please feel free to reach out.
Regards
Sunaina Gill

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5737
Investigation Summary: A fix for AMS CR MFTBCFFR-5210, intended to default the vehicle "Service Person" field to blank instead of "Siebel Administrator", unintentionally affected standard ODI functionality. As a result, the Asset number was not captured in the Serial Number field. The MFTBCFFR-5210 changes were reverted in production and affected records were recovered.
Important Findings: ['The MFTBCFFR-5210 change correctly set the vehicle "Service Person" field to blank by default; previously it was set to "Siebel Administrator".', 'The MFTBCFFR-5210 implementation unintentionally impacted standard ODI functionality.', 'The impact was that the Asset number was not updated/captured in the Serial Number field.', 'In Sales Order, header VIN# is obtained from "Vehicle No C#" on the Vehicle Screen, while Form Applet VIN# is obtained from "Key" on the Vehicle Screen.', 'Records requiring recovery were identified and recovered.', 'Incidents 5642, 5674, and 5737 were caused by similar issues and were fixed in the production environment.']
Root Cause: The fix implemented for AMS CR MFTBCFFR-5210 unintentionally affected standard ODI functionality, preventing the Asset number from being captured in the Serial Number field.
Resolution: Reverted the changes made for MFTBCFFR-5210 in the production environment and performed recovery for affected records; an alternative fix approach for MFTBCFFR-5210 was to be considered.
Technical Entities: ['MFTBCFFR-5737', 'AMS CR MFTBCFFR-5210', 'Service Person', 'Siebel Administrator', 'standard ODI functionality', 'Asset number', 'Serial Number field', 'Sales Order', 'VIN#', 'Vehicle Screen', 'Vehicle No C#', 'Form Applet', 'Key', 'production environment', '5642', '5674']

Timestamp: 2026-05-13T10:40:00
Author: Animesh
Comment: The issue of this incident is caused due to fix done for AMS CR MFTBCFFR- 5210.
* Upon analysing the issue, it has been found that the fix implemented in MFTBCFFR: 5210 fixed the issue of that incident which was to set field *Personnel in charge of service* for the vehicle as blank initially. Before the change, it was being set as 'Siebel Administrator'.
* While the functionality for MFTBCFFR-5210 is working as expected, the implemented fix plan unintentionally impacted the standard ODI functionality, resulting in the *Asset Number* not being updated into the *Serial Number* field.
* In Sales Order, the *VIN#* in the header is coming from Vehicle Screen (*Vehicle No C#*) and the *VIN#* in the Form applet is coming from Vehicle Screen (*Key*).
* For, now we have reverted the changes done as per the fix of 5210, and look for a different fix plan for MFTBCFFR 5210.
* Also, We have found records in which recovery needs to be done. We have attached the file for which we have done the recovery.
 We request you to please close this incident.
 
Regards,
Animesh

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5737
Timestamp: 2026-05-14T10:29:00
Comment: Thank you very much for your continued support.
This incident occurred due to the modification of AMS CR "MFTBCFFR-5210".
As a result of our investigation, we have confirmed that the modification implemented in MFTBCFFR-5210 is working correctly to set the vehicle's "Service Person" field to blank by default.
Before the change, "Siebel Administrator" was set.
On the other hand, the modifications implemented for MFTBCFFR-5210 unintentionally affected the standard ODI function, resulting in an event where the Asset number was not captured in the serial number field.
In ordering, the VIN# in the header is obtained from "Vehicle No C#" on the vehicle screen, and the VIN# on the Form Applet is obtained from "Key" on the vehicle screen.
We are currently reverting the changes made to support 5210, and are considering another modification method for MFTBCFFR-5210.
We have also confirmed the data that requires recovery, and have already performed recovery on the target data.
Please check the attached list of data that can be recovered.
Attachment:
・
Please note that 5642, 5674, and 5737 are caused by similar issues.
All of these issues have been fixed in the production environment, and we do not expect similar issues to occur in the future.
We apologize for the inconvenience, but please close all incidents.
Thank you for your support.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5715
Investigation Summary: In UAT1, spreadsheet 1-502819545 appeared not to send an approval request after recovery in SR# 5709, although a pending request remained in the approver's Inbox. Recovery changed the spreadsheet from Spreadsheet Requested to Spreadsheet Created and removed its approval history without removing the associated Inbox request entity. When the approver approved the remaining request, the spreadsheet changed to Spreadsheet Approved; JVs were created for the affected Job Cards. The system was determined to be behaving as expected, and the recovery procedure will be updated to deactivate pending approval requests during recovery.
Important Findings: ['Recovery in SR# 5709 changed the spreadsheet status from Spreadsheet Requested to Spreadsheet Created and removed approval history.', "The request entity remained in the designated approver's Inbox after approval history was removed.", 'A subsequent approval submission did not create approval history, creating the appearance that no approval request had been sent.', 'Approving the remaining Inbox request changed spreadsheet 1-502819545 in UAT1 to Spreadsheet Approved.', 'JVs were created for 37 Job Cards associated with the Insurance Spreadsheet, totaling 148 Journal Voucher Items.', 'Future recovery procedures must deactivate pending approval requests to prevent hidden approvals.']
Root Cause: The recovery performed in SR# 5709 removed the spreadsheet approval history but did not remove the pending approval request entity from the approver's Inbox, disrupting the normal approval-history flow.
Resolution: Created JVs for the 37 affected Job Cards (148 Journal Voucher Items) and updated the recovery procedure requirement to deactivate pending approval requests to designated approvers during spreadsheet recovery.
Technical Entities: ['UAT1', 'Sheet# 1-502819545', 'SR# 5709', 'Spreadsheet Requested', 'Spreadsheet Created', 'Spreadsheet Approved', 'approval history', 'Inbox', 'Insurance Spreadsheet', 'Job Cards', 'JVs', 'Journal Voucher Items']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5715
Timestamp: 2026-05-08T11:52:00
Author: Saad
Comment: Thank you for your support and cooperation.
We have analysed this issue and would like to share with you the root cause.
As per our analysis, we have figured out the steps, leading to cause of this incident. They are listed as follows: -
*1)* Initially, the spreadsheet was in the status *Spreadsheet Requested.*
*2)* In SR# 5709, Recovery was performed and the status of the spreadsheet was changed back to *Spreadsheet Created.* As part of recovery, the *approval history was removed from the spreadsheet* as well. The request entity was not removed from the Inbox item of the concerned approver.
*3)* So, the next time when the user submitted an approval request, the approval history was not created in the spreadsheet, leading to an illusion of the approval never being sent, but the approval request item was still present in the inbox of the approver.
*4)* Now, when the approver approved the request entity, the status of spreadsheet changed to *Spreadsheet Approved.*
*Sheet#* 1-502819545 (UAT1)
We have replicated this issue following the steps mentioned above.
We will share with you the fix plan as soon as we device one.
Meanwhile, let us know in case of any query.
Best Regards,
Saad

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5708
Investigation Summary: The 'Create Activity' button was inactive in UV Sales Order after an Activity had been created. Code-level analysis found that the existing logic created one Activity for all Service Effort line items and then disabled the button. The functionality was changed to allow creation of a second Activity when the previous JCO is in Closed or Cancelled status, tested in FDP UAT-1, and deployed to production.
Important Findings: ['For Order# E000452245 on Shikoku Prod, two Service Effort line items existed when the Activity was created.', "The original logic created only one Activity for all Service Effort line items in a Sales Order and then set the 'Create Activity' button to inactive.", 'The updated functionality allows a second Activity to be created in UV Sales Order if the previous JCO status is Closed or Cancelled.', 'The change was tested successfully in FDP UAT-1 using UV SO# E001304686.', 'The fix was applied to the production environment through the regular release on the 23rd.']
Root Cause: The existing 'Create Activity' button logic disabled the button after creating one Activity for all Service Effort line items, without allowing another Activity based on the status of the previous JCO.
Resolution: Updated the UV Sales Order logic to enable creation of a second Activity when the previous JCO is Closed or Cancelled; tested in FDP UAT-1 and deployed to production.

Comment: Dear Tsunoda-San,
The following improvements have already been implemented and released as Kaizen.
# Archive data load history of regularly executed TOB ODI package
Implementation details
In the process of importing data received from TOB and D2S into Siebel, previously the past import history was overwritten on the database when the same ODI package was re-executed. Therefore, it was not possible to investigate or refer to past data.
To address this issue, we have implemented the following improvements.
Created an archive table to hold all data ingestion history.
The archive table stores information necessary for future investigation, such as order number/asset number, import status, import source file name, and package name.
The data import process has been updated so that the history is automatically saved to the archive table each time it is imported.
If data import fails, we have added a mechanism to automatically send email notifications to the support team, allowing for prompt investigation and response.
The above is Kaizen content that has already been implemented.
As a result of our investigation into this incident, there are currently no additional system improvements that can be implemented to prevent similar incidents.
If you have any questions or concerns, please let us know.
 
Thank you for your support.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5693
Investigation Summary: The incident involved duplicate Vehicle records and duplicate Chassis Orders, causing a shipment to be created while the chassis-order status was not updated. The established analysis attributes the duplication to a Model Code change that caused a mismatch between an existing Vehicle and its Chassis Order when a D21A file was received from TOB. A fix was implemented in the SC version under INC6267864 and INC6273871, but the FDP deployment and shipment-status validation remained pending.
Important Findings: ['Duplicate Vehicle records and duplicate Chassis Orders were created for C# 20287.', 'A Model Code change on an existing Vehicle resulted in different Model Codes between the Vehicle and the existing Chassis Order.', 'When D21A was received from TOB, the mismatch caused creation of a new Vehicle and a new Chassis Order with the old Model Code.', 'After D21N was received, the combination associated with PO Number B000362896 was shipped, while the combination associated with PO Number B000350487 remained in C# contact.', 'The SC fix matches the incoming TOB Model Code against the Chassis Order Line Item rather than the Vehicle record, and simultaneously updates the Vehicle Model Code.', 'The final feedback states that shipping had not been updated and required reconfirmation.']
Root Cause: A Model Code change on an existing Vehicle created a Model Code mismatch with the existing Chassis Order; subsequent D21A processing created duplicate Vehicle records and duplicate Chassis Orders.

Timestamp: 2026-05-08T05:06:00
Comment: Mr. Tsunoda
Thank you for your help.
Problem:
The shipment was created, but the status of the chassis order was not updated.
Cause analysis:
This issue occurred because duplicate vehicles were created. Duplicate chassis orders were then created.
The cause of this problem is that the model code of the existing vehicle has been changed. This resulted in different model codes for existing vehicles and existing chassis orders. 
When a new D21A file was received with model code information based on the existing chassis order, a new vehicle was created and a new chassis order with the old model code was also created.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5691
Investigation Summary: A TOB chassis invoice record in DT01 for C#: FP84HG-500043 did not create a Journal Voucher (JV). The record resulted in a NULL line type/product type because the relevant product-type field was NULL and Siebel did not have logic to create a JV for that condition. Subsequent analysis also found that the invoice line had no matching Chassis Order Line Item, causing the default Project Code AA00000000 rather than a chassis order number. Manual recovery was validated to process all TOB invoice scenarios without omissions.
Important Findings: ['The affected record was FP84HG-500043 in the DT01 Chassis Invoice file for the Okayama FDP environment.', 'The billing-data type is identified from the 25th character; the affected record was identified as Post-OP.', 'For the Post-OP record, the 2-character product-type value after the 66th character was NULL, causing the line type/product type to be NULL.', 'Siebel did not contain logic to create a JV when the line type was NULL, so no JV was created.', 'The corresponding invoice data did not exist in the Chassis Order Line Items, although it existed in an associated Sales Order line item; therefore reconciliation could not set the Chassis Order Number as Project Code (CSJS211).', 'When no matching Chassis Order Line Item is found, AA00000000 is assigned as the default project code; manual recovery was confirmed to process all TOB invoices without omission.']
Root Cause: The DT01 Post-OP invoice record had a NULL product-type field, which produced a NULL line type; Siebel had no JV-creation logic for records with a NULL line type. The related invoice line also had no matching Chassis Order Line Item for reconciliation.
Resolution: Manual recovery was validated to process all TOB invoice scenarios without omissions. Future TOB invoice processing will be monitored, and a JV will be created manually when a DT01 record does not produce a JV.

The character *“A” (at position 3 within this segment)* denotes that this is an *Additional Body order*.
* As per current logic, for *Additional Body (A)* and *Option* records, the system reads the *product identifier from the 66th position (from the start of the record)*.

Observed segment around this position:
{{250614SHUSEI (__) 7204}} → the required field between these values is missing.
* Due to the absence of this value, the system was *unable to determine the product*, resulting in the *line type being set to NULL*.
* Conclusion: The incoming data record *does not conform to the expected format/configuration*.
* Action Taken: Enhancements have been implemented on the *Siebel side* to handle such cases where the expected field is blank.
* Impact: *No changes required from TOB side*. Similar records will be handled correctly going forward.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5691
Timestamp: 2026-05-14T05:37:00
Comment: *Overview:*
This issue is related to JV coordination for February's TOB invoice. 
During the first week of each month, specifically the first business day of the month, the TOB sends the previous month's chassis and recycling billing data to Siebel. These data will be used for JV creation and coordination with the KB system. 
The following two types of files are sent to Siebel. 
DT01 - Chassis Invoice
DT27 - Recycling bill
These two types of files are being submitted for 8 FDP environments each.
*Question details:*
The issue reported in Incident# 5691 is related to chassis billing in an Okayama FDP environment. 
The DT01 file contained the following billing data string: 
Among them, the data corresponding to C#: FP84HG-500043 (data highlighted in yellow) was not processed correctly, and as a result, a JV was not created for the data. 
*Survey details:*
After conducting a detailed investigation into this matter, we have come to the following conclusions. 
In each data string, the value in the blue position (25th character from the left) is used to determine the type of billing data. 
The current Siebel configuration defines the following identification settings for TOB billing data: 
1: Model code
4: Color
8: S-bodywork
C: Change (chassis)
A：Post-OP
Other codes: Options
After identifying the data type, the system uses additional position information within the string to determine the product type. 
This data corresponded to the Post-OP type. For Post-OP types, the system uses the orange position value to determine the product type. 
However, the current settings did not handle cases where a Null value was set at the relevant position. 
As a result, the JV creation process was failing. 
*Conclusion:*​
Based on the results of the investigation into the cause, we have now made changes to the settings so that this case can be handled appropriately in the TOB data. 
Similar issues are not expected to occur in the future.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5691
Timestamp: 2026-06-11T08:48:00
Comment: San,
 
Thank you very much for your continued support.
 
We would like to report the results of investigating the logic and related data regarding this matter.
 
TOB billing processing is performed for chassis order details. However, the details corresponding to the TOB billing data received in this case did not exist in the target chassis order details.
 
Therefore, during the reconciliation process with billing data, it was not possible to identify matching chassis order details.
 
  
Typically, if a matching chassis order line is found, that chassis order number will be set as the JV's project code (CSJS211). However, in this case, there was no matching chassis order details, so the chassis order number could not be set in the project code.
 
On the other hand, the item in question existed in the order details associated with the chassis order, and billing data for that item was also received.
 
However, since orders are not subject to reconciliation billing processing, the default project code "AA00000000" has been set as the standard behavior of the system.
 
This event is an extremely rare case, and no other similar events have been confirmed since FDP began operation.
 
Additionally, as a result of checking the operation of existing functions, we have confirmed that the system is operating as designed, and we have determined that no system modifications are necessary at this time.
 
As a future measure, we will monitor TOB claim processing in order to detect such rare cases at an early stage.
 
If a JV is not created for a record in the TOB request file (DT01 file), we will detect it through monitoring and create a JV manually if necessary.
 
Based on the above investigation results, we would appreciate your approval to close this incident.
 
Please let us know if you have any questions or additional questions.
 
Additionally, if you have an opportunity to meet with Mr. Tsunoda at his convenience, we may be able to explain this incident to you.
 
Thank you for your support.
 
(English)
Thank you for your support.
 
Apologies for the delay. We have reviewed the logic and analyzed the data related to this issue. Our findings are as follows:
The TOB invoicing is performed for Chassis Order Line Items. However, the TOB invoice data received in this case does not exist in the corresponding Chassis Order Line Items. Therefore, during the reconciliation process, no matching Chassis Order Line Item could be found based on the invoice data.
When a matching Chassis Order Line Item is found, the Chassis Order Number is used as the Project Code (CSJS211) in the JV. In this case, since no matching Chassis Order Line Item existed, the Project Code could not be set as the Chassis Order.
However, the line item does exist in the Sales Order associated with this Chassis Order, and invoice data was received for that line item. Since reconciliation invoicing is not performed for Sales Orders, the default Project Code *AA00000000* was used.
 
This appears to be an extremely rare case and has been observed only once since the FDP system went live. We have reviewed the existing functionality and confirmed that it is working as designed

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5680
Investigation Summary: The incident involved an error when requesting acceptance inspection approval in FDP. Investigation identified that the Approval Master Data did not contain all required requester positions/UIDs; the master was updated in UAT-1 and deployed to Production in the 11 June FDP release.
Important Findings: ['FDP approval requests are permitted only for UIDs maintained as valid requestors in the master data.', 'Users not listed as valid requestors receive the error message "Please select a valid approver" when generating an approval request.', 'The existing master was compared with positions provided by Shiromoto San, and missing positions were added.', 'The updated Approval Master Data included existing requestors and newly added requestors.', 'The fix was validated in UAT-1 before deployment to Production.']
Root Cause: Required requester positions/UIDs were missing from the Approval Master Data, causing FDP approval requests from those users to be rejected as invalid.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5657
Investigation Summary: The D2S Invoice Mismatch screen had slow loading caused by inefficient processing in the PDQ. Initial indexing and removal of the sort specification did not fully resolve the production issue. The PDQ "01 アンマッチ(全件)" was subsequently optimized, significantly improving screen loading time while preserving export functionality.
Important Findings: ['The PDQ scanned the full available dataset because unmatched records from all periods must remain available for review and export.', 'Initial analysis identified sorting on _D2S SO Number_, _D2S Line Number_, and _Part Number_ as a performance factor because the fields were not indexed.', 'An index based on the sort order was deployed to UAT and then production, but additional performance improvements were still required.', 'The configured sort order was D2S Order Number, Sales Order Item, and Part Number; the sort specification was removed, but the issue persisted after production release.', 'Optimizing PDQ "01 アンマッチ(全件)" significantly improved loading performance, and export functionality was verified successfully.']

RCA:
The slowness observed in loading the ‘D2S Invoice Mismatch’ screen is due to the following reasons:

2. The system sort records based on _D2S SO Number_, _D2S Line Number_, and _Part Number_. Since these fields are not indexed, the sorting process takes longer resulting in the delay.

1. We can restrict the PDQ to fetch data for the last 30 days to reduce the data volume.
2. We can create index in the table for the columns that are being used in the sorting to optimize query execution.
Please confirm the fix plan so that we can proceed with the fix of this issue.

Root Cause: The Service Cost Price calculation on the UV Sales Quote form did not include costs for part line items.
Resolution: Updated the service cost calculation to include parts added through the Job Card; the change was validated in UAT and released to production in the 13 May FDP release.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5643
Investigation Summary: The initial analysis attributed inconsistent price-master processing to D2S records containing end year "9998" instead of "9999", which caused existing records to receive end dates and prevented creation of new records. Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5643
Timestamp: 2026-04-17T04:51:00
Author: Soham Modi
Comment: Thanks for your support.
*Recovery Status:*
The recovery is completed for the affected records across all FDP’s.
*RCA:*
This issue occurred due to the data received from the D2S team on 14th in the price master file was inconsistent, where the end date was provided with the year as “9998” instead of the expected “9999”. 
Please find below the sample data from the file received from D2S:
, 
So the data discrepancy happened in our system for these records where the year was received as “9998”. In our system logic, an end date with year “9999” is treated as an open-ended validity and is set as blank (NULL) on the UI. However, since the received data contained “9998”, it did not meet this condition and was processed differently by the system.
As a result, the system set the end date in previous record and new record processing was stopped due to the error. 
For example, Part#: ML356628:
The following data was received in the file - 
This led to inconsistencies in the Siebel system and caused the batch processing job to fail. Due to this failure, new records with updated start dates could not be created, while existing records had their end dates updated based on the current logic. 
*Fix:*
We have handled this condition in our new package processing so that no discrepancies occur in future based on Date. This issue has been fixed on FDP-PROD.
We’ll also ask Hirata san to investigate on D2S side that why the end date was sent as “9998” instead of “9999” for some records.
Meanwhile please let us know in case of any other queries.
Best Regards,
Soham Modi

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5638
Investigation Summary: A delivery approval error occurred in a UV Sales Order when completing the delivery process. Investigation reproduced the issue in FDP UAT-1 and determined that the associated Purchase Order had been unmapped after the Body line item was deleted from Sales Quote Revision 2, but its status was not changed to 'Cancelled'. Important Findings: ["A Body line item with Net Price '¥135,000' and Cost '¥85,000' was added in Sales Quote Revision 1, and a Purchase Order was created for it.", 'The Body line item was deleted in Sales Quote Revision 2.', "The Purchase Order was unmapped in the UV Sales Order without updating its status to 'Cancelled'.", "Delivery completion then displayed the error message 'Please map all purchase orders'.", 'The issue was replicated in FDP UAT-1 for UV Sales Order# E001303730 and Assessment# H000053287.', 'Recovery for the affected record was completed.']
Root Cause: The user unmapped the Purchase Order for the deleted Body line item without changing the Purchase Order status to 'Cancelled', causing the delivery process to require all Purchase Orders to be mapped.
Resolution: Recovered the affected record. No product fix was required because the incident was caused by user misoperation; the Purchase Order status must be updated to 'Cancelled' before/unmapping it.

Comment: Dear Tsunoda-San,
The following improvements have already been implemented and released as Kaizen.
# Archive data load history of regularly executed TOB ODI package
Implementation details
In the process of importing data received from TOB and D2S into Siebel, previously the past import history was overwritten on the database when the same ODI package was re-executed. Therefore, it was not possible to investigate or refer to past data.
To address this issue, we have implemented the following improvements.
Created an archive table to hold all data ingestion history.
The archive table stores information necessary for future investigation, such as order number/asset number, import status, import source file name, and package name.
The data import process has been updated so that the history is automatically saved to the archive table each time it is imported.
If data import fails, we have added a mechanism to automatically send email notifications to the support team, allowing for prompt investigation and response.
The above is Kaizen content that has already been implemented.
As a result of our investigation into this incident, there are currently no additional system improvements that can be implemented to prevent similar incidents.
If you have any questions or concerns, please let us know.
 
Thank you for your support.

Additionally, as part of our investigation and improvement activities regarding this incident, we have already implemented and released the best and final measures that can be taken on the system side into the production environment.

Comment: Dear Tsunoda-San,
The following improvements have already been implemented and released as Kaizen.
# Archive data load history of regularly executed TOB ODI package
Implementation details
In the process of importing data received from TOB and D2S into Siebel, previously the past import history was overwritten on the database when the same ODI package was re-executed. Therefore, it was not possible to investigate or refer to past data.
To address this issue, we have implemented the following improvements.
Created an archive table to hold all data ingestion history.
The archive table stores information necessary for future investigation, such as order number/asset number, import status, import source file name, and package name.
The data import process has been updated so that the history is automatically saved to the archive table each time it is imported.
If data import fails, we have added a mechanism to automatically send email notifications to the support team, allowing for prompt investigation and response.
The above is Kaizen content that has already been implemented.
As a result of our investigation into this incident, there are currently no additional system improvements that can be implemented to prevent similar incidents.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5625
Timestamp: 2026-07-21T08:17:00
Comment: Dear Tsunoda-San,
The following improvements have already been implemented and released as Kaizen.
# Archive data load history of regularly executed TOB ODI package
Implementation details
In the process of importing data received from TOB and D2S into Siebel, previously the past import history was overwritten on the database when the same ODI package was re-executed. Therefore, it was not possible to investigate or refer to past data.
To address this issue, we have implemented the following improvements.
Created an archive table to hold all data ingestion history.
The archive table stores information necessary for future investigation, such as order number/asset number, import status, import source file name, and package name.
The data import process has been updated so that the history is automatically saved to the archive table each time it is imported.
If data import fails, we have added a mechanism to automatically send email notifications to the support team, allowing for prompt investigation and response.
The above is Kaizen content that has already been implemented.
As a result of our investigation into this incident, there are currently no additional system improvements that can be implemented to prevent similar incidents.
If you have any questions or concerns, please let us know.
 
Thank you for your support.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5622
Investigation Summary: Sales Quotation BIP displayed an incorrect Branch Manager Name because its mapping logic did not use the branch associated with the quotation. Earlier logic derived Manager Name from the Sales Rep/creator's parent position, which could return the wrong branch manager when the creator moved between branches. The logic was revised in FDP UAT-1 and FDP UAT-4, then deployed to Production through the June 2 emergency release.
Important Findings: ['The initial BIP mapping for Branch Sales Manager name was incorrect.', "The prior BIP logic displayed the Last Name of the Sales Rep's Parent Position as Manager Name.", "The required logic is to display the Branch-Head of the branch from which the quotation originated, rather than the quotation creator's current branch or position hierarchy.", 'Using the creator/Sales Rep as the reference could display a different branch manager when the creator moved from branch A to branch B.', 'After the Production deployment, BIP displays blank when no branch manager exists in the target organization hierarchy.']
Root Cause: Incorrect Sales Quotation BIP mapping logic derived Branch Manager Name from the Sales Rep/creator's parent position instead of the branch associated with the quotation.
Resolution: Changed the BIP logic to display the Branch-Head of the quotation's originating branch, validated the change in FDP UAT-1 and FDP UAT-4, and deployed it to Production via the June 2 emergency release.
Technical Entities: ['Sales Quotation BIP', 'BIP Report', 'Branch Manager Name', 'Branch Sales Manager', 'Sales Rep', 'Parent Position', 'Branch-Head', 'Organization', 'Employee Master', 'FDP', 'FDP UAT-1', 'FDP UAT-4', 'Production', 'Iwate Production', 'UAT-1', 'UAT-4', 'NV Quote', 'NV Quotation', 'D8YNIINU', 'D0X20949', '1-1BW1BP', '1-88T8SD', '1-JSTMC', '1-G81P7', '1-M8FQ3', '1-7789RV', '1-1020HK', '1-E8OG5', '1-47SUZE']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5606
Investigation Summary: An error screen occurred when users clicked an approval notification email link after the related approval request had already been approved from the inbox. The approval request was moved to the "Completed Items List", while the email URL continued to reference the original pending request. The behavior was replicated in UAT1 and confirmed as expected system behavior; the incident was closed.
Important Findings: ['The issue occurs when an approval request is approved directly from the inbox before the notification email link is opened.', 'Approved requests are automatically moved from the inbox pending list to the "Completed Items List".', 'The notification email URL still references the original pending approval request after approval.', 'Opening the stale email URL after approval results in the error screen.', 'The behavior was replicated in UAT1 and determined not to be a bug.']
Root Cause: The notification email link references a pending approval request that is no longer available after the request has been approved and moved to the "Completed Items List".
Resolution: Confirmed the behavior as expected system behavior, rejected the incident, and closed it.
Technical Entities: ['inbox', 'approval request', 'Completed Items List', 'UAT1', 'notification email', 'URL']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5606
Timestamp: 2026-04-07T06:33:00
Author: Atul Yadav
Comment: Thank you for your support.
We have checked this issue and following is our finding:
*Root Cause:*
This error occurs when an approval request is approved directly from the inbox, and the link in the notification email is clicked afterward.
When an approval request is approved, it is automatically moved to the "Completed Items List" in the inbox. However, the URL in the email still references the original pending approval request. Since the request has already been approved and removed from the inbox pending list, clicking the link results in the error screen.
This is expected system behavior and not a bug. So, we would like to reject this incident.
We have also replicated this on UAT1 where we approved the request from inbox and then clicked the URL from email.
Please let me know in case of any queries.
Best Regards,
Atul Yadav

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5594
Investigation Summary: D/N prices were not reflected across FDPs because D2S price master files contained Cost Price but omitted list price, and the old package therefore did not set D/N price in PT_Price_List. Recovery completed and prices were reflected across all FDPs. The Bulk Price batch was scheduled on Production for all FDPs and its execution times were adjusted so price updates complete before 07:00 JST.
Important Findings: ['D2S price master files contained Cost Price but were missing list price.', 'The old package did not set D/N price in PT_Price_List when list price was absent.', 'Recovery completed and D/N prices were reflected across all FDPs for the affected part numbers.', 'Bulk Price batch was scheduled for all FDPs on Production to process price files received from D2S.', 'Job timings were changed to 04:30 JST and 05:00 JST so updates complete before 07:00 JST.', 'Price updates were confirmed as working correctly on all FDPs, including FDP-OKAYAMA.']
Root Cause: Price master files received from D2S omitted list price; during execution of the old package, this prevented D/N price from being set in PT_Price_List.
Resolution: Completed recovery, scheduled the Bulk Price batch for all FDPs on Production, and adjusted job timings to 04:30 JST and 05:00 JST to complete price updates before 07:00 JST.
Technical Entities: ['D/N price', 'FDPs', 'D2S', 'Cost Price', 'list price', 'PT_Price_List', 'Bulk Price batch', 'Production', 'FDP-OKAYAMA', 'Okayama prod', 'MX954092', 'M69BES1723']

Root Cause: Inappropriate field values entered by the user for financial information were not correctly transferred to Service Request Details, preventing creation of AP and AR.
Resolution: The user was asked to create a new SR for the required account registration and to share values entered for all fields at each step before submission for further analysis. The incident was then closed.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5588
Investigation Summary: BIP reports generated through the Siebel "Submit" button included only the selected order line when a user selected a specific line item. This was identified as standard behavior of the vanilla BIP; selecting the Sales Order Header before submission included all line items. The issue was fixed in FDP UAT-1 and the changes were deployed to Production on April 07 after business hours.
Important Findings: ['The Siebel standard (vanilla) BIP invoked through the "Submit" button cannot be modified.', 'When a specific order line item is selected, the "Submit" BIP report includes only that selected line item.', 'Selecting the Sales Order Header before using "Submit" causes the BIP report to include all line items.', 'The custom BIP accessed through the "Generate" button was provided as an alternative to avoid the line-item selection behavior.', 'The same behavior was observed in the SC UAT-1 environment for Reference Order #: A027129251.', 'The issue was fixed in FDP UAT-1 for NV Sales Order#: A001297322 and A001256624, then deployed to Production.']
Root Cause: The standard Siebel vanilla BIP generated through the "Submit" button scopes the report to the selected order line item when a line is selected.
Resolution: Changes were validated in FDP UAT-1 and deployed to the Production environment on April 07 after business hours; users were advised to use the custom "Generate" BIP or select the Sales Order Header before using "Submit".
Technical Entities: ['Siebel', 'BIP', 'Submit', 'Generate', 'Sales Order Header', 'SC UAT-1', 'FDP UAT-1', 'Production', 'Reference Order #: A027129251', 'NV Sales Order#: A001297322', 'NV Sales Order#: A001256624']

Timestamp: 2026-04-02T10:31:00
Author: Sunaina Gill
Comment: Thank you for your continued support.
Please note that the BIP generated using the "Submit" button is a standard (vanilla) BIP provided within Siebel and it cannot be modified. To avoid any discrepancies for users, we have provided a custom BIP, which can be accessed via the "Generate" button.
Additionally, please note the following behavior:
When a user generates the BIP report by clicking the Header and then using the "Submit" button, the BIP Report correctly includes all line items.
However, if a user selects a specific line item and then generates the BIP Report, only the selected line item will appear in the Report.
This is standard system behavior. Therefore, we recommend that users either:
Use the "Generate" button for the custom BIP, or
Click on the Sales Order Header before using the "Submit" button to ensure all line items are included.
The same behavior can also be observed in the SC UAT-1 environment. For your reference, we have attached the relevant BIP reports (Reference Order #: A027129251).
 
Please let us know if you have any additional query.
Best regards,
Sunaina Gill

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5584
Investigation Summary: LUMF part prices were received in D2S files dated 20 and 25 March but were not processed while the daily batch execution was temporarily stopped. Root Cause: Daily batch execution was temporarily stopped due to high-volume bulk files from D2S, preventing processing of the received LUMF part prices.
Resolution: Created the LUMF part prices on all FDP environments.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5575
Investigation Summary: Duplicate chassis orders and pool cost orders were created when the same D21A chassis information was processed before and after its model code became available in master data. D21A_19112025200850 (TOB) created chassis order B000303862 without model code MS06GPQGUCV-9 because the code was absent from master data; after TCH01 created the code, D21A_17122025200816 (TOB) created B000332117 with the model code. The behavior matches the current system design, but a permanent corrective measure was not agreed or completed.
Important Findings: ['D21A processing created a chassis order even when the received model code was not present in system master data.', 'Model code MS06GPQGUCV-9 was created by TCH01 on 17 December 2025 after a business request, rather than through normal daily file processing.', 'When the same chassis information was re-received through D21A after the model code became available, the system created a new chassis order instead of updating the existing order.', 'The duplicate chassis orders resulted in duplicate pool cost orders.', 'The requested automatic upsert of a newly available model code to an existing chassis order is not possible within the current D21A/Siebel design because D21A creates both vehicle data and chassis order data and changes may affect dependent systems and business processes.', 'Including MC-9 model codes in daily TCH01 processing was proposed as a future prevention option, but it was rejected as not being a solution.']
Root Cause: The model code MS06GPQGUCV-9 was unavailable in system master data during the initial D21A processing, so the system created a chassis order without the model code. After TCH01 created the model code, re-receipt of the same D21A information was processed as a new chassis order rather than an update, causing duplicate chassis and pool cost orders.

The analysis results for MFTBCFFR-5575 are as follows.
Root cause analysis
The first D21A file was received on November 20, 2025 without a model code attached.
At that time, the model code was not registered, so the system created a chassis order without linking model information.
Subsequently, the type master file was received on December 17, 2025, and the corresponding type code was generated and registered on the same day.
Subsequently, the D21A file was received again on December 18, 2025. At this point, the model code already existed, so the system processed the file and created a new chassis order containing the model code.
As a result, two chassis orders were created for the same D21A input, one without a model code and one with a model code, resulting in the creation of duplicate pool cost orders.
|Chassis Order|Pool Cost Order|VIN #|Fuso Rec#|
|B000303862|B000338198|MS06GP-20016|038765|
|B000332117|B000339371| |

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5575
Timestamp: 2026-05-15T08:44:00
Comment: Thank you very much for your continued support.
 
Investigation into the cause confirmed that the observed system behavior is consistent with the current design and file processing sequence.
 
 
|File reception date|File name|Order details/Model code details|Status|System operation|
|November 18, 2025|D21A_19112025200850 (TOB)|B000303862 (No model code)|Chassis order was received with model code information, but
The model code did not exist in the system's master data at that time. |Chassis order created without model code|
|December 17, 2025|TCH01 (Additional requirements from the business side)|MS06GPQGUCV-9
(Model that was in the previous D21A file)|Master data for the corresponding model code has been created on the system|Master data has been updated on the system|
|December 18, 2025|D21A_17122025200816 (TOB)|B000332117 (with model code)|The same chassis order information was re-received and
This time the model code was already available on the system. |A new chassis order will be created with the model code|
 
 
Description:
 
On November 18, 2025, we received D21A file D21A_19112025200850 (TOB) with model code (MS06GPQGUCV-9).
 
However, during processing, model code MS06GPQGUCV-9 was not present in the system master data. Therefore, a chassis order (B000303862) was created without a model code.
 
On December 17, 2025, the TCH01 file was executed at the request of the business side, and model code MS06GPQGUCV-9 was successfully created in the system.
Then, on December 18, 2025, the D21A file D21A_17122025200816 (TOB) containing the same model code MS06GPQGUCV-9 was received again. Since the model code was already in the system at this point, the system created a new chassis order (B000332117) with the model code entered.
 
Important points:
 
Although TCH01 files are received daily, the corresponding model code MS06GPQGUCV-9 was not available through normal daily file processing, so it was specifically executed based on the business's request.
 
Regarding system change requests:
 
As a business requirement, if a model code becomes available later on the system, it is required to automatically update (upsert) the model code to an existing chassis order.
 
However, since D21A processing is responsible for creating both of the following, this modification is not possible within the scope of the current system design.
 
vehicle data
Chassis order data
 
If you implement an update to a chassis order that has already been created, it may impact multiple other systems and related business processes that depend on it.
 
Additionally, to avoid such problems in the future, TOB can include the MC-9 model code in the daily TCH01 file. Currently, the model code category corresponding to MC-9 is not included in daily file processing, so the required model code was not available on the system at the time of the first D21A processing.
 
For your reference, we have attached a detailed timeline analysis, so please take a look.
We would like to close this incident.
 
If you have any questions, please contact us.
Thank you for your support.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5564
Investigation Summary: A recycle fee order was not created in the Chugoku Production environment because the received D21F file was not executed. The failure was attributed to a temporary server-related issue during D21F ODI package execution on 03-Mar-2026. The affected record was recovered, and Cubastion email notifications were implemented to detect failed TOB file executions and enable prompt recovery and investigation.
Important Findings: ['The D21F file for the affected recycle order was successfully received on 03-Mar-2026.', 'A temporary server-side issue in the Chugoku Production environment prevented D21F ODI package execution, so the recycle fee order was not created.', 'Execution logs were unavailable because the log retention period had passed, preventing further detailed root-cause analysis.', 'Subsequent FDP executions did not show the same issue.', 'Cubastion implemented automatic email notifications to the support team when TOB file execution fails.', 'The affected record recovery was completed.']
Root Cause: A temporary server-related issue in the Chugoku Production environment caused the D21F ODI package execution to fail or not occur after the D21F file was received, preventing creation of the recycle fee order. Further detailed cause analysis was not possible because execution logs were no longer retained.
Resolution: Recovered the affected record and implemented Cubastion email notifications for failed TOB file executions so unprocessed or failed files can be detected and recovered promptly.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5564
Timestamp: 2026-07-23T12:43:00
Author: Deepika Raheja
Comment: Dear Tsunoda-San,
Thank you for your continued support.
Regarding MFTBCFFR:5564, we would like to inform you as follows.
■ Cause analysis (RCA)
As a result of our investigation, we have confirmed that the D21F file related to the targeted recycling fee order was successfully received on March 3, 2026.
 
However, due to a temporary server-related issue in the China production environment, the file was not executed and the recycling fee order was not created.
 
Furthermore, since the log retention period has passed, there are no execution logs left, so a more detailed cause analysis is not possible.
 
■ Monitoring and response in case of recurrence
Although monitoring itself is not a permanent measure, it is implemented as an effective measure to detect similar events at an early stage.
Cubastion has introduced a mechanism that automatically sends an email notification to the support team if the TOB file fails to execute. 
This makes it possible to quickly detect unprocessed or failed files and take prompt recovery actions.
Additionally, if a similar event occurs in the future, an investigation can be started while the execution log is retained, making it possible to conduct a more detailed cause analysis.
 
If you have any questions or concerns, please let us know.
 
Thank you for your support.
 
(English)

Thanks for your support.
Please find below the updates for MFTBCFFR:5564
*Root Cause Analysis (RCA):*
We analyzed the incident and confirmed that the D21F file for the affected recycle order was successfully received on *03-Mar-2026*. However, due to a temporary server-related issue in the Chugoku Production environment, the file execution did not take place. As a result, the recycle fee order was not created at that time.
Since the execution logs are no longer available due to the log retention period, it is not possible to perform any further detailed root cause analysis.
 
*Monitoring / Preventive Action:*
Although monitoring is not a permanent solution, it serves as an effective preventive measure to detect similar issues at the earliest opportunity.
Cubastion has implemented email notifications to automatically alert the team whenever any TOB file execution fails. This allows the team to quickly identify unprocessed or failed files and perform timely recovery actions, minimizing any potential business impact.
If a similar incident occurs in the future, the monitoring mechanism will enable prompt investigation while the relevant execution logs are still available, allowing us to perform a more detailed root cause analysis.
 
Best Regards,
Deepika Raheja

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5559
Investigation Summary: All UV 2-05 FDP reports failed to display data because a hidden SO# filter applied during the 2025 deployment of Profit column logic caused backend queries to process unnecessary data and exceed resource limits. The filter was removed/fixed, and the reports are now correctly visible. Future deployments will include Power BI filter validation and post-deployment report checks in UAT and PROD.
Important Findings: ['A hidden SO# filter was applied to the reports during the 2025 deployment of Profit column logic.', 'The filtered SO# is not available in any FDP except Okinawa.', 'The mismatch caused backend queries to process unnecessary data, exceed resource limits, and return an error when displaying data.', 'The issue affected all UV 2-05 FDP reports.', 'Power BI filters and report visibility will be revalidated after deployments in UAT and PROD.']
Root Cause: A hidden SO# filter applied during the 2025 Profit column logic deployment referenced an SO# unavailable in FDPs other than Okinawa, causing backend queries to process unnecessary data and exceed resource limits.
Resolution: The report issue was fixed and all UV 2-05 FDP reports are correctly visible. Post-deployment Power BI filter validation and report-display sanity checks in UAT and PROD will be added to release communication.
Technical Entities: ['UV 2-05 FDP reports', 'SO#', 'Profit column logic', 'Okinawa', 'FDPs', 'Power BI', 'UAT', 'PROD']

Timestamp: 2026-04-07T10:14:00
Author: Divyesh Ghiya
Comment: Thanks for your support.
Please find below the updates on this incident:
We have fixed the issue occurring in all the UV 2-05 FDP reports and reports are correctly visible now. Please find below the RCA and countermeasure:
*RCA:*
•The issue is caused by a applied hidden filter on SO# in the reports during the deployment of Profit column logic last year in 2025.
•However, that SO# is not available in any of the FDPs except Okinawa.
•Because of this mismatch, the backend query is processing unnecessary data.
•As a result, the query is exceeding resource limits and throwing an error to display the data.
*Countermeasures:*
# We will revalidate the Power BI filters after deployment in both UAT and PROD environments.
# Additionally, we will verify whether all reports are displaying data correctly post-deployment.
# These post-deployment sanity checks will be included in the release communication.
Since no further action is pending on this Jira, kindly allow us to close this ticket and let us know if you have any query.
Regards,
Divyesh Ghiya

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5553
Investigation Summary: Sales Order A050609736 was not synchronized to the latest Quote Revision and remained at revision 2. Error monitoring showed that the Sales Order synchronization failed because an order line record was modified by another user/session after retrieval. The affected record was recovered; no product fix was required because the process was functioning normally, including in UAT.
Important Findings: ["The failure occurred in step 'Sync Sales Order' using service 'EAI Siebel Adapter' and method 'Synchronize' (SBL-BPR-00162).", "'WriteRecord' for business component 'MF RF Order Entry - Line Items' and integration component 'MF Order Item' returned SBL-DAT-00523 and SBL-EAI-04451.", 'Accessories line item Part#: QZ034500 with Total List Price ¥57,100 was being updated from another browser tab or session during Quote-to-Sales-Order synchronization.', 'The concurrent modification prevented the Sales Order from being synchronized to the latest Quote Revision.', 'Recovery was completed for the affected Sales Order record; no fix was required.']
Root Cause: Concurrent modification of the Accessories line item Part#: QZ034500 from another browser tab or session while the user synchronized the quote to the Sales Order caused a record-lock/concurrency error (SBL-DAT-00523), leaving Sales Order A050609736 at revision 2.
Resolution: Recovered the affected Sales Order record. No product fix was implemented because the issue was attributed to rare simultaneous user operations and the process was operating normally.
Technical Entities: ['Sales Order A050609736', 'Quote Revision', 'Sync Sales Order', 'EAI Siebel Adapter', 'Synchronize', 'SBL-BPR-00162', 'MF RF Order Entry - Line Items', 'MF Order Item', 'WriteRecord', 'SBL-DAT-00523', 'SBL-EAI-04451', 'Accessories line item', 'QZ034500', '¥57,100', 'UAT']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5553

Comment: Thank you for your support.
Issue: The Sales Order#: A050609736 is not synced to latest Quote Revision.
RCA: In this case the sales order was stuck at revision 2. This issue is recorded in our error log monitor:
"An error occurred while executing service 'EAI Siebel Adapter', method 'Synchronize' in step 'Sync Sales Order'. (SBL-BPR-00162)
In method 'WriteRecord' of business component 'MF RF Order Entry - Line Items' (integration component 'MF Order Item'), a record with search criteria ' = 14""' returned the following error: ""The selected data has been modified by another user since it was retrieved. Please continue. (SBL-DAT-00523)""(SBL-EAI-04451)"""
This happened because a Accessories line item with Part#: QZ034500 and Total List Price: ¥57,100 was being updated or modified from another browser tab or session at the same time when user tried to sync quote to sales order. Because of this multi-session activity, the order was not synced to latest revisions. This is a case of user misoperation.
Fix Plan: Our backend error logging clearly mentions that record was simultaneously modified by another user. It is a very rare occurrence where user performs two operations at the same time.
Currently process is working fine, which can be tested on UAT as well. No fix required.
Recovery: The recovery has been completed for the affected record. Kindly verify.
Please let us know if you need any further information or assistance on this.
Regards
Sunaina Gill

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5539
Investigation Summary: The incident involved inconsistent behavior when setting the "Bill to Basic Account Code" field in Siebel. Analysis identified missing explicit sequencing of field-value setting, similar to a prior issue involving "Bill to Basic Account Name". The sequencing fix was implemented at the Business Component level, validated in UAT, and released to production on the 23rd.
Important Findings: ['AR and AP Account Ids depend on the User Account Id being set first.', 'Incorrect field-value setting order previously caused failures when fetching AR and AP Account Ids for "Bill to Basic Account Name".', 'The "Bill to Basic Account Code" field did not have equivalent explicit sequence handling and was identified as the cause of inconsistent results.', 'The fix was implemented at the Business Component level, covering MF Job Card Detail Applet, MF JC List Applet (@JC), and MF Job Card List Applet (@Vehicle Master).', 'MF JC Change Order Payment Form Applet (@Change Order) already had the required sequencing and required no change.', 'The change was deployed to all FDP-PRODs and applied to the production environment in the release on the 23rd.']
Root Cause: The "Bill to Basic Account Code" field lacked explicit sequencing to set the User Account Id before retrieving dependent AR and AP Account Ids, resulting in inconsistent behavior.
Resolution: Implemented the required field-value sequencing at the Business Component level, tested it in UAT, and deployed the change to all FDP-PRODs.
Technical Entities: ['Siebel', 'UAT', 'PROD', 'FDP-PRODs', 'Bill to Basic Account Name', 'Bill to Basic Account Code', 'User Account Id', 'AR Account Ids', 'AP Account Ids', 'Business Component (BC)', 'MF Job Card Detail Applet', 'MF JC List Applet (@JC)', 'MF Job Card List Applet (@Vehicle Master)', 'MF JC Change Order Payment Form Applet (@Change Order)', 'MFTBCFFR-4975']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5539
Timestamp: 2026-04-05T17:59:00
Author: Saad
Comment: Thank you for your support and cooperation.
With regards to the issue 4975, we had found that the incorrect order of field value setting resulted in the failure of fetching the AR and AP Account Ids. These Ids are dependent on the setting of the User Account Id first. There was no explicit handling done for the sequence in which this Id had to be set. So we configured the proper sequencing, such that it was ensured that this ID was always set first so that the AR and AP Ids could be fetched without any issue.
This was handled for the Bill to Basic Account Name field previously.
 
Our analysis and speculation tells us that, since this sequence handling is not done explicitly for the Bill to Basic Account Code field, this could be the reason for the inconsistent results. We will implement the same sequence of field value setting as we had done for the field in the previous issue.
Best Regards,
Saad

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5509
Investigation Summary: Consumption Tax on the BIP invoice is sourced from the NV Quote field "Registration Commission Fee Tax," which is calculated as 10% of "Registration Total Commission Fee." Testing in UAT-1 and code/UI regression testing reported that the calculated value displays and updates correctly unless the editable field is manually changed, and changed values propagate to subsequent Quotes and Sales Orders. However, the discussion did not provide conclusive evidence that a user manually changed the affected production record, and the proposed read-only change was not approved.
Important Findings: ['"Registration Commission Fee Tax" is automatically calculated as 10% of "Registration Total Commission Fee."', 'Consumption Tax in the invoice/Expense BIP is derived from "Registration Commission Fee Tax" in the NV Quote.', 'The field is editable in the UI by design for FDP, allowing manual value changes.', 'A changed "Registration Commission Fee Tax" value is synchronized to subsequent Quote revisions and Sales Orders, then reflected in BIP invoices.', 'The behavior was reproduced in FDP UAT-1 using Quote# 1-85UN3O and Sales Order# A001303334.', 'Testing reported no calculation or screen-refresh defect, but no conclusive production-record evidence of manual user modification was provided.']

Timestamp: 2026-07-21T04:46:00
Comment: Mr. Tsunoda
As we have already explained, as a result of our investigation, we have confirmed that the consumption tax on the BIP invoice is calculated from the "Registration fee tax amount" item on the NV estimate.
The tax amount was calculated correctly in Siebel, but the value of the item was manually changed by the user, and as a result of the changed value being carried over to subsequent estimates and SO, we have confirmed that the same value is reflected in the invoice BIP.
In the UAT environment, we reproduced a similar scenario of manually changing item values ​​and conducted various test cases and regression tests. The value only changed when the user made a manual update, otherwise the value was calculated and maintained correctly. Also, no other factors were identified that could change this value. Therefore, we have confirmed that this issue is not a functional issue with Siebel, but rather a data modification by the user.
*About countermeasures*
As explained at the meeting, the current countermeasure is to make the existing "Registration Fee Tax Amount" item for reference only and add another editable item on the same screen. We believe that this will allow users to clearly understand the values ​​that have been manually changed, and will make it easier to identify the cause of similar discrepancies in the future.
On Siebel's side, the investigation into this matter has been completed, and no issues have been identified with current functionality, nor are there any events that require additional preventive measures at this time. Additionally, since this event has only occurred in one case so far, we have not determined that the issue is due to Siebel functionality.
Thank you for your support.
Tanish

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5505
Investigation Summary: Vehicle base price was blank on NV Order Sheet-3 for NV Sales Order# A000413141. The initial assumption that blank output was expected for non-Bus vehicles was corrected after identifying that Trailer and Forklift Product Classes were not handled by NV Order Sheet-3. A fix was validated in UAT-1 and deployed to Production in the March 25 FDP planned release.
Important Findings: ["NV Sales Order# A000413141 has Product Class of Vehicle set to 'Trailer'.", 'Trailer and Forklift Product Classes were not handled in NV Order Sheet-3, causing the vehicle base price to remain blank.', 'The initial BRD-based explanation that Order Sheet-3 output should be blank for non-Bus vehicles did not meet the required behavior equivalent to specification 2.', 'The fix was implemented and verified in UAT-1 using NV Sales Order# A001301436.', 'The fixed changes were applied to the Production environment in the March 25 FDP regular release.']
Root Cause: NV Order Sheet-3 did not handle Trailer and Forklift Product Classes, resulting in a blank vehicle base price for Trailer sales orders.
Resolution: Updated NV Order Sheet-3 to handle Trailer and Forklift Product Classes; validated the change in UAT-1 and deployed it to Production on March 25.
Technical Entities: ['NV Order Sheet-3', 'NV Sales Order# A000413141', 'NV Sales Order# A001301436', 'Product Class of Vehicle', 'Trailer', 'Forklift', 'Bus-type vehicles', 'BRD', 'specification 2', 'UAT-1', 'BIP reports', 'Production environment', 'FDP']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5495
Investigation Summary: Individual Invoice PaymentDueDate was calculated from the Planned Delivery Date in the Quote/NV Quote instead of the Sales Order/NV Sales Order. This caused an incorrect invoice payment date when the Quote and Sales Order planned delivery dates differed. The mapping for Planned Payment Date calculation was changed to use the Sales Order and was validated in UAT-1 before deployment to PROD in the May 13 release.
Important Findings: ['The affected invoice showed PaymentDueDate 2026-03-31 because Payment Term was 1 and the Quote Planned Delivery Date was 2026-02-25.', 'As an immediate recovery, the Quote Planned Delivery Date was updated to 2026-03-17, matching the Sales Order date, and the invoice displayed the correct value after regeneration.', 'The confirmed defect was that Individual Invoice PaymentDueDate/Planned Payment Date was sourced from NV Quote rather than NV Sales Order.', 'UAT1 tests confirmed that when the Sales Order Planned Delivery Date was present, PaymentDueDate was calculated from the Sales Order date; the test response was sent to KB for invoice report generation.', 'Holiday handling was clarified to include Saturdays, Sundays, and defined public holidays; adding holiday-aware Planned Payment Date calculation was identified as a separate Project Change Request requirement.', 'The mapping fix was released to PROD in the May 13 release.']
Root Cause: The Planned Delivery Date used to calculate Individual Invoice PaymentDueDate was mapped from the Quote/NV Quote instead of the Sales Order/NV Sales Order.
Resolution: Updated the Planned Delivery Date mapping for Planned Payment Date calculation from Sales Quote/NV Quote to Sales Order/NV Sales Order, validated the change in UAT-1, and released it to PROD on May 13.
Technical Entities: ['Individual Invoice', 'PaymentDueDate', 'Planned Payment Date', 'Planned Delivery Date', 'Payment Term', 'Quote', 'Sales Quote', 'NV Quote', 'Sales Order', 'NV Sales Order', 'UAT1', 'UAT-1', 'PROD', 'KB', 'invoice report generation', 'testable APIs', 'Baseline Type: Closing', 'Baseline Type: On Delivery', 'Payment Date: EOM', 'Closing Date: EOM', 'Payment due date (holiday flag) vehicle', 'Project Change Request (CR)', 'incident #5472']

Comment: HelloWe have checked this issue and found that the PaymentDueDate in Individual Invoice comes from Planned Delivery Date of Quote which is 25th February, 2026. 
As per the logic, if Payment Term is 1 and month of Planned Delivery Date is of February, then PaymentDueDate month will be February + 1 , i.e. March. This is why {{2026-03-31}} is being shown in Invoice.
Recovery: We have updated the Planned Delivery Date in quote to {{2026-03-17}}(date in Sales Order) and after updating correct values are being shown in invoice data. Please find attached the JSON data for individual invoice. 
Fix Plan: To fix this issue , a change in existing functionality is required. So, we will update the mapping and change it from Quote to Sales Order’s Planned Delivery Date.
Please ask the user to print the invoice again, and also check the fix plan.
Regards,
Atul Yadav
