Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5493
Investigation Summary: Amounts differed between the SV_SIEBEL and KB reports because the KB Bip report showed incorrect UnitPrice values for some line items. When an existing JCO was updated or synchronized after a user changed List Unit Price in Quote Line Items, JCO retained and forwarded the old price. The fix was implemented and validated in UAT-1, then deployed to production in the regular release on the 23rd.
Important Findings: ['The KB Bip report displayed incorrect UnitPrice values for some line items, causing differences from SV_SIEBEL.', 'Updating List Unit Price in Quote Line Items did not update the price selected by JCO.', 'The issue occurred only when an existing JCO was updated/synced.', 'The previous price was saved and sent forward despite the user-entered price change.', 'The fix was verified successfully in UAT-1 before production approval.', 'The fix was applied to production during the regular release on the 23rd.']
Root Cause: For updates/synchronizations of an existing JCO, JCO picked up the old List Unit Price instead of the newly updated price in Quote Line Items.
Resolution: Fixed the JCO price-selection behavior in UAT-1, validated the result, and deployed the fix to production in the regular release on the 23rd.
Technical Entities: ['SV_SIEBEL', 'KB reports', 'KB Bip report', 'UnitPrice', 'List Unit Price', 'Quote Line Items', 'JCO', 'UAT-1', 'production environment', 'JC#I001303575']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5488
Investigation Summary: Profit values between the UV Sales Order and the latest UV Sales Quote revision became misaligned when a Sub Quote was synced after the Sales Quote had already completed approval and been synced to the Sales Order. The issue was reproduced in FDP UAT-1 using UV Quote#: 1-6UW1UZ and UV SO#: E001303159. A validation preventing post-approval Sub Quote updates was released to Prod on 9th April, and recovery was completed.
Important Findings: ['Sub Quote 1-7DUHTZ was synced to the UV Sales Quote after the Sales Quote had been approved and synced to the Sales Order.', 'The "Update Customer Quote" button remained active in the Sub Quote detail view when the UV Sales Quote status was "Initial Approval Completed".', 'Service items synced to the UV Sales Quote after approval were not synced to the UV Sales Order.', 'The issue was replicated in FDP UAT-1 with UV Quote#: 1-6UW1UZ and UV SO#: E001303159.', 'Recovery was completed before the production fix release.']
Root Cause: The "Update Customer Quote" button allowed Sub Quote updates after the UV Sales Quote reached "Initial Approval Completed" and had already been synchronized to the UV Sales Order, causing later Service items to update the quote but not the order.
Resolution: Added validation to display "Sales Quote has already been completed." when "Update Customer Quote" is selected after the UV Sales Quote reaches "Initial Approval Completed". The change was released to Prod on 9th April.
Technical Entities: ['UV Quote Rev 2', 'UV Sales Order', 'UV Sales Quote', 'Sub Quote 1-7DUHTZ', 'Update Customer Quote', 'Initial Approval Completed', 'FDP UAT-1', 'UV Quote#: 1-6UW1UZ', 'UV SO#: E001303159', 'Activity', 'Job Card', 'Work Order', 'Service Quote', 'Update Sales Quote', 'Generate Approval', 'Prod', 'Sales Quote has already been completed.']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5488
Timestamp: 2026-03-25T11:13:00
Author: Sunaina Gill
Comment: Thank you for your continued support.
We would like to share the analysis details for incident MFTBCFFR-5488, regarding the sync issue in the UV Sales Order.
Issue:
The Profit of the Sales Order and the latest Quote revision are not aligned.
Root Cause Analysis (RCA):
The issue occurred because Sub Quote 1-7DUHTZ was synced to the UV Sales Quote after the sales quote had already been approved and synced to the Sales Order. This was possible because the "Update Customer Quote" button on the Sub Quote detail view remains active even after the Sales Quote status is set to "Initial Approval Completed".
We have successfully replicated this issue in the FDP UAT-1 environment (Reference Record: UV Quote#: 1-6UW1UZ, UV SO#: E001303159).
Steps to Reproduce:
# Create a UV Sales Quote and add an Activity.
# Create a Job Card from the Activity.
# In the UV Sales Quote, click 'Generate Approval' and proceed to create the UV Sales Order.
# In the Job Card, complete the Work Order and create a Service Quote.
# Click "Update Sales Quote" button in the Service Quote to create a Sub Quote under the UV Sales Quote.
# Observe that the UV Sales Quote status is "Initial Approval Completed", but the "Update Customer Quote" button remains active.
# Click "Update Customer Quote" to sync Service items to the UV Sales Quote.
# Note that these items are not synced to the UV Sales Order.
Fix Plan:
Once the UV Sales Quote status is "Initial Approval Completed", if a user attempts to click the "Update Customer Quote" button in the Sub Quote tab, a validation message will be displayed:
"Sales Quote has already been completed."
Recovery Status: Recovery has been completed.
Kindly review the proposed fix plan and let us know if you have any questions or concerns.
Regards,
Sunaina Gill

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5481
Investigation Summary: Duplicate vehicle records were created when a vehicle was initially registered without a model code because the model code was unavailable in the Production environment. After the model code was added, the update process searched by model code and could not match the original record, so it created a new record. Impacted Sales Orders and vehicles were recovered, and monitoring was deployed across all FDP environments to detect and recover similar records promptly.
Important Findings: ['The initial vehicle record was created without a model code because the code was not available in the Production environment.', 'The update process uses the model code to locate an existing vehicle record.', 'Because the original record lacked the model code, the system could not identify it and created a duplicate vehicle record with the correct model code.', 'Example impacted record: Hakodate Production vehicle MS06GP-20085; initial record created on 19 Dec 2025, model code added on 23 Dec 2025 under SR MFTBCFFR-5162, and duplicate creation occurred during the 24 Dec 2025 update.', 'Impacted Sales Orders and vehicles required recovery; recovery of the Hakodate vehicle was completed.', 'A monitoring script was deployed across all FDP environments to send email alerts for similar records so they can be recovered immediately.']
Root Cause: The model code was unavailable when the original vehicle record was created, leaving that record without a model code. After the code was added, the system's model-code-based update lookup could not find the original record and created a duplicate vehicle record.
Resolution: Recovered impacted Sales Orders and vehicle records, and deployed a monitoring script across all FDP environments that sends email alerts for records matching this condition, enabling immediate recovery.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5481

Author: Divyesh Ghiya
Comment: Thank you for your support.
We have analyzed this issue thoroughly and below are our findings:
*RCA*: When the first vehicle record was created, the model code for that vehicle was not yet available in the Production environment. Because of this, the vehicle was created without a model code. Later, the model code was added to the Production environment.
When the system tried to update the existing vehicle record, it searched for a vehicle with that model code. Since the original vehicle record did not contain the model code, the system could not find the existing vehicle. As a result, the system created a new vehicle record with the correct model code, which led to duplicate vehicle records.
Example: Hakodate Production
Vehicle: MS06GP-20085
*19 Dec 2025:* First vehicle record created (without model code).
*23 Dec 2025:* Model code was added to Production(SR MFTBCFFR-5162).
*24 Dec 2025:* System attempted to update the vehicle record.
Since the original record had no model code, the system created another vehicle with the correct model code, causing duplication.
*Recovery Plan:* We have extracted all the impacted Vehicles and Sales order on which recovery is required. We are proceeding with recovering all the Sales Order first so that users can proceed with business operations. Please find attached list of all the impacted Vehicles and Sales Orders. We are performing the recovery and will inform you soon once it gets completed. 
*Fix Plan:* No Fix plan is required as this is a data issue rather than a system issue. This issue occurred because the model code was not available in the production environment. Same occurrence is also observed in SC version also. 
Please let us know if you have any query or need any additional support.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5474
Investigation Summary: Registration Request tax-related line items were not created when the Vendor Code derived from the Registration Request Master had no Account Payable Information. This prevented required values from being maintained and could prevent tax finalization/JV creation. The solution was aligned with the SC version, tested in UAT-1, and released to PROD on 13 May.
Important Findings: ['In NV Sales Order, the Vendor Code for a Registration Request is derived from the Registration Request Master based on the Registration Location.', 'When the derived Vendor Code lacked Account Payable Information, tax-related Registration Line Items were not generated.', 'JV creation requires tax Registration Items with Part# S02, S03, or S06 and an actual amount greater than zero.', 'Before tax finalization, mandatory vendor payment fields are required when the actual amount including tax is greater than zero.', 'The fix was changed to match the SC version by making Customer Code, Customer Payment Date, and Customer Payment Method editable in Registration Request line items.', 'The changes were implemented in UAT-1, tested with SO# A001302470 and A001303987, and released to PROD on 13 May.']
Root Cause: The system did not create tax-related Registration Request line items when the Vendor Code derived from the Registration Request Master lacked Account Payable Information, leaving users unable to maintain required information for tax finalization.
Resolution: Updated Registration Request line-item behavior in accordance with the SC version, including editable Customer Code, Customer Payment Date, and Customer Payment Method fields; the change was released to PROD in the 13 May release.
Technical Entities: ['NV Sales Order', 'Registration Request', 'Registration Request Master', 'Registration Location', 'Vendor Code', 'Account Payable Information', 'Registration Line Items', 'JV', 'Part# S02', 'Part# S03', 'Part# S06', 'Actual amount including tax', 'Vendor Payment Method', 'Payment Term', 'Vendor Payment Term', 'Vendor House Bank', 'Customer Code', 'Customer Payment Date', 'Customer Payment Method', 'Customer Payment Type', 'Customer Master', 'SC version', 'Siebel', 'UAT-1', 'FDP UAT-8', 'Chugoku Production', 'SO# A001302470', 'SO# A001303987']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5472
Investigation Summary: Invoices could not be issued because the Payment Date was blank when the source Payment Date was null in NV Sales Order and NV Quote. The investigation established that the system lacked the required fallback logic to derive the invoice payment date from delivery-related dates under the configured payment-deadline conditions. The logic was iteratively corrected and tested in UAT-1, then released to PROD in the 13th May release.
Important Findings: ['Payment Date on the Invoice was blank because the corresponding value was null in NV Sales Order and NV Quote.', 'The original behavior required a manually entered Payment Date after selecting a month in Payment Term Type, which did not satisfy the required invoice behavior.', 'For Payment Due Date (Baseline Type) Vehicle = "After Delivery", a null Payment Date must use the planned delivery date before Sales Posting and the Actual Delivery Date after Sales Posting.', 'The required fallback behavior was expanded beyond Payment Due (Term) Vehicle = "00"; dates also had to be displayed for terms other than "00".', 'For Payment Due Date (Baseline Type) Vehicle = "After Deadline", the proposed behavior was to display Payment Scheduled Date when Payment Date was null and make the field mandatory at Quote.', 'The proposal to replace the Actual Delivery Date with the system-generated actual sales date was rejected.']
Root Cause: When Payment Date was null in NV Sales Order and NV Quote, the Invoice logic did not derive a payment date from the required delivery-related dates and payment-deadline conditions.
Resolution: Implemented the corrected payment-date derivation logic based on user feedback, completed UAT-1 testing, and released the change to PROD in the 13th May release.
Technical Entities: ['Invoice', 'Payment Date', 'NV Sales Order', 'NV Quote', 'Payment Term Type', 'UAT1', 'UAT-1', 'PROD', 'Invoice Bugyo', 'Payment Due Date (Baseline Type) Vehicle', 'Payment Due (Term) Vehicle', 'After Delivery', 'After Deadline', 'Sales Posting', 'Planned Delivery Date', 'Actual Delivery Date', 'Payment Scheduled Date', 'Quote', 'actual sales date', 'Incident 5495', 'FDP release']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5462
Investigation Summary: Sales Price in Quote Line Items was not set to zero for non-chargeable YS4A, YS5A, and YS6A line items. Investigation found that the existing zero-price condition for non-chargeable line items excluded these parts. The condition was updated, validated in UAT1 using JC Number I001303010, and deployed to production in the March 25 regular FDP release.
Important Findings: ['The issue affected Sales Price in Quote Line Items for non-chargeable YS4A, YS5A, and YS6A line items.', 'Existing logic set Sales Price to 0 for non-chargeable line items but did not include YS4A, YS5A, or YS6A parts.', 'The fix added YS4A, YS5A, and YS6A parts to the existing zero-price condition.', 'The fix was validated in UAT1 with test record JC Number I001303010; Sales Price could be controlled by Line Item Type.', 'The fix was applied to the production environment through the March 25 FDP regular release.']

Resolution: Updated the existing non-chargeable line-item condition to include YS4A, YS5A, and YS6A parts, validated the change in UAT1, and deployed it to production in the March 25 FDP release.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5452
Investigation Summary: Sales Orders were displayed in the logged-in user's 'My' view even when the user was not the sales person in charge. Investigation determined that visibility was granted to all members listed in the Other Team Members/Sales Order team context. The visibility logic was changed so that only the logged-in user who is the Primary Employee of the order's primary position association can view the order in 'My'; the change was deployed to Production on 23/04/2026.
Important Findings: ['Entity Transfer added users to the Sales Order team, causing multiple users to be associated with an order.', "The issue occurred because Sales Orders were visible in 'My' view for all members shown in the Other Team Members applet.", "The required behavior was that selecting 'My' must not display orders belonging to other sales representatives.", 'The final visibility rule uses the logged-in user as the Primary Employee of the primary position association with the order.', 'The same correction was applied to the NV Quotes tab.', 'The production deployment was completed in the release on 23/04/2026.']
Root Cause: The 'My' view visibility logic allowed all users associated through the Other Team Members/Sales Order team to view a Sales Order, instead of restricting visibility to the logged-in user who is the Primary Employee of the order's primary position association.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5451
Investigation Summary: An incorrect approval flow was triggered for an NV Quote revision because the backend field "Profit Amount High Flag" was set to "Y" incorrectly. The issue was replicated in FDP UAT-1 using multi-browsing activity, while other approval-flow scenarios operated correctly. A code-level fix was implemented to recalculate the field from the latest Quote revision updates and was deployed to Production in the April 23 FDP release.
Important Findings: ['The incorrect value "Y" in "Profit Amount High Flag" caused the "FDP Operating Profit Quote Change" approval flow to be triggered incorrectly.', '"Profit Amount High Flag" is a backend field used in approval-flow conditions for NV Quote revisions based on Sales Profit changes.', 'For revised NV Quotes, the flag should be "Y" when Sales Profit remains the same or increases, and "N" when Sales Profit decreases.', 'The issue was replicated in FDP UAT-1 using multi-browsing activity; other tested approval-flow cases were reported as working correctly.', 'The implemented fix recalculates "Profit Amount High Flag" based on the latest updates made during Quote revision.', 'The fix was deployed to Production through the FDP release on April 23.']
Root Cause: During NV Quote revision, "Profit Amount High Flag" was incorrectly updated to "Y" due to multi-browsing activity, causing the "FDP Operating Profit Quote Change" approval flow to trigger instead of the applicable flow.
Resolution: Implemented a code-level fix to recalculate "Profit Amount High Flag" using the latest Quote revision updates, validated the NV Quote approval process in FDP UAT-1, and deployed the change to Production in the April 23 FDP release.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5436
Investigation Summary: A delivery approval error occurred for an NV Sales Order after the associated Chassis Order was moved to "Pending" through an SR and then reprocessed to "Ordered." The system attempted to create another Vehicle record; because a Vehicle already existed, the existing Vehicle was unmapped from the Chassis Order and Sales Order. The issue was replicated in UAT-1, the affected record was recovered on February 27, and the user subsequently completed Sales Posting.
Important Findings: ['Approving an NV Sales Order with Product Class "Trailer" automatically created a Chassis Order.', 'Setting the Chassis Order to "Ordered" created a Vehicle that was mapped to both the Chassis Order and Sales Order.', 'After the Chassis Order was set to "Pending" through an SR and reprocessed to "Ordered," the system attempted to create a new Vehicle record.', 'Because a Vehicle record already existed, no new Vehicle was created and the existing Vehicle was unmapped from both related orders.', 'The behavior was replicated in UAT-1 using SO# A001302411 and Chassis Order# B001302412.']
Root Cause: Recovery performed under an SR changed the Chassis Order status to "Pending" after a Vehicle had already been created. Reprocessing the order to "Ordered" caused the system to attempt Vehicle creation and unmap the existing Vehicle from the Chassis Order and Sales Order.
Resolution: Recovered the affected record on February 27; the user successfully completed Sales Posting for the Sales Order.
Technical Entities: ['Delivery Approval Error', 'NV Sales Order', 'Product Class', 'Trailer', 'Chassis Order', 'Vehicle', 'Sales Order', 'UAT-1', 'SO# A001302411', 'Chassis Order# B001302412', 'Siebel', 'SR', 'Sales Posting']

|Incident Number|MFTBCFFR-5436|

|Root Cause (RCA)|Kindly note the user steps for the mentioned issue:
1.) User a created a NV Sales Order with Product Class as 'Trailer'.
2.) A Chassis Order was automatically created after the Sales Order was approved.
3.) The user processed the Chassis Order, and its status was updated to “Completed”.
4.) When the status of Chassis order is set to 'Ordered', a corresponding Vehicle was created and correctly mapped to both Chassis Order and Sales Order.

Please note that this issue has been successfully replicated in the UAT-1 environment.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5429
Investigation Summary: The Tax exemption/Non Tax Flag was always set to "Y" because the corresponding flag was disabled in Siebel configuration, preventing its logic from executing. An initial UAT1 configuration fix did not cover the "Both" case for new registration of accounts receivable and payable when the Tax exemption flag was unchecked. Additional changes were made and verified in UAT1, then deployed to production through an emergency release on March 5, 2026.
Important Findings: ['The Consumption Tax Exempt flag/Non Tax Flag was inactive in Siebel configuration, so its logic processing did not execute and the field defaulted to "Y".', 'The initial configuration change resolved part of the issue in UAT1 but failed for "New registration of both accounts receivable and payable" when the Tax exemption flag was unchecked.', 'Necessary changes were made for the "Both" case on UAT1, and user testing confirmed that everything was working as expected.', 'The validated fix was applied to the production environment in an emergency release on March 5, 2026.']
Root Cause: The Consumption Tax Exempt flag/Non Tax Flag was disabled in Siebel configuration, preventing logical processing and causing the field to default to "Y".
Resolution: Updated the required configuration, including changes for the "Both" accounts receivable and payable registration case; the fix was verified in UAT1 and deployed to production via an emergency release on March 5, 2026.
Technical Entities: ['Siebel', 'Consumption Tax Exempt flag', 'Non Tax Flag', 'Tax exemption flag', 'UAT1', 'New registration of both accounts receivable and payable', 'FDP', 'production environment']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5428
Investigation Summary: The incident involved duplicate Chassis Orders/Purchase Orders and Recycle Fees, plus blank Pool Cost items in NV Pool Cost Order. Duplicate Purchase Orders were traced to duplicate Vehicle records in Chugoku production for chassis# MS06GP-20140, caused when a Vehicle Model Code update created records with different model codes. Pool Cost Master End Date values were corrected in FDP Chugoku and affected records were recovered, but the recurrence-prevention fix for the duplicate-order issue remained pending deployment to FDP.
Important Findings: ['Receiving multiple D21A files from TOB is normal and was not the confirmed cause of the duplicate-order issue.', 'Chugoku production contained two Vehicle records for chassis# MS06GP-20140 with different Model Codes, resulting in duplicate Purchase Orders.', 'Updating the Model Code on a Vehicle was identified as causing duplicate Purchase Order and Vehicle records; a similar issue was recorded in MFTBCFFR-4952.', 'Pool Cost Master End Date values in FDP Chugoku remained set to 2025, causing blank Pool Cost items; the End Date was corrected and affected records were recovered.', 'The SC fix changes Model Code matching to use the Chassis Order Line Item rather than the Vehicle record and synchronously updates the Vehicle Model Code from the incoming TOB file.', 'The duplicate-order fix was implemented in the SC version under INC6267864 and INC6273871, but deployment to FDP required SC approval.']
Root Cause: A Vehicle Model Code update created duplicate Vehicle records with different Model Codes for the same chassis#, which generated duplicate Purchase Orders/Chassis Orders. Separately, Pool Cost Master End Date values in FDP Chugoku had not been updated and remained set to 2025.

Comment: Thank you for your support and cooperation.
With regards to this incident, our analysis tells us that Siebel System has sent the correct response for the concerned 3 lubrication lines to the KB system.
The response sent corresponding to the 3 lubrication line items is as follows :-
 
MFLineItems Qty="8" TaxRateType="0" UnitPrice="7,840" ConsumptionTax="" SalesAmountTotalIncludingTax="" Discount="0" LineNumber="30300" ServiceItemNumber="18930001" Sub-totalAmountwithoutTax="7,840" ServiceItemName="Engine Oil Super DH-2" G-flag="" TaxRate="10"
MFLineItems Qty="2" TaxRateType="0" UnitPrice="3,512" ConsumptionTax="" SalesAmountTotalIncludingTax="" Discount="0" LineNumber="30310" ServiceItemNumber="30109001" Sub-totalAmountwithoutTax="3,512" ServiceItemName="Brake Fluid" G-flag="" TaxRate="10"
MFLineItems Qty="3" TaxRateType="0" UnitPrice="4,257" ConsumptionTax="" SalesAmountTotalIncludingTax="" Discount="0" LineNumber="30320" ServiceItemNumber="17460001" Sub-totalAmountwithoutTax="4,257" ServiceItemName="Wheel Bearing Grease" G-flag="" TaxRate="10"
 
KB side is printing the standard amount for the above 3 line items as :-
 
18930001 : 10800
30109001 : 3520
17460001 : 4110
It can clearly be observed from the above response that the above three values being printed on KB Invoice Sheet was never sent by Siebel.
We have also conveyed the above to Yoshihara San in this regard.
Our speculation is that the KB team needs to review their calculation logic for this field.
We are also attaching the entire response for your reference.
 
Best Regards
Saad

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5383
Investigation Summary: When a new Assessment Request reused a VIN from a cancelled previous Assessment Request, approving Stock In Verification activated the "Previous Assessment Flag". The flag prevented UV Body Building POs for that VIN from being mapped to a new sales order. Data was recovered, making the BB POs available on the "Map" screen, and the incident was closed.
Important Findings: ['Reusing a VIN from a cancelled previous Assessment Request triggered the "Previous Assessment Flag" after Stock In Verification approval for the new assessment number.', 'The "Previous Assessment Flag" indicates that the VIN and its associated UV BB POs already exist in a previous assessment.', 'The flag prevented UV Body Building POs associated with the VIN from being mapped to a new sales order.', 'Data recovery restored availability of the BB POs on the "Map" screen.']
Root Cause: The "Previous Assessment Flag" was activated because the VIN and associated UV BB POs were already present in a previous Assessment Request, blocking PO mapping for the new sales order.
Resolution: Recovered the data so that the BB POs became available on the "Map" screen.
Technical Entities: ['Assessment Request', 'VIN', 'Previous Assessment Flag', 'Stock In Verification', 'UV Body Building POs', 'UV BB POs', 'sales order', 'Map']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5383
Timestamp: 2026-02-18T07:27:00
Comment: Thank you for your continued support.
We have analyzed the issue and here are our findings:
 1.When we create a new Assessment Request and add the VIN of the previous Assessment Request after cancelling the previous Assessment Request.
 2.Then a Flag called "Previous Assessment Flag" gets activated after we approve stock In Verification corresponds to the new assessment number.
 3. This Flag does not allow the UV Body Building POs corresponding to the VIN to be mapped in new sales order.
 Here, the previous assessment flag means, the VIN and UV BB POs correspond to this VIN are present already in a previous assessment.
 This is the current functionality as of now.
Feel free for further assistance.
Regards
Ravi Raghuvanshi

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5374
Investigation Summary: A UV Quote approval record was affected when the approver and alternative approver updated the Action simultaneously from multiple browsers. The concurrent Approved and Rejected actions caused other approvals to become Auto Rejected while the first approval remained Approved. The behavior was replicated in UAT-1 and classified as user miss-operation rather than a system defect. The affected record was recovered by changing the UV Quote status to In Progress so the approval process could continue.
Important Findings: ['Approval history timestamps indicated concurrent user actions.', 'The approver set Action to Approved while the alternative approver simultaneously set Action to Rejected.', 'The concurrent actions caused other approvals to become Auto Rejected and retained the first approval as Approved.', 'The scenario was replicated in UAT-1 using UV Quote "1-7XXRK3".', 'The affected UV Quote was recovered by setting its status to In Progress.']
Root Cause: Simultaneous Action updates by the approver and alternative approver from multiple browsers, resulting in conflicting Approved and Rejected actions.
Resolution: Recovered the affected record by changing the current UV Quote status to In Progress, allowing the user to continue the Quote Approval process.
Technical Entities: ['Approval history', 'Action', 'Approved', 'Rejected', 'Auto Rejected', 'UAT1', 'UAT-1', 'UV Quote', '1-7XXRK3', 'In Progress', 'Quote Approval process']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5342
Investigation Summary: In NV FDP China, trade-in vehicles were not displayed on the Sales Order Sheet, and Stamped Model Code, Registered Year, and C/# number were blank in NV quotations and sales orders. Investigation confirmed that Order Sheet BIP displays trade-in items only when Trade-In Amount is greater than 0, while Registered Year and Stamped Model Code are sourced from the Product ID of the linked Model Code. The observed values were blank in FDP production and SC production; C/# number is designed to remain blank in both environments.
Important Findings: ['Order Sheet BIP displays trade-in items only when Trade-In Amount is greater than 0.', 'The target NV quotation had Trade-In Amount set to 0 on the trade-in vehicle detail line, so the trade-in item was not displayed.', 'Registered Year and Stamped Model Code are populated from the Product ID of the linked Model Code.', 'The applicable Model Code had blank Registered Year and Stamped Model Code values in both FDP production and SC production.', 'C/# number is always blank by design in both SC and FDP environments.', 'SC production SO# A037817024 also had Trade-In Amount of 0 and therefore did not display the trade-in item in Order Sheet BIP.']
Root Cause: The trade-in vehicle was not displayed because its Trade-In Amount was 0, which does not meet the Order Sheet BIP condition of Trade-In Amount greater than 0. Blank Registered Year and Stamped Model Code resulted from blank values on the applicable linked Model Code; C/# number is blank by design.
Resolution: No corrective change was applied. The behavior was confirmed as existing Order Sheet BIP logic and existing data/configuration; updating C/# number was offered if requested.
Technical Entities: ['NV FDP China', 'NV quotation', 'Sales Order Sheet', 'Order Sheet BIP', 'Trade-In Amount', 'Stamped Model Code', 'Registered Year', 'C/# number', 'Product ID', 'Model Code', 'FDP production environment', 'SC production environment', 'SC production', 'SO# A037817024']

Root Cause: The backend column value in the Dealer master record, required for the join that retrieves the Dealer code in EC BIP, was not updated in the affected FDP Production environment.
Resolution: Updated the backend data in the Dealer master record so EC BIP retrieves and displays the correct Dealer code value.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5333
Investigation Summary: In FDP UAT-1, cancelling a Work Order line item after Quote customer approval updated the Quote price but left the JCO price unchanged when the Job Card was closed without creating and approving a new Quote. The issue was compared with SC behavior and a synchronization fix was implemented in UAT-1. The fix was released to the production environment on March 11.
Important Findings: ['The issue was reproducible in UAT-1 when a labor, parts, or lubrication line item was cancelled after the Quote was customer approved.', 'Cancelling a Work Order line item immediately updated the Quote total, but did not update the corresponding JCO price.', 'JCO pricing was previously refreshed only when a new Quote was created and customer approved after the line-item cancellation.', 'The resulting mismatch affected Labor List Price between the Quote and JCO when the Job Card was closed without re-syncing the Service Quote.', 'In FDP, the JCO Subtotal price is sent to KB, making JCO price synchronization required.', 'The fix was tested in UAT-1 using SC behavior as the reference and then deployed to production.']
Root Cause: The FDP JCO price was not synchronized when Work Order line items were cancelled after Quote customer approval; JCO was updated only after a subsequent Quote creation and customer approval.
Resolution: Implemented a JCO price synchronization fix in FDP UAT-1, aligned with the SC reference behavior, and released it to production on March 11.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5333
Timestamp: 2026-02-09T14:20:00
Author: Ayaz
Comment: Thanks for your support.
This issue is replicable on UAT, please follow these steps to replicate it on UAT-1 ->
1) Create a New Job Card
 2) Create a work order and add Line Items (Parts, Labor and Lubrication) in it.
 3) Create/Sync Quote and make the quote customer approved.
 4) Now Labor list price will be same in JCO and Quote.
 5) Go to Work Order Line Items cancel one of the labor.
 6) In quote the price of cancelled labor is removed, but in JCO price of cancelled labor is still there. so, there is a difference in
   Labor List Price at Quote and JCO.
 7) Now close the Job Card without syncing service quote to JCO
 
 At this point, we can see a price mismatch:
 Quote shows the reduced labor price
 JCO still shows the higher labor price.
 
 We have performed thorough analysis of this issue and found the root cause:-
RCA:
 When a user cancels any line item (labor/parts/lubricants) in the Work Order, the system immediately updates the total price in the Quote.
 However, the JCO price is not updated at the same time.
 The JCO price is updated only when a quote is created and customer approved after the cancellation of Line Items.
 So, if a line item is cancelled after quote is customer approved, and user does not create and customer approved a new quote but he directly closes the Job Card. Then the JCO continues to display the old price, while the Quote shows the updated price.
 This is why a price difference appears between the Quote and the JCO.
 
Fix Plan:
We are currently evaluating different possible fix options for this issue.
 Please allow us to schedule a meeting with you, so we can discuss the available approaches and decide on the most suitable fix plan.
 Meanwhile Let us know in case of any query.
Regards,
 Ayaz

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5325
Investigation Summary: A print status error occurred when the print button was clicked because a connection to the Canon server could not be established. Review of FDP production records found the issue affected only one record; requests before and after it completed successfully. No related record was found in monitoring, and the incident was closed after normal operation was confirmed.
Important Findings: ['The print status error was caused by failure to establish a connection to the Canon server when the print button was clicked.', 'The issue occurred for only one FDP production record.', 'Requests before and after the affected record were processed successfully.', 'No related record was found in monitoring at the time of review.', 'Printing was confirmed to be working normally before closure.']
Root Cause: The connection to the Canon server could not be established when the print button was clicked.
Resolution: No corrective action was documented; the issue was isolated to one record, normal processing was confirmed, and the incident was closed.
Technical Entities: ['Canon server', 'FDP production records', 'monitoring', 'print button', 'print status error']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5317
Investigation Summary: An Assessment Request for an Unstock Vehicle could not be updated to "Completed" because it became read-only after reaching "Vehicle for Quotation". The request was created by user D8HIHARA with the Branch-Sales-Staff role, for which existing functionality permits editing only specific statuses. Recovery was completed on February 3 by updating the Assessment Request to "Cancelled", and a logic change was planned for UAT to keep "Vehicle for Quotation" editable.
Important Findings: ['The Assessment Request was created by user ID D8HIHARA with the Branch-Sales-Staff role.', 'The "Quotation Vehicle Allocation" flag was set to "Y", causing the request to be treated as an Unstock Vehicle case.', 'For Assessment Requests created by Branch-Sales-Staff, statuses outside the configured editable-status list are read-only.', 'When the request status became "Vehicle for Quotation", UV staff could not update it to "Completed" because the status was read-only.', 'A review of the FDP production environment found no other similar incidents.']
Root Cause: Existing editability logic made Assessment Requests created by Branch-Sales-Staff read-only when their status was set to "Vehicle for Quotation", preventing UV staff from changing the status to "Completed".
Resolution: On February 3, the affected Assessment Request status was updated to "Cancelled". A follow-up change was planned in the UAT environment to keep "Vehicle for Quotation" editable even when the request was created by Branch-Sales-Staff.
Technical Entities: ['Assessment Request', 'Unstock Vehicle', 'D8HIHARA', 'Branch-Sales-Staff', 'Submitted to UV', 'Quotation Vehicle Allocation', 'Y', 'Vehicle for Quotation', 'Completed', 'Cancelled', 'UV', 'JAAI Assessment In Progress', 'Assessment In Progress', 'Rejected', 'In progress', 'Assessment Completed', 'FDP production environment', 'UAT environment']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5317
Timestamp: 2026-02-10T02:33:00
Comment: |mailto:hideaki.shiromoto@daimlertruck.com] San,
 Thank you very much for your continued support.
 Regarding the incident*, the investigation results are as follows.
|Incident number|MFTBCFFR-5317|
|Event Details|The status of the Assessment Request cannot be updated to "Completed" or "Cancelled." |
|RCA|This case is a request for appraisal regarding an Unstock Vehicle.
 
The appraisal request was created by user ID D8HIHARA (role: Branch-Sales-Staff).
After approval, the status of the appraisal request is updated to "Submitted to UV".
 
Then, when UV staff processes the assessment request,
By setting the "Quotation Vehicle Allocation" flag to "Y",
This appraisal request has been determined as an Unstock Vehicle case.
 
With existing functionality, if an appraisal request is created by Branch-Sales-Staff,
Only the following statuses can be edited.
 
Submitted to UV
 
JAAI Assessment In Progress
 
Assessment In Progress
 
Rejected
 
In progress
 
Assessment Completed
 
If a status other than the above is set, the appraisal request will be read-only.
 
In this case, the status of the appraisal request was set to “Vehicle for Quotation”, so
The status was set to Read-Only, and UV staff were unable to update it to "Completed." |
|Recovery status|Based on your instructions, we implemented recovery measures on February 3rd.
The status of the appraisal request has been updated to "Cancelled". |
|Correction Plan|As a result of checking the entire FDP production environment, no other incidents similar to this issue have occurred.
We have confirmed that the phenomenon itself is operating as the existing function.
 
However, in light of this issue, we plan to implement the following modifications.
 
Even if the appraisal request is created by Branch-Sales-Staff,
When the status is set to “Vehicle for Quotation”,
Change the logic to still set the status to Editable.
 
Once we receive approval for this response policy, we will proceed with modifications to the UAT environment. |
|Scheduled date of implementation of UAT|February 10, 2026|
 
Please contact us if you have any questions.
 Thank you for your understanding.
 Himanshu Tandon

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5306
Investigation Summary: UV Sales Quote profit calculation mismatched for production record AR#: H000522508, Quote#: 2-AJ8LJK, an Unstock Vehicle case. A blank Vehicle ID on the Model Code line item caused it to be classified as a Non-Vehicle Line Item and its price to be deducted twice. The affected record was recovered, and the Non-Vehicle Line Item search specification was corrected, validated in UAT1, and released to Production on February 19.
Important Findings: ['The affected record was an Unstock Vehicle, where the chassis number was not mapped to the assessment.', 'Vehicle and Non-Vehicle line item prices in UV Sales Quote are calculated separately based on the Vehicle ID in the Model Code line item.', 'For Unstock Vehicle cases, the Model Code line item has no chassis and its Vehicle ID remains blank.', 'The blank Vehicle ID caused the Model Code line item to be treated as a Non-Vehicle Line Item, resulting in its price being deducted twice during Sales Profit calculation.', "The corrected Non-Vehicle Line Item search condition identifies records with blank Vehicle ID only when Product Type is not 'Model Code'.", 'The fix was implemented in UAT1 using AR#: H000052299 and UV Quote#: 1-7WLRVD, then released to Production on February 19.']
Root Cause: For an Unstock Vehicle, the Model Code line item had a blank Vehicle ID because no chassis was present. The Non-Vehicle Line Item search logic therefore misclassified the Model Code line item as non-vehicle, causing the Model Code price to be deducted twice during UV Sales Quote profit calculation.
Resolution: Recovered the affected record and updated the Non-Vehicle Line Item search specification to exclude records with Product Type 'Model Code' when Vehicle ID is blank. The fix was validated in UAT1 and released to Production on February 19.
Technical Entities: ['MFTBCFFR-5306', 'UV Sales Quote', 'Profit Calculation Mismatch', 'Production', 'AR#: H000522508', 'Quote#: 2-AJ8LJK', 'Unstock Vehicle', 'Chassis#', 'assessment', 'Vehicle ID', 'Model Code line item', 'Vehicle Line Item', 'Non-Vehicle Line Item', 'Sales Profit calculation', 'Product Type', 'UAT1', 'AR#: H000052299', 'UV Quote#: 1-7WLRVD']

(English)
Thank you for your support.
We would like to share the analysis details for the incident MFTBCFFR-5306, related to Profit Calculation Mismatch in UV Sales Quote.
Please find the summary below:
|Incident Number |MFTBCFFR-5306|
|Description|UV Sales Quote Profit Mismatch|
|Root Cause (RCA)|This issue occurred because the affected Production Record (AR#: H000522508, Quote#: 2-AJ8LJK) is a case of Unstock Vehicle. In this scenario, the Chassis# is not mapped to the assessment.
During profit calculation in UV Sales Quote, Vehicle and Non-Vehicle line item prices are calculated separately based on the Vehicle ID, which is present only in the Model Code line item.
In the case of Vehicle Unstock, Chassis is not present in Model Code line item and thus its Vehicle Id remains blank. Due to this Model Code is considered as Non-Vehicle Line Item. Since the system fails to correctly identify the Model Code line item during Sales Profit calculation, this results in the Model Code price being deducted twice.|
|Recovery status|Recovery has been completed on January 30.|
|Fix Plan|To fix this issue, we have updated the search spec for Non-Vehicle Line Items. Now it will identify records which are having Blank Vehicle Id and the Product Type is not 'Model Code'.
This will ensure that in case of Unstock Vehicle, Model Code Line item is not considered as Non-Vehicle line item.|
|Planned UAT date|The fix has been implemented on UAT1 environment.
Reference record:
AR#: H000052299
UV Quote#: 1-7WLRVD|

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5305
Investigation Summary: A Total List Price mismatch occurred between SV Quote and UV Quote labor line items because the quotes used different pricing logic. SV Quote directly stored Adjusted List Price for specified Labor Billing Types, while UV Quote multiplied by Qty in all cases. The SV Quote logic was implemented in UV Quote, validated in UAT-1, and released to Production on February 19.
Important Findings: ['The mismatch affected Total List Price between SV Quote and UV Quote.', 'For Shaken, 3-month Inspection, 6-month Inspection, 12-month Inspection, 24-month Inspection, MPC Shaken, PDF Shaken, MPC + PDF Shaken, and Spare Tire – Toolbox, SV Quote stores Adjusted List Price directly.', 'UV Quote applied multiplication by Qty for all Labor Billing Types, including types requiring directly stored Adjusted List Price.', 'The updated UV Quote pricing behavior was validated in UAT-1 using UV Sales Quote# 1-7VR5H1 and SV Quote# 1-7VR5I9.', 'The fix was released to Production in the February 19 FDP release.']
Root Cause: UV Quote did not implement the SV Quote pricing logic for specified Labor Billing Types and instead multiplied the price by Qty in all cases.
Resolution: Implemented the SV Quote pricing logic in UV Quote so that Adjusted List Price is stored directly for the affected Labor Billing Types; validated in UAT-1 and released to Production on February 19.

In the SV Quote, for the following Labor Billing Types:
 - Shaken
 - 3-month Inspection
 - 6-month Inspection
 - 12-month Inspection
 - 24-month Inspection
 - MPC Shaken
 - PDF Shaken
 - MPC + PDF Shaken
 - Spare Tire – Toolbox
the Adjusted List Price is stored directly.
 However, in the UV Quote, this logic is not implemented, and the multiplication with Qty is applied in all cases.
As a recovery measure, we propose manually updating the price in the UV Quote. Please confirm whether this recovery approach is correct and meets your expectations.
To permanently resolve this issue, we plan to implement the same pricing logic used in the SV Quote into the UV Quote.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5297
Investigation Summary: Parts added through the “ASENT”/“Ascent” button in Parts Internal Order did not receive a Sales Order ID, causing the incident. The issue was replicated in UAT using Parts Internal Order M001301558, fixed and tested in UAT-1, and deployed to production in the 19/02/2026 regular release.
Important Findings: ['When parts or other line items were added using the “ASENT” button in Parts Internal Order, the Sales Order ID was not populated on the line items.', 'The issue was replicated in UAT with Parts Internal Order M001301558.', 'The same issue had been identified and fixed in SC under incident INC5623286, and the fix was planned for FDP.', 'UAT-1 testing used sales orders A001301627 and A001301641 with Parts Internal Orders M001301628 and M001301642; Registration and Delivery completed with no error during final approval for sales posting.', 'Testing of the Ascent function requires a parts-staff user; SSO login availability initially prevented user validation.']
Root Cause: The Sales Order ID was not populated on Parts Internal Order line items when parts or other line items were added through the “ASENT”/“Ascent” button.
Resolution: Implemented the fix to populate the Sales Order ID for line items added through Ascent, validated it in UAT-1, and applied it to the production environment in the 19/02/2026 regular release.
Technical Entities: ['Parts Internal Order', 'Sales Order ID', '“ASENT” button', 'Ascent', 'UAT', 'UAT-1', 'SC', 'FDP', 'INC5623286', 'M001301558', 'A001301627', 'M001301628', 'A001301641', 'M001301642', 'A001301651', 'parts-staff', 'D0X20906', 'SSO login', 'Registration and Delivery', 'final approval', 'sales posting', 'production environment']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5288
Investigation Summary: Adding AR or AP from the Finance Info tab of Accounts failed when the account had a value in DUNS No. Non-null DUNS No values existed only for Chugoku accounts migrated from SC, where TSR functionality from CR-0574 had existed but was removed in FDP. DUNS No was removed from account 0000U08057 to allow AR creation, and the incident was closed with a wait-and-see approach because the case was considered rare.
Important Findings: ['The error occurred when adding AR or AP from the Finance Info tab of Accounts with a non-null DUNS No field.', 'Accounts with non-null DUNS No values existed only in the Chugoku region and were migrated from SC.', 'TSR functionality implemented in SC under CR-0574 had been removed in FDP and was identified as causing the issue.', 'Removing DUNS No from account 0000U08057 allowed the user to proceed with AR creation.', 'Removal of TSR logic was proposed, but no permanent correction was implemented; the case was classified as rare and closed.']
Root Cause: TSR logic related to DUNS No remained applicable to Chugoku accounts migrated from SC, despite the TSR functionality from CR-0574 having been removed in FDP.
Resolution: Removed DUNS No from account 0000U08057 to enable AR creation. No permanent TSR-logic change was made; the issue was closed for observation.
Technical Entities: ['Finance Info', 'Accounts', 'AR', 'AP', 'DUNS No', 'Chugoku', 'SC', 'TSR functionality', 'CR-0574', 'FDP', '0000U08057']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5283
Investigation Summary: Quote revisions failed when the copied 'Promissory Note Due Date' was earlier than the quote revision/creation date and triggered validation. The underlying cause was an incorrect backend date-field format that made date values non-comparable. The date format was corrected, successfully tested in UAT-1 on Quote '1-2MZIQ2', and deployed to PROD in the 5-Feb-2026 regular release.
Important Findings: ["Validation requires 'Promissory Note Due Date' to be greater than or equal to the quote creating date.", 'During quote revision, historical promissory-note dates caused validation errors for quotes including 1-6YMFWCN, 1-6Z3N4YR, and 1-6Z3N60P.', 'Temporary recovery changed affected promissory-note due dates to the current date so users could complete quote revisions, then restored the original dates.', "Existing quote-revision behavior creates the revised quote with a blank 'Promissory Note Due Date' when the original date is earlier than the quote revising date; the user can then enter a new date manually.", "Quote copy does not copy the 'Promissory Note Due Date'; it is entered manually and must satisfy the quote-creation-date validation.", 'The proposed change to disable validation during quote revision was not required after identifying the backend date format defect.']
Root Cause: The backend date field format was incorrect, making 'Promissory Note Due Date' values non-comparable and causing validation errors during quote revision.
Resolution: Corrected the backend date field format, validated the fix in UAT-1 using Quote '1-2MZIQ2', and deployed the fix to PROD in the 5-Feb-2026 regular release.
Technical Entities: ['Promissory Note Due Date', 'quote revision', 'quote creating date', 'quote revising date', 'Quote copy', 'UAT-1', 'PROD', '1-6YMFWCN', '1-6Z3N4YR', '1-6Z3N60P', '1-2MZIQ2']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5279
Investigation Summary: An error occurred while creating an Assessment Request when multiple Assessment Requests existed for the same Chassis#. The issue was replicated in UAT-1 and traced to an incorrect code-level Search Specification that queried Purchase Quote using the wrong Assessment Request number. The corrected Search Specification was deployed to UAT-1, verified by successful creation of a new Assessment Request, and released to Production on February 5, 2026.
Important Findings: ['The issue was reproduced in UAT-1 for Chassis# Test-60VX using Assessment Requests H000052187, H000052188, and H000052190.', 'Purchase Quote associated with Assessment Request H000052187 was incorrectly selected when processing another Assessment Request.', 'The affected Production records had the same root cause as the UAT-1 reproduction.', 'Recovery for the affected records was completed before the permanent code fix.', 'After the UAT-1 fix, users could create a new Assessment Request for the same Chassis#.']
Root Cause: An incorrect code-level Search Specification queried Purchase Quote using the wrong Assessment Request number, causing the Purchase Quote for Assessment Request H000052187 to be selected incorrectly.
Resolution: The Search Specification was corrected to query Purchase Quote using the correct Assessment Request number. The fix was deployed to UAT-1 on January 27, 2026 and released to Production in the February 5 FDP regular release.
Technical Entities: ['Assessment Request', 'Purchase Quote', 'Search Specification', 'UAT-1', 'Production environment', 'FDP', 'Chassis#', 'Test-60VX', 'H000052187', 'H000052188', 'H000052190']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5275
Investigation Summary: The VECT button transition was affected because the PR object in the manifest management screen was inactive. The inactive configuration originated during CR-4982 testing in the development environment and was migrated to RT2 and production. The configuration was corrected in all production and UAT environments, restoring VECT integration.
Important Findings: ['During CR-4982 testing, the PR object in the manifest management screen was changed to inactive in the development environment.', 'The inactive PR configuration was migrated from the development environment to RT2 and production.', 'An inactive PR file affected the transition triggered by pressing the "VECT" button.', 'The configuration was fixed in all production and UAT environments.', 'Preventive actions include migration checks for unnecessary production configuration changes and adding VECT verification to the daily morning sanity check.']
Root Cause: The PR object in the manifest management screen was set to inactive during CR-4982 testing and that configuration was migrated to RT2 and production, causing the PR file to be inactive and affecting VECT button transitions.
Resolution: Corrected the PR object configuration in all production and UAT environments.
Technical Entities: ['VECT', 'CR-4982', 'PR object', 'manifest management screen', 'development environment', 'RT2', 'production', 'UAT', 'PR file', 'VECT button', 'daily morning sanity check']

Timestamp: 2026-01-27T03:37:00
Comment: |mailto:yuji.yoshihara@daimlertruck.com] San,
Thank you very much for your continued support.
As a result of investigating this issue, we confirmed that when testing CR-4982, the PR object in the manifest management screen was changed to inactive in the development environment.
The configuration was then migrated to RT2 and production.
This event occurred because the PR file became inactive, affecting the transition when pressing the "VECT" button.
The configuration has now been fixed and the issue is resolved in all production and UAT environments. As a preventative measure, we will conduct additional checks during migration to ensure that no unnecessary configuration changes have been reflected in the production environment.
In addition, we will add confirmation of the "VECT" function to the daily morning sanity check items to create a system that can detect and prevent similar events at an early stage.
We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience caused. We will strive to prevent similar incidents from occurring again in the future. 
Thank you for your support.

Important Findings: ['The branch sales manager name in BIP is derived from the corresponding department configuration.', 'The reported issue was attributed to omitted settings during personnel changes.', 'Department 7020 was updated and the corrected value was reflected in BIP.', 'All director names for base 70 departments were updated.', 'The corrected data was confirmed in Prod and reflected in the BIP report.']
Root Cause: Department configuration values for branch sales manager/director names were not updated during personnel changes.
Resolution: Updated the name values in all base 70 department configurations, including Department 7020, in Prod; the corrected values were reflected in BIP reports.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5252
Investigation Summary: BIP delivery-slip reports inserted blank pages for shipments with more than 90 line items and reports exceeding 15 pages. Investigation found that BIP configuration and alignment did not handle the higher line-item volume correctly. The BIP changes were updated for the new delivery-slip format, validated on UAT-1 for shipment O000181209, and confirmed to work for up to 96 line items; production release was approved for the FDP release scheduled for 2026-07-23.
Important Findings: ['Reports with 88 and 90 records generated correctly, while shipment O000181209 with 93 records generated blank pages.', 'The blank-page issue occurred when shipments had more than 90 line items and the BIP report exceeded 15 pages.', 'BIP configuration and alignment were not aligned for reports containing more than 90 items.', 'The initial UAT-1 changes had to be applied to the new delivery-slip format implemented under CR-0869.', 'The PDF-generation error in the new format was resolved, and the bottom-page feed names Delivered and Quantity Delivered were corrected to display on one line.', 'The BIP report was confirmed to work correctly for up to 96 line items.']
Root Cause: BIP configuration and alignment did not correctly support delivery-slip reports with more than 90 line items, causing blank pages in reports exceeding 15 pages.
Resolution: Updated the BIP changes for the new delivery-slip format, resolved the PDF-generation error and bottom-page feed-name wrapping, and validated the report on UAT-1 for up to 96 line items. Production release was approved and planned for the FDP release scheduled for 2026-07-23.

Root Cause: The Hinmoku field was not configured correctly in the backend master that maps file columns to Siebel columns.
Resolution: Corrected the Hinmoku field configuration in the backend master and verified the process on all production environments.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5228
Investigation Summary: Sales prices in PowerBI reports did not consistently match Siebel for JC records, including special labor and billing-type scenarios. Investigation identified mismatched sales-price logic in ODI, including Net Operation Time handling and report-specific logic differences. ODI logic was modified for reports 1-10A, 1-15A, and 1-12A, but final release validation for all affected reports was not confirmed in the comments.
Important Findings: ['The issue affected sales-price discrepancies between Siebel and PowerBI across reports, not only SV 1-12 Report.', 'Special scenarios included labor code .004330 and Billing Type "Spare tire toolbox".', 'PBI-UAT initially included Net Operation Time in the Special Sales Price calculation, although this was reported as incorrect for the tested Billing Type.', 'Testing in UAT1 (FDP Okoyama) found mismatches for JC I001301489: Siebel 43,200 versus differing values in reports 1-01, 1-10A, 1-12A, 1-15A, and no update in 1-02.', 'ODI code was modified to correct Sales price values in PowerBI Report 1-10A and to align sales-price logic in reports 1-10A, 1-15A, and 1-12A.']
Root Cause: ODI sales-price calculation logic in PowerBI did not match Siebel logic for special labor and Billing Type scenarios, including incorrect Net Operation Time handling and inconsistent report logic.

Timestamp: 2026-01-07T09:32:00
Author: Saad
Comment: Thank you for your support and cooperation.
We would like to respond to your queries.
We are concerned with three columns in the sample data provided.
Column D, H & F
*What each column corresponds to?*
*Column D* -> It corresponds to the *Affiliated Company Code,* this is set in accordance to the organization of the selected *position* for the employee. In summary, this the Branch Code.
This is read only setting
41 - Matsuyama Service Centre
43 - Uwajima Service Centre
*Column H* -> It corresponds to the *Affiliated Department Code*, this is the department code within the branch. This is also set in accordance to the position selected for the employee.
This is read only setting
4133 - Matsuyama Service Centre Sales Department
4333 - Uwajima Service Centre Sales Department
*Column F* -> It corresponds to the *Affiliated Location Code,* this can be changed by the user. It corresponds to the employee's location. i.e The employee at present is affiliated to which branch's location.
So in our case,
We believe
The position for employee code *5109*, was set to *43 - Uwajima Service Centre,* but the *Affiliated location code* was still set as *41*
Everything is working fine as per the settings, the *affiliated located code* for the employee is at user's discretion to set.
Please let us know in case of any additional information required.
Best Regards,
Saad

Comment: Thank you for you support and cooperation.
We have performed our analysis on the issue and would like to provide you with the root cause along with answering the questions given.
*1) Why this vehicle data was registered ?*
These vehicles are created from the *TCB01* files. By default, the *Name of Personnel in charge of service* is set to be *Administrator*. For this name the *Code of personnel in charge of service* is blank in the master data. Since, this is a default setting, this should not be characterized into an issue.
*2) Solutions to prevent this issue*
Since, this is a agreed upon default setting. We believe the solution to prevent this issue is to change the default value as per the business requirement.
*3) How to recover existing data ?*
If business decides to change the default value. Data patching could be performed to recover the data with the newly decided default value.
Please do let us know in case of any additional query
Best Regards
Saad

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5210
Timestamp: 2026-01-06T12:42:00
Comment: Thank you very much for your continued support.
 
We have investigated this issue and would like to inform you of the cause and answers to your questions as follows.
 
1) Regarding the reason why the vehicle data was registered
The vehicle in question was created through the TCB01 file.
As a default specification of the system, the "Service Person Name" is set as Administrator by default.
Please note that the "Service Personnel Code" associated with this person's name is blank in the master data, but this is based on the default settings and does not correspond to a system malfunction.
 
2) Regarding countermeasures to prevent this event
Since this incident was based on pre-agreed default specifications, we believe that an effective measure to prevent recurrence is to change the default values themselves in accordance with business requirements.
 
3) How to restore existing data
If the business side decides to change the default values, existing data can be corrected by implementing data patching based on the newly determined default values.
 
If you have any questions or additional questions, please feel free to let us know.
 
Thank you for your support.

With regards to the vehicles created or updated via the TCB01 files 
have the maintenance person in charge set as 'Siebel Administrator'.
 
With regards to the vehicles created via the DJ2A sent from TOB in response to the request sent upon creating the Chassis Order by the user.
The user that creates the chassis order is set as the maintenance person in charge. This operation takes place, whenever the DJ2A file sent by TOB is processed in response to the chassis order. 
 
*(2) Is there a difference between the SC version and the FDP version regarding (1)?*
No, there is no difference in SC and FDP version with regards to the above operations as of now.

With regards to the vehicles created via DJ2A files, we will need to update the current functionality in accordance to the business requirements. 
These changes can only be performed under an AMS CR.
 
*(2) Perform the recovery of existing data after completing the program changes in (1).*

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5208

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5202
Investigation Summary: The incident was caused by the JPN screen cache not being cleared after master data upload because the JPN screen was unavailable for maintenance during the holiday period. The ENU screen cache had been cleared. The incident was confirmed not to be a Siebel issue and was dismissed after preventive operational steps were defined.
Important Findings: ['The ENU screen cache was cleared during the holiday period.', 'The JPN screen was down for maintenance, preventing its cache from being cleared.', 'The issue was reported before the JPN screen cache was cleared the following morning.', 'Cache clearing for the JPN screen will be prioritized in post-master-data-upload verification and morning sanity checks.', 'The incident was confirmed not to be a Siebel issue.']
Root Cause: The JPN screen cache was not cleared because the screen was unavailable for maintenance during the holiday period.
Resolution: Add JPN screen cache clearing as a priority post-master-data-upload verification item, perform it during morning sanity checks, and confirm execution with relevant teams.
Technical Entities: ['ENU screen', 'JPN screen', 'Siebel', 'master data upload', 'morning sanity check']

comments.comment:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5202
Timestamp: 2026-01-05T05:06:00
Comment: Thank you very much for your continued support.
We apologize for any inconvenience caused regarding this matter.
During the holiday period, the cache on the ENU screen was cleared, but the JPN screen was down for maintenance, so the cache could not be cleared.
 This event was then reported before the cache was cleared this morning.
In the future, we will work to prevent recurrence by adding this response as a priority item to the confirmation process after master data is uploaded, and by clearing the cache on the JPN screen during the morning sanity check.
 Additionally, we will thoroughly check with the relevant teams to ensure that this response is implemented from next time onwards.
 
Please note that this incident is not a Siebel issue, so we would like to dismiss this incident.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5180
Investigation Summary: A Tax amount finalization error was replicated in UAT-1 using UV Sales Quote 1-6XPN5P revision 5 and UV Sales Order E001300882. The issue occurred after a user manually changed an Expense Item to Type 'Tax'; the affected YN6M line item was not updated to Invoiced when the invoice was created. The incident was classified as user misoperation, with no affected cases found in any FDP Production Environment; users should revise the UV Sales Quote and restore the correct expense line items.
Important Findings: ['The issue was replicated in UAT-1 with UV Sales Quote 1-6XPN5P revision 5 and UV Sales Order E001300882.', "Creating an invoice automatically updates standard line items with Type 'Tax' to status Invoiced.", "The manually changed line item with Part Number YN6M and Type 'Tax' was not updated to Invoiced.", "Tax Finalization requires all line items with Type 'Tax', including manually updated lines, to be Invoiced.", "No cases of manually changing an Expense Line item to 'Tax' were found in any FDP Production Environment."]
Root Cause: User manually changed an Expense Item to Type 'Tax', causing the YN6M line item to remain outside the expected invoicing-status update and not be set to Invoiced before Tax Finalization.
Resolution: No system fix or recovery was required. The user should revise the UV Sales Quote and update the correct expense line items.
Technical Entities: ['UAT-1', 'UV Sales Quote', '1-6XPN5P', 'UV Sales Order', 'E001300882', 'Invoice', 'Registration Request', 'Finalize Tax Amount', 'YN6M', 'FDP Production Environment', 'Tax', 'Expenses', 'Expense Item', 'Invoiced']

Comment: Thank you for your continued support.
We would like to share the analysis details for the Incident MFTBCFFR-5180, related to Tax amount finalization error.
Please find the summary below:
|Incident Number |MFTBCFFR-5180|
|Description|Tax amount finalization error|
|User Steps|Step 1: In the related UV Sales Quote, user has manually changed the items of Tax and Expenses and updated one Expense Item to 'Tax'.
Step 2: User created a Sales Order.
Step 3: User created an Invoice and completed it.
Step 4: User created a Registration Request and clicked on 'Finalize Tax Amount' button.|
|Root Cause (RCA)|We have successfully replicated this issue in UAT-1 environment (Reference Record: UV Sales Quote : 1-6XPN5P revision 5, UV Sales Order : E001300882).
When an invoice is created, the status of line items with Type as 'Tax' is automatically updated to Invoiced. However, a manually updated line item with Part Number 'YN6M' and Type as 'Tax' did not have its status changed to Invoiced.
During Tax Finalization, the status of all line items having Type as 'Tax', including manually updated ones (such as part number YN6M), must be set to Invoiced.|
|Recovery status|Please note that we have checked and found that no such case of manually updating the Expense Line item to 'Tax' has been observed in any FDP Production Environment.
As this is a case of user misoperation, so no recovery is required.
Kindly ask the user to revise the UV Sales Quote, and update the correct expense line items. |
|Fix Plan|NA|
As this is a case of user mis-operation, we would like to proceed with closing this Jira ticket.
If you require further clarification or assistance, please feel free to reach out.
Best Regards
Sunaina Gill

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5176
Investigation Summary: The issue was reproduced for JC# I001300905 on FDP - UAT1: a Quote Item showed Line Discount % as 0% after manually entering List Unit Price for Dummy Lubricant (..999999), while the synced JCO Order Item showed 100%. Investigation identified differing Line Discount % calculation behavior between Quote Item and Order Item, associated with a null Lubrication Price. A JCO-side fix was implemented in UAT and deployed to PROD in the January 22 regular release.
Important Findings: ['The issue was replicated on FDP - UAT1 for JC# I001300905.', 'When List Unit Price was manually entered for Dummy Lubricant (..999999) while the Quote was In Progress, Quote Item Line Discount % was 0%.', 'After the Quote became Customer Approved and the JCO was created/synced, the Order Item Line Discount % became 100%.', 'Quote Item and Order Item used different Line Discount % calculation behavior.', 'The issue was associated with Lubrication Price being null.', 'The initially proposed approach to make List Unit Price read-only was rejected; the fix was changed on the JCO side.']
Root Cause: Different Line Discount % calculation behavior between Quote Item and Order Item when Lubrication Price was null caused the JCO Order Item Line Discount % to become 100% while the Quote Item remained 0%.
Resolution: A JCO-side fix was implemented and validated in UAT, then deployed to PROD in the January 22 regular release.
Technical Entities: ['JC# I001300905', 'FDP - UAT1', 'Okayama-PROD', 'Quote', 'Quote Item', 'Order Item', 'JCO', 'Line Discount %', 'List Unit Price', 'Dummy Lubricant (..999999)', 'Lubrication Price', 'In Progress', 'Customer Approved', 'UAT', 'PROD']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5174
Investigation Summary: Chassis Orders were created with a blank/missing model code because the relevant model code was not registered when the TOB/D21A processing occurred. The model code "MS06GPHZMAV-9" was created on 15-Dec-2025 after the chassis order had been created on 10-Dec-2025. Impacted records were recovered after model-code creation was restored across FDP environments; the investigation also identified that not all TOB master files are automatically updated.
Important Findings: ['The affected chassis order was created on 10-Dec-2025, while model code "MS06GPHZMAV-9" was created on 15-Dec-2025.', 'Model code "MS06GPQUCV-9" was missing from the Chugoku, Wakayama, and Okayama Model Master, preventing chassis-order creation in those environments.', 'Affected Chassis Orders were recovered by correcting master data and reprocessing the relevant records; recovery was reported complete for all impacted records.', 'Model codes with MC "9" were manually updated in Chugoku and Wakayama on 26-Dec-2025 after receipt of the required TCH01 file.', 'TCH01 is the TOB PC Master 2 - Model Master inbound batch interface to Siebel via SFTP and is scheduled as a daily package run in Siebel PROD; not all TOB master interfaces are scheduled for daily PROD processing.', 'The proposed preventive control is to prevent Chassis Order creation when a model code is absent, notify the AMS team by email, correct data, and reprocess the record.']
Root Cause: The required model code was not registered in the system when the TOB/D21A file was processed. Specifically, "MS06GPHZMAV-9" was created after the corresponding Chassis Order, and TOB master updates were not configured so that all master files were automatically updated.
Resolution: Model-code creation was restored and missing model codes were manually updated in the affected FDP environments. The impacted Chassis Orders were recovered and reprocessed after the required master data was available.

Comment: Dear Tsunoda San,
 
If the model code is not registered in the system at the time of D21A file processing, it is possible to implement the following measures.
 
If the model code does not exist, do not create a chassis order.
Automatically notify the AMS team of target record information via email.
The AMS team confirms the notification contents, makes necessary data corrections, and then reprocesses.
 
This feature prevents chassis orders from being created with unregistered model codes, and enables early detection and prompt response to problems.
 
If you have any questions or concerns, please feel free to contact us.
 
Thank you for your support.
 
(English)
 
In such scenario where Model Code is not present in the system at the time of D12A file execution. We can apply changes in the system such that in such cases the Chassis Order will not be created in the system and report of the affected record will be send to the AMS team over mail to track for the issue and do the necessary correction for the issue.
Please let us know in case of some further query.
 
 
Best Regards,

Comment: Dear Tsunoda-San,
We would like to report on the survey results.
Chassis order was created by TOB file on December 10, 2025. On the other hand, the model code "MS06GPHZMAV-9" in the TOB file was created on December 15, 2025, so the model code did not exist at that time, and this event occurred.
Subsequently, on December 26, 2025, we implemented restoration measures for model code creation in all FDP environments, and this issue has been resolved.
Also, regarding TOB master update, there is no mechanism in which all master files are automatically updated.
Regarding this point, a meeting regarding TOB batch processing is scheduled for July 24, 2025.
After the meeting, we will report again on the processing details of the TOB file.
Thank you for your support.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5145
Investigation Summary: The reported amount mismatch between the order form and sales estimate was initially observed as different discount mappings between Quotation BIP and Order Sheet BIP. The final investigation determined that the Quote price was changed after Quote approval and Sales Order creation without re-approval, so the updated price was not reflected in the Sales Order. This was classified as a user mis-operation rather than a product defect.
Important Findings: ['Quotation BIP showed a Discount amount of -819798 from MF Vehicle Discount Amount, while Order Sheet BIP showed -60000 from MF UV Discount.', 'The Quote price was changed after the Quote had been approved and the Sales Order had been created.', 'A price change made after Quote approval without re-approval is not reflected in the Sales Order.', 'The incident was determined not to be a bug and was proposed for rejection.']
Root Cause: The user changed the Quote price after Quote approval and Sales Order creation without re-approving the Quote, so the updated price was not reflected in the Sales Order.
Resolution: Users should avoid changing the Price after Quote Approval; the incident was rejected as a user mis-operation rather than a bug.
Technical Entities: ['UV FDP Shikoku', 'Quotation BIP', 'Order Sheet BIP', 'Discount', 'MF Vehicle Discount Amount', 'MF UV Discount', 'Quote', 'Sales Order', 'SO']

Root Cause: Tax rate configuration in PO Invoice BIP in Service Purchase Order did not handle tax-exempt line items.
Resolution: Updated the PO Invoice BIP logic to handle tax-exempt line items and return a 0% tax rate in SV_Invoice when the Tax Exempt flag is Y; released in the regular FDP release on 9 January.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5121
Investigation Summary: Individual Invoice Branch Code validation compared the entered Branch Code with the JCO creator's Primary Location Code, preventing invoicing when the codes differed. For I000111578 (D8YOOSEK), the relevant Primary Location Code was "70"; for I000111572 (D8MICSAS), it was "00". CR MFTBCFFR-4379 removed the Branch Code filter, allowing Individual Invoice issuance from Branch Code "00"; Bulk Invoice was unaffected because it selects Branch from the JC Header.
Important Findings: ["The entered Branch Code was validated against the JCO creator's Primary Location Code, which can be checked in the employee Location Code.", 'I000111578 (D8YOOSEK) had Primary Location Code "70", while I000111572 (D8MICSAS) had Primary Location Code "00".', 'Before the MFTBCFFR-4379 release, I000111578 could be invoiced using Branch Code "70".', 'MFTBCFFR-4379 removed the Branch Code validation/filter for Individual Invoice, allowing invoice issuance from Branch Code "00".', 'Bulk Invoice was not affected because Branch is selected from the JC Header.']
Root Cause: Individual Invoice Branch Code validation/filter required the entered Branch Code to match the JCO creator's Primary Location Code, causing failures when the codes differed.
Resolution: Deployed CR MFTBCFFR-4379, which removed the Branch Code validation/filter for Individual Invoice.
Technical Entities: ['Individual Invoice', 'Bulk Invoice', 'Branch Code', 'Primary Location Code', 'Primary Department Code', 'Employee Location Code', 'JCO creator', 'I000111578', 'D8YOOSEK', 'I000111572', 'D8MICSAS', 'MFTBCFFR-4379', 'JC Header', 'API', 'JSON']
