investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5113
Investigation Summary: Department Code values CSJS200 and CSJS300 in PO - Trailer & Forklift JV were sourced from the Purchase Order creator instead of the intended Sales Order Location Code. The mapping was corrected and validated in UAT1. The change was released to FDP prod in the 17 December planned release; no recovery Journal Vouchers were created.
Important Findings: ["Department Code in PO - Trailer & Forklift JV was mapped from the Purchase Order's Creator.", "The required mapping source was Sales Order's Location Code.", "UAT1 validation included Sales Order Location Code 10 and Last Approver's Location Code 50.", 'Recovery through reverse and corrected Journal Vouchers was not required.', 'The mapping correction was released to FDP prod on 17 December 2025.']
Root Cause: Department Code mapping for PO - Trailer & Forklift JV incorrectly sourced the value from the Purchase Order's Creator rather than the Sales Order's Location Code.
Resolution: Changed the Department Code mapping to use Sales Order's Location Code, validated the change in UAT1, and released it to FDP prod on 17 December 2025. No recovery was performed.
Technical Entities: ['Department Code', 'CSJS200', 'CSJS300', 'PO - Trailer & Forklift JV', 'Purchase Order', "Purchase Order's Creator", 'Sales Order', "Sales Order's Location Code", 'Journal Voucher', 'UAT1', 'FDP prod', 'FDP release']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5088
Investigation Summary: The Expense Invoice BIP report displayed the value from "Integrated Address(J)" instead of "Address(J) character-chome(Vender)". The issue affected all FDP Production environments and resulted from a required BIP report update not being completed after the code changes associated with MFTBCFFR-4625. The report mapping was corrected, validated in UAT, and released in the 17th Dec FDP release.
Important Findings: ['Expense Invoice BIP report used "Integrated Address(J)" rather than "Address(J) character-chome(Vender)" for the address value.', 'For Invoice 1-130032159 and Account 0C00240272, the report was corrected to display "1-4-11 Minami-Shinozakicho, Edogawa-ku, Tokyo".', 'The issue was not specific to Chugoku; it existed in all FDP Production environments.', 'A necessary BIP report update was missed after code changes related to MFTBCFFR-4625.', 'The corrected address display was validated in UAT before production approval.']
Root Cause: A required BIP report update was not completed after the code changes associated with MFTBCFFR-4625, causing Expense Invoice BIP to map the address to "Integrated Address(J)" instead of "Address(J) character-chome(Vender)".
Resolution: Updated the Expense Invoice BIP report to display the correct "Address(J) character-chome(Vender)" value, validated the change in UAT, and deployed it in the 17th Dec FDP release.
Technical Entities: ['Expense Invoice BIP report', 'Integrated Address(J)', 'Address(J) character-chome(Vender)', 'Invoice 1-130032159', 'Account 0C00240272', 'FDP Production environments', 'MFTBCFFR-4625', '17th Dec FDP release']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5069
Investigation Summary: Delivery Approval failed for NV Sales Order records A000009087 and A000011464 in the Wakayama Production environment. The failure was traced to a Vehicle ID mismatch between the automatically created Purchase Order and its corresponding Sales Order. The affected records were recovered, but the underlying reason the Vehicle ID was not populated on the Sales Order could not be determined because required historical system information was no longer retained.
Important Findings: ['Both affected NV Sales Orders had product class "Trailer", which automatically creates a "Trailer & Forklift" Purchase Order after Sales Order approval.', 'When the Purchase Order status changed to "Ordered", a new Vehicle record was created and its Vehicle ID was populated on the Purchase Order but not on the corresponding Sales Order.', 'Delivery Approval validates Vehicle information between the Purchase Order and Sales Order; the Vehicle ID mismatch caused the validation error and blocked Delivery Approval.', 'The issue could not be reproduced in UAT or FDP UAT, and no similar recurrence was observed in production environments during subsequent monitoring.', 'The affected Purchase Orders were processed in March 2025 but the incident was reported in December 2025, after the required system-information retention period had expired.', 'System log retention is planned to be extended from one month to two months to support investigation of future occurrences reported within the retention period.']
Root Cause: The immediate cause of the Delivery Approval error was a Vehicle ID mismatch: the newly created Vehicle ID was populated on the Purchase Order but not on the corresponding Sales Order. The reason the Vehicle ID was not populated on the Sales Order could not be determined.
Resolution: Affected records were recovered. No defect was identified in the current implementation and no reproducible code fix was confirmed; continued monitoring and extension of system log retention from one month to two months were planned for future investigation and recurrence prevention.
Technical Entities: ['NV Sales Order', 'A000009087', 'A000011464', 'Wakayama Production environment', 'Trailer', 'Purchase Order', 'Trailer & Forklift', 'Ordered', 'Vehicle record', 'Vehicle ID', 'Delivery Approval', 'UAT', 'FDP UAT', 'UAT-1', 'POrder', 'SO', 'system logs']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5069
Timestamp: 2026-06-17T12:05:00
Comment: thank you always.
We would like to report the results of our investigation regarding the delivery approval error (MFTBCFFR-5069) for NV orders in the Wakayama production environment, which was reported on December 4, 2025.
|Incident number|MFTBCFFR-5069|
|Event|An error occurred when approving the delivery of the NV order, and an event occurred that made it impossible to complete the process. |
|RCA|We have confirmed that the product class of the applicable NV orders (A000009087, A000011464) is "Trailer". In this case, once the order is approved, the system will automatically create a purchase order of type "Trailer & Forklift".
If you then change the status of the purchase order to "Ordered", a new vehicle record will be automatically created and that vehicle ID will be set on the purchase order and related orders.
In the target record, order approval and purchase order creation were completed successfully, and even when the purchase order was changed to "Ordered", the vehicle record was created successfully.
However, although the vehicle ID of the created vehicle was successfully set on the purchase order, it was not set on the corresponding sales order.
In the vehicle delivery approval process, a consistency check is performed between the vehicle information on the purchase order and the received order, but in this case, because the vehicle IDs did not match, a validation error occurred and the vehicle delivery could not be approved. |
|Recovery status|Completed|

|Description|A delivery approval error was displayed in NV Sales Order, thus preventing the user from completing the process.|
|Root Cause (RCA)|Please note that both affected NV Sales Order# A000009087 and A000011464, have product class as 'Trailer'. In this case, when the Sales Order is Approved, a purchase order having type as 'Trailer & Forklift' is automatically created.
Subsequently, when the status of this Purchase Order is updated to "Ordered", the system creates a new Vehicle record and populates its Vehicle ID in both the Purchase Order and the corresponding Sales Order.
For the affected records in Wakayama Production, the Sales Orders were approved successfully and the corresponding Purchase Orders were generated. When the Purchase Orders status was updated to "Ordered", new Vehicle records were created as expected.
However, the issue occurred because the Vehicle Id of this newly created Vehicle was populated correctly in the Purchase Order but was not populated in the corresponding Sales Order. During the Delivery Approval process, the system validates the Vehicle information between the Purchase Order and Sales Order. Due to the Vehicle ID mismatch, the validation failed and the Delivery Approval error message was displayed.|

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5063
Investigation Summary: JV Base Amount for Outsource Non IBOS was mapped from the Outsource order's Total Selling Price instead of the Purchase Order Total price. Body Building Order JVs also selected incorrect account codes when Vehicle Type was null. The mapping was changed and validated on UAT1, then released to Prod in the 17th Dec FDP release; recovery reverse and corrective JVs were requested for affected BB orders.
Important Findings: ['Outsource Non IBOS JV Base Amount was sourced from Total Selling Price in the Outsource order, which was 5000 for the investigated case.', 'The required mapping for both IBOS and Non-IBOS cases was Purchase Order Total price; when multiple POs exist in an Outsourcing order, a JV must be created for each PO.', 'For PO - Body Building Order - Non IBOS, a null Vehicle Type caused selection of account code 038, rather than the required Account Code CSJS201: 031 and Subsidiary Account Code CSJS202: 60.', 'Incorrect Account Item Code CSJS201 records were identified for recovery through reverse JVs and corrected JVs based on the Vehicle Class.', 'The Purchase Order Total price mapping was fixed and validated on UAT1 using SO# A001300621, then released in the 17th Dec FDP release.', 'Account Item Code CSJS201 & 301 issues were being addressed through CR MFTBCFFR-4627.']
Root Cause: JV mapping used the Outsource order Total Selling Price rather than Purchase Order Total price, and Body Building Order JV account-code selection defaulted to account code 038 when Vehicle Type was null.
Resolution: Changed the JV Base Amount mapping to Purchase Order Total price on UAT1, validated the change, and released it to Prod in the 17th Dec FDP release. Recovery required reverse and corrected JVs for affected BB orders with posting date 20251211.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5060
Investigation Summary: Parts Internal Return Orders for NV and UV Order Department did not have Vehicle Id, causing VIN# and Registration# to remain blank in Siebel and PBI. The initial analysis incorrectly assessed Parts Sales Return Orders; subsequent investigation confirmed the issue also existed in the SC version. The Parts Internal Return process was changed to populate Vehicle Id from the parent Internal Order, validated in FDP-UAT1, released to FDP-PROD on 17/12/2025, and historical records were data-patched.
Important Findings: ['The initial analysis of Parts Sales Return Orders was not applicable because the reported issue concerned Parts Internal Return Orders.', 'For NV and UV Order Department, Parts Internal Return Orders did not contain Vehicle Id; the same behavior existed in the SC version.', 'Missing Vehicle Id resulted in blank VIN# and Registration# on both Siebel and PBI.', 'The corrected process populates Vehicle Id on the Parts Internal Return Order from its parent Internal Order.', 'The fix was validated in FDP-UAT1 using NV record M001300645 and UV record M001300655, with VIN# and Registration# populated in Siebel and PBI.', 'Data patching was completed for affected FDP-PROD records through 17/12/2025.']
Root Cause: The Parts Internal Return process did not populate Vehicle Id from the parent Internal Order for NV and UV Order Department, leaving VIN# and Registration# blank.
Resolution: Updated the Parts Internal Return process to populate Vehicle Id from the parent Internal Order, released the fix in the 17/12/2025 FDP release, and data-patched affected FDP-PROD records.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5060
Timestamp: 2025-12-05T07:41:00
Author: Abhinav
Comment: Thank you for your continued support.
We have completed our analysis of the reported issue and would like to share our findings. 
RCA (Root Cause Analysis):
During our of Parts Sales Return Orders where the VIN# and Registration# fields were blank, we observed that the corresponding parent Parts Sales Orders and the originating Parts Quotes also contained blank values for these fields. Since the VIN# and Registration# details were not entered at the initial Parts Quote stage, the same was carried forward to the Parts Sales Order and subsequently to the Parts Sales Return Order.
For validation, we created two sample records  on FDP UAT1 for Parts Sales Return Orders:
M001300484 – with VIN# and Registration# populated
M001300482 – with no VIN# and Registration# 
The PBI report(PT5-10) correctly reflected the VIN of M001300484 as VIN values added in Parts quote.
 
Based on our analysis, this behavior is not an issue on the Siebel side or the PBI side. The root cause is that the VIN# and Registration# fields were not entered by the user at the time of creating the initial Parts Quote.
Since it is not a system issue, kindly allow us to reject this incident.  
Please let us know if you require any further information.
Best Regards,
Abhinav

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5052
Investigation Summary: When changing the Sales Rep on a Sales Order, the Entity Transfer functionality did not initially display D8OKATAR because the Employee Applet search logic required the same Primary Position Type as the current Sales Rep. Removing the Sales Rep Primary position Id condition allowed users from other locations to appear. The search logic was corrected to display only users whose branch matches the Sales Order's Branch 2 Digit Code, and the fix was released in the 17th Dec FDP release.
Important Findings: ['The original Entity Transfer condition required users to be in the same organization and have the same Primary Position Type as the primary Sales Rep.', 'D8OKATAR was excluded because its Primary Position Type was Branch-Sales-Staff, while D8TAKOUN and D8THORIK had Branch-Sales-Manager.', 'The Primary Position Type condition had been added under MFTBCFFR-4341, but the requested behavior was branch-based selection without a job/position-type restriction.', "Removing the Sales Rep Primary position Id condition made positions in the Sales Rep's department visible, but also displayed users from other locations.", "The Employee Applet search logic was revised so Entity Transfer displays users with the same branch as the Sales Order's Branch 2 Digit Code."]
Root Cause: The Employee Applet/Entity Transfer search logic used a Sales Rep Primary Position Type condition rather than limiting eligible users solely by the Sales Order branch; after that condition was removed, the logic was still insufficiently constrained and displayed users from other locations.
Resolution: Corrected the Employee Applet search logic to show only users whose branch matches the Sales Order's Branch 2 Digit Code. The change was released in the 17th Dec FDP release.
Technical Entities: ['MFTBCFFR-5052', 'MFTBCFFR-4341', 'Entity Transfer functionality', 'Transfer Applet', 'Employee Applet', 'Sales Order', 'Sales Rep', 'Sales Rep Primary position Id condition', 'Primary Position Type', 'Branch-Sales-Manager', 'Branch-Sales-Staff', 'Branch 2 Digit Code', 'D8TAKOUN', 'D8THORIK', 'D8OKATAR', 'UAT1', 'A001300568', 'PROD', 'FDP release', 'Affiliated Company Code', 'Affiliated Department Code']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5024
Timestamp: 2025-11-27T16:41:00
Author: Soham
Comment: Thanks for your support.
*RCA*:
*(1) Reason for Payment Terms were included in UAT4–8 but not reflected in PROD:*
 The Payment Condition values displayed in the BIP are based on the PO Sheet master. During the initial setup for Wave-3, the master data for these Payment Conditions was not provided by biz.
 When the incident *MFTBCFFR-4978* was raised, the missing values were added across all UAT environments, and the master data was uploaded based on the values that were already present in *OKAYAMA-PROD*. However, since the required master data was not available during the initial PROD deployment, the Payment Terms were not reflected in the Wave-3 PROD environments.
*(2) Reason for differences across FDP environments (Wave-3 & Chugoku):*
 In the Shikoku and Wakayama PROD environments, hardcoded Payment Condition values already exist in the BIP configuration. Therefore, Payment Terms appear only in these specific FDP environments.
 In contrast, other FDPs i.e. *Iwate, Okinawa, and Chugoku,* do not have such hardcoded values, which results in the observed differences in Payment Term display across Wave-3 PROD environments.
*Fix and release plan:*
As discussed in the meeting, after the issue was fixed on UAT and since all the UAT environments are in sync now, we are planning to release the UAT changes to PROD on *29th November after business hours*.
Kindly review and approve the PROD release for the respective FDPs so that we can proceed with the changes to PROD on *29th November*.
Please let us know in case of any queries.
Best Regards,
Soham

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5019
Investigation Summary: Users could not print the "Specification 2" BIP report because a part line item had a null price. The price for Part MK645741 became null after its quantity was edited directly in the Sales Order, rather than through the Quote. The quantity field for parts line items was made read-only in UAT-1 and released to FDP Production on 26 November.
Important Findings: ['The "Specification 2" BIP report fails when a part line item price is null.', 'Part MK645741 had a null price.', 'Editing quantity directly in the Sales Order caused the part price to be set to null.', 'Quantity changes must be performed through the Quote, not the Sales Order.', 'Epic MFTBCFFR-3485 had made only body tab line-item quantity read-only; this incident required the same restriction for parts line items.', 'The parts line-item quantity field was made read-only in UAT-1 and deployed to FDP Production.']
Root Cause: A user edited the quantity of Part MK645741 directly in the Sales Order, causing its price to become null; BIP reports cannot process part line items with a null price.
Resolution: Made the quantity field read-only for parts line items in the Sales Order, validated the change in UAT-1, and released it to FDP Production in the 26 November planned FDP release.
Technical Entities: ['"Specification 2" BIP report', 'BIP', 'Part MK645741', 'Sales Order', 'Quote', 'SC version', 'INC4031968', 'Epic MFTBCFFR-3485', 'body tab line items', 'parts line items', 'UAT-1', 'FDP Production']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5019
Timestamp: 2025-11-26T01:23:00
Author: Divyesh Ghiya
Comment: Dear Tsunoda-san,
Thank you for your continued support.
We have thoroughly investigated this issue, and our findings are as follows:
*Issue:*
 The user was unable to print the "Specification 2" BIP report.
*Root Cause:*
 The price for Part MK645741 was found to be null, which caused the BIP report to fail, as the price field cannot be null for part line items.
 Additionally, we identified that users are able to edit the quantity directly in the Sales Order, which is not aligned with the correct business process. Quantity changes must be performed through the Quote. Since the user modified the quantity in the Sales Order, the price was set to null, resulting in the BIP failure.
A similar incident occurred previously in the SC version (INC4031968). As part of the fix for that issue, the quantity field was made read-only to prevent modifications in the Sales Order.
Please find below the screenshot of UAT test record for your reference:
*Fix Plan:*
 We will apply the same approach by making the quantity field read-only for parts. This will prevent null price errors and ensure that BIP reports are generated successfully.
Kindly review and confirm our proposed fix plan. Please let us know if you have any questions or need further clarification.
Regards,
 Divyesh Ghiya

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-5016
Investigation Summary: After SO Sales Posting, revising an NV/UV Quote to change the Customer Account created only the 'Revise Sales Posting Selling' JV and omitted the Consumption Tax JV. The issue was reproduced on UAT1 for SO # A001299134 and A001299093. The logic was updated and validated on UAT1, then deployed to FDP Production in the 26th November planned release.
Important Findings: ['The issue occurred when an NV/UV Quote was revised after SO Sales Posting and the Customer Account changed without a Sales Amount change.', "Existing logic created revised Journal Voucher items only when the Sales Amount changed; otherwise, it created only the 'Revise Sales Posting Selling' JV.", 'The missing Consumption Tax JV was reproduced on UAT1 for SO # A001299134 and A001299093.', 'The same functionality and affected logic apply to UV and across all FDPs.', 'Past JVs have been affected because the logic has existed since FDP go-live.']
Root Cause: Existing revised Journal Voucher logic created Consumption Tax Journal entries only for Journal Voucher items with a Sales Amount change. When only the Customer Account or other non-amount values changed, it created only the 'Revise Sales Posting Selling' JV.
Resolution: Updated the logic to create the Consumption Tax Journal together with the 'Revise Sales Posting Selling' Journal even when the Sales Amount is unchanged and fields such as Customer Account change. The fix was validated on UAT1 and deployed to FDP Production in the 26th November planned release.
Technical Entities: ['JV', 'Accounts Receivable', 'NV', 'UV', 'Quote', 'SO Sales Posting', 'Customer Account', 'Revise Sales Posting Selling', 'Consumption Tax JV', 'Consumption Tax Journal', 'Revised Journal Voucher', 'UAT1', 'SO # A001299134', 'A001299093', 'FDP', 'FDP Production']

Timestamp: 2025-11-25T09:28:00
Author: Atul Yadav
Comment: We would like to share the analysis details for the incident MFTBCFFR-5016 reported on 25th November 2025, related to the JV of consumption tax of Accounts Receivable was not created, after Sales Posting Customer Account was Changed.
Please find the summary below:
|Incident Number |MFTBCFFR-5016|
|Description|NV FDP China No consumption tax journal entry due to change of business partner after sales |
|Root Cause (RCA)|When NV/UV Quote is revised after SO Sales Posting, and certain field values(Price and other info) are changed, Revised Journal Vouchers are created
 with the updated values. In this case, Customer Account is changed and upon quote approval, only 'Revise Sales Posting Selling' JV was created, Consumption Tax JV was not created. We have replicated this issue on UAT1:
SO # A001299134, A001299093
This issue occurred because as per the existing logic, Revise Journal Voucher is created only for those Journal Vouchers Items where Sales Amount is changed, if Selling Amount is not changed then in that case only one JV 'Revise Sales Posting Selling' is created.|
|Recovery status|Will do after confirmation from Shiromoto San|
|Fix Plan|To fix this, we will update the logic so that Consumption Tax Journal is created with 'Revise Sales Posting Selling' Journal
​even if Sales Amount is not changed and other values like account is changed.
We will fix it on UAT by today end of day, if fix approval is received.|
|Planned UAT date|25th November, 2025|
|Next update|26th November, 2025|
Also, response to your queries is :
 1. *Is there any past JV? * >> Since this logic has been in place since FDP go-live, there are past JVs affected.
2. *For UV, is it in the same situation of After Sales Posting?* >> Yes, the same functionality applies to UV as well.
3. *Do other FDPs have same specification?*>> Yes, the logic is same across all FDPs.
The issue has been *fixed on UAT1* after receiving your approval for the fix plan.
 We have also received *production deployment approval* from Shiromoto San, and this will be released in the *26th November release*.
If you require further clarification or assistance, please feel free to reach out.
We appreciate your continued cooperation.
      
Best Regards,
 Atul Yadav

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4988
Timestamp: 2025-11-17T14:07:00
Author: Abhinav
Comment: Thank you for your support.
We have investigated this issue and would like to share our findings with you.
*Root Cause Analysis (RCA):*
 We have successfully replicated the issue on Parts Purchase Return Order *#N001300132* on *FDP-UAT1*.
 Our analysis showed that *Return Good Qty* and *Return Defective Qty* fields become editable when the shipment is processed using the *“Shipped”* button. As a result, users are able to modify these quantities even after the shipment is marked as shipped. This leads to the creation of incorrect actions and transactions for the line item.
*Fix Plan:*
 * We will make *Return Good Qty* and *Return Defective Qty* permanently *read-only*, regardless of shipment status.
 * We will fix this issue on *FDP-UAT1 by 18/11/2025 (EOD)*.
Please let us know if you have any questions or require further clarification.
Best Regards,
Abhinav

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4978
Investigation Summary: SV master data was missing after the Wave-3 data migration because the required master file was not received from Biz. BIP report text retrieves values from this master data, causing incorrect or missing display. Master data was updated to match FDP-Okayama in FDP-UAT environments UAT4–UAT8, validated by the customer, and deployed to production in the 30 November FDP emergency release.
Important Findings: ['SV master data was missing following the Wave-3 data migration because the required master file was not received from Biz.', 'BIP report text is configured to fetch values from master data.', 'Master data in FDP-UAT UAT4, UAT5, UAT6, UAT7, and UAT8 was updated according to FDP-Okayama/Okayama-PROD values.', 'The updated UAT4–UAT8 master data was validated as displaying correctly with correct values.', 'The production fix was deployed in the 30 November FDP emergency release.']
Root Cause: During the Wave-3 data migration, the required SV master-data file was not received from Biz, leaving SV master data missing.
Resolution: Updated master data in FDP-UAT UAT4–UAT8 to match FDP-Okayama/Okayama-PROD, obtained validation, and deployed the fix to production in the 30 November FDP emergency release.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4975
Investigation Summary: When an Account was selected from the pick applet for the "Bill To Basic Account Name" field, Payer Details were not updated correctly. Analysis identified an internal configuration conflict. The fix was validated in UAT-1 and deployed to FDP Prod in the 17th December 2025 release.
Important Findings: ['Selecting an Account from the pick applet in "Bill To Basic Account Name" caused Payer Details to remain incorrect.', 'The issue was caused by an internal configuration conflict.', 'The affected record was recovered before the permanent fix was completed.', 'UAT-1 validation confirmed that Customer Info updated correctly when the Account Name changed.', 'The fix was deployed to FDP Prod in the 17th December 2025 release.']
Root Cause: An internal configuration conflict prevented Payer Details from being updated correctly when an Account was selected from the pick applet in the "Bill To Basic Account Name" field.
Resolution: Fixed the configuration issue, validated the correction in UAT-1, and deployed the fix to FDP Prod in the 17th December 2025 release.
Technical Entities: ['Bill To Basic Account Name', 'Account', 'pick applet', 'Payer Details', 'Customer Info', 'UAT1', 'UAT-1', 'FDP Prod', '17th December 2025 release']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4955
Investigation Summary: In rare cases, Quote processing failed to calculate the 'Trade In Consumption Tax' after entering a Trade in Amount. Investigation identified a code-efficiency timing issue: the link updating the Quote could complete slower than the line-item tax update script, causing the update to break. The code was optimized with a more efficient link, validated on UAT-1, and released to FDP Production on 26-Nov-25.
Important Findings: ["The issue affected calculation of 'Trade In Consumption Tax' in Quote in rare cases.", 'Entering a Trade in Amount triggers a tax update in the line item and a linked update in the Quote.', 'The Quote update failed when the link executed slower than the script; normally, the link completed faster.', 'The issue was not attributable to user mis-operation or functional mis-operation and could not be replicated.', 'A more efficient link was implemented to prevent the timing-related failure.', 'The fix was deployed to FDP Production in the 26-Nov-25 planned release.']
Root Cause: A code-efficiency timing issue caused the link that updates the Quote to run slower than the line-item tax update script, breaking the update and preventing calculation of 'Trade In Consumption Tax'.
Resolution: Optimized the code by replacing the link with a more efficient link; the fix was tested on UAT-1 and released to FDP Production on 26-Nov-25.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4952
Investigation Summary: A duplicate Vehicle, Chassis Order, and recycle fee order/line items were created when the D21A ODI package processed a TOB file whose Model Code did not match the Model Code stored in the Vehicle record. The affected data was recovered in production, including JV recovery and cancellation of duplicate Chassis Order B050481404. The evidence did not conclusively establish that a user changed the Model Code through the Administration Vehicle screen. A preventive fix was implemented in the SC version and proposed for FDP after approval.
Important Findings: ['Chassis Order B050208984 and its Vehicle record were initially created with Model Code FBA20B21W00F-5-G830; the Vehicle record later contained FBA20B21W00F-4-G830.', 'A TOB D21A file received on 7 November 2025 contained Model Code FBA20B21W00F-5-G830.', 'Because the D21A ODI package did not match the incoming Model Code to the Vehicle record, it treated the data as new and created duplicate Chassis Order B050481404, a new Vehicle, and duplicate recycle fee order and line items.', 'JV recovery was completed and the duplicate order was cancelled in the production environment; recycle fee attributes became visible after recovery.', 'The claimed user mis-operation through the Administration Vehicle screen was disputed and was not proven by the recorded last-updated user or replication results.', 'The SC-version fix matches the TOB Model Code against the Chassis Order Line Item rather than the Vehicle record and updates the Vehicle Model Code from TOB; equivalent FDP implementation was pending approval.']
Root Cause: A Model Code mismatch between the incoming TOB D21A file/original Chassis Order Line Item (FBA20B21W00F-5-G830) and the Vehicle record (FBA20B21W00F-4-G830) caused the D21A ODI package to identify the data as new and create duplicate Vehicle, Chassis Order, and recycle fee records.
Resolution: Completed JV recovery and cancelled duplicate Chassis Order B050481404 in production. A preventive fix was implemented in the SC version under INC6267864 and INC6273871; FDP implementation was proposed pending approval.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4952
Timestamp: 2025-12-08T08:05:00
Author: Divyesh Ghiya
Comment: Thank you for your support.
We have investigated this issue thoroughly and below are our findings:
This issue occurred due to a difference in the Model Codes.
 
The user initially created the Chassis Order B050208984 with the Model Code FBA20B21W00F-5-G830, and the corresponding vehicle record was also created with this Model Code on 30 May 2025.
 
On 7 November 2025, a D21A file was received from TOB, containing the same Model Code FBA20B21W00F-5-G830.
 
However, after the vehicle was created on 30 May 2025, the Model Code in the vehicle record was modified by user from FBA20B21W00F-5-G830 to FBA20B21W00F-4-G830.
 
Due to this mismatch, the current D21A ODI package identified the data as a new record and consequently created a new vehicle and a new chassis order B050481404, resulting in duplication in chassis order and recycle fee order and line items.
This is a case of User mis-operation where user updated the model code in vehicle due to which correct file with MC 5 created a duplicate order. 
Additionally, these type of cases will be handled by Vehicle cleansing CR. Since, recovery is completed and no further action is pending on this Jira, kindly allow us to close this incident. 
Please let us know if you have any query or need any additional support.
Regards,
Divyesh Ghiya

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4948
Investigation Summary: Bulk Invoice records for multiple shipments were missing from month-end closing files sent to KB, requiring recovery data to be manually created and transmitted. Investigation found that the post-extraction SQL updated the sent-to-KB flag by order number instead of shipment, causing all shipments under an order to be marked as sent when only one shipment was processed. The SQL was corrected in all production environments, impacted records were recovered, and subsequent December month-end Bulk Data verification found no issues.
Important Findings: ['The issue affected Bulk Invoice data for shipments in FDPs including Okayama, Iwate, and Shikoku that were not included in closing data sent to KB.', 'After data extraction, an update SQL set the sent-to-KB flag based on the order number rather than the shipment.', 'When one shipment under an order was selected for KB processing, the SQL updated the flag for all shipments of that order.', 'Missing November 30 records had X_IF_STATUS set to Y before the SQL fix, causing them to be excluded from Bulk Invoice processing.', 'Recovery Bulk Invoice data was created and manually sent to KB for identified impacted records.', 'December month-end Bulk Data was verified and no further issue was found.']
Root Cause: The post-extraction update SQL updated the sent-to-KB flag, X_IF_STATUS, using the order number instead of the shipment, incorrectly marking all shipments for an order as sent to KB.
Resolution: The SQL was corrected in all production environments to update flags by shipment, recovery Bulk Invoice data was generated and sent to KB for impacted records, and month-end Bulk Invoice executions were monitored through December.

We have investigated this issue thoroughly and below are our findings:
After the data extraction, an update SQL is used to update the flag of the record that is been sent to KB in bulk processing. This SQL was updating the flag on the basis of the order number rather than shipment. If any order had one target shipment to be sent to KB, the flag was updated for all the shipment. 
We have now fixed this SQL on all the production environment and correct flag updates are made now. 
Additionally, we have identified the recovery target for 20th closing and performed the recovery yesterday and all the correct data has been sent to KB. We will continue our monitoring till November EOM closing.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4937
Investigation Summary: Duplicate JVs were created for insurance order processing associated with request# I050063671. Investigation found that a user could change the status back to Spreadsheet Approved, causing another JV to be created; the affected JV predated the fix delivered in MFTBCFFR-4382. Reverse JVs were recreated after an incorrect initial recovery amount, approved, and loaded to production for nightly processing.
Important Findings: ['Request# I050063671 created three insurance orders.', 'Only insurance order Q050076191 had Clerical Error flag set to "N", and a JV was created only for this order.', 'The duplicate JV resulted from the user being able to set the status to Spreadsheet Approved again.', 'The affected JV was created before the release of MFTBCFFR-4382.', 'The MFTBCFFR-4382 fix was tested successfully in UAT.', 'Recovery required reverse JVs; the initial recovery amount was reported as incorrect and corrected recovery data was loaded to production.']
Root Cause: A user could change an insurance order status to Spreadsheet Approved again, which triggered creation of a duplicate JV. The affected JV was created before this behavior was fixed by MFTBCFFR-4382.
Resolution: Created corrected reverse JVs for the duplicate JV recovery and loaded the approved recovery data to production for nightly processing. The recurrence was prevented by the fix delivered in MFTBCFFR-4382 and validated in UAT.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4933
Timestamp: 2025-11-07T12:02:00
Author: Soham Modi
Comment: Thanks for your support.
*RCA*: The performance issue in the “Order Confirmation Shipment” screen while using the PDQ '02_Today's sales' was caused primarily by the query design. The PDQ uses the condition JulianMonth() = JulianMonth(Today()), which applies a function directly on the date column. This makes the condition non-searchable using indexes, preventing the database from using the index on and forcing a full table scan. Additionally, multiple OR conditions on and further increased query complexity, and the absence of row limits resulted in large data retrieval, slowing both screen loading and data export. Since the same PDQ logic is used across all FDP environments, the slowness was observed in all FDP-PROD except for FDP-Okayama where the PDQ does not exist.
We'll provide the detailed analysis on the ways for improving the load time for this screen soon since multiple parameters are involved. Meanwhile, please let us know in case of any query.
Best Regards,
Soham Modi

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4928
Investigation Summary: Duplicate Insurance Orders were created when a Policy Number was manually entered in Siebel rather than returned through the Ejibai interface. Testing on UAT4 reproduced the behavior: manual entry left the backend User Key null, so a subsequent Ejibai policy response could not match the original record and created a duplicate. The issue was determined to be user mis-operation rather than a system defect; users should not manually update the policy number.
Important Findings: ['Insurance Orders are created in Siebel and Policy Numbers are generated through the Ejibai interface.', 'When the Ejibai response populates the Policy Number, the backend User Key is updated automatically.', 'Manually updating the Liability Insurance Policy # leaves the User Key null.', 'A later Policy Number response from Ejibai cannot locate the original record without the User Key and creates a duplicate Insurance Order.', 'The issue was replicated on UAT4 using Insurance Order Q000037255 and duplicate Q000037256.']
Root Cause: The Liability Insurance Policy # was manually updated instead of being populated through the Ejibai interface, leaving the backend User Key null and preventing subsequent Ejibai responses from matching the original Insurance Order.
Resolution: Instruct users to avoid manual updates to the Liability Insurance Policy # and allow the Ejibai interface response to populate the Policy Number and User Key.
Technical Entities: ['Siebel', 'Ejibai', 'Ejibai interface', 'Insurance Order', 'Policy Number', 'Liability Insurance Policy #', 'User Key', 'UAT4', 'Q000037255', 'Q000037256']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4928
Timestamp: 2025-12-09T06:40:00
Author: Divyesh Ghiya
Comment: Thank you for your support.
We have thoroughly analyzed this issue, and our findings are as follows:
The user is creating an Insurance Order and then generating the Policy Number through the Ejibai interface. However, the Ejibai response is not being sent back to Siebel. Instead, the policy is created in Ejibai, and the user is manually updating the Liability Insurance Policy # field in the Insurance Order, as it is currently editable.
When the Policy Number is populated in the Insurance Order through the Ejibai response, the backend field User Key gets updated automatically. However, when the Policy Number is entered manually, the User Key remains null. Therefore, when that same policy is sent again from Ejibai to Siebel, the system does not find the original record (due to the missing User Key) and creates a duplicate order.
We successfully replicated this issue on UAT4 with the help of Gayatri-san. Please refer to the Insurance Order Q000037255 and its duplicate Q000037256.
Replication steps performed:
Step 1: Created an Insurance Order in Siebel and proceeded with policy creation on the Ejibai side.
Step 2: Manually updated the Liability Insurance Policy # in the Insurance Order instead of sending the response from the Ejibai interface.
Step 3: Sent the Policy Number again from Ejibai.
Conclusion:
This is not a system defect but a user mis-operation, where the Policy Number is being updated manually rather than being linked through the Ejibai interface. Kindly inform the user to avoid such manual updates to prevent duplication issues.
Since no further action is pending on this Jira, kindly allow us to close this incident. Please let us know if you have any query or need any additional support.
Regards,
Divyesh Ghiya

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4915
Investigation Summary: An error occurred when Liability Insurance Information entered by the user did not match a Liability Insurance record in the master. The existing behavior could not resolve the insurance name and displayed an error instead of handling the unmatched master data as a zero-cost item. The fix was implemented in UAT-1 and released to Prod to create a zero-price Liability Insurance Quote Line Item when no matching master record exists.
Important Findings: ["The entered liability insurance information was not maintained in the master for the applicable combination of MD Classification 'M', Insurance Vehicle Type 'Omnibus', and Mainland Category 'Mainland'.", 'Liability Insurance Term values 1 through 13 were identified as available for the applicable master-data combination.', 'The initial error message occurred because the system could not find the insurance name, rather than because no insurance information had been entered.', 'The required behavior was to retain the expense name and display a zero amount when master data does not match, consistent with Taxes and other expenses behavior.', 'The implemented fix creates a Liability Insurance record in the Quote Line Item with zero price when Liability Insurance is not maintained in the master.', 'The change was completed on UAT-1 and subsequently released to Prod.']
Root Cause: No Liability Insurance master record matched the user-entered Liability Insurance Information, and the existing logic treated the unresolved insurance name as an error instead of creating a zero-price item.
Resolution: Modified the logic to create a dummy Liability Insurance in the Quote Line Item with zero price when no matching Liability Insurance master record is found; the change was tested on UAT-1 and released to Prod.
Technical Entities: ['Liability Insurance', 'Liability Insurance Information', 'master', 'Liability Insurance Term', "MD Classification 'M'", "Insurance Vehicle Type 'Omnibus'", "Mainland Category 'Mainland'", 'Taxes and other expenses', 'Quote Line Item', 'UAT-1', 'Prod']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4913
Investigation Summary: The Order Detail BIP report failed to generate for Trailer and Forklift sales orders. Investigation found that a missing Planned Delivery Date in the Sales Quote resulted in a null Tax rate being passed to the Sales Order. A fix was deployed to UAT1, approved for production, and released to Prod.
Important Findings: ['The affected function was generation of the Order Detail BIP report.', 'Tax rate is calculated in the Sales Quote based on the Planned Delivery Date and is passed to the Sales Order.', 'Trailer and Forklift Sales Quotes did not validate Planned Delivery Date before approval.', 'When Planned Delivery Date was empty, Tax rate remained null in both the Sales Quote and Sales Order.', 'The null Tax rate caused the BIP report generation failure.', 'The affected sales order was recovered, allowing BIP to be printed.']
Root Cause: Trailer and Forklift Sales Quotes lacked Planned Delivery Date validation, allowing approval with an empty date. This prevented Tax rate calculation and passed a null Tax rate to the Sales Order, causing the Order Detail BIP report to fail.
Resolution: A fix addressing the issue was deployed to UAT1 and then released to Prod after approval; the affected sales order was recovered so BIP could be printed.

Comment: Thank you for your support and cooperation.
As per our discussion and demonstration in the meeting. We explained why the Order Detail BIP report failed to generate in case of Trailer & Forklift.
 *Issue* : Failure in generation of Order Detail BIP report.
 *Cause* : Tax rate was null in Sales Order as well as in Sales Quote. *Tax rate* is calculated on the basis of *Planned Delivery Date* in the sales quote which is then passed on to the Sales Order. In case of Trailer and Forklift, the validation on Planned Delivery Date is not present to get the Sales Quote approval due to which, the tax rate is not calculated *whenever the date field is left empty* in the sales quote. As a result null tax rate is passed on to the Sales Order causing the BIP to fail.
 We plan and hope to provide the fix by today EOD on UAT environment.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4903
Investigation Summary: NV Quote and NV Sales Order contained different model codes because users could directly edit fields in the Chassis & Options tab of NV Sales Order line items. Affected records were recovered, and the editability issue was corrected and validated in FDP-UAT1 before release to PROD. The fix was released to PROD on 13 November.
Important Findings: ['The Chassis & Options tab in NV Sales Order line items was editable for some responsibility categories.', 'Users changed the model code directly in NV Sales Order instead of changing it in NV Quote and synchronizing the Quote to the Sales Order.', 'The correct business process is to update the model code in NV Quote and then sync the Quote to NV Sales Order.', 'The before-fix condition was available in FDP-RT2, where SO# A000055765 had editable Chassis & Options line-item fields.', 'In FDP-UAT1, fields in NV Sales Order were made read-only, including Product Name, Line#, and C#.', 'Recovery was completed for the shared affected records; no additional affected records were found in other FDP environments.']
Root Cause: The Chassis & Options tab of NV Sales Order line items was editable for some responsibility categories, allowing users to directly modify model codes in NV Sales Order and create mismatches with NV Quote.
Resolution: Made NV Sales Order Chassis & Options fields read-only, including Product Name, Line#, and C#, validated the change in FDP-UAT1, and released the fix to PROD on 13 November.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4903
Timestamp: 2025-10-31T11:52:00
Author: Divyesh Ghiya
Comment: Thank you for your support.
We have analyzed this issue thoroughly and below are our findings:
*Issue*: Different Model Codes were present in Quote and Sales Order.
*RCA*: We have found that Chassis & Options Tab in Line Items of NV Sales Order is editable for some responsibilities.
 
 Instead of changing the Model code from NV Quote, some users were changing the Model Code from this tab in Sales Order. Please find attached all the impacted NV Sales Orders. 
 
*Fix Plan*: Model Code should not be changed from the NV Sales Order. The correct business procedure for changing Model code is to change the model code from the NV Quote and then sync the Quote to Sales Order. Hence we will make the Product Name field read only in Chassis & Options tab. This will ensure that no such user miss-operations happens again. 
Kindly approve this fix plan. 
Please let us know if you have any query or need any additional information.
Regards,
Divyesh Ghiya

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4903
Timestamp: 2025-11-03T12:06:00
Comment: thank you always.
 
We have conducted a detailed analysis of this matter and would like to report the results below.
 
■ Question details:
There were different model codes in the quote and order (SO).
 
■ Cause (RCA):
The Chassis & Options tab in the NVSO details was editable for some responsibility categories.
So, we found that instead of changing the model code from the NV quote, some users were changing it directly on this tab (NVSO).
Please see the attached file (Recovery_Records_FDP.xlsx) for a list of affected NVSOs.
 
■ Fix Plan:
The model code cannot be changed directly from NVSO.
The correct operating procedure is to change the model code in the NV quotation and then synchronize the quotation to the sales order.
Therefore, we have set the Product Name field in the Chassis & Options tab to read-only to prevent similar mistakes in the future.
 
Please approve the above revised plan.
 
Please let us know if you have any questions or need additional information.
 
Thank you for your support.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4880
Investigation Summary: The 'Outsourcing Lubricant Carry-in' field in WO was defaulting to 'N' for dummy lubrication parts in UAT-1. Investigation confirmed that the executed Lubrication Master file for MFTBCFFR - 4830 contained Generic Flag = 'N', which directly drove the field's pre-default value. The Generic Flag was reset to 'Y' for the dummy parts, and the issue was confirmed as incorrect master data rather than a system defect.
Important Findings: ["The 'Outsourcing Lubricant Carry-in' field is pre-defaulted from the Generic Flag in Lubrication Master data.", 'The default logic was the same in UAT and prod; the discrepancy between UAT-1 and UAT-8 was caused by master data values.', "The Lubrication Master file executed for UAT1 and FDP-Okayama under MFTBCFFR - 4830 contained Generic Flag = 'N'.", "For dummy lubrication parts ..888888 and ..999999, the Generic Flag must always be 'Y' to default the Carry-in Flag correctly.", 'Price-only updates must use Lubricant Price Master; Lubrication Master additions or information changes must use SVC_LUBR_00_209 with only changed records.']
Root Cause: Incorrect master data: the Lubrication Master file executed for UAT1 and FDP-Okayama contained Generic Flag = 'N' for dummy lubrication parts, causing 'Outsourcing Lubricant Carry-in' to default to 'N'.
Resolution: Recovery was completed by resetting the Generic Flag to 'Y' for the dummy lubrication parts. The SOP will be updated to validate the Generic Flag for dummy parts whenever a Lubrication Master file is received.

*RCA*:
As discussed in the meeting, this issue occurred due to the execution of the file received for the Lubrication Master (i.e. MFTBCFFR - 4830) for UAT1 and FDP-Okayama. The file contained the value ‘N’ for the Generic Flag field. As a result, the pre-default logic in the Lubrication Master led to the 'Outsourcing Lubricant Carry-in' field being set to ‘N’, since this value is directly derived from the Lubrication Master data.
For Dummy Lubrication Parts, the value of this flag should always be ‘Y’ in the master data.
The recovery has been completed, and we have reset the value of the Generic Flag back to ‘Y’.

->Provide both Lubrication Master and Lubrication Price Master files if new lubrication data needs to be added in the FDPs.
Additionally, we will update our SOP to include a check for the Generic Flag value for dummy parts whenever a Lubrication Master file is received. We will also inform you in case any data update is required to maintain consistency across systems.
Since this was a data issue and not a system issue, please allow us to close this incident.
Please let us know in case of any queries.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4873
Investigation Summary: Retrofit order B050024442 could not progress from Ordered to Completed because Actual Completion Date 01 was not registered in the TOB Logistics Info tab. Investigation confirmed that TOB did not send the Actual Completion Date via the D21Z file. The order status was manually recovered to Completed, and no further action was required for this Jira.
Important Findings: ['Actual Completion Date 01 is a mandatory condition for updating the order status.', 'The Actual Completion Date registered through D21Z files is displayed as Actual Completion Date 01 in the TOB Logistics Info tab.', 'Order B050024442 did not have an Actual Completion Date registered.', 'TOB confirmed that the Actual Completion Date was not sent for order B050024442.', 'The status was recovered by changing the order from Ordered to Completed.']
Root Cause: TOB did not send the Actual Completion Date for retrofit order B050024442 through the D21Z file, leaving Actual Completion Date 01 unregistered and preventing the status update.
Resolution: Manually changed order B050024442 status from Ordered to Completed; the ticket was closed after TOB confirmed the missing Actual Completion Date transmission.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4865
Investigation Summary: The Sales Order Owner field was changing based on Ship To Account, Bill To Account, or Payer Account updates made during Sales Quote revision. Analysis confirmed that Sales Order Owner was expected to retain the Sales Quote Customer Name value. The Owner-field mapping was corrected in UAT-1, approved for production, and released to Prod on 13 November.
Important Findings: ['On Sales Quote revision, changes to Ship To Account, Bill To Account, and Payer Account caused the Sales Order Owner value to change.', 'Sales Order Owner is expected to match the Customer Name field on the Sales Quote.', 'The issue was reproduced on UAT1 using Assessment# H000050988, Sales Quote# 1-6Q119Q, and Sales Order# E001299696.', 'The mapping for the Sales Order Owner field was updated to use Sales Quote Customer Name.', 'The fix was validated in UAT-1 and released to Prod.']
Root Cause: The Sales Order Owner field mapping was influenced by Ship To Account, Bill To Account, and Payer Account values during Sales Quote revision instead of being mapped to the Sales Quote Customer Name field.
Resolution: Updated the Sales Order Owner mapping to match the Sales Quote Customer Name field, validated the change in UAT-1, and released it to Prod.
Technical Entities: ['Owner', 'Sales Order', 'Sales Quote', 'Customer Name', 'Ship To Account', 'Bill To Account', 'Payer Account', 'UAT1', 'UAT-1', 'Prod', 'Assessment# H000050988', 'Sales Quote# 1-6Q119Q', 'Sales Order# E001299696', 'FDP']

Investigation Summary: Incorrect sales prices were identified on JC line items with Line Item Type "51: Claim" and Item Status "Lubrication Shipped", where the required sales price was 0. investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4848
Investigation Summary: The Map button was inactive for lot Sales Order A000181823 with Requested Quantity 2. Investigation confirmed that its Purchase Orders were mapped to child sales orders A000181829 and A000181830, both in "Sales Posting Completed" status, rather than to the parent sales order. This was determined to be expected behavior, not a system issue.
Important Findings: ['Lot Sales Order A000181823 has Requested Quantity 2.', 'The lot Sales Order has child sales orders A000181829 and A000181830.', 'Both child sales orders were in "Sales Posting Completed" status.', 'Purchase Orders are mapped at the child sales order level rather than the parent sales order for this lot Sales Order.', 'The Map button is inactive because Purchase Orders are mapped to the child sales orders.']
Root Cause: For the lot Sales Order, Purchase Orders were mapped to child sales orders A000181829 and A000181830 rather than parent sales order A000181823, causing the Map button to be inactive.
Resolution: No corrective action was required; the inactive Map button was expected behavior for this lot Sales Order configuration.
Technical Entities: ['Sales Order', 'lot Sales Order', 'A000181823', 'A000181829', 'A000181830', 'Requested Quantity', 'Purchase Orders', 'Map button', 'Sales Posting Completed']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4838
Investigation Summary: Power BI export failed for JPN when two columns had identical Japanese translations, producing duplicate alias names in the export query. English exports succeeded because Power BI automatically appended suffixes such as _1 and _2. A fix to make the Japanese field titles unique was deployed to UAT and then released to production.
Important Findings: ['Two columns with the same Japanese translation generated the same alias name in the Power BI export query.', 'Duplicate column names made the export query invalid and caused the error: “File creation failure – An error occurred while executing the query for the data export operation.”', 'English Power BI exports handled duplicate aliases by appending suffixes such as _1 and _2.', 'For JPN, adding _2 to one duplicated field title prevented title duplication.', 'The fix was deployed to UAT and subsequently released to production.']
Root Cause: Duplicate Japanese translations caused two exported columns to receive the same alias name, resulting in an invalid Power BI export query with duplicate column names.
Resolution: Updated one of the duplicate Japanese field titles by adding _2, then deployed the fix to UAT and production.
Technical Entities: ['Power BI', 'JPN', 'English', 'UAT', 'production', 'export query', 'File creation failure – An error occurred while executing the query for the data export operation.', '_1', '_2']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4834
Investigation Summary: The issue affected population of the "Internal Order (Charge To)" field for Job Cards created from UV Inventory. Investigation found that the program logic did not correctly update the field during UV Inventory JC creation and, after initial remediation, did not update it when "Update JC" was clicked for a Request for Reservation-only scenario. The logic was updated, validated in UAT-1 for both Quote Request and Reservation Request scenarios, and released to PROD.
Important Findings: ['For a JC created from UV Inventory with Department set to "UV", "Internal Order (Charge To)" should be populated with "UV".', 'The current program did not properly update "Internal Order (Charge To)" when a Job Card was created from the UV Inventory side.', 'After the initial UAT fix, the field still did not update when "Update JC" was clicked in an Only Request for Reservation scenario.', 'The logic was updated to populate "Internal Order (Charge To)" on button click.', 'UAT-1 validation confirmed that "Internal Order (Charge To)" had a value for both Quote Request and Reservation Request scenarios.', 'The fix was released to PROD.']
Root Cause: The program logic did not update the "Internal Order (Charge To)" field for UV Inventory Job Cards, including when "Update JC" was clicked for an Only Request for Reservation scenario.
Resolution: Updated the "Internal Order (Charge To)" logic for UV Inventory Job Cards and for the "Update JC" button flow; validated in UAT-1 and deployed to PROD.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4828
Investigation Summary: In UAT1 test record "1-6WGYRW", using Change Records to update Manual Discount% after selecting all quote line items with Ctrl+A changed the editable field initially clicked by the user. The behavior was reproduced in Service Quotes and parts quote and was identified as a Siebel Vanilla functionality defect rather than a business-process configuration issue. Users were instructed to initiate the operation from a read-only field or manually select records when the cursor is in an editable field.
Important Findings: ['The issue occurred when a user clicked an editable field, selected all lines with Ctrl+A, and used Change Records to update Manual Discount%.', 'After confirming Change Records, the editable field initially selected in step 1 was changed.', 'The behavior was reproduced on Service Quotes and parts quote, including UAT1 test record "1-6WGYRW".', 'The current business process configuration was confirmed to be correct.', 'Change Records is a Siebel Vanilla functionality, and the behavior was identified as a Siebel bug.', 'As a workaround, users should click a read-only field before using Ctrl+A and Change Records, or manually select records if the cursor is in an editable field.']
Root Cause: A Siebel bug in the vanilla Change Records functionality causes the initially selected editable field to be changed when all records are selected with Ctrl+A and a bulk update is performed.
Resolution: Communicate the operational workaround to Hakodate branch users: start the Change Records operation from a read-only field, or manually select records when the cursor is in an editable field.
Technical Entities: ['UAT1', '1-6WGYRW', 'Service Quotes', 'parts quote', 'Change Records', 'Manual Discount%', 'Siebel', 'Siebel Vanilla functionality', 'Hakodate branch', 'Ctrl+A']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4828
Timestamp: 2025-12-16T09:38:00
Author: Divyesh Ghiya
Comment: Thank you for your support.
We have investigated this issue thoroughly and below are our findings:
User is performing the following steps in service quote line item while updating the manual discount % in all the line items:
UAT1 test record "1-6WGYRW":
Step 1: Click on an editable field:
Step 2: Now select all lines by clicking "Ctrl+A":
Step 3: Click on Change Records and select the Manual Discount% and enter the field value to be updated for all line items and then click OK:
Step 4: After clicking OK on Change records applet, the editable field in which user clicked in step 1 is changed :
RCA: Change Records is a Siebel Vanilla functionality where it is observed that above steps in all quote line items leads to changing the value in initially selected editable fields. This phenomenon can be observed in other editable fields as well:
Also this is not limited to Service Quotes only, we have replicated the same steps on parts quote too. 
This is a Siebel bug where the change record functionality is behaving in this manner. Current business process configuration is correct but this issue is arising because of the existing Siebel bug, 
Countermeasure: We should inform the users of Hakodate branch to perform such operations on read only fields so that such occurrence can be avoided. Users can click on read only fields or instead of selecting all the fields at once by ctrl+A they can select the records manually(If the cursor is at an editable field). This will ensure that such issue do not occur again. 
Since no further topic is pending on this Jira, kindly allow us to close this ticket. Please let us know if you have any query or need any additional support.
Regards,
Divyesh Ghiya

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4809
Investigation Summary: Duplicate JVs were created for D2S Invoice records with a blank PO Number (X_ATTRIB_02) because the processing flag was not updated to "S" after JV creation. The flag-update logic was corrected and tested in UAT8 so PO-blank records are processed only once. The fix was deployed to Production in the 23rd October FDP release, and recovery data was completed for the affected duplicate JV records.
Important Findings: ['JV creation is triggered when the D2S Invoice flag is not "S".', 'The existing flag-update logic required PO Num, Invoice Num, and Inv Dt to be non-null.', 'PO Number (X_ATTRIB_02) being blank is normal for D2S invoices received by Siebel.', 'For PO-blank records, the flag was not updated to "S" after JV creation, allowing duplicate JVs to be created.', 'The issue affected three records on Chugoku.', 'Recovery was required for duplicate JV types D2S Inv Amt, D2S Inv CommFee, and D2S Inv CT.']
Root Cause: The flag-update filter required PO Num to be non-null. When PO Number (X_ATTRIB_02) was blank, the D2S Invoice record was not updated to flag "S" after JV creation and was eligible for duplicate JV creation.
Resolution: Updated the flag-update logic so records with blank PO Num are updated to "S" after processing, tested the change in UAT8, and deployed it to Production in the 23rd October FDP release. Created and completed Production recovery data for the duplicate JVs.
Technical Entities: ['JV', 'D2S Invoice', 'FDP-UAT8', 'UAT8', 'Chugoku PROD', 'Chugoku', 'KB', 'PO Number', 'X_ATTRIB_02', 'Flag', 'S', 'Invoice Num', 'Inv Dt', 'Siebel', 'Production', 'FDP release', 'D2S Inv Amt', 'D2S Inv CommFee', 'D2S Inv CT', 'Data Set Separator', 'OBCD001', 'Posting Date', 'CSJS005']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4804
Investigation Summary: The issue occurred when an Assessment Request was created for a selected Chassis with a blank Full Model Code field. Important Findings: ['The selected Chassis had a blank Full Model Code value, which caused the issue.', 'Affected users were instructed to cancel the existing Assessment Request and create a new one.', 'A validation check for blank Full Model Code values on selected chassis was implemented in FDP-UAT1.', 'Test Assessment Request AR#: H000050796 was created in FDP-UAT1.', 'The approved change was released to PROD on 23 October as part of the scheduled FDP release.']
Root Cause: The Full Model Code field was blank for the selected Chassis.
Resolution: Implemented and released a validation check that displays a validation message when the Full Model Code is blank for a selected Chassis.
Technical Entities: ['Full Model Code', 'Chassis', 'Assessment Request', 'Generate Approval', 'Create Quote', 'FDP-UAT1', 'PROD', 'FDP', 'AR#: H000050796']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4790
Investigation Summary: A Sales Order did not synchronize to the latest of 9 approved Quote revisions and remained at revision 7. Error logs showed a concurrent-update conflict during the Quote-to-Sales Order synchronization, and the scenario was reproduced in UAT by modifying the same Sales Order line item while synchronization was running. The affected record was recovered on Wakayama Prod; no system change was implemented, and the proposed prevention was to avoid concurrent updates to the same record.
Important Findings: ['The Sales Order remained at revision 7 after 9 Quote revisions had been created and approved.', "The failure occurred in step 'Sync Sales Order' using service 'EAI Siebel Adapter' and method 'Synchronize' with error SBL-BPR-00162.", "Business component 'MF RF Order Entry - Line Items' failed in 'WriteRecord' with SBL-DAT-00523 and SBL-EAI-04451, indicating the record had been modified after retrieval.", 'The issue was reproduced in UAT when another user modified a Sales Order line item while Quote-to-Sales Order synchronization was running; the synchronization update succeeded and the manual update received the error.', 'The affected record was recovered on Wakayama Prod.', 'Regression testing in FDP did not reproduce the issue; SC UAT and FDP were identified as different applications.']
Root Cause: A concurrent update to the same Sales Order line-item record during Quote-to-Sales Order synchronization caused a Siebel record-update conflict, preventing the Sales Order from synchronizing to the latest Quote revision.
Resolution: The affected record was recovered on Wakayama Prod. The proposed preventive measure was to instruct users not to update the same record simultaneously from different sessions or screens.
Technical Entities: ['Wakayama Prod', 'Quote', 'Sales Order', 'Sales Order line item', 'Sync Sales Order', 'EAI Siebel Adapter', 'Synchronize', 'SBL-BPR-00162', 'MF RF Order Entry - Line Items', 'MF Order Item', 'WriteRecord', 'SBL-DAT-00523', 'SBL-EAI-04451', 'BB Vendor Code: 0000186686', 'Total List Price', 'UAT', 'SC UAT', 'FDP', 'Siebel']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4785
Investigation Summary: Journal Voucher ordering was investigated for records that were grouped in an unexpected sequence. When Timestamp and Global Order Number are identical, sorting falls back to Data Set Separator, which can produce this scenario. Configuration was confirmed identical across all FDPs, and the behavior was reproduced in UAT1 and UAT2; no recovery was required, and the scenario will be monitored through daily AMS monitoring.
Important Findings: ['Journal Voucher sorting order is Timestamp > Global Order Number > Data Set Separator.', 'When Timestamp and Global Order Number are the same, grouping is determined by Data Set Separator.', 'The issue was initially observed for a small number of records in Okayama, but no Okayama-specific configuration discrepancy was found.', 'The scenario was reproduced in UAT1 and UAT2 and is possible for all FDPs.', 'Implementing a logic fix would require significant changes to the existing logic.', 'Recovery was not required for the affected orders; similar occurrences will be monitored and recovered if needed.']
Root Cause: A Journal Voucher sorting tie occurs when both Timestamp and Global Order Number are identical; sorting then uses Data Set Separator, resulting in the observed grouping sequence.
Resolution: No recovery was performed because it was not required. The Jira was closed, and the scenario was added to daily AMS monitoring for detection and recovery of future occurrences.
Technical Entities: ['Journal Voucher', 'Timestamp', 'Global Order Number', 'Data Set Separator', 'Okayama', 'FDPs', 'Shipped button', 'sales order', 'UAT1', 'UAT2', 'daily AMS monitoring', 'M000204765', 'M000244090', 'M000303799', 'M000315069', 'M000364233', 'M000401254', 'M000433410', 'M000442591', 'M001299572', 'O000184578', 'O000184577', 'M000056000', 'O000015922', 'O000015921']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4776
Investigation Summary: Status Code values differed between SC and FDP because each environment sourced the value from a different table and represented a different status type. Changes were implemented and validated in FDP UAT, with the final Status Code LOV filter update deployed to production for Report #1-15A across all FDPs. Validation in PBI-PROD confirmed the change was correct and the incident was resolved.
Important Findings: ['In FDP, Status Code is sourced from WC_SERVICE_ORDER_F and represents Order Status.', 'In SC, Status Code is sourced from W_SRVREQ_MD and represents Service Request Status.', 'The differing source tables caused different Status Code filter values between SC and FDP.', 'The Order Code LOV displayed correctly in FORCE FDP (UAT), but the line item Order Code (JC Status) was initially not displayed.', 'The requested LOV change for Report #1-05 was withdrawn because it was technically difficult.', 'The Status Code LOV for Report #1-15A was changed correctly for all FDPs in PBI-PROD.']
Root Cause: SC and FDP used different source tables for Status Code: WC_SERVICE_ORDER_F in FDP for Order Status and W_SRVREQ_MD in SC for Service Request Status.
Resolution: Deployed the Status Code LOV filter change for Report #1-15A to production for all FDPs; the change was validated successfully in PBI-PROD.
Technical Entities: ['SC', 'FDP', 'WC_SERVICE_ORDER_F', 'W_SRVREQ_MD', 'Order Status', 'Service Request Status', 'FDP UAT Okoyama', 'FORCE FDP (UAT)', 'PBI-PROD', 'FDP-PROD', 'Status Code', 'Status Code LOV', 'Order Code LOV', 'Order Code (JC Status)', 'Report #1-05', 'Report #1-10A', 'Report #1-12A', 'Report #1-15A']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4752
Investigation Summary: Invoice data for Parts Purchase Order line items was not inserted into D2S Invoice Mismatch when the D2S SO Item Number and Product did not match the D2S invoice file. The insertion logic was corrected on FDP-UAT1, including a filter-condition update for null X_ATTRIB_02 values, and was released to Production on 23rd October. Historical mismatch records were recovered across affected FDPs and their creation dates were aligned to the invoice-received date.
Important Findings: ['D2S Invoice Mismatch excluded invoice data when D2S SO Item Number and Product values in a PO line item did not match the D2S invoice file.', 'A filter condition failed when X_ATTRIB_02 was null, causing incorrect values to be selected for records with blank PO numbers.', 'After the fix, invoice data was inserted into D2S Invoice Mismatch even when PO line items differed from the D2S Invoice file.', 'D2S Invoice Mismatch records are stored in CX_MISM_TOB / siebel.CX_MISM_TOB.', 'Recovery was required for mismatch records on Iwate, Aomori, Shikoku, and FDP Chugoku; recovered records had their creation dates updated to the invoice-received date.', 'Creation dates for invoice 8000115382 items 000010 and 000020 in siebel.CX_MISM_TOB were corrected to August 4, 2025 to match siebel.cx_d2s_recon.']
Root Cause: D2S Invoice Mismatch insertion logic excluded invoice data when PO line-item D2S SO Item Number and Product did not match the D2S invoice file; a related filter condition also failed when X_ATTRIB_02 was null.
Resolution: Updated the insertion and filter conditions on FDP-UAT1, released the fix to Production in the 23rd October scheduled FDP release, and recovered affected mismatch records with corrected creation dates.

1. Why did data inconsistency occur between quotations and orders due to data migration?

In this case, a "promissory note due date" was set in the quotation, but the corresponding item was not set in the corresponding order.
During the order completion process, a consistency check is performed on important items in the quotation and order. In this case, the order completion process was stopped normally because the inconsistency was detected.
Please note that the validation function to detect such inconsistencies is working normally as designed.
At this time, we do not have any additional information to conduct further investigation.
Additionally, we have confirmed that this issue is not reproducible, and we have determined that the same issue will not occur with new records created in FDP in the future.
The system functions are operating normally, so please approve the closing of this ticket.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4720
Investigation Summary: The "Internal Order (Charge To)" field was not being updated correctly by the existing program, requiring recovery of affected Internal Orders. The issue had existed for an extended period and was not caused by a recent configuration change or release. The program was corrected, validated in FDP-UAT1/UAT-01, and deployed to Production in the 9th October FDP Release.
Important Findings: ['Data recovery was required for Internal Orders, with September JC Create Date Required orders prioritized.', 'For TYPE "22: NV Modification (Transfer)" and "23: NV Stock Modification (Pool)", Internal Order (Charge To) had to be recovered as NV; for TYPE "26: UV Repair (Transfer)", it had to be recovered as SV.', 'The existing program was not working properly to update the "Internal Order (Charge To)" field.', 'No configuration change was identified as the cause; the issue had existed since at least SR MFRBCFFR-1824.', 'Orders were prevented from proceeding with JCO when the field was not populated because a validation required the field before JCO.', 'The fix passed testing in UAT1 and was deployed to Production on 9th October.']
Root Cause: The existing program did not correctly update the "Internal Order (Charge To)" field. The defect was longstanding and was not attributed to a recent configuration change or release.
Resolution: Recovered affected Internal Orders, updated the program that populates "Internal Order (Charge To)", validated the fix in FDP-UAT1/UAT-01, and deployed it to Production in the 9th October FDP Release.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4691
Investigation Summary: The incident involved correcting Journal Vector recovery data and identifying JVs from WO line items. investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4682
Investigation Summary: Changing the customer code in the JC header did not immediately update the customer code in all child applet placeholders. The values updated correctly only after manually refreshing the child applet. Refresh functionality was added to JC More Info and other screens in FDP-UAT1, then deployed to Production in the 9th October FDP Release.
Important Findings: ['Customer code changes in the JC header were not propagated to all placeholders in the child applet.', 'The correct customer code was reflected after the child applet was refreshed, based on the JC header value.', 'The fix added refresh functionality so changes are reflected immediately without a manual applet refresh.', 'The fix was implemented in FDP-UAT1, approved for Production monitoring, and deployed in the 9th October FDP Release.']
Root Cause: Customer code updates in the JC header were not updating all placeholders in the child applet until the applet was refreshed.
Resolution: Added refresh functionality on JC More Info and other screens to immediately reflect JC header customer code changes; deployed to Production in the 9th October FDP Release.
Technical Entities: ['JC header', 'child applet', 'JC More Info', 'Quote', 'JCO More Info', 'FDP-UAT1', 'PROD', 'Production', '9th October FDP Release']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4674
Timestamp: 2025-09-19T09:04:36+00:00
Author: Atul Yadav
Comment: Dear  San,
Thank you for your support.
We have checked this issue and following are the root cause , impacted records, fix plan and recovery plan for this issue:
*Root Cause:*
We have found that in Re-Edit CR logic, if Re-edit button is clicked on same day as job card was created, then *Sent to KB* flag is updated to "Y" for all JVs except latest closed ones. To do this, we query using Voucher Abstract in JV, and Expense JV(Tax - Weight Tax, Tax - Automobile Type, 'Tax - Automobile Env') are created when expense is completed i.e., it is created before latest Job Card JV is created.
So sent to KB flag was getting updated to "Y".
*Fix plan:* 
We will fix this issue on UAT and exclude Job Card JVs with Order Type *'Tax - Weight Tax, Tax - Automobile Type, 'Tax - Automobile Env'.*
*Recovery Plan:*
We have checked all FDP environments and only I000213439 and I000224933 *Tax - Weight Tax JVs* were found. To recovery this we will retrigger these two JVs and it will be linked to KB in tonight's daily batch.
Kindly let us know in case of any queries.
Regards,
Atul Yadav

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4671
Investigation Summary: The JV Department Code was populated from the Sales Order Creator’s Department Code, causing Department Code "05" from user D8TOSANA to appear in the JV. The mapping was changed and validated in UAT1, then deployed to Production in the 9th October 2025 FDP Release.
Important Findings: ['Department Code in JV was mapped from the Creator’s Department Code.', 'The Sales Order creator user D8TOSANA had Department Code "05", which was therefore shown in the JV.', 'The required mapping was to populate the JV Department Code from the Primary Sales Rep’s Department Code (Current Sales Rep).', 'The fix was completed in UAT1 and deployed to Production in the 9th October 2025 FDP Release.']
Root Cause: The JV Department Code mapping used the Sales Order Creator’s Department Code instead of the Primary Sales Rep’s Department Code (Current Sales Rep).
Resolution: Modified the JV Department Code mapping to use the Primary Sales Rep’s Department Code (Current Sales Rep), validated the fix in UAT1, and deployed it to Production in the 9th October 2025 FDP Release.
Technical Entities: ['JV', 'Department Code', 'Sales Order Creator', 'Creator’s Department Code', 'D8TOSANA', 'Primary Sales Rep', 'Current Sales Rep', 'UAT1', 'Production', '9th October 2025 FDP Release']

Root Cause: DAILY LOAD PLAN overlapped with the Siebel backup, delaying completion and preventing scheduled report refreshes from running as intended.
Resolution: Rescheduled the affected report refreshes to start from 5:30 AM JST, after DAILY LOAD PLAN completes around 4:45 AM JST.
