investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4653
Investigation Summary: The department-code mapping used during UV Trade - In JV creation was corrected in UAT1 and deployed to Production in the 9th October FDP Release. The mapping was changed from the Sales Order Branch Code fetched from the Assessment of the UV PO to the Branch Code of the Parent Order. UAT validation was completed using SO #A001299134 after an internal test record created duplicate journal entries.
Important Findings: ['UV Trade - In JV creation previously derived the department code from the Branch Code of the Sales Order fetched from the Assessment of the UV PO.', 'The mapping was changed to use the Branch Code of the Parent Order, where the Purchase Order is mapped.', 'SO #A001299093 was an internal test record and created three journal entries due to testing, not a system error.', 'SO #A001299134 was provided for UAT verification of the corrected mapping.', 'The fix was deployed to Production in the 9th October FDP Release.']
Root Cause: The department code in UV Trade - In JV creation was mapped from the Branch Code of the Sales Order obtained from the Assessment of the UV PO instead of from the Branch Code of the Parent Order.
Resolution: Changed the department-code mapping in UV Trade - In JV creation to use the Parent Order Branch Code, validated the fix in UAT1, and deployed it to Production in the 9th October FDP Release.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4648
Timestamp: 2025-09-24T08:18:00+00:00
Author: aina Sun
Comment: Dear Tsunoda-san,
Thank you for your continued support.
We have analyzed the issue, and please find our findings and resolution details below:
Issue: For recycle order, response from TOB side is received but not reflected in the order.
RCA: This issue occurs when duplicate recycle orders exist with the same Vehicle ID. In such cases, the TOB response is being reflected in the duplicate order instead of the correct one due to the matching Vehicle ID.
 For MS06GP-15519(Recycle Order: B000286143,Duplicate Order: B000283229)
 For MS06GP-15518(Recycle Order: B000286144,Duplicate Order: B000283228)

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4634
Timestamp: 2025-09-12T05:57:37+00:00
Author: Harsh Kumar
Comment: Dear san,
Thank you very much for your continued support.
Cause analysis (RCA)
The current logic is that a validation check is performed before a delivery is approved to see if there are any items that are "Open" for shipping parts. If applicable shipments exist, a validation error message will be displayed when approving the shipment.
The current logic checks the shipping status of "Parts Purchase Orders" and excludes "Parts Internal Orders."
 
Modification details
In line with the original intent of validation, we will modify the logic to check the shipping status of "internal parts orders" instead of "parts purchase orders."
This prevents canceled parts (purchase orders) from causing errors during delivery approval.
 
Please check the revision policy and let us know if you have any questions.
 
Thank you for your support.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4634
Timestamp: 2025-09-12T05:26:32+00:00
Author: Soham Modi
Comment: Dear san,
 
Thank you for your support, and apologies for the inconvenience. Your understanding is correct.
 
*RCA*:
In the current logic, Before delivery approval a validation check is applied which checks if shipment of any parts line item is Open or not. If such shipments are found then Validation message occurs on Delivery Approval. According to the current logic, shipment of Parts Purchase Orders are checked rather then Parts Internal Order. 
 
*Fix*:
To align with the validation, we will update the logic to check shipment of Parts Internal Order rather then Parts Purchase Order. This will ensure that no such cancelled parts(with Purchase Orders) cause error in Delivery Approval.
 
Kindly confirm our fix plan and let us know if you have any query.
 
Best Regards,
Soham

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4623
Investigation Summary: Copied Job Cards could receive an incorrect Asset Id and MF Vehicle Id, resulting in a Chassis# different from the source Job Card. The issue occurred when duplicate vehicle registration-field values caused the copied Job Card to be reassigned to a different vehicle. The fix was validated in FDP UAT-1 and released to all FDP-PROD environments on 25 September.
Important Findings: ['Copy Job Card initially populates Asset Id, MF Asset Id, and MF Vehicle Id from the parent Job Card.', 'After Registration Number (L/#) is copied, Asset Id and MF Vehicle Id are updated from Auto Vehicle using Registration No Class No, Registration No. Land Name Area Name, Registration No Japanese Kana, and Registration No Sequence No.', 'Two vehicles in Chugoku prod had identical registration-field values, causing copied JC I050382306 to use chassis# FB51AB-552056 instead of chassis# FS54VZ-532935.', 'The fix was verified in FDP UAT-1 using copied JC I001298557 and source JC I001273076; the copied Job Card received the correct Chassis# (Key#) from the VM- tab.', 'The patch was released in the 25 September scheduled FDP release and applied to all FDP-PROD environments.']
Root Cause: Duplicate vehicle values for the registration fields used by Auto Vehicle caused a copied Job Card to update its Asset Id and MF Vehicle Id to a different vehicle, resulting in an incorrect Chassis#.
Resolution: The issue was fixed, validated in FDP UAT-1, and the patch was deployed to all FDP-PROD environments in the 25 September scheduled FDP release.
Technical Entities: ['Job Card', 'Copy Job Card', 'Asset Id', 'MF Asset Id', 'MF Vehicle Id', 'Registration Number (L/#)', 'Auto Vehicle', 'Registration No Class No', 'Registration No. Land Name Area Name', 'Registration No Japanese Kana', 'Registration No Sequence No', 'Chugoku prod', 'I050382306', 'FB51AB-552056', 'FS54VZ-532935', 'Service History', 'FDP UAT-1', 'I001298557', 'I001273076', 'Chassis# (Key#)', 'VM- tab', 'FDP-PROD', 'FDP']

Timestamp: 2025-09-16T04:47:00
Author: Akash
Comment: Thank you for your ongoing support.
 
We have checked and found that when a JC is copied using Copy Job Card button its *Asset Id* , *MF Asset Id* and *MF Vehicle Id* populated from the parent JC from which it is copied.
But when Field *Registration Number (L/#)* of Job Card is populated from the parent JC *Registration Number (L/#)*
 
Asset Id and MF Vehicle Id of new JC is updated again from the Auto Vehicle using the value of fields 
1. Registration No Class No, 
2. Registration No. Land Name Area Name , 
3. Registration No Japanese Kana, 
4.Registration No Sequence No
 
As there are two vehicles with same field values on Chugoku prod *Asset Id* and *MF Vehicle Id* of Copied JC (I050382306) populated from vehicle with Chassis# FB51AB-552056 instead of Vehicle with chassis# FS54VZ-532935.
As a result copying a JC from Service History, the JC will have a different Chassis# than the source.
 
Please check and confirm.
Let us know in case of any query.
 
Regards,
Akash

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4611
Timestamp: 2025-10-03T05:24:21+00:00
Author: Atul Yadav
Comment: Dear  San,
Thank you for your support and cooperation.
The problem earlier was failure in generation of BIP report (Order Detail) generated after getting the Sales Order approved.
 This problem was occurring because the user might have entered the last contract date someday before the year 2020. 
 For example 09/10/2018. This field in editable so later on the user might have corrected it after sales order approval.
 This back date of 09/10/2018 was leading to fetching of null value in tax rate. This tax rate is calculated in the basis of last contract date by comparing it to the Start and End date of the Tax Value in the Tax Master table. The start date in the table is a day of year 2020. So entering a date before this day will lead to failure in BIP generation.
 We are attaching the issue replication steps. Following these steps, earlier their was issue of failure in BIP generation but now there will not be an issue anymore.
 
Please let us know in case of any query.
Best Regards,
 Saad

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4600
Investigation Summary: System instability during peak traffic was investigated and linked to a timeout parameter increase from 1 hour to 2 hours. The longer session duration increased session retention and memory utilization at the web layer, amplifying existing memory leaks. Reverting the timeout parameter to 1 hour restored system stability.
Important Findings: ['The timeout parameter was changed from 1 hour to 2 hours before the instability occurred.', 'During peak traffic, prolonged sessions caused higher memory utilization and session retention at the web layer.', 'Extended sessions amplified memory leaks in the system.', 'Oracle and Siebel best practices recommend synchronizing timeout settings between web and application layers and avoiding long timeout values.', 'Reverting the timeout parameter from 2 hours to 1 hour restored stability.', 'Future timeout increases should be made gradually, such as in 10-minute intervals, with stability monitoring after each change.']
Root Cause: Changing the timeout parameter from 1 hour to 2 hours extended user sessions during peak load, increasing web-layer session retention and memory utilization and amplifying memory leaks.
Resolution: Reverted the timeout parameter from 2 hours to 1 hour, restoring system stability.
Technical Entities: ['Oracle', 'Siebel', 'web layer', 'application layers', 'timeout parameter', 'memory leaks']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4600
Timestamp: 2026-05-14T03:12:00
Comment: HelloPlease find the below mentioned details of the issue.
*1.Root Cause:*
Timeout parameter was changed from 1 hour to 2 hours, which led to extended user sessions during peak load, amplifying memory leaks in the system.
*2. Technical Observation:*
During peak traffic, prolonged sessions resulted in higher memory utilization and session retention at web layer.
*3. Oracle / Siebel Recommendation:*
As per Oracle and Siebel best practices, timeout synchronization between web and application layers must be maintained. Setting a long timeout value is not recommended due to possible performance impact.
*4. Action Taken:*
Timeout parameter was reverted from 2 hours back to 1 hour. Post-change, system stability was restored.
*5. Countermeasure / Preventive Action:*
For any future requirement to extend the session time, it is advised to increase the timeout parameter gradually (e.g., in 10-minute intervals) and monitor system stability after each change.
*6. Future Plan:*
If performance instability persists even after gradual adjustment, infrastructure-level tuning will be considered to ensure long-term system stability.
Thank you.
Please let us know in case of some further query.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4579
Investigation Summary: The incident matched MFTBCFFR-4243 and involved a Trade-In Assessment that could not be deleted after the Trade-In Flag was manually changed from "Y" to "N" in NV Quote Header revision 2. Unchecking the flag makes related Trade-In fields read-only, preventing required backend updates during assessment deletion. The issue is resolved by rechecking the Trade-In Flag to "Y" before deleting the Trade-In Assessment.
Important Findings: ['In revision 1, the Trade-In Flag in NV Quote Header was set to "Y".', 'In revision 2, the user manually unchecked the Trade-In Flag, changing it to "N".', 'When the Trade-In Flag is unchecked, related Trade-In fields become read-only.', 'Read-only Trade-In fields prevent backend field updates required to delete the Trade-In Assessment.', 'The correct process is to delete the Trade-In Assessment first, then uncheck the Trade-In Flag.']
Root Cause: The Trade-In Flag was changed to "N" before deleting the Trade-In Assessment, causing related Trade-In fields to become read-only and blocking the backend updates required for deletion.
Resolution: Recheck the Trade-In Flag in NV Quote Header to "Y", delete the Trade-In Assessment, and only then uncheck the flag if required.
Technical Entities: ['MFTBCFFR-4243', 'Trade-In Flag', 'NV Quote Header', 'Trade-In Assessment']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4579
Timestamp: 2025-09-02T04:27:00
Author: Atul Yadav
Comment: Thanks for your support.
 We have thoroughly investigated and this issue is same as MFTBCFFR-4243.
 *User Steps:*
 In Revision 1, the Trade-In Flag in NV Quote Header was selected as “Y”.
 However in revision 2, user manually unchecked the flag, changing it to “N”.
 If a user intends to delete the Trade-In Assessment, the correct process is to delete the assessment record first and then uncheck the Trade-In flag.
 *RCA:*
 When the Trade-In flag is unchecked in the NV Quote header, the related Trade-In fields become read-only. This prevents deletion, as certain backend field updates required during deletion cannot occur in this state.
 *Recovery Plan:*
 No recovery action is required. The user can resolve the issue by rechecking the Trade-In flag to “Y”. This will allow deletion of the Trade-In Assessment as needed.
Conclusion:
 This is a case of user mis operation, not a system defect. Hence, kindly allow us to reject this incident.
 Please advise the user to follow the steps outlined above. Please let us know if you have any query or need any additional support.
Regards,
 Atul Yadav

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4576
Investigation Summary: The incident concerned incorrect account information in Individual Invoice. Investigation confirmed that the existing Client Code (CSJ208) mapping in Journal Voucher used the Bill To Account from UV Sales Order. Root Cause: The existing mapping used Client Code (CSJ208) in Journal Voucher from the UV Sales Order Bill To Account, rather than the required Account Code and Account field mapping.
Resolution: Implemented the revised mapping: Account Code from Bill To Account Customer Code and Account from Customer Name; validated in UAT1 and deployed to production.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4557
Timestamp: 2026-07-09T16:13:21+00:00
Author: Ayaz Farooqui
Comment: Dear San,
 
Thank you for your continued support.
 
We have completed our investigation into this issue and would like to report the cause (RCA).
 
When a D21Z file corresponding to a Retro-fit Chassis Order is received and the actual completion date (data starting with "J" starting from the 106th digit) is set, the status of the Retro-fit Chassis Order will be updated to **Completed**.
 
As a result of our investigation, the reason why the status was not updated to "Completed" was because the code of the order was searched for ** "11SC" during ODI processing. On the other hand, in FDP, the code for the target order was created in "Headquarters"**, so the conditions did not match and the status was not updated.
 
This issue is caused by the ODI processing settings, and we are currently making the necessary corrections to the target file. As a result, we do not expect similar incidents to occur regarding Retro-fit Chassis Orders in the future.
 
The above is the cause of this issue.
 
Please check the contents and feel free to contact us if you have any questions.
 
Thank you for your support.
 
(English)
Thank you for your support and cooperation.
We have completed our analysis for this issue and would like to share with you the root cause of this issue.
Whenever we receive the D21Z file for any corresponding “Retro-fit Chassis Order“ with Actual Completion Dates ( Starting with the character J at position 106 upto 4 Characters ). The Retrofit Chassis Order’s status should change to ‘Completed’.
As of now, the orders were not getting their Statuses set to “Completed” because the search command was matching the Order’s Division Type Code with ‘11SC’, however in FDP, the orders are created with their Division Type Codes as ‘Headquarters’.
Due to this mismatch the Orders were not getting their Statuses updated. This issue is related to the ODI executions. We have implemented the required changes in the respective files. We hope the issue will not occur for any Retrofit Orders in the future.
We request you to please review the above RCA and let us know in case of any query.
Best Regards,
Saad

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4528
Investigation Summary: Recovery JV data contained an invalid/blank account code for affected orders. Investigation found that Account Code Master had no configuration for Vehicle Type "Trailer" with OrderType "PO" and entity type "NV", causing the account code to be blank in JV. A Trailer-specific master record was created, validated on uat1, and released to production in the 13th September scheduled FDP release.
Important Findings: ['The recovery JV initially contained unknown account code "038" "30".', 'Correct recovery JV data was uploaded to Hakodate-PROD and scheduled for linking through the KB Batch.', 'Affected orders had Vehicle Type "Trailer".', 'Account Code Master lacked a record for Vehicle Type "Trailer", OrderType "PO", and entity type "NV".', 'Debit Account Code and Credit Account Code were requested for event name "ChassisBody Order - Map" for the Trailer configuration.', 'The configuration fix was tested on uat1 before production release.']
Root Cause: No Account Code Master record existed for Vehicle Type "Trailer" with OrderType "PO" and entity type "NV", causing the account code to be blank in the JV.
Resolution: Created the Account Code Master record for the Trailer vehicle type using the provided Debit Account Code and Credit Account Code, validated the fix on uat1, and released it to production in the 13th September scheduled FDP release.
Technical Entities: ['recovery JV', 'Account Item Code', 'posting date', 'Unknown code "038" "30"', 'Hakodate-PROD', 'KB Batch', 'Vehicle Type "Trailer"', 'Account Code Master', 'OrderType "PO"', 'entity type "NV"', 'Debit Account Code', 'Credit Account Code', 'ChassisBody Order - Map', 'Map & Unmap', 'uat1', 'production', 'FDP release']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4498
Investigation Summary: Duplicate recycle fee orders were repeatedly created when multiple D21F files were processed for the same chassis order. The investigation determined that the recycle fee order creation logic generated a new order for each D21F processing rather than updating an existing order. A logic enhancement was documented to prevent duplicate creation, but the timeline contains no confirmation that the fix was approved or that D21F content updates, such as amount changes, are handled.
Important Findings: ['For C# number 610083, D21F files were received on February 7 and August 4 for the same Chassis Order.', 'SIEBEL created duplicate recycling orders when the same D21F file or multiple D21F files for the same chassis order were processed.', 'The number of recycle fee orders created matched the number of D21F processing occurrences.', 'Repeated operational recoveries removed duplicate orders and updated recycle status/order status to completed, but did not prevent recurrence.', 'A CR was planned to handle multiple D21F files for the same C# number, and duplicate recycle order checks were added to daily AMS monitoring across FDP production environments.', 'The proposed logic change prevents subsequent processing from creating another recycle fee order when one already exists for the chassis order and dealer code; handling of D21F updates such as amount changes was queried but not answered.']
Root Cause: The recycle fee order creation logic was not idempotent: it created a new recycle fee order each time D21F data was processed for the same chassis order instead of identifying and updating the existing order.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4498
Timestamp: 2026-05-19T06:56:00
Author: Soham Modi
Comment: Dear Tsunoda-san,
Thank you for your support.
Issue:
Previously, when the D21F file was processed multiple times for the same dealer, duplicate recycle fee orders were created for the same chassis order. The number of recycle fee orders generated matched the number of times the file was processed, resulting in duplicate recycle orders.
Fix Implemented:
We have updated the recycle fee order creation logic and with this enhancement, once a recycle fee order is created for a chassis order under a specific dealer code, subsequent processing of the same D21F file will no longer generate duplicate recycle fee orders.
Result:
Only one recycle fee order will be created for each chassis order, ensuring that duplicate recycle fee orders are no longer generated.
We kindly request your approval for the Fix plan.
Please let us know if any additional information is required from our side.
Best Regards,
Soham Modi

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4487
Investigation Summary: Bulk Invoice Data and Journal Voucher data were reviewed for the provided Job Cards. The existing Siebel functionality was confirmed to operate according to the initial requirement: Bulk Invoice data was sent based on the Job Card Bill to Basic Account Code closing date, and the orders were linked to KB through Bulk Invoice only once. The requested change to Journal Voucher creation and Bulk Invoice/real-time behavior will be handled through CR MFTBCFFR-4039; the incident was dismissed.
Important Findings: ['JV Account was set as described in the Jira for the reviewed Job Card.', 'Bulk Invoice data was sent according to the closing date of the Bill to Basic Account Code in the Job Card.', 'The reviewed orders were linked to KB through Bulk Invoice only once.', 'Siebel was functioning normally under the initial requirement.', 'Changes to Bulk Invoice, real-time functionality, and Journal Voucher creation are being developed under CR MFTBCFFR-4039.']
Root Cause: No product defect was identified; the reported behavior required a change to the Journal Voucher creation method and related Bulk Invoice/real-time functionality beyond the initial requirement.
Resolution: Dismissed the incident and routed the requested functional changes to CR MFTBCFFR-4039.
Technical Entities: ['Bulk Invoice Data', 'Journal Voucher', 'JV Account', 'Job Card', 'Bill to Basic Account Code', 'KB', 'Siebel', 'Bulk Invoice', 'real time functionality', 'MFTBCFFR-4039']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4461
Investigation Summary: The incident was recovered in Wakayama-PROD. Investigation determined that D21F files could arrive before the corresponding D21A file creates the Chassis Order, due to a TOB-side file sequencing issue. Siebel cannot be modified to prevent this; the permanent correction must be implemented on the TOB side, while FDP records and TOB files are monitored and recovered as needed.
Important Findings: ['Monitoring began on 11th July, but the affected record was created in June and was therefore not captured initially.', 'The issue is caused by TOB-side file sequencing: D21F is received before D21A creates the Chassis Order.', 'This is not a Siebel-side issue; a Siebel-side fix is not possible.', 'D21F files are monitored across FDP environments, and affected files are re-run after the required Chassis Order is created on the TOB side.', 'The incident is similar to SC Incident INC5105271 and MFTBCFFR-3546; future updates are tracked in MFTBCFFR-3546.']
Root Cause: TOB-side file sequencing issue in which D21F files are received before the corresponding D21A file creates the Chassis Order.
Resolution: Recovery was completed in Wakayama-PROD. Ongoing monitoring and recovery are performed on the Siebel side; a permanent fix is pending implementation by the TOB side.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4456
Investigation Summary: Button enablement in FDP used an RF status condition even though RF Status is not available in FDP, causing incorrect button behavior. The implementation was revised to control Send Recycle Fee, Modify/Change Order, and CUT/Cancel Order behavior using TOB and Recycle Fee Order statuses, including a one-day rule based on receipt of a successful TOB response. The final changes were tested in UAT1, approved for production, and released in the 23 October 2025 scheduled FDP release.
Important Findings: ['The original button logic depended on RF STATUS = Null, but RF Status is not used in FDP.', 'The requested behavior was to make the Request for modification and CUT buttons unavailable from the day after a successful TOB response when the recycle order status is Completed or Recycle Order Changed.', 'The One Day Window requirement was corrected: CUT and Modify buttons must be enabled for the full day on which a successful TOB response is received, not the day the TOB request is sent.', 'For UAT1 verification, a TOB response was simulated for Chassis Order # B001217339 and Recycle Fee Order # B001217574; the record Last Modified date was used to identify the successful-response date.', 'The implementation also needed to preserve Send Recycle Fee availability after CUT success or a modification TOB error, rather than relying only on TOB response date and TOB status.', 'The incident was released to Production in the 23 October 2025 scheduled FDP release.']
Root Cause: Legacy RF STATUS-based button-enable conditions were retained although RF Status is not available in FDP, resulting in incorrect enablement control for the TOB-related buttons.
Resolution: Reworked the FDP button-control logic to use TOB Status and Recycle Fee Order Status, with CUT and Modify enabled only on the date a successful TOB response is received; the finalized changes were released to Production on 23 October 2025.
Technical Entities: ['FDP', 'UAT1', 'Production', 'Prod', 'TOB', 'RF Status', 'RF STATUS', 'TOB Status', 'Recycle Fee Order Status', 'Recycle Fee Order', 'Send Recycle Fee', 'Confirmation Report - Send Recycle Fee Button', 'Request for modification', 'Modify', 'Modify Order Button', 'Change Order', 'CUT', 'Cancel Order', 'One Day Window', 'Submitted to TOB', 'TOB Success', 'TOB Error', 'Completed', 'Recycle Order Changed', 'Recycle Change In Progress', 'Recycle Cancel Pending', 'Pending', 'Cancelled', 'Chassis Order # B001217339', 'Recycle Fee Order # B001217574', '23rd October scheduled FDP release']

[TOB status where button is disabled]
 
Submitted to TOB

Completed

Modification completed (Recycle Order Changed)
CUT in progress (Recycle Cancel Pending)

Creating (Pending)
Cancelled

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4446
Investigation Summary: The affected record was recovered, but the incident was traced to an earlier incorrect recovery of Recycle Order# : B000363504 mapped to the Sales Order. Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4424
Investigation Summary: The issue was replicated in the UAT1 environment for Sales Quote 1-6FHJ0C and Opportunity 1-6FHIYB. Investigation found that the Model Code had been manually removed from the Vehicle, preventing line-item creation in the UV Quote. The incident was classified as user misoperation rather than a system issue; the user was instructed to correct and re-map the Vehicle before recreating the Quote.
Important Findings: ['The issue was reproduced in the UAT1 environment.', 'Sales Quote 1-6FHJ0C and Opportunity 1-6FHIYB were used for investigation.', 'The Model Code was manually removed from the Vehicle.', 'Without a Model Code on the Vehicle, line items were not created in the UV Quote.', 'The corrective process is to delete the Vehicle from the UV Opportunity, add the appropriate Model Code, re-map the Vehicle, and create the Quote again.', 'The incident was determined to be user misoperation, not a system issue.']
Root Cause: The Model Code was manually removed from the Vehicle, causing UV Quote line items not to be created.
Resolution: Delete the Vehicle from the UV Opportunity, add the appropriate Model Code to the Vehicle, re-map the Vehicle to the UV Opportunity, and create the Quote from the Opportunity again.
Technical Entities: ['UAT1', 'Sales Quote', '1-6FHJ0C', 'Opportunity', '1-6FHIYB', 'Model Code', 'Vehicle', 'UV Quote', 'UV Opportunity']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4408
Investigation Summary: A record was reported as visible in Siebel but missing from PBI Reports; sample order Q050163081 was provided. Investigation found that the editable Request# field in the Siebel UI had been populated with an Opportunity# instead of the Insurance Quote request number. Recovery was completed, and the Request# is now displayed in the FDPC Report.
Important Findings: ['Sample affected order: Q050163081.', 'The Request# field in the Siebel UI is editable.', 'Users can mistakenly enter an Opportunity# in the Request number field of an Insurance Quote.', 'The issue also occurs on SC.', 'After recovery, the Request# was displayed in the FDPC Report.']
Root Cause: User misoperation: an Opportunity# was entered in the editable Request# field of an Insurance Quote instead of the correct request number.
Resolution: Completed recovery of the affected record; the Request# is now displayed in the FDPC Report.
Technical Entities: ['Q050163081', 'Siebel', 'PBI Reports', 'Request#', 'Opportunity#', 'Insurance Quote', 'SC', 'FDPC Report']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4383
Investigation Summary: Zero-amount Journal Vouchers (JVs) were created because JV-creation filters did not consistently evaluate the same Base Amount fields used by the JV. In Okinawa prod, the fix from MFTBCFFR-3779 was ineffective for two Journal Event types because of an extra space in the deployed filter. The Okinawa fix was released on July 24, 2025, and the corrected filters for the remaining Journal Event types were validated in UAT/UAT1 and released to FDP Production on August 27, 2025.
Important Findings: ['Zero-amount JVs were found in FDP prod for multiple Journal Event types where the filter field differed from the JV Base Amount field.', 'The JV-creation filter is intended to prevent JV creation when Base Amount equals zero.', 'For Okinawa prod, the MFTBCFFR-3779 fix for "Service Correction Sales Amount Non-Taxable" and "Service Correction Sales Amount Red Slip Non-Taxable" failed because of an extra space in the deployed filter.', 'The corrective logic uses the same fields as "Credit Base Amount" and "Debit Base Amount" and applies a "Base amount not equal to zero" condition.', 'The fix was validated in UAT1, where zero-amount JVs were no longer created.']
Root Cause: Incorrect JV-creation filter configuration: filters used fields different from the JV Base Amount fields; additionally, an extra space in the deployed filter prevented the prior MFTBCFFR-3779 fix from working in Okinawa prod.
Resolution: Released a corrected "Base amount not equal to zero" filter using the same fields as "Credit Base Amount" and "Debit Base Amount". The Okinawa prod correction was released on July 24, 2025, and changes for the remaining Journal Event types were released to FDP Production on August 27, 2025.
Technical Entities: ['MFTBCFFR-4383', 'MFTBCFFR-3779', 'Journal Voucher', 'JV', 'Base Amount', 'Credit Base Amount', 'Debit Base Amount', 'Service Correction Sales Amount Non-Taxable', 'Service Correction Sales Amount Red Slip Non-Taxable', 'Service Purchase CT', 'Re-Edit Red Slip Job Card Sales Amount Non-Taxable', 'Job Card Sales Amount Taxable', 'ConsTax PO - UV Body Building Order', 'ConsTax PO - Body Building Order - Non IBOS', 'FDP prod', 'FDP Production', 'Okinawa prod', 'Okinawa production environment', 'UAT1', 'UAT', 'KB side']

*"*

This filter is used at the time of JV creation on "Base Amount" field of journal voucher where we check if value of this field is not equal to zero, if it is zero JV will not be created. In earlier release, we fixed this issue for the case issue that was reported.
The problem is not occurring for other Journal Event types above, and zero amount JV was not reported for all other cases that we have mentioned for that specific case after the 12th June release. 
Since we have found some cases for this issue again we checked all JVs where this issue has occurred in recent times, we will fix it for all the cases where filter is incorrect, we will use base amount field logic which will prevent this issue.
We will provide you the data you asked by today end of day.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4361
Investigation Summary: The incident concerned differing workshop and department values across JC, JCO, and JV. Investigation confirmed that the values followed existing logic based on the branch code of the user who created the Job Card and the user who customer-approved the quote. The case was classified as a rare Operation Miss; no system changes or recovery were performed, and the incident was closed.
Important Findings: ['Workshop Code in JC reflects the Branch Code of the user who created the Job Card; it was 23 in this case.', 'JCO Workshop Name reflects the Branch Code of the user who Customer Approved the Quote; it was 21 in this case.', 'JV Department Code (CSJS200) and Department Code (CSJS300) come from the JCO Site, which was 21.', 'JVs had already been sent to KB.', 'The observed behavior was confirmed as current logic rather than a defect requiring a change.', 'The case was considered a rare Operation Miss, so no changes were made.']
Root Cause: A rare Operation Miss caused different branch-derived values to be used: JC used the Job Card creator's Branch Code (23), while JCO and JV used the Customer Approved Quote user's/JCO Site Branch Code (21).
Resolution: No corrective system change was made. The incident was closed after confirming the existing logic and classifying the case as a rare Operation Miss.
Technical Entities: ['JC', 'Workshop Code', 'Branch Code', 'Job Card', 'JCO', 'JCO Workshop Name', 'Customer Approved the Quote', 'JV', 'Department Code (CSJS200)', 'Department Code (CSJS300)', 'JCO Site', 'KB', 'Operation Miss']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4353
Investigation Summary: A Service Request could not be completed because of invalid data in the Service Request Details. The issue was traced to user mis-operation when entering fields in Tasks before creating the Service Request. Support rejected the affected Service Request and instructed the user to create it again; the recreated request completed successfully and Account Receivable was created.
Important Findings: ['A data issue in Service Request Details prevented the Service Request from reaching Completed status.', 'The invalid data originated from user mis-operation while entering fields in Tasks before creating the Service Request.', 'The affected Service Request was rejected rather than corrected in place.', 'Creating the Service Request again completed successfully.', 'Account Receivable was created after the Service Request was recreated.']
Root Cause: User mis-operation when entering fields in Tasks before creating the Service Request, resulting in invalid Service Request Details data that prevented completion.
Resolution: Rejected the affected Service Request and had the user create it again; the new Service Request completed successfully and created Account Receivable.
Technical Entities: ['Service Request Details', 'Service Request', 'Tasks', 'Account Receivable']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4341
Investigation Summary: The incident concerned Entity Transfer behavior for Sales Rep transfers, particularly transfers within special sales. Multiple UAT issues were identified, including unavailable target users due to organization and position configuration, duplicate Position Id values, and incorrect user filtering. The final implementation restricts Sales Rep Transfer to users in the same Organization and with the same Position type as the Primary Sales Rep's Position, and was deployed to Production in the 25 September FDP release.
Important Findings: ['Entity Transfer initially displayed only configured position types; requested additional position types were added to the Entity Transfer logic on UAT1.', 'A transfer between D0X20852 and D0X20851 was blocked because their primary organizations differed: D0X20852 was in Default Organization, 000000000O, while D0X20851 was in Okayama East Branch, 10.', 'A transfer did not reflect because both users had the same Position Id; the Position Id issue was corrected.', "Person selection was unavailable for one Sales Order because no user was assigned to the current Sales Rep's position; the position was assigned to users.", "The final Entity Transfer rule allows Sales Rep Transfer only to users in the same Organization and with the same Position type as the Primary Sales Rep's Position.", 'The self-approval validation was separately identified as introduced to FDP through CR-0836 and was removed from NV Quote on UAT1 for testing.']
Root Cause: Entity Transfer user-selection and transfer behavior did not meet the required special-sales transfer criteria; additional issues were caused by different user organizations, duplicate Position Id values, and missing user assignments for the current Sales Rep position.
Resolution: Updated Entity Transfer to allow Sales Rep Transfer only among users in the same Organization and with the same Position type as the Primary Sales Rep's Position; corrected duplicate Position Id configuration and assigned missing positions to users. The changes were deployed to Production in the 25 September FDP release.
Technical Entities: ['Entity Transfer', 'Entity Transfer screen', 'Transfer button', 'pick applet', 'FDP', 'FDP prod', 'FDP-UAT1', 'UAT1', 'Production', 'FDP release', 'Sales Rep', 'Primary Sales Rep', 'Primary Position', 'Primary Organisation', 'Position Id', 'Sales Order A001297018', 'D8AKITYO', 'D0X20851', 'D0X20852', 'D0X20843', 'D0X20838', 'D0X20839', 'D0X20836', 'D0X20892', 'D0X20840', 'D0X20855', 'Default Organization, 000000000O', 'Okayama East Branch, 10', 'HQ-TAJ-Fleet-SnrMgr', 'Bus-Staff', 'SCHQ-Sales-UV-Staff', 'Branch-CS-Head', 'HQ-TAJ-Fleet-Staff', 'Bus-Area-Mgr', 'HQ-TAJ-Fleet-Mgr', 'Branch-Sales-Mgr', 'SCHQ-Sales-UV-Mgr', 'SCHQ-Sales-Vehicle-Staff', 'Branch-Sales-Staff', 'Branch-Head', 'Branch-Assistant-Staff', 'SCHQ-Sales-NV-Mgr', 'Branch NV/UV Sales Staff', 'SCHQ-BizMgmt-Staff', 'NV Quote', 'CR-0836', 'self-approval check']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4335
Investigation Summary: Bulk invoice data was not sent on 30 June because the existing logic determines the send schedule from the closing date of the original account identified by "Ship to Basic Account Code" in Change Order. The relevant account had a closing date of 20, so the data was scheduled for 20 July rather than 30 June. The behavior was confirmed as consistent with the current logic, and a change is being addressed through project CR MFTBCFFR-4402.
Important Findings: ['Recovery was completed and the data was linked to KB again.', 'Bulk invoice data is fetched using "Ship to Basic Account Code" in Change Order, which represents the original Account.', 'The closing date used for bulk invoice processing is taken from the account identified by "Ship to Basic Account Code".', 'The original Account closing date was 20; therefore, data was expected to be sent on 20 July, not 30 June.', 'Current logic does not fetch bulk invoice data using the closing date of "Bill to basic Account Code".', 'A logic change is being tracked under project CR MFTBCFFR-4402.']
Root Cause: The bulk invoice workflow uses the closing date of the original Account identified by "Ship to Basic Account Code" in Change Order, rather than the closing date of "Bill to basic Account Code". Because that account's closing date was 20, the data was not scheduled to send on 30 June.
Resolution: Recovered the incident data by linking it to KB again. The required logic change is being handled through project CR MFTBCFFR-4402.
Technical Entities: ['KB', 'bulk invoice data', 'Change Order', 'Ship to Basic Account Code', 'Bill to basic Account Code', 'Account', 'MDIS', 'MFTBCFFR-4402']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4326
Investigation Summary: Users could manually change a UV Purchase Quote status from "Approved" to "Order Intake" through the "My Branch" view, but could not change it back to "Approved", blocking the business process. Recovery was completed for the affected record. The Status field was made read-only in UAT and then deployed to Production in the July 24 regular FDP release.
Important Findings: ['UV Purchase Quote status could be manually updated from the "My Branch" view.', 'A status change from "Approved" to "Order Intake" was permitted, while reverting from "Order Intake" to "Approved" was not possible.', 'The one-way status transition blocked the business process.', 'Recovery for the affected record was completed.', 'The selected fix was to make the Purchase Quote Status field read-only.', 'The fix was implemented in UAT and released to Production on July 24.']
Root Cause: The UV Purchase Quote Status field was manually editable from the "My Branch" view, allowing an "Approved" to "Order Intake" transition that could not be reversed.
Resolution: Made the Purchase Quote Status field read-only, validated the change in UAT, and deployed it to Production in the July 24 FDP regular release.
Technical Entities: ['UV Quotes', 'UV Purchase Quote', 'Purchase Quote', 'Status Field', 'Approved', 'Order Intake', 'My Branch', 'FDP UAT1', 'UAT environment', 'Prod environment', 'Production environment', 'FDP']

Timestamp: 2025-07-08T18:00:00
Comment: Thank you very much for your continued support.
 
We have conducted a detailed investigation into this matter and will report the findings as follows.
 
■Survey results
 In UV quotation, it is possible to change the status from "Approved" to "Order Intake", but once it becomes "Order Intake", it is not possible to change it back to "Approved" again.
 This behavior is a hindrance to business processes.
 
■Revision proposal
 As a response to this issue, we are considering a fix that would restrict status changes using one of the following methods.
 
Make status changes globally read-only in UV estimates
 
Restrict only status changes from "Approved" to "Order Intake"
 
We would appreciate it if you could confirm and instruct us which amendment should be applied.

 Recovery for the corresponding record has been completed.
 
Please check the revision policy and let us know if you have any questions or additional requests.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4313
Investigation Summary: A Model Price update file received from TOB on the shared part was picked up by the Okinawa production ODI package, causing incorrect price updates for 13,329 Model Code records in PROD. Root Cause: A Model Price update file received from TOB on the shared part was picked by the Okinawa production ODI package, resulting in incorrect price updates for 13,329 Model Code records.
Resolution: Prepared corrected and recovery data, then recovered the affected model-price records, Quotes, and Sales Orders on PROD; all recovery processes were confirmed complete.

Root Cause: Insurance Order Q036607132 was missed during data patching for MFTBCFFR-4125 because its JV had already been created on 7th February 2025 and was therefore not included in the patch.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4293
Investigation Summary: A recovery JV was created with a blank Client Code because the Vendor Finance Code was blank in the Body Building Order. The affected JV was recovered using branch code 7000 and was scheduled to link to KB in the nightly daily batch. The issue could not be reproduced in UAT, and monitoring of FDP production environment through July 31 found no further JVs with null Client Code.
Important Findings: ['The Vendor Finance Code was blank in the Body Building Order, resulting in a blank Client Code in the JV.', 'The affected JV recovery was completed using branch code 7000 and was to be linked to KB in the nightly daily batch.', 'The issue could not be replicated in UAT despite checking all logic scenarios.', 'Daily monitoring of FDP production environment found no additional JVs with null Client Code through July 31.', 'The incident was treated as a one-time occurrence and closed after the monitoring period.']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4275
Investigation Summary: Duplicate Journal Vouchers were created for Body Building Orders in FDP Production, including Chugoku prod. Investigation found that the validation introduced under MFTBCFFR-3809 checked only for an existing Completed JV trigger, allowing a second trigger while the original trigger was still in progress. The validation was updated and tested in UAT1, then released to FDP Production on 27th August.
Important Findings: ['Affected duplicate Journal Vouchers were recovered using reverse Journal Vouchers and linked to KB through the daily batch.', 'The MFTBCFFR-3809 validation prevented new JV triggers only when a Completed trigger existed for the Body Building Order.', 'A duplicate Journal Voucher was created two minutes after the original because the original JV trigger had not yet reached Completed status.', 'The corrected validation prevents creation of another JV trigger when any trigger exists for the original Journal Voucher, regardless of status.', 'UAT testing confirmed that multiple Shipment Details responses from IBOS send the Journal Voucher trigger only once.', 'The fix was deployed to FDP Production in the 27th August planned release.']
Root Cause: The validation check added by MFTBCFFR-3809 searched only for existing Completed JV triggers. When another trigger was received before the original trigger completed, the validation did not detect the in-progress trigger and created a duplicate Journal Voucher.
Resolution: Updated the JV-trigger validation to block creation of a new trigger when any trigger exists for the original Journal Voucher, regardless of trigger status. The fix was implemented in UAT1 and released to FDP Production on 27th August.
Technical Entities: ['MFTBCFFR-4275', 'MFTBCFFR-3809', 'Journal Voucher', 'JV trigger', 'Reverse Journal Voucher', 'Body Building Order', 'bodywork order', 'Chugoku prod', 'FDP China (Chugoku) production environment', 'FDP Production', 'UAT', 'UAT1', 'IBOS', 'IBOS response', 'Shipment Details response', 'KB', 'daily batch', 'Journal Event Type', 'PO - Body building Order IBOS', 'Completed trigger', 'Search Specification', 'Generate Approvals', 'Request Approval', 'Acceptance Verification Done', 'Shipped', 'B033646702', 'B034169101']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4275
Timestamp: 2025-07-15T05:37:00
Author: Divyesh Ghiya
Comment: Thank you for your support.
We have analyzed this incident and below are our findings:
 For the fix of MFTBCFFR-3809 Incident, we added a Validation check where if Journal Voucher of the Body Building Order already exist then no additional trigger of Journal Voucher will be created. But in this check, condition used to search for existing Journal Voucher needs to be improved. 
 Currently, our Validation checks that if a Completed Trigger exist for that Body Building Order, but we need to update the condition to: if a trigger with any status exist then we will not create another JV trigger. 
 Duplicated Journal Voucher was created after 2 minutes of original Journal Voucher, our validation checked for Completed trigger but since original trigger was not completed at that time, another duplicate trigger was sent. We need to update our check so that if any trigger exist for Original Journal Voucher than no duplicate Journal Voucher will be created. 
This will resolve duplicate Journal Voucher issue.
Kindly check and approve our fix plan.
Please let us know if you have any query or need any additional detail.
Regards,
 Divyesh Ghiya

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4275
Timestamp: 2025-07-15T06:07:00
Comment: Thank you very much for your continued support.
As a result of analyzing this incident, we would like to report the following.
 
MFTBCFFR-3809 To correct the incident, a validation check has been added to prevent creating a new journal entry trigger if a journal entry slip already exists for a bodywork order.
However, it was found that there was room for improvement in the conditions for searching existing journal entry vouchers.
 
In the current validation, we only check whether a "Completed" trigger exists, but in the future, we will need to change the condition to not create a new journal entry trigger if any trigger exists, regardless of the status.
 
This time, the duplicate journal entry voucher was created two minutes after the original journal entry voucher. Validation only checked for "completed" triggers, which resulted in another trigger being sent before the original one had completed yet.
 
Therefore, in the future, we will correct the validation so that duplicate journal vouchers are not created "even if any trigger exists for the original journal voucher."
 
This correction is expected to resolve the issue of duplicate journal entry vouchers.
 
Please review and approve the proposed amendment.
If you have any questions or need additional information, please let us know.
 
Thank you for your support.

Root Cause: No user with position SCHQ-BizMgmt-SnrMgr was configured in branch 02 of Wakayama Prod Employee Master for Cycle Count ID 1-27LEMV, resulting in a blank approver.
Resolution: Recovered Cycle Count ID 1-27LEMV and completed its associated cycle count batch job. No system or code fix was required; an SR is needed to add the required position to branch 02 if needed.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4262
Investigation Summary: Duplicate recycle fee orders were created during manual recovery for Jira ticket MFTBCFFR-4173. The recovery was confirmed after the duplicate recycle fee order was removed and the correct Purchase Orders displayed in the Sales order. The incident was caused by inadvertently executing the batch scheduled for D21F during the manual recovery; an additional backend-data verification step was added to the recovery process.
Important Findings: ['A recycle fee order for the respective chassis order was missing and was manually recovered.', 'The batch scheduled for D21F was inadvertently executed during recovery, creating two recycle fee orders.', 'The chassis order screen displayed only one recycle fee order and did not reveal the duplicate backend entry.', 'The duplicated recycle fee order was removed, and correct Purchase Orders were displayed in the Sales order.', 'Recovery procedures now require backend-data verification before completion.']
Root Cause: Manual error during recovery for Jira ticket MFTBCFFR-4173: the batch scheduled for D21F was inadvertently executed while manually recovering a missing recycle fee order, resulting in duplicate recycle fee orders.
Resolution: Removed the duplicated recycle fee order and added a backend-data verification step to the recovery process to detect duplicate entries before completion.
Technical Entities: ['MFTBCFFR-4173', 'recycle fee order', 'chassis order', 'D21F', 'Purchase Orders', 'Sales order', 'chassis order screen', 'backend']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4262
Timestamp: 2025-06-30T07:37:00
Author: Ujjwal Goel
Comment: Dear Tsunoda-san,
Apologies for the inconvenience caused.
This issue occurred due to a manual error during the recovery process for Jira ticket MFTBCFFR-4173. In this case, the recycle fee order for the respective chassis order was missing, so we recovered it manually. However, during this recovery, the batch scheduled for D21F was also inadvertently executed, which resulted in two recycle fee orders being created.
For verification, we checked from the chassis order screen, where only one recycle fee order is visible. However, this did not reflect the duplicate entry created in the background.
To prevent such issues in the future, we have now included an additional verification step that involves checking the data from the backend as well before completing any recovery process.
Thank you for your understanding, and please let us know if you have any questions.
Best regards,
Ujjwal Goel

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4243
Investigation Summary: The user could not delete the UV Trade-In Assessment after manually changing the UV Trade-In Flag in the UV Quote Header from "Y" to "N" in Revision 4. Unchecking the flag made related Trade-In fields read-only, preventing required backend updates during assessment deletion. The issue was classified as user misoperation rather than a system defect; the flag must be rechecked to "Y" before deleting the assessment.
Important Findings: ['The UV Trade-In Flag was "Y" in Revision 2 and Revision 3, then manually changed to "N" in Revision 4.', 'When the UV Trade-In Flag is unchecked in the UV Quote Header, related Trade-In fields become read-only.', 'Read-only Trade-In fields prevent backend field updates required to delete the UV Trade-In Assessment.', 'The required sequence is to delete the UV Trade-In Assessment first and then uncheck the UV Trade-In Flag.', 'The incident was determined to be user misoperation, not a system defect.']
Root Cause: The user unchecked the UV Trade-In Flag before deleting the UV Trade-In Assessment, causing related Trade-In fields to become read-only and blocking the backend updates needed for deletion.
Resolution: Recheck the UV Trade-In Flag to "Y", delete the UV Trade-In Assessment, and only then uncheck the flag if required.
Technical Entities: ['UV Trade-In Flag', 'UV Quote Header', 'UV Trade-In Assessment', 'Revision 2', 'Revision 3', 'Revision 4', 'Jira Status']

Timestamp: 2025-06-24T10:21:00
Author: Divyesh Ghiya
Comment: Thank you for your support. 
 
 We have thoroughly investigated and below are our findings:
 
 *User Steps:*
 * In Revision 2 and Revision 3, the UV Trade-In Flag in UV Quote Header was selected as “Y”.
 * However, in Revision 4, the user manually unchecked the flag, changing it to “N”.
If a user intends to delete the UV Trade-In Assessment, the correct process is to delete the assessment record first and then uncheck the UV Trade-In flag.
*RCA:*
When the UV Trade-In flag is unchecked in the UV Quote header, the related Trade-In fields become read-only. This prevents deletion, as certain backend field updates required during deletion cannot occur in this state.
Recovery Plan:
No recovery action is required. The user can resolve the issue by rechecking the UV Trade-In flag to “Y”. This will allow deletion of the UV Trade-In Assessment as needed.
 
*Conclusion:*
This is a case of user mis operation, not a system defect. Hence, kindly allow us to reject this incident.
Please advise the user to follow the steps outlined above. Please let us know if you have any query or need any additional support.
 
 Regards,
 Divyesh Ghiya

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4241
Investigation Summary: For quotation 1-DOS1L, MC 6 Model Code was unavailable in the catalogue when the body type was Cabover. Cabover could incorrectly persist when the product class was changed from a truck class to LB, despite LB allowing only Other. A fix was implemented to refresh body type options when changing the product class to LB, preventing Cabover from remaining selected; it was validated in UAT and released to Prod on 10th July 2025.
Important Findings: ['MC 6 Model Code is not displayed in the catalogue when the body type is set to Cabover.', 'Changing the body type to Other makes the MC 6 Model Code available.', 'Cabover could be retained for LB by selecting a truck class, setting body type to Cab Over, saving, and then changing the truck class to LB.', 'The fix automatically refreshes body type options when the product class is changed to LB, so Cabover is no longer available for LB.', 'The fix was applied to UAT before release to Prod on 10th July 2025.']
Root Cause: The system did not refresh body type options when the product class was changed to LB, allowing the invalid Cabover body type to persist for LB.
Resolution: Implemented a functionality fix to automatically refresh body type options when changing the product class to LB, preventing Cabover from being available or retained; deployed to UAT and released to Prod on 10th July 2025.
Technical Entities: ['1-DOS1L', 'MC 6 Model Code', 'catalogue', 'Cabover', 'Other', 'LB', 'Opportunity', 'product class', 'body type', 'UAT', 'Prod']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4232
Investigation Summary: Users could add an Option line item through the Parts and Internal Work Applet in a UV quote by entering it in Part#. Options were not displayed in the Parts and Internal Work screen, preventing users from deleting them; saving produced an error while adding the record. A validation restricting permitted product types was implemented in the FDP UAT Environment and released to Prod on 10 July 2025.
Important Findings: ['The Parts and Internal Work Applet allowed an Option to be entered in Part# and saved as a line item.', 'The Parts and Internal Work screen displayed only Parts, so Option line items were not visible and could not be deleted by users.', 'Saving the affected record displayed an error but still added the record; a UAT1 reference was 1-19MOBS.', 'Production recovery was completed before the permanent fix was deployed.', 'The fix restricts the Parts and Internal Work Applet to Parts, Labor, Accessories, and Lubricant product types.']
Root Cause: The Parts and Internal Work Applet lacked validation to prevent unsupported product types, allowing Option line items to be added even though the related screen displayed only Parts.
Resolution: Implemented validation in the Parts and Internal Work Applet to allow only Parts, Labor, Accessories, and Lubricant. The fix was deployed to the FDP UAT Environment on 27 June 2025 and released to Prod on 10 July 2025.
Technical Entities: ['Parts and Internal Work Applet', 'Parts and Internal Work screen', 'UV quote', 'Part#', 'Option', 'Parts', 'Labor', 'Accessories', 'Lubricant', 'UAT1', '1-19MOBS', 'Production', 'Prod', 'FDP UAT Environment', 'FDP Release']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4226
Investigation Summary: Duplicate journal entries (JVs) were identified as the same issue addressed in MFTBCFFR-4187. JVs for Segment2 Codes MS06GP-15099 and MS06GP-150100 were re-created on May 7, 2025 because manually added data under MFTBCFFR-3743 did not have its Sent Flag updated. Reverse JV recovery was completed after validation and approval for production.
Important Findings: ['Duplicate JVs other than MS06GP-15099 and MS06GP-150100 already had reverse JVs created on June 13, 2025 through MFTBCFFR-4187.', 'The JVs with Segment2 Codes MS06GP-15099 and MS06GP-150100 originated from manually added data in MFTBCFFR-3743.', 'The Sent Flag was not updated for the manually added data, causing the JVs to be created again on May 7, 2025.', 'Reverse JV data for MS06GP-15099 and MS06GP-150100 was validated and approved for production.', 'The TOB/D2S Invoice Recovery SOP was updated to prevent recurrence.']
Root Cause: The Sent Flag was not updated for manually added data created under MFTBCFFR-3743, causing duplicate JVs to be re-created.
Resolution: Created, validated, approved for production, and completed reverse-JV recovery for Segment2 Codes MS06GP-15099 and MS06GP-150100; updated the TOB/D2S Invoice Recovery SOP.
Technical Entities: ['MFTBCFFR-4226', 'MFTBCFFR-4187', 'MFTBCFFR-3743', 'MFTBCFFR-3723', 'JV', 'reverse JV', 'Segment2 Code', 'MS06GP-15099', 'MS06GP-150100', 'Sent Flag', 'TOB/D2S Invoice Recovery SOP', 'Service Request (SR)', 'prod']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4212
Investigation Summary: The incident concerned three tax amounts finalized through the Tax Finalize button not being reflected in the Sales Order Tax and Expenses amounts. Investigation established that Tax Finalize did not trigger tax-amount synchronization; synchronization occurred only when the "Actual amount including Tax" field was manually changed. A change was implemented and tested in UAT/UAT-1 to synchronize taxation line-item prices on tax finalization, then released to Prod.
Important Findings: ['The issue was not caused by Quote revision or Registration Request creation timing; the reported issue was Sales Order values not updating after tax confirmation.', 'Three tax amounts are finalized by clicking the Tax Finalize button.', 'Before the fix, clicking Tax Finalize performed validations and froze values but did not synchronize the Tax Amount to the Sales Order.', 'Tax Amount synchronized only when the "Actual amount including Tax" field was manually changed.', 'A UAT test identified that after a Quote revision changed the three tax amounts, clicking Tax Finalize did not update the Sales Order Tax and Expenses amount.', 'The synchronization change was tested successfully in UAT-1 and released to Prod.']
Root Cause: The Tax Finalize button did not trigger synchronization of finalized Tax Amount values to the Sales Order; synchronization was only triggered by manual changes to the "Actual amount including Tax" field.
Resolution: Implemented synchronization so the taxation line-item price/finalized Tax Amount is synchronized to the Sales Order/Registration Request when Tax Finalize is performed. The change was tested in UAT/UAT-1 and released to Prod.
Technical Entities: ['Tax Finalize button', 'Tax Amount', 'Actual amount including Tax', 'Sales Order', 'Tax and Expenses', 'Registration Request', 'Quote', 'Quote sync process', 'Taxation line item', 'Expenses & Recycle Fee', 'UAT', 'UAT-1', 'UAT5', 'UAT7', 'Wakayama Production', 'Prod', 'Quote 1-8OC74', 'A000033644', 'A000033319', 'A000033944', 'A000033946', 'A001282514']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4212
Timestamp: 2025-06-18T07:00:00
Author: Ujjwal Goel
Comment: Dear Tsunoda-san,
 
Thank you very much for your continued support.
 
Regarding the issue raised, we have identified it as a case of user mis-operation. In Revision 1 of Quote 1-8OC74, the line item for automobile tax (classification) was listed with a tax value of ¥8,600. At that stage, only the Sales Order and Invoice were created based on this revision.
 
Subsequently, in Revision 2 of the quote, the user updated the tax value for the same line item to ¥9,700. However, the Registration Request was created after this revision and derived its values from the existing invoice, which was originally generated based on Revision 1. As a result, the tax value reflected in the Registration Request remains ¥8,600.
 
To correct this, the appropriate action would have been for the user to generate a new invoice(has to cancel the existing invoice) after updating the tax value in Revision 2 of the quote.
 
Please let us know if any further clarification is needed.
 
Best regards,
Ujjwal Goel

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4212
Timestamp: 2025-06-18T07:15:00
Comment: Mr. Tsunoda,
 
Thank you very much for your continued support.
 
We would like to inform you that we have determined that the issue you pointed out was caused by user operation.
 
In revision 1 of quotation number "1-8OC74", the tax amount of the item "Automobile tax (classification)" is stated as ¥8,600, and a sales order and invoice were created based on this revision.
 
Later, in revision 2 of the quote, the tax amount on the same line was updated to ¥9,700. However, although the Registration Request was created after this revision, the tax amount on the Registration Request is still ¥8,600 because it references the amount from the original invoice (based on revision 1).
 
In such a case, you would have needed to update the estimated tax amount to revision 2, cancel the existing invoice, and reissue a new invoice.
 
If you have any questions, please feel free to let us know.
 
Thank you for your support.
Himanshu

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4211
Investigation Summary: Parts were not being updated in the Siebel system from Ascent for Wave-3 Environments. Investigation found that Ascent users for Iwate, Shikoku, Okinawa, and Wakayama had expired. The users were restored and configured to never expire; other FDP users were confirmed to already be in a never-expiry state.
Important Findings: ['Expired Ascent users prevented parts from being updated to the Siebel system.', 'Affected Wave-3 Environments were Iwate, Shikoku, Okinawa, and Wakayama.', 'Users for the affected environments were restored and marked as never expired.', 'Users for other FDPs—Okayama, Aomori, Hakodate, and Chugoku—were already configured as never-expiry users.']
Root Cause: Ascent users for Wave-3 Environments (Iwate, Shikoku, Okinawa, Wakayama) had expired, blocking part updates from Ascent to the Siebel system.
Resolution: Restored the expired Ascent users for the affected Wave-3 Environments and configured them as never-expired users.
Technical Entities: ['Ascent', 'Siebel system', 'Wave-3 Environments', 'Iwate', 'Shikoku', 'Okinawa', 'Wakayama', 'FDPs', 'Okayama', 'Aomori', 'Hakodate', 'Chugoku']

Ticket key: MFTBCFFR-4198
Ticket type: Service Request
Ticket Summary: SV_Changed the logic for setting the posting date of the Re-edit red slip
Ticket Description: 1. Regarding the posting date when creating **JV** Red Den by clicking the *SV** re-edit button, we have returned to the original logic with **MFTBCFFR-4056**, but if re-editing is performed across months, the posting date will be created with the year and month of the previous month, resulting in a **KB** interface error. *
*This issue continues to be monitored and recovered. *

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4189
Investigation Summary: Monthly invoice data showed incorrect Delta amount rounding because the batch calculation for Customer Pay Amount did not apply rounding at the required step. This caused values such as 0.5 to round to 1 in the invoice file's SMDO067 column, differing from Siebel UI logic. Root Cause: The batch logic calculating Customer Pay Amount did not apply rounding at the required calculation step, causing incorrect Delta amount values in monthly invoice data.
Resolution: Updated the Monthly Invoice batch logic in UAT8 to apply correct rounding consistent with Siebel UI; the fix was approved for deployment to Prod in the June 26 release.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4187
Investigation Summary: Duplicate JVs were created during June invoicing for records manually recovered under MFTBCFFR-3723. The manual recovery did not update the "Sent Flag" to "Y", causing eligible DT01* records to be processed again. Reverse JV data was prepared for each affected environment and applied to Prod; the recovered data was scheduled to link to KB in the nightly daily batch.
Important Findings: ['MFTBCFFR-3723 addressed JVs not being created for Line Type Color and was released on 12th June 2025.', 'During manual recovery for MFTBCFFR-3723, the "Sent Flag" was not updated to "Y".', 'Records with stamp code "MS06GP" and Line Type "4" in the DT01* file were created again during June invoicing.', 'The duplicate JVs affected manually recovered DT01 TOB Invoice records across FDP environments.', 'Reverse JV data was created for the affected records and recovery was completed on Prod.', 'The SOP will be updated to include validation of all recovery conditions, including the "Sent Flag".']
Root Cause: An oversight during the manual recovery process for MFTBCFFR-3723 left the "Sent Flag" unset instead of updating it to "Y", causing recovered records to be processed again in June invoicing and creating duplicate JVs.
Resolution: Reverse JVs were created and applied on Prod for the affected records. The SOP will be updated to require validation of recovery conditions to prevent recurrence.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4183
Investigation Summary: An Assessment Request with Assessment Purpose set to "User Purchase" could be directly mapped to an NV Quote as a Trade-in Vehicle, allowing a UV Purchase Order to be mapped to an NV Sales Order. The issue was replicated in UAT1 and the affected record was recovered. Validation was implemented for both NV Quote Trade-in and UV Quote Trade-in processes, validated in UAT, and released to Prod on July 24, 2025.
Important Findings: ['The issue was replicated in UAT1 using NV SO# A001295706, PO# F001295707, and AR# H000047991.', 'AR# H000047991 had Assessment Purpose "User Purchase" and could be selected as a Trade-in Vehicle on an NV Quote.', 'The unrestricted assessment mapping allowed a UV Purchase Order to be mapped to an NV Sales Order.', 'The affected production record was recovered.', 'A validation message was added to prevent selection of irrelevant trade-in vehicles in NV Quote Trade-in and UV Quote Trade-in processes.', 'The fix was applied to Prod in the regular release on July 24, 2025.']
Root Cause: The NV Quote Trade-in process allowed Assessment Requests with non-trade-in Assessment Purpose values, including "User Purchase", to be directly mapped as Trade-in Vehicles.
Resolution: Implemented validation restricting NV Quote and UV Quote Trade-in selection to assessments related to Trade-in assessment purposes only; released to Prod on July 24, 2025.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4179
Investigation Summary: PO allocation failures occurred in FDP Shikoku, Okayama, Aomori, and Chugoku for Parts Purchase Orders received from D2S; the issue was also observed in the SC version. Investigation determined that D2S sent a ZFTX cancellation trigger for parts that had not been registered in order line items. Affected orders were recovered in the relevant production environments, and preventing recurrence requires order-line-item registration before cancellation.
Important Findings: ['Current logic registers parts in order line items only when the received part is Norm(ZFTN) or Bans(ZFTS).', 'D2S sent ZFTX triggers directly to cancel parts that were not present in the order line items.', 'Cancellation and PO allocation failed because the target parts did not exist in the order line items.', 'The issue affected FDP and was also observed in the SC version.', 'Affected orders were recovered in FDP - PROD, FDPC - PROD, FDPA - PROD, and FDPO - PROD.']
Root Cause: D2S sent a ZFTX cancellation trigger before the relevant part had been registered in the order line items. Since only Norm(ZFTN) and Bans(ZFTS) parts are registered under the current logic, the cancelled parts did not exist in the line items and could not be cancelled or allocated.
Resolution: Recovered the affected orders in the applicable FDP production environments. To prevent recurrence, order line item registration must occur before the ZFTX cancellation trigger is processed.
Technical Entities: ['FDP', 'FDP - PROD', 'FDPC - PROD', 'FDPA - PROD', 'FDPO - PROD', 'FDP Shikoku', 'FDP Okayama', 'FDP Aomori', 'FDP Chugoku', 'SC version', 'D2S', 'PO Allocation', 'PO Shipment', 'Parts Purchase Orders', 'order line items', 'Norm(ZFTN)', 'Bans(ZFTS)', 'ZFTX', 'N050230771', 'N000384489', 'N000261534']

Timestamp: 2025-06-30T06:20:00
Author: Soham
Comment: Thanks for your support.
*RCA*: According to the current logic, if the part received is Norm(ZFTN) or Bans(ZFTS), then it is registered in the line items.
 In this case  D2S send the trigger directly for the ZFTX i.e. to cancel the part, which were not present in the order line items, As these parts were not present in the order line items due to this reason cancellation of these parts were not possible.
 So, if the order line item registration happens before cancellation, then this issue will not occur.
Please let us know in case of any query.
Best Regards,
Soham

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4159
Investigation Summary: IBOS estimate responses were not reflected because new body specification/bodywork records in the IBOS response were not created. The backend data map operation was configured as "update", which only modified existing records. The operation was changed to "upsert" in UAT so that existing records are updated and new records can be created; IBOS response testing and demonstration remained pending.
Important Findings: ['The issue affected reflection of IBOS estimate responses for NV Body quotes.', 'The existing backend data map operation was set to "update", preventing creation of new body specification/bodywork records received from IBOS.', 'The configuration issue was associated with changes made when the Body Building sub-quote was removed from FDP.', 'Changing the data map operation to "upsert" allows both updates to existing records and creation of new records from the IBOS response.', 'The fix was reported as implemented and tested on UAT/UAT1, but end-to-end IBOS response testing was still pending.', 'Requested verification was to submit an NV quote with a body using "Submit to IBOS" and confirm that the IBOS quote response updates the relevant records.']
Root Cause: The backend data map operation was set to "update", which only updated existing records and prevented creation of new body specification/bodywork records included in IBOS estimate responses.
Resolution: Changed the backend data map operation from "update" to "upsert" in UAT/UAT1, enabling IBOS responses to update existing records and create new body specification/bodywork records as needed.
Technical Entities: ['IBOS', 'IBOS Quote Response API', 'FDP', 'Body Building sub-quote', 'FDP FORCE', 'data map', 'backend', 'update', 'upsert', 'NV quote', 'NV Quotes', 'NV Body quote', 'Submit to IBOS', 'body specification records', 'bodywork records', 'UAT', 'UAT1', 'UAT-01', 'UAT2', 'RT2', 'SIT', 'SOAP']

Currently, the operation has been changed to "upsert". This will update existing records and create new body specification records as needed, based on the IBOS response.
 
If you have any questions or concerns, please feel free to contact us.
 
Thank you for your support.
Himanshu

Root Cause: A condition in the search specification of the ODI View caused the issue.

Comment: Thank you for your support.
Regarding the issues mentioned below, we would like to confirm our findings:
# Parts included in Internal Work not displayed under Parts
We have verified this in the Production environment as well as in the old existing BIP. We could not identify any discrepancy.
We are attaching both the old and the revised BIP outputs for reference (parts name and data).
 
Current system logic:
If any Part, Labor, or Accessory is used in the Job Card, its respective name is displayed under Internal Works.
If it is not used in any Job Card, the name is displayed under Body Spec 1 BIP.
We also verified Body Spec 2 BIP, and the respective parts are displayed correctly with no inconsistencies. Old and new BIP samples are attached for confirmation.
# Not all internal works are displayed
We verified this as well, and in BIP Body Spec 1, 14 line items meet the eligibility criteria for display (Record : A027136675).
We are attaching both UI and BIP screenshots (old and new) for reference.
Only Parts, Labor, and Accessories from the line items are used in Body Spec 1, and they are displayed accordingly.
(Verification has been done using the Production environment.)
For Body Spec 2, we also compared old and new outputs and did not find any discrepancy.
(8 - Labor, 6 - Parts)
# Decimal values appearing in amount fields
In the current Production environment, decimals appear only for selected line items.
We can modify this so that all line items consistently display decimal points.
However, please confirm:
If a value has no decimals, the format will look like 2345.00.
Is this aligned with business requirements?
Request for discussion
Since we are not able to find discrepancies based on our analysis, would it be possible to schedule a short call to avoid misunderstandings and resolve the issues efficiently?
Thanks & Regards,
Manav

Root Cause: The JV was manually created using an admin ID without a branch during MFTBCFFR-4124 SR recovery, causing the department code to be null.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4138
Investigation Summary: Stock records were visible in SIEBEL/Siebel DB but missing from the PBI 5-02 report because they were excluded by ODI filtering conditions. The affected Shikoku parts were corrected by changing their item category to LUMF and creating/executing the required Price Master; recovery completed and the records became visible in PBI 5-02. For part #101244115, the remaining root cause was identified as an inventory update timestamp outside the effective date range of its price-list item.
Important Findings: ['Shikoku Branch 42 parts HB06MS2, HB511, HD72T, HD72U, HD72V, and MB05A were present in SIEBEL but absent from PBI 5-02.', "These parts were excluded from the PBI datamart by ODI because they failed the condition S_PRI_LST.SUBTYPE_CD = 'Parts Price List'.", 'The affected parts were incorrectly categorized as NORM instead of LUMF, so the expected LUMF price lists with List price and D/N price set to 0 had not been created.', 'After the item category was manually changed to LUMF, Price Master was created and executed, and the affected parts appeared in PBI 5-02.', "Part #101244115 failed the ODI condition S_PROD_INV.LAST_UPD BETWEEN S_PRI_LST_ITEM.EFF_START_DT AND NVL(S_PRI_LST_ITEM.EFF_END_DT,'31-12-9999') because its LAST_UPD timestamps were later than the configured EFF_END_DT of 2025-04-26."]
Root Cause: Invalid or missing price-list master data caused ODI exclusions: the affected parts were categorized as NORM rather than LUMF and lacked a 'Parts Price List'; for part #101244115, S_PROD_INV.LAST_UPD was outside the S_PRI_LST_ITEM effective-date range.
Resolution: Manually changed the affected parts' item category to LUMF, created and executed the Price Master, and completed recovery so the parts became visible in the PBI 5-02 report.
Technical Entities: ['SIEBEL', 'Siebel DB', 'PBI 5-02', 'PBI datamart', 'ODI', 'Shikoku', 'Branch 42', 'HB06MS2', 'HB511', 'HD72T', 'HD72U', 'HD72V', 'MB05A', '#101244115', 'S_PRI_LST.SUBTYPE_CD', 'Parts Price List', 'LUMF', 'NORM', 'Price Master', 'List price', 'D/N price', 'S_PROD_INV.LAST_UPD', 'S_PRI_LST_ITEM.EFF_START_DT', 'S_PRI_LST_ITEM.EFF_END_DT', 'AVAIL_CD', 'Reserved', 'On Hand', 'In Transit']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4127
Investigation Summary: Control logic was initially fixed and validated in FDP-UAT1/UAT-1, then released to PROD, including a correction for expense item "41: Other service expenses". A later review found that JC Type "32" allowed an amount despite requiring the same free-cost control as JC Types 22-51. JC Type 32 was added to the current logic in UAT1 so that all JCs from 22-51 use the same free-cost condition; production approval was requested.
Important Findings: ['The initial fix was verified in UAT-1 and released to PROD on 12 June 2025.', 'Expense item "41: Other service expenses" was subsequently found to be outside the control logic and was fixed in FDP-UAT1 under reference JC I001296258.', 'After the correction, the functionality was confirmed to work correctly in the production environment.', 'JC Type "32" contained an amount although it should have the same free-cost control as other free expense items in the JC Type 22-51 range.', 'JC Type 32 was added to the current logic in UAT1, and all JCs from 22-51 were configured with the same free-cost condition.']
Root Cause: JC Type "32" was not included in the existing free-cost control logic applied to JC Types 22-51, allowing an amount to be entered.
Resolution: Added JC Type "32" to the current free-cost control logic in UAT1 so that all JCs from 22-51 have the same condition; approval for Production deployment was requested.
