investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4125
Investigation Summary: Journal Voucher data for Liability Insurance Orders was not sent to KB because the department code was null. Investigation found that migrated Liability Insurance Orders had a null PR_POSTN_ID (Primary Position Id), which resulted in missing department code in the Insurance Order and Journal Voucher. The impacted orders were patched, recovery JVs were created, and recovery data was added to Prod for transmission to KB in the nightly batch.
Important Findings: ['On 22 May, a Journal Voucher was created after spreadsheet approval but was not sent to KB because its department code was not set.', 'Migrated Liability Insurance Orders had a null PR_POSTN_ID (Primary Position Id).', 'A null Primary Position Id caused the department code to be null in both the Insurance Order and the Liability Insurance Journal Voucher.', 'Liability Insurance Orders with status "Spreadsheet Approved" were excluded from the recovery.', "PR_POSTN_ID was patched by mapping the Sales Rep's Primary Position for the impacted Insurance orders.", 'Recovery JVs were created and added to Prod for delivery to KB in the nightly batch.']
Root Cause: Migrated Liability Insurance Orders had a null PR_POSTN_ID (Primary Position Id), causing the department code to be null in the Insurance Order and Journal Voucher and preventing JV data from being sent to KB.
Resolution: Patched PR_POSTN_ID for impacted Liability Insurance Orders using the Sales Rep's Primary Position, created recovery JVs, and added the recovery data to Prod for transmission to KB.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4093
Investigation Summary: A duplicate Shipment was created for Parts Sales Return Orders when the user generated approval and subsequently saved the order header using Ctrl + S. The issue was replicated and fixed on FDP UAT-1, then released to Prod on 2 June 2025 with the MFTBCFFR-4018 emergency release.
Important Findings: ['Recovery was completed for Order# M000121562.', 'The issue was replicated on FDP UAT-1 using Order# M001295374.', "Selecting Generate Approval changed the Parts Sales Return Order status to 'Approved' and created a Shipment.", 'Pressing Ctrl + S on the Parts Sales Return Order Header created an additional Shipment.', 'The fix was verified on FDP UAT-1 and released to Prod on 2 June 2025.']
Resolution: The issue was fixed on FDP UAT-1, verified, and deployed to Prod on 2 June 2025 as part of the MFTBCFFR-4018 emergency release.
Technical Entities: ['Order# M000121562', 'FDP UAT-1', 'Order# M001295374', 'Generate Approval Button', 'Parts Sales Return Order', 'Approved', 'Shipment', 'Ctrl + S', 'Parts Sales Return Order Header', 'MFTBCFFR-4018', 'Prod']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4087
Investigation Summary: A blank trade-in line item could be created in an NV Quote when the AR# was removed and the line item was saved during a quote revision. Replication in UAT confirmed that clearing the AR# cleared the trade-in line item's asset_id, resulting in the blank line item. A validation was implemented and tested in UAT to prevent saving a trade-in line item with a blank assessment number, then released to PROD on June 26, 2025.
Important Findings: ['The issue was replicated in UAT using NV Quote #: 1-KHY8Z, Rev-3.', "In NV Quote #: 1-IQZEL, Rev-2, removing AR#: H000001601 from a trade-in vehicle while creating Rev-3 and then deleting the record cleared the trade-in line item's asset_id.", 'A new trade-in vehicle with AR#: H000001602 could then be added while the cleared asset_id caused a blank line item to display in the NV Quote.', 'The implemented validation prevents users from saving a trade-in line item when the AR# / assessment number is blank.', 'Users can still update the AR# through the standard process or delete the trade-in line item.', 'The UAT test record was UAT1, NV Quote #: 1-6AFG8S; the validation error message was changed to “Assessment No. is a required field and cannot be left blank.”']
Root Cause: The trade-in line item process allowed the AR# to be removed and the line item saved, which cleared asset_id and created a blank trade-in line item in the NV Quote.
Resolution: Implemented validation in UAT and released it to PROD on June 26, 2025, preventing a trade-in line item from being saved with a blank AR# / assessment number.
Technical Entities: ['Okinawa-PROD', 'UAT', 'PROD', 'NV Quote', 'NV Quote #: 1-KHY8Z, Rev-3', 'NV Quote #: 1-IQZEL, Rev-2', 'AR#: H000001601', 'AR#: H000001602', 'asset_id', 'trade-in line item', 'UAT1', 'NV Quote #: 1-6AFG8S', 'Assessment No. is a required field and cannot be left blank.']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4087
Timestamp: 2025-06-05T05:32:00
Author: Sunaina Gill
Comment: Dear Tsunoda-san,
 Thank you for your continued support.
We have completed our analysis regarding the reported issue in the JIRA ticket. We successfully replicated the issue in the UAT environment using the reference record NV Quote #: 1-KHY8Z, Rev-3, and confirmed that this is a case of user misoperation.
 Here are the steps the user followed that led to the issue:
 1.) In NV Quote #: 1-IQZEL, Rev-2, the user added a trade-in vehicle with AR#: H000001601.
 2.) While creating Rev-3, the user removed the AR# from the trade-in vehicle line item and then deleted the record.
 3.) Subsequently, the user added a new trade-in vehicle with AR#: H000001602.
As a result of this sequence, the asset_id in the trade-in line item was cleared, leading to the display of a blank line item in the NV Quote.
 To avoid this issue, we suggest the user to delete the existing trade-in line item entirely and then, create a new line item with the desired trade-in vehicle information or to change the AR# directly without erasing it.
Please feel free to contact us if you have any questions or need further assistance.
Best regards,
Sunaina Gill

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4073
Investigation Summary: Invoice API field mappings were reviewed and updated in FDP UAT-1 to align CustomerName and DeliveryNumber values with billing requirements. CustomerName now uses Prospect Account Name when it is populated on the JC Header, otherwise Ship To Customer Name; DeliveryNumber uses Bill To Basic Account Name. The approved changes were released to PROD on 12 June 2025.
Important Findings: ['The original CustomerName mapping populated the API value from Ship To Customer Name in the JC Header.', 'The mapping was revised after review of vehicle-name consistency for individual and monthly billing invoices, including change orders, versus Siebel delivery notes.', 'In FDP UAT-1, CustomerName is populated from Prospect Account Name when the field is not null; otherwise it is populated from Ship To Customer Name.', 'DeliveryNumber in the Invoice is populated from Bill To Basic Account Name.', 'The updated program was approved for deployment and released to PROD on 12 June 2025.']
Root Cause: The existing Invoice API mapping always sourced CustomerName from Ship To Customer Name and did not use Prospect Account Name when it was available.
Resolution: Updated the CustomerName mapping to use Prospect Account Name when populated and Ship To Customer Name when null, updated DeliveryNumber to use Bill To Basic Account Name, and released the changes to PROD on 12 June 2025.
Technical Entities: ['API', 'CustomerName', 'DeliveryNumber', 'FDP UAT-1', 'PROD', 'Invoice', 'JC Header', 'Ship To Customer Name', 'Prospect Account Name', 'Cash Receipt Flag', 'Bill To Basic Account Name', 'Siebel', 'delivery note', 'individual billing invoices', 'monthly billing invoices', 'change orders', 'I001293538', 'I001290345', 'I001295584']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4040
Investigation Summary: Journal Voucher client-code assignment logic for recycle invoice data was found to be incorrect. The logic was corrected and validated in UAT1 using Okayama May invoice test data and corresponding Journal Voucher data. The approved change was released to Production on 10 July 2025.
Important Findings: ['The original logic set Debit Client Code CSJ208 to Okayama Fuso (0000108561) and Credit Client Code CSJ208 to MFTBC Account (0000010006).', 'For credit account code 211-10, CSJ208 must be set to "Own company" and CSJS308 must be set to "MFTBC code".', 'Recycle invoice data and Journal Voucher data were created in UAT1 for validation.', 'The updated logic was verified in UAT1 before Production approval.', 'The fix was released to Production on 10 July 2025.']
Root Cause: Incorrect client-code assignment logic for Journal Voucher processing, specifically for credit account code 211-10.
Resolution: Updated the logic so that, when credit account code is 211-10, CSJ208 is set to "Own company" and CSJS308 is set to "MFTBC code"; validated in UAT1 and released to Production on 10 July 2025.
Technical Entities: ['CSJ208', 'CSJS308', 'Okayama Fuso', '0000108561', 'MFTBC Account', '0000010006', '211-10', 'UAT1', 'Recycle invoice data', 'Journal Voucher Data', 'JV', 'Production']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4024
Investigation Summary: SV & PT Orders with Customer Code "0000328018" were omitted from the February EOM Bulk Invoice transfer to KB after the account closing was changed from 20 to EOM on 6 February. Bulk Invoice processing was limited to the last 30 days, excluding data from 20 January to 28 January. Recovery Bulk Invoice data was sent to the MDIS team, completing the recovery.
Important Findings: ['Affected SV & PT Orders were I000012952, I000020814, and M000015656.', 'The account closing was changed from 20 to EOM on 6 February.', 'The orders were expected to be sent to KB on the 20th closing, but were instead deferred to the February EOM run.', 'Bulk Invoice logic included only the previous 30 days, so data from 20 January to 28 January was not sent to KB.', 'An ongoing CR will extend the Bulk Invoice range from 30 days to 60 days to prevent similar omissions.']
Root Cause: Bulk Invoice logic was designed to process only the last 30 days of data. Changing the account closing from 20 to EOM caused 20 January to 28 January data to fall outside the February EOM processing window.
Resolution: Recovery Bulk Invoice data was sent to the MDIS team for delivery to KB; all recoveries were completed.

Timestamp: 2025-05-22T06:34:00
Author: Divyesh Ghiya
Comment: Thank you for your support.
We have analyszed this issue thorughly and below are our findings:
 On 6th February, User changed the closing of the mentioned account from 20 to EOM. 
Since, Bulk Invoice logic includes only 30 days of data, this data was not sent in February EOM. 
 These orders were supposed to be sent to KB on 20th closing, but user changed the closing from 20 to EOM. Now in Feb EOM, this data is supposed to be sent to KB but since Bulk Invoice logic only includes data of last 30 days, 20th Jan to 28th Jan data was not sent to KB. 
This is not a system bug, during initial development of the Bulk Invoice functionality, only 30 days range was included. There is a ongoing CR where we will change this range from 30 days to 60 days. By this CR, such cases will be avoided. 
Kindly verify our analysis and please let us know if you have any query or need any additional information.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4018
Investigation Summary: Journal events of type "Inv Cancellation Sales Amount" and "Purchase Return NORM" could generate an incorrect Department Code. Investigation found that the Department Code was sourced from the Location Code of the shipment's Parent Order creator instead of the relevant inventory name. The mapping was corrected, released to Prod on 2 June 2025, and recovery JVs were completed for Shikoku, Okinawa, and Chugoku.
Important Findings: ['For "Inv Cancellation Sales Amount" and "Purchase Return NORM", Department Code was fetched from the Location Code of the shipment\'s Parent Order creator.', 'The corrected logic uses the Purchase Return Order inventory name as the Department Code and uses the inventory name for "Inv Cancellation Sales Amount" JV lines.', 'The fix was deployed to UAT1 for testing before Prod release.', 'Recovery required reverse JV and correct JV data with the correct JV_Department_Code.', 'Recovery was completed in Prod for Shikoku, Okinawa, and Chugoku and linked to KB through the daily batch.']
Root Cause: Incorrect Department Code mapping: the system used the Location Code of the shipment's Parent Order creator rather than the applicable inventory name for "Inv Cancellation Sales Amount" and "Purchase Return NORM" journal events.
Resolution: Updated the Department Code mapping to use inventory name, released the fix to Prod on 2 June 2025, and created reverse and corrective recovery JVs for affected orders in Shikoku, Okinawa, and Chugoku.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-4001
Investigation Summary: Statistics were not collected for tables in the Wakayama environment because the Oracle-recommended coe_Siebel_stats.sql script locked tables below its configured data-volume cutoff. The affected tables were unlocked and statistics were gathered, resolving the incident on 19 May 2025 at 13:45 JST. As a permanent measure, Wakayama will use monthly manual statistics collection through DBMS statistics instead of coe_Siebel_stats.sql.
Important Findings: ['coe_Siebel_stats.sql locks tables with fewer rows, preventing statistics collection for those tables.', 'The Wakayama tables had insufficient data volume to exceed the script cutoff value.', 'The cutoff value is defined by the Oracle-provided and recommended script and cannot be changed by the support team.', 'A similar issue occurred in the FDP Hakodate environment in February 2025.', 'Unlocking statistics on the affected tables followed by gathering statistics restored collection.']
Root Cause: The Oracle-recommended coe_Siebel_stats.sql script locked Wakayama tables whose data volume was below its configured cutoff, preventing statistics from being collected.
Resolution: Unlocked statistics for the affected tables and reran statistics gathering. Wakayama will manually collect statistics monthly using DBMS statistics rather than coe_Siebel_stats.sql.
Technical Entities: ['Oracle', 'coe_Siebel_stats.sql', 'Wakayama', 'FDP Hakodate', 'DBMS statistics']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3986
Investigation Summary: The price difference between the Service Change Order – Bulk Invoice and the CO Delivery Slip was investigated as a mapping issue. The real time invoice interface was originally configured only for Job Card Order; Change Order was not included in the BRD for the real time Invoice CR. The issue was tracked under MFTBCFFR-3251, where a related fix had been deployed to UAT-1, while mapping was requested for a future Project-CR.
Important Findings: ['Service Change Order – Bulk Invoice is mapped to Job Card Order fields.', 'The Bulk Invoice and CO Delivery Slip use different mapping logic, causing the price difference.', 'Only Job Card Order was configured during initial development of the real time invoice interface.', 'Change Order was not included in the BRD for the real time Invoice CR.', 'A similar issue was tracked in MFTBCFFR-3251, with a fix deployed on UAT-1.']
Root Cause: The real time invoice interface was designed only for Job Card Order, and Change Order mapping was not included in the BRD for the real time Invoice CR, resulting in mapping logic differences between the Bulk Invoice and CO Delivery Slip.
Technical Entities: ['MFTBCFFR-3251', 'UAT-1', 'Service Change Order – Bulk Invoice', 'Job Card Order', 'CO Delivery Slip', 'real time invoice interface', 'Change Order', 'BRD', 'real time Invoice CR', 'Project-CR']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3963
Investigation Summary: Recycle Invoice data was received on May 1, 2025, while the Invoice Calendar processing date was May 7, 2025. Under the current functionality, only files received on the same date as the monthly Invoice Calendar date are executed, so the file did not run in any FDP environment. Recovery was completed by manually processing the recycle invoice data on all FDP production environments.
Important Findings: ['Recycle Invoice data was received on May 1, 2025, before the May 7, 2025 date configured in the Invoice Calendar.', 'Current functionality executes monthly files only when their receipt date matches the Invoice Calendar date.', 'The date mismatch prevented the Recycle Invoice data file from executing in FDP environments.', 'The behavior was determined to be consistent with the initial requirements and not a system bug.', 'A modification to support early file receipt would require an AMS CR.', 'Recovery was completed by manually processing the recycle invoice data on all FDP production environments.']
Root Cause: The Recycle Invoice data file was received before its configured Invoice Calendar date; the existing logic processes files only when the receipt date exactly matches the Invoice Calendar date.
Resolution: Recycle Invoice data was manually processed for recovery on all FDP production environments.
Technical Entities: ['Recycle Invoice data', 'Invoice Calendar', 'FDP', 'FDP production environments', 'AMS CR', 'journal entry voucher (JV)']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3953
Investigation Summary: Account information registered in SIEBEL was not interfaced to KB because the complete Account master linkage in Shikoku Production had been intentionally suspended. The suspension was requested until the MFTBCFFR-3040 CR is deployed to Production after incorrect Account master column mappings were identified. The incident was closed, with KB-side manual recovery continuing while CR development and production release remain pending.
Important Findings: ['The Account master interface from SIEBEL to KB is suspended for all accounts in Shikoku Production, not for specific account codes.', 'Account code 1000007404 was created in April and was not sent to KB because the Account master bulk linkage had already been stopped before April.', 'MFTBCFFR-3040 identified incorrect mappings in some Account master data columns sent to KB; the incident fix was deployed to all FDP environments.', 'A further CR requested after MFTBCFFR-3040 is still pending development and Production deployment.', 'KB-side manual recovery is being performed while the Account master linkage remains suspended.']
Root Cause: The SIEBEL-to-KB Account master bulk interface in Shikoku Production was intentionally suspended for all accounts at Miyauchi's request until the MFTBCFFR-3040 CR is released to Production, following incorrect Account master column mappings.
Resolution: The incident was closed as expected behavior; KB-side manual recovery is ongoing, and the Account master linkage will remain suspended until the pending CR is developed and released to Production.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3931
Investigation Summary: Recycle Fee Order creation was missing for affected VIN records, including FBAV0-610627, after D21F files were received before D21E files. The issue matched the known pattern tracked in MFTBCFFR-3546. Recovery was completed for all affected records in FDP environments, while Kaizen monitoring and proactive recovery activities continued under MFTBCFFR-3546.
Important Findings: ['For VIN FBAV0-610627, the required D21 file had initially not been received from TOB; chassis, recycling fee, and pool cost orders depend on file receipt.', 'D21F was received before D21E, preventing Recycle Fee Order creation for the affected VINs.', 'The incident was identified as similar to MFTBCFFR-3546 and is tracked under that Jira.', 'Recovery was completed for all affected records in FDP environments.', 'Kaizen activity was in progress to monitor and proactively recover similar file-ordering events.']
Root Cause: D21F file receipt before D21E file caused Recycle Fee Order not to be created for the affected VINs.
Resolution: Recovered all affected records in FDP environments; ongoing monitoring and proactive recovery are tracked in MFTBCFFR-3546.
Technical Entities: ['FBAV0-610627', 'FEB80-611353', 'D21 file', 'D21E file', 'D21F file', 'TOB', 'Chassis order', 'Recycle Fee Order', 'Recycling fee order', 'Pool Cost order', 'FDP environments', 'MFTBCFFR-3546', 'Kaizen']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3923
Investigation Summary: The March 31 Bulk Invoice file from Cubastion showed that all referenced JCs were successfully sent from Siebel to KB, so the Bulk Invoice process was operating normally. The investigation identified that the Account master linkage from Siebel to KB had been intentionally suspended for all accounts in Shikoku Production pending deployment of the MFTBCFFR-3040 CR. KB was performing manual recovery while the interface remained suspended, and the incident was closed as not being a system issue.
Important Findings: ['All referenced JCs were included in the March EOM (March 31) Bulk Invoice file and were successfully sent to KB.', 'Siebel sends Bulk Invoice data to KB; no information was available regarding CSS Invoice processing.', 'MFTBCFFR-3040 addressed incorrect mapping in some Account master data columns sent to KB; the incident fix was deployed to all FDP environments.', 'A further CR requested after MFTBCFFR-3040 remained pending for Production deployment.', 'Under MFTBCFFR-3149, the complete Account master interface was stopped in Shikoku Production for all accounts, not only specific account codes.', 'Account code 1000007404, created in April, was not sent to KB because Account master bulk processing had been stopped before April.']
Root Cause: The complete Account master linkage from Siebel to KB was intentionally suspended in Shikoku Production at Miyauchi's request until the MFTBCFFR-3040 CR is deployed to Production.
Resolution: KB performed manual recovery while the Account master linkage remained suspended pending CR development and Production deployment; the incident was closed as not being a system issue.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3922
Investigation Summary: In a Payer Change Order, changing the payer in Bill to Basic Account did not refresh the Closed Date from the newly selected payer. The retained old Closed Date prevented the change order from being processed at EOM (31 March), and the JC lines and change order lines were instead sent to KB on 20 April. The issue was identified as similar to MFTBCFFR-3672 and was tracked through that incident.
Important Findings: ['Bill to Basic Account and Ship to basic account values are initially fetched from JCO when a Payer Change Order is created.', 'Changing the payer in Bill to Basic Account should update Closed Date and Payment term based on the new payer.', 'Closed Date retained its previous value after the payer change and was not updated to EOM (31 March).', 'K000076384 was output in billing data on 20 April rather than at the end of March.', 'The issue was tracked under MFTBCFFR-3672.']
Root Cause: Changing the payer in Bill to Basic Account did not update the Closed Date value in the Payer Change Order, leaving the previous date and preventing EOM processing.
Technical Entities: ['Payer Change Order', 'Bill to Basic Account', 'Ship to basic account', 'JCO', 'Closed Date', 'Payment term', 'EOM (31 March)', 'KB', 'JC lines', 'change order lines', 'K000076384', 'billing data', 'SIEBEL', 'FDP Chugoku', 'Chugoku Prod', 'MFTBCFFR-3672']

Author: Akash

When user creates a Payer Change Order, values in Bill to Basic Account and Ship to basic account is fetched from JCO. Then user changes the payer in Bill to Basic Account and values in Closed Date and Payment term should be reflected according to new Payer entered. Because of this, closed date was not changed to EOM (31 March) in the change order and hence not sent to KB. Since the date was 20 April, all the JC lines and change order lines were sent to KB on 20 April.
This issue is similar to MFTBCFFR-3672, So we are tracking this issue through MFTBCFFR-3672.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3920
Investigation Summary: Journal Voucher department code assignment for employee D8NOOSHI failed because the Employee master contained an incorrect department assignment for the employee's Branch CS Staff position. Department code 0108, a Headquarter department code, was assigned instead of the appropriate branch department. The Employee master data was corrected, and subsequent Journal Vouchers populated the correct department code.
Important Findings: ['D8NOOSHI created Job Cards with a Branch CS Staff position, but the department code was not fetched correctly.', 'The Employee master had department code 0108 assigned to the Branch CS Staff position; 0108 is a Headquarter department code.', 'The incorrect Employee master department assignment caused the Branch CS Staff position to be created with an HQ department and caused the Journal Voucher to fail.', "After correcting D8NOOSHI's Employee master department code, the correct department code was populated in Journal Vouchers.", 'Okinawa Prod Job Card I000035491, created by D8NOOSHI and closed on 2025/05/30 10:56:21 AM, confirmed the corrected Journal Voucher department code.']
Root Cause: Incorrect Employee master data assigned Headquarter department code 0108 to employee D8NOOSHI's Branch CS Staff position.
Resolution: Corrected the Employee master department code for D8NOOSHI; Journal Vouchers subsequently populated the correct department code.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3893
Investigation Summary: Affected records, including A000020793, were recovered, and no additional records requiring recovery were identified. Investigation confirmed that Activity statuses could be manually changed through the UI and were not automatically set to "Work Completed" when the associated Job Card (JC) was set to "Closed". A fix was implemented and verified in UAT 1.
Important Findings: ['The affected records were recovered, and no other records requiring recovery were found.', 'The issue was replicated during investigation.', 'Users could manually perform all Activity status transitions through the UI: Open → Request for Reservation → Reservation Confirmed → Work Completed → Closed.', 'Activity status did not automatically update to "Work Completed" when the Job Card (JC) status was set to "Closed".', 'The implemented fix updates Activity status to "Work Completed" regardless of its previous status and makes it read-only afterward.', 'The fix was implemented and confirmed to work as expected in UAT 1.']
Root Cause: The Activity status was not automatically synchronized to "Work Completed" when the associated Job Card (JC) status changed to "Closed", while users could manually modify Activity statuses through the UI.
Resolution: Implemented a fix in UAT 1 that automatically sets the Activity status to "Work Completed" when the Job Card (JC) status is set to "Closed", regardless of the prior Activity status, and makes the Activity status read-only after the update.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3887
Investigation Summary: The incident concerned activity status changes in the UI and the relationship between Activity status and Job Card (JC) status. Investigation confirmed that users could manually perform all standard Activity status transitions. A fix was implemented so that closing a JC automatically sets the Activity status to "Work Completed" and makes it read-only; it was validated in UAT 1 and released to production on 26 May 2025.
Important Findings: ['The standard Activity status flow is "Open" → "Request for Reservation" → "Reservation Confirmed" → "Work Completed" → "Closed".', 'Users were able to manually change Activity status through the UI, including all standard transitions.', 'When Job Card (JC) status is set to "Closed", the fix updates the Activity status to "Work Completed" regardless of its prior status.', 'After an Activity status is updated to "Work Completed", the status becomes read-only and cannot be manually modified.', 'The fix was implemented and validated in UAT 1 before release to the FDP production environment on 26 May 2025.']
Root Cause: The UI allowed users to manually modify Activity status, and Activity status was not automatically set to "Work Completed" when the associated Job Card (JC) status was set to "Closed".
Resolution: Implemented automatic Activity status update to "Work Completed" when JC status is set to "Closed", regardless of previous Activity status, and made the Activity status read-only after that update. The fix was validated in UAT 1 and released to the FDP production environment on 26 May 2025.
Technical Entities: ['Activity', 'UI', 'Open', 'Request for Reservation', 'Reservation Confirmed', 'Work Completed', 'Closed', 'Job Card (JC)', 'JC status', 'UAT 1', 'FDP production environment', 'SC version']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3874
Investigation Summary: The Invoice CustomerName mapping was reviewed because it was selecting different customer sources based on the Cash Receipt Flag on the JC Header. An interim UAT-1 change mapped CustomerName to Prospect Account Name when the flag was Y, but the final validated requirement was to always use Ship To Customer Name. The final mapping was approved for PROD deployment, with release planned for 14 May.
Important Findings: ['The original CustomerName logic used Vehicle Owner Name when Cash Receipt Flag was Y and Ship To Customer Name when it was N.', 'An interim FDP UAT-1 change mapped CustomerName to Prospect Account Name when Cash Receipt Flag was Y.', 'The final FDP UAT-1 mapping sets CustomerName from Ship To Customer Name regardless of the Cash Receipt Flag value.', 'Validation confirmed CustomerName uses the JC customer even when the Vehicle Owner in the vehicle master differs from the JC customer.', 'The final Xlms value was validated and approved for PROD deployment.']
Root Cause: CustomerName was mapped conditionally to Vehicle Owner Name or other sources based on the Cash Receipt Flag, instead of consistently using Ship To Customer Name.
Resolution: Updated the CustomerName tag mapping in FDP UAT-1 to use Ship To Customer Name regardless of Cash Receipt Flag, validated the results, and approved the change for PROD release on 14 May.
Technical Entities: ['Invoice', 'CustomerName', 'JC Header', 'Cash Receipt Flag', 'Vehicle Owner Name', 'Ship To Customer Name', 'Prospect Account Name', 'FDP UAT-1', 'PROD', 'Chugoku Prod', 'RT invoice API', 'vehicle master', 'Xlms value', 'MFTBCFFR-3753', 'SV_Invoice Vehicle Owner issue(＠Chugoku)']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3863
Investigation Summary: A Consumption Tax JV line was missing for the "Job Card Sales CT" journal event because a search specification evaluated a consumption tax amount of 0.8 as zero. The search specification was corrected to use the proper rounding behavior, validated in UAT-1/UAT-01, and released to Production on 14 May.
Important Findings: ['JV line creation uses a Search Specification to prevent creation of zero-amount JV lines.', 'The consumption tax amount of 0.8 should have been rounded to 1.', 'Incorrect rounding in the Search Specification treated 0.8 as 0.', 'As a result, no JV line was created for the "Job Card Sales CT" journal event.', 'The affected JC was recovered and the Consumption Tax JV was added in Production.', 'The corrected Search Specification was tested in UAT-1/UAT-01 and released to Production on 14 May.']
Root Cause: The Search Specification used to determine whether a tax amount was zero applied incorrect rounding, causing consumption tax amount 0.8 to be treated as 0 and suppressing creation of the "Job Card Sales CT" JV line.
Resolution: Corrected the Search Specification rounding behavior, validated the fix in UAT-1/UAT-01, released it to Production on 14 May, and recovered the affected JC by adding the Consumption Tax JV in Production.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3863
Timestamp: 2025-04-24T06:35:00
Author: Divyesh Ghiya
Comment: san,
Thank you for your support.
We have analysed this issue thoroughly and below are our findings:
While creating Journal voucher line, system checks whether the amount is equal to zero or not. Since, we do not create zero amount JV, we have added a search specification which check if the tax amount is equal to zero or not. If the tax amount is equal to zero then JV line is not created. In this case, consumption tax amount 0.8 which should be rounded to 1. But the search specification did not follow the correct rounding procedure and estimated 0.8 as 0. Hence, no JV line was created for "Job Card Sales CT" Journal event.
Fix Plan: We will fix the search specification which follows the incorrect rounding procedure. We will share the fix on UAT1 by today EOD. Please let us know if you have any query.
Regards,
Divyesh Ghiya

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3863
Timestamp: 2025-04-24T06:42:00
Comment: Mr. Miyauchi, Mr. Yoshiwara,
Thank you for your continued support.
As a result of a detailed investigation into this matter, we found the following.
When creating a journal entry (JV) line, the system checks whether the amount is 0. Since the specification is not to create journal entry slips with an amount of 0, we have set a search condition (Search Specification) to determine whether the tax amount is 0. If the tax amount is 0, no journal entry line is created.
In this case, the consumption tax amount is "0.8" and should have been rounded to "1", but the correct rounding process was not performed within the search conditions and it was treated as "0". As a result, the line for the "Job Card Sales CT" journal event was not created.
Response policy:
We will correct the search conditions that perform inaccurate rounding. This modification is scheduled to be reflected in the UAT1 environment today.
If you have any questions, please feel free to let us know.
Thank you very much for your support.

Root Cause: User mis-operation: the UID was updated after Generate Approval was triggered, leaving the Sales Quote in Pending Approval.
Resolution: Recovery was completed for the affected Sales Quote, allowing the user to proceed.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3851
Investigation Summary: Department Code was null in JV records for orders whose Job Cards were created by Headquarter users without a Branch ID. The current logic derives Department Code from the Branch Code on the Job Card and Service Purchase Order. Recovery was completed by linking the correct JV to KB and adding the correct Department Code before the night batch; the permanent fix was transferred to MFTBCFFR-3920.
Important Findings: ['Department Code became null in JV when a Headquarter user without a Branch ID created the Job Card.', 'Current logic sets Department Code from the Branch Code on the Job Card and Service Purchase Order.', 'Recovery involved linking the correct JV to KB and adding the correct Department Code from the JC or SPO before the night batch.', 'The required permanent logic for records created by non-branch users was moved to MFTBCFFR-3920.', 'The branch or Department Code to assign for Headquarter users required confirmation.']
Root Cause: A Headquarter user without a Branch ID created the Job Card, while the existing logic derives Department Code from the Job Card and Service Purchase Order Branch Code, resulting in a null Department Code in JV.
Resolution: Completed recovery by linking the correct JV to KB and populating the Department Code before the night batch. Permanent fix work was tracked under MFTBCFFR-3920.
Technical Entities: ['JV', 'KB', 'Department Code', 'Job Card', 'Branch ID', 'Branch Code', 'Service Purchase Order', 'SPO', 'JC', 'Headquarter', 'UAT', 'MDIS', 'night batch', 'MFTBCFFR-3920', 'J000024407', 'J000025114', 'I000014741']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3833
Investigation Summary: Incorrect Total PO Cost on the Service Purchase Order (SPO) was investigated in UAT1 for SPO J001294885 and JC I001294884. The behavior was caused by the configured labor-line quantity calculation logic for labor code .004330, not a system defect. Changing the Zero Effort Flag from Y to N corrected the SPO value, and the incident was withdrawn.
Important Findings: ['For labor code .004330, Quantity Requested defaults to 1 when Zero Effort Flag is Y, Billing Type is not Customer, and PO Cost Flag is N.', 'The Quantity Requested default of 1 is applied regardless of actual labor effort or operation time.', 'The resulting Total PO Cost can be higher than the actual cost because it is calculated using the default quantity of 1.', 'The behavior is designed according to the existing validation rules.', 'Changing the Zero Effort Flag from Y to N caused the correct value to be reflected in the SPO in UAT1.']
Root Cause: Labor code .004330 was configured with Zero Effort Flag = Y, Billing Type other than Customer, and PO Cost Flag = N, which triggered designed logic that defaulted Quantity Requested to 1 and produced an incorrect Total PO Cost.
Resolution: Changed the Zero Effort Flag from Y to N in UAT1, which corrected the value in the SPO. The incident was withdrawn as a flag-setting issue rather than a system issue.
Technical Entities: ['Service Purchase Order (SPO)', 'Total PO Cost', 'Labor Line Item', 'labor code .004330', 'Zero Effort Flag', 'Billing Type', 'Customer', 'PO Cost Flag', 'Quantity Requested', 'SPO J001294885', 'JC I001294884', 'UAT1']

*RCA:* The issue with the incorrect Total PO Cost in the Service Purchase Order (SPO) is as per the current system logic for calculating quantity on labor line items. Specifically, for labor code '.004330', the Zero Effort Flag is set to 'Y', the Billing Type is not 'Customer', and the PO Cost Flag is 'N'. According to the current functionality, when these conditions are met, the Quantity Requested is defaulted to 1, instead of using the actual labor effort or operation time.
As a result, the Total PO Cost is calculated using the formula:
 * 1, leading to higher cost being reflected in the SPO. This behavior is functioning as designed based on existing validation rules.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3833
Timestamp: 2025-04-24T05:22:00
Comment: Mr. Yoshiwara,
Thank you for your continued support.
Cause analysis (RCA):
The issue with the incorrect display of Total PO Cost on Service Purchase Orders (SPOs) is due to the current system logic for calculating Labor Line Item quantities.
Specifically, for Labor code '.004330', if the following conditions apply:
Zero Effort Flag is set to “Y”
Billing Type is set to something other than "Customer"
PO Cost Flag is set to “N”
If all the above conditions are met, the system will automatically set Quantity Requested to "1" regardless of the actual working time or effort.
Therefore, Total PO Cost (total order amount) is calculated by the following formula: × 1
This behavior, where a higher cost than the actual one is reflected in the SPO, is the designed behavior based on the current validation rules.
It has been confirmed that if the Zero Effort Flag is changed from "Y" to "N", the correct value will be reflected on SPO.
Please see the attached master and SPO screenshots.
SPO#(J001294885) screenshot: For {*JC#: I001294884*} in UAT1:
If you would like to change the current functionality, please review and let us know.
thank you.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3819
Investigation Summary: JCO Payment Term values were affected when Payer Basic Account Code did not align with the Bill To account after account changes. Investigation confirmed that Payment Term and Payer Basic Account Code are populated from the Bill To Basic Account Code in the JC Header. The mapping was corrected so Payer and Sold To values synchronize with Bill To, validated in FDP UAT-1, and released to PROD.
Important Findings: ['Payment Term and Payer Basic Account Code are populated based on the Bill To Basic Account Code selected in the JC Header.', 'JCOs with missing Payment Term had a different Payer Basic Account Code than JCOs without the issue.', 'If the Payer Account Code is invalid, Payment Term can be blank because the value cannot be referenced from Account Code (AR).', 'Payer Code and Name are sourced from Bill To Customer.', 'All Sold To values also needed to be mapped to Bill To because Sold To fields are hidden in the FDP version.', 'The fix could not be reproduced in UAT after deployment and was released to PROD on 26 June.']
Root Cause: Payer Basic Account Code and Sold To values were not consistently mapped/synchronized to the Bill To account in the JC, causing Payment Term lookup failures when the Payer Account Code differed from or was invalid for the Bill To account.
Resolution: Updated the FDP UAT-1 mapping so Payer To and Sold To values synchronize with Bill To of the JC; the validated fix was released to PROD on 26 June.
Technical Entities: ['JCO', 'Payment Term', 'Payer Basic Account Code', 'Bill To Basic Account Code', 'JC Header', 'Account Code (AR)', 'Bill To Customer', 'Payer Code', 'Payer Name', 'Sold To', 'Payer To', 'FDP UAT-1', 'UAT-2', 'UAT', 'PROD', 'Chugoku-PROD', 'I000053798', 'I000184372', 'I000182228', 'I039034531', 'K050206969', 'MFTBCFFR-3917', 'Payer Mapping Change(Bill To Customer Code).xlsx']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3818
Investigation Summary: Individual invoice generation failed for JCO# I050019559 because the Branch Code used for issuance did not match the creator's Primary Branch Code. The behavior was confirmed as consistent with current functionality and similar to MFTBCFFR-3534. The incident was rejected as no product defect was identified.
Important Findings: ['JCO# I050019559 was created by user D8TKANEM.', "The creator's Primary Branch Code was UG.", 'Individual invoice issuance used Branch Code 7331, mapped to UF, which did not match UG.', 'The Branch Code mismatch caused individual invoice generation to fail.', 'A blank Closed Date does not affect individual invoice issuance.', 'The behavior is consistent with current functionality and similar to MFTBCFFR-3534.']
Root Cause: The Branch Code used to generate the individual invoice (7331 → UF) did not match the JCO creator's Primary Branch Code (UG).
Resolution: No system change was made; the incident was rejected because the behavior was working as per current functionality.
Technical Entities: ['MFTBCFFR-3818', 'MFTBCFFR-3534', 'JCO# I050019559', 'D8TKANEM', 'Primary Branch Code', 'UG', 'Branch Code', '7331', 'UF', 'individual invoice', 'Closed Date']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3807
Investigation Summary: During migration to FDP-Chugoku, duplicate vehicle records with the same VIN/Fuso Reception Number caused the first matching vehicle to be mapped to Purchase Orders instead of the correct vehicle. The incorrect mapping to Chassis Orders prevented creation of Recycle Fee Orders and Pool Cost Orders. Recovery required correcting vehicle mappings, executing TOB files, restoring related Chassis, Sales, and Body Orders, and resolving a duplicate recycle fee order; final verification reported no further recovery required.
Important Findings: ['SC data was confirmed correct; the issue occurred during migration to FDP-Chugoku.', 'Serial numbers were identified from Purchase Orders, and duplicate vehicle data caused the first vehicle with the same VIN to be selected regardless of SC data.', 'Incorrect vehicle-to-Chassis Order mapping resulted in missing Recycle Fee Orders and Pool Cost Orders.', 'Recovery initially updated only Chassis Orders; affected Sales Orders and Body Orders also required recovery.', 'A remaining record had conflicting model codes FK62FK4J, FQ62FU6B, and FK65FK4, with product code 012 identified as invalid/garbage data.', 'A duplicate recycle fee order was identified and recovered.']
Root Cause: A data-migration matching issue: duplicate vehicle records with the same VIN/Fuso Reception Number caused the first matching vehicle to be linked to Purchase Orders and Chassis Orders instead of the correct vehicle.
Resolution: Correct vehicle records were re-linked to affected Chassis Orders, TOB files were executed, related Sales Orders and Body Orders were recovered, and the duplicate recycle fee order was recovered. The recovered records were subsequently verified and reported as requiring no further recovery.
Technical Entities: ['SC', 'SC Prod', 'FDP-Chugoku', 'Purchase Orders', 'Chassis Orders', 'Sales Orders', 'Body Orders', 'Recycle Fee Orders', 'Pool Cost Orders', 'TOB files', 'D21G file', 'VIN', 'Fuso Reception Number', 'vehicle data', 'serial number', 'model code', 'product code', 'FK62FK4J', 'FQ62FU6B', 'FK65FK4', '012', 'C/#', '295612', '295565', '295982', '295365', '295512', '285024', '295978', '295364', '295576', '295335']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3797
Investigation Summary: Purchase Orders were created by user D8NOOSHI, who belongs to the Headquarter division and therefore had no Branch Code. Because the Journal Voucher Department Code is derived from the Branch Code, it was blank. Recovery was completed by setting Branch Code to 10, and the user was to update the employee master.
Important Findings: ['User D8NOOSHI is part of the Headquarter division and did not have a Branch Code.', 'The Journal Voucher Department Code is populated from the Branch Code.', 'Blank Branch Code caused the Department Code in the Journal Voucher to be blank.', 'Recovery was performed by setting Branch Code to 10 for the affected records.', 'The issue was determined not to be a system issue; the employee master required updating.']
Root Cause: User D8NOOSHI's employee master did not contain a Branch Code because the user belongs to the Headquarter division, resulting in a blank Journal Voucher Department Code derived from that Branch Code.
Resolution: Set Branch Code to 10 for the affected records and update the user's employee master.
Technical Entities: ['Purchase Orders', 'JIRA', 'D8NOOSHI', 'Headquarter division', 'Branch Code', 'Department Code', 'Journal Voucher', 'employee master', 'KB']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3791
Investigation Summary: Journal vouchers (JV) were missing for Chassis Orders migrated from SC to Chugoku Production. The Siebel Job that creates JVs did not select the migrated orders because their Batch RF Status was "Sent to Create RF", which is not included in the job's filter criteria. The affected orders were recovered, and JVs will be created automatically for remaining orders once their status becomes "Shipment Instructed".
Important Findings: ['The JV creation process is executed by a Siebel Job for Chassis Orders.', 'The Siebel Job selects orders with Status = "Shipment Instructed" and Batch RF Status in ("Send Shipment to RF", "Send Create to RF", "").', 'Orders migrated from SC to Chugoku Production had Batch RF Status "Sent to Create RF", so they were excluded from JV creation.', '383 missing-GR JV records were identified and provided in the recovery attachment.', 'JV creation under the existing logic applies only to orders with Status = "Shipment Instructed".']
Root Cause: Migrated Chassis Orders from SC to Chugoku Production had Batch RF Status "Sent to Create RF", which did not match the Siebel Job filter values for JV creation.
Resolution: Recovery was completed for the affected orders. Remaining orders will generate JVs automatically after their status is updated to "Shipment Instructed".
Technical Entities: ['JV', 'Chassis Orders', 'Chassis GR', 'Siebel Job', 'Status', 'Batch RF Status', 'Shipment Instructed', 'Send Shipment to RF', 'Send Create to RF', 'Sent to Create RF', 'SC', 'Chugoku', 'Chugoku Production', 'VIN']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3791
Timestamp: 2025-04-15T06:20:00
Author: Shivam
Comment: Thank you for your continued support.
We have checked the issue and found the following:
RCA: The JV for Chassis Orders is created by a Siebel Job that filter orders based on Status and Batch RF Status.
The conditions used to filter the orders are:
Status = 'Shipment Instructed'
Batch RF Status in ("Send Shipment to RF", "Send Create to RF", "")
Since the orders migrated from SC to Chugoku had Batch RF Status 'Sent to Create RF', these orders were not picked up when the Siebel Job was executed.
We have attached the list of migrated Chassis Orders along with their current status in Chugoku Production.
We will recover all the listed orders. However, as per the current logic, JV will only be created for orders with Status = 'Shipment Instructed'.
For the others, the JV will be created automatically once their status is updated to 'Shipment Instructed'.
Best Regards,
Shivam

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3782
Investigation Summary: TOB transmissions triggered after 5:00 PM JST could receive no TOB response, preventing Siebel from identifying the asynchronous transaction as failed and retrying it the following morning. The issue was observed across multiple FDP records and had a similar incident in SC. A countermeasure was developed in UAT1 to retrigger records with completed interfaces but no TOB response, but no completed UAT, production deployment, or final resolution was confirmed.
Important Findings: ['Normally, TOB triggers sent after 5:00 PM JST are not accepted and result in a Siebel asynchronous-transaction failure.', 'For affected records, TOB did not return a response, so Siebel did not mark the record as failed and the next-day batch job did not retrigger it.', 'The behavior was observed across multiple records in all FDP environments and was also associated with an incident in SC: INC4990796.', 'The proposed countermeasure is to retrigger records for which the interface is completed but no TOB response is received.', 'The retrigger logic must avoid resubmission on days when TOB is not open, such as Sundays.', 'Development of the proposed fix was completed in UAT1, but UAT completion and deployment were not confirmed.']
Root Cause: TOB did not return a response for requests triggered after 5:00 PM JST. As a result, Siebel did not classify the asynchronous transaction as failed, so its next-day batch job did not resend the affected records.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3782
Timestamp: 2026-05-14T23:49:00
Author: Soham Modi
Comment: Thanks for your support.
Regarding this issue, when Siebel sends a request to the TOB system, we have observed scenarios where TOB does not return a response.
In the normal process flow, TOB does not accept triggers from the Siebel side after 5:00 PM JST. If a trigger is sent to TOB after 5:00 PM JST and not accepted by TOB then the corresponding records fail in the asynchronous transaction on the Siebel side. Subsequently, a Siebel batch job runs on the next day and reprocesses all failed records by resending them to TOB.
However, in this particular case, the request was accepted by TOB, and no response was received from the TOB side. As a result, the record was not identified as failed on the Siebel side and therefore was not retriggered by the batch job on the next morning as expected.
Kindly review the above and let us know the next action required from the Cubastion side.
Please let us know in case of any queries or if any additional information is required from our side.
Best Regards,
Soham Modi

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3779
Investigation Summary: The incident involved Journal Vector (JV) creating non-taxable line items when the related Sales Price was "0", including after Change Order processing. Initial UAT1 fixes addressed re-edit and Price Change scenarios, but validation found the issue persisted for Payer Change and Price and Payer Change scenarios. The additional fix was validated in UAT-1, and the incident was deployed to PROD on 12 June 2025.
Important Findings: ['For taxable Account Codes, all line items are taxable, but Change Order (Price Change) could generate Non-Tax Line Items with a value of "Zero" in the Journal Vector.', 'The initial UAT1 correction passed JC Close, JC Close And Re-Edit, and JC Close And Change Order (Price Change) scenarios for both Tax and Non-Tax cases.', 'UAT-1 validation found [Service Correction Sales Amount Non-Taxable] line items were still created when Sales Price was "0" for Payer Change and Price and Payer Change scenarios.', 'After the follow-up fix, Payer Change scenarios no longer created a JV line item when Sales Price was "0".', 'UAT was completed and the fix was released to PROD on 12 June 2025.']
Root Cause: The zero-value line-item suppression did not cover Change Order workflows involving Payer Change or Price and Payer Change, allowing [Service Correction Sales Amount Non-Taxable] JV line items to be created when Sales Price was "0".
Resolution: Updated the UAT1/UAT-1 fix to suppress JV line-item creation for zero Sales Price in Payer Change scenarios; the correction was validated in UAT and deployed to PROD on 12 June 2025.
Technical Entities: ['UAT1', 'UAT-01', 'UAT-1', 'PROD', 'Journal Vector', 'JV', 'Account Codes', 'Change Order', 'Price Change', 'Payer Change', 'Price and Payer Change', 'Sales Price', 'Service Correction Sales Amount Non-Taxable', 'JC Close', 'JC Close And Re-Edit', 'JC Close And Change Order', 'I001295240', 'I001295241', 'I001295232', 'I001295233', 'I001295234', 'K001295249', 'I001295235', 'K001295251', 'I001295236', 'K001295254', 'I001295237', 'K001295256', 'I001295238', 'K001295258', 'I001295239', 'K001295260']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3765
Investigation Summary: Chassis Price was not displayed in Aomori Production while pricing was available in UAT2. Investigation confirmed that the affected Production pricing/master data was absent because the final Production model-code file did not include the required model code. The affected Production record was recovered and a file was executed to align Production pricing with UAT; subsequent UAT2 alignment with Production was identified as requiring a separate SR.
Important Findings: ['The initial issue was caused by the absence of the Price Master for the affected Chassis in Aomori Prod.', 'The affected Production record was recovered; model code FED90K74S00H could not be found in the files previously executed on Aomori Prod.', 'The January 2024 UAT setup file included model code FED90G73S00H, but the final Production file shared in July 2024 did not include it.', 'The file executed in Aomori Production through SR MFTBCFFR-3780 contained updated model-code pricing, creating a pricing difference with UAT2.', 'Production setup files were agreed to be applied only to Production; applying them to UAT requires a separate service request.']
Root Cause: The final model-code file supplied for the Aomori Production setup did not include the required model code/pricing data, while the earlier UAT setup file did.
Resolution: The affected Aomori Production record was recovered and the relevant file was executed, aligning Production model-code pricing with UAT. Any subsequent UAT2 update to match Production was to be requested through a separate SR.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3763
Investigation Summary: The request concerned applying the "Do Not Print" feature to real-time invoices. Analysis confirmed that "Do Not Print" was deployed to FDP during FDP Okayama sprint development, but no requirement was provided to apply it to Cubastion real-time invoice functionality. The request was classified as an additional requirement rather than a defect and requires a Change Request (CR).
Important Findings: ['The "Do Not Print" feature was applied to FDP during FDP Okayama sprint development.', 'The business team was coordinating Cubastion and real-time invoice capabilities at the time of deployment.', 'No requirement was provided to apply "Do Not Print" functionality to real-time invoices.', 'The reported behavior was confirmed not to be a bug.', 'Implementing the feature for real-time invoices requires a Change Request (CR).']
Root Cause: "Do Not Print" functionality was not included in the requirements for Cubastion real-time invoices.
Resolution: Ticket rejected as not a bug; submit a Change Request (CR) if "Do Not Print" functionality is required for real-time invoices.
Technical Entities: ['Do Not Print', 'FDP', 'FDP Okayama', 'Cubastion', 'real-time invoice', 'Change Request', 'CR']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3750
Investigation Summary: Commission fee and tax calculations were triggered when "Create Spreadsheet" was selected for a Liability Order. The button could be enabled through the Clerical Error workflow before "Vehicle Liability Insurance Certificate Issue Date" had a valid value, creating incorrect commission details. The enablement logic was updated in UAT, recovery JVs were processed and linked to KB, and the fix was released to production on April 24.
Important Findings: ['Commission calculation occurs when the "Create Spreadsheet" button is clicked within an order.', '"Vehicle Liability Insurance Certificate Issue Date" is populated when "Liability Insurance Policy #" is entered on the order.', 'The issue was reproduced on UAT8 using liability order Q050023214 by setting the order to "Liability Clerical Error", clearing the Clerical error flag, and then creating a Liability Spreadsheet.', 'The "Create Spreadsheet" button was enabled without requiring a valid "Vehicle Liability Insurance Certificate Issue Date".', 'Recovery required creation of Reverse JV and Correctr JV with the posting date set to the current date; the JVs were linked to KB through the nightly batch.', '"Create Spreadsheet" is visible only in the My Branch and All Insurance Orders views under Liability Order, and testing used user D0X20922.']
Root Cause: The "Create Spreadsheet" button could be enabled through the "Liability Clerical Error" workflow while "Vehicle Liability Insurance Certificate Issue Date" was not valid, allowing commission calculation to run with incomplete order data.
Resolution: Updated the "Create Spreadsheet" enablement condition to require a valid "Vehicle Liability Insurance Certificate Issue Date". The fix was validated in UAT, recovery Reverse JV and Correctr JV entries were linked to KB, and the change was deployed to production in the April 24 scheduled release.
Technical Entities: ['Create Spreadsheet', 'Vehicle Liability Insurance Certificate Issue Date', 'Liability Insurance Policy #', 'Liability Insurance Opportunity', 'Liability Insuracne Quote', 'Liability Order', 'Clerical error flag', 'Liability Clerical Error', 'Liability Spreadsheet', 'Q050023214', 'UAT8', 'UAT1', 'UAT', 'production environment', 'Reverse JV', 'Correctr JV', 'Posting date', 'KB', 'nightly batch', 'D0X20922', 'My Branch', 'All Insurance Orders']

Timestamp: 2025-04-07T10:28:00
Author: Shivam
Comment: Thanks for your continued support.
RCA: The calculation of the commission is being done when we click the "Create Spreadsheet" button in the order.
 Based on current logic, if the "Vehicle Liability Insurance Certificate Issue Date" is null, the commission fee and tax calculation is done correctly.
 This field gets populated once the "Liability Insurance Policy #" is filled in the order.
To replicate the issue, we created the liability order Q050023214 on UAT8 and followed the steps below:
 1. Create an Liability Insuracne Opportunity.
 2. Create an Liability Insuracne Quote.
 3. Create an Liability Order.
 4. Check the clerical error flag In Order.
 5. Now change the Status of Order to "Liability Clerical Error".
 6. Now uncheck the clerical error flag In Order.
 7. Now the button of "Create Spreadsheet" is enable.
 8. Now Create the Liability Spreadsheet through "Create Spreadsheet" button.
Now We get the commission fee details same Chugoku Production Order.
Fix Plan: We recommend adding one more condition to enable the "Create Spreadsheet" button — the "Vehicle Liability Insurance Certificate Issue Date" should have a valid value before the button is enabled.
Kindly validate the RCA and approve the fix plan. 
Please let us know if any recovery is required. 
Best Regards,
 Shivam

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3743
Investigation Summary: Negative-amount TOB invoice JV records were present but were not processed or created in the system. Investigation identified an overlap between RCR and KB batch processing on Chugoku caused primarily by high data volume. Affected records were recovered, and the FDP-Chugoku DT-01 processing schedule was moved earlier to provide sufficient time for DT-01 processing and JV creation.
Important Findings: ['JV for negative-amount TOB invoices was not created although the underlying data existed in the system.', 'The unprocessed records were associated with overlapping RCR and KB batch processing on Chugoku.', 'The overlap was primarily driven by a large volume of data.', 'Affected records were recovered and shared through email and the night batch.', 'FDP-Chugoku DT-01 file processing was changed from 7:00 PM JST to 6:00 PM JST.']
Root Cause: RCR and KB batch processing overlapped on Chugoku due primarily to large data volume, preventing timely processing and JV creation for negative-amount TOB invoices.
Resolution: Recovered the affected records and moved FDP-Chugoku DT-01 file processing from 7:00 PM JST to 6:00 PM JST to allow sufficient time for DT-01 processing and JV creation.
Technical Entities: ['JV', 'TOB invoice', 'RCR', 'KB batch processing', 'Chugoku', 'FDP-Chugoku', 'DT-01 file', 'night batch']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3729
Investigation Summary: AR# H000109757 and multiple other AR# records were excluded from aggregated Power BI visuals because X_REPAIR_COST was null in both Warehouse DB and Siebel DB. Power BI SUM aggregation ignored null values rather than treating them as zero. Power BI logic was updated to replace null X_REPAIR_COST values with 0, validated in UAT1 for the PBI UV2_01 report, and released to production on April 14.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3718
Investigation Summary: Price updates were missing for material ZC116610 and several other parts in FDP Okayama. ZC116610 was absent from the D2S Material Master file for FDPs that had been updated on SC-PROD on March 13. The missing part was exported from SC, all FDP environments were updated with prices, and the remaining affected prices were updated in Okayama-PROD.
Important Findings: ['ZC116610 was not displayed in Material master because it was missing from the D2S Material Master file for FDPs.', 'The affected D2S Material Master file had been updated on SC-PROD on March 13.', 'Only FDP Okayama had not updated prices for the reported list of parts.', 'The missing D2S part was exported from SC and all FDP environments were updated along with prices.', 'Remaining affected part prices were updated in Okayama-PROD.']
Root Cause: Part ZC116610 was missing from the D2S Material Master file for FDPs, preventing its display in Material master and application of its price.
Resolution: Exported the missing D2S part from SC, updated all FDP environments with the part and prices, and updated the remaining affected prices in Okayama-PROD.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3711
Investigation Summary: A JV was not sent to KB because its credit and debit Department Code was set to "10V1", derived from the order Shop Code. "10V1" was absent from KB Department Code Mapping, preventing the JV from linking to KB. The required mappings were added, remaining attached shop codes were mapped to 0001, and the recovery JV was sent through the KB batch.
Important Findings: ['The credit and debit Department Code "10V1" was derived from the order Shop Code.', '"10V1" was not present in KB Department Code Mapping, so the JV was not linked to KB.', 'SR MFTBCFFR-3727 was created and completed to add the required mapping in Prod.', 'All remaining attached shop codes were mapped to 0001.', 'The recovery JV for "10V1" was processed through the KB batch with posting date 04/APR/2025.']
Root Cause: The order-derived Shop Code "10V1" was used as the credit and debit Department Code but did not exist in KB Department Code Mapping, preventing the JV from being linked and sent to KB.
Resolution: Added the required Department Code/shop-code mappings in Prod, mapped the remaining attached shop codes to 0001, and reprocessed and sent the "10V1" recovery JV to KB.
Technical Entities: ['JV', 'KB', 'Department Code', 'Credit and Debit Department Code', 'Shop Code', '10V1', 'KB Department Code Mapping', 'Chugoku', 'SR MFTBCFFR-3727', 'Prod', '0001', 'KB batch', '04/APR/2025']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3706
Investigation Summary: A job card of type "51: Complaint" could become linked to a new vehicle order by first creating it as "22: New car modification (movement)", linking the order, and then changing the JC Type before completion. The investigation confirmed that the relevant internal-order fields were retained when the JC Type changed. A Service Job Card fix was implemented in FDP UAT1, validated, and released to Production on 13 September.
Important Findings: ['"51: Complaint" job cards cannot be directly linked to a new car order by design.', 'New vehicle order A000121450 was linked by creating a "22: New car modification (movement)" job card, setting the new car order in the internal order field, and changing the JC Type to "51: Claim" before completion.', 'The system allowed the linkage because internal-order values persisted after the JC Type was changed.', 'The fix resets "Internal Order (Charge To)" and "Internal Order Number" whenever the JC Type is changed.', 'UAT-1 validation confirmed that changing JC Type from "22" to another type, including "26", correctly resets the values.', 'The fix was released to Production in the 13 September scheduled FDP release.']
Root Cause: Service Job Card did not reset the internal-order fields when the JC Type was changed, allowing a new car order linked under JC Type "22: New car modification (movement)" to remain linked after changing the job card to "51: Claim".
Resolution: Implemented a Service Job Card change to reset "Internal Order (Charge To)" and "Internal Order Number" whenever the JC Type changes; validated in FDP UAT1/UAT-1 and deployed to Production on 13 September.
Technical Entities: ['MFTBCFFR-3706', 'Service Job Card', 'JC Type', '51: Complaint', '51: Claim', '22: New car modification (movement)', '26', 'new car order', 'new vehicle order A000121450', 'Internal Order (Charge To)', 'Internal Order Number', 'UAT', 'FDP UAT1', 'UAT-1', 'Production', 'Prod', 'FDP', 'SC', 'AMS CR']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3702
Investigation Summary: Sales approval was blocked because no Recycle Fee order was mapped to the Sales Order for C# 10360. Investigation confirmed that TOB did not send the D21F file, so no Recycle Fee order was created; only D21A, D21R, and D21N files were received. Recovery was completed and Sales Posting was completed without a recycling order. The reported “major component is missing” message was considered inappropriate for this rare scenario and will be monitored for recurrence.
Important Findings: ['No D21F file was received for C# 10360.', 'Only D21A, D21R, and D21N files were received for C# 10360.', 'Without a D21F file, no Recycle Fee order was created or mapped to the Sales Order.', 'During Generate Approval/Request Approval, Siebel validates whether a Recycle Fee order is mapped to the Sales Order; this behavior is the same as SC.', 'The “major component is missing” error message was reported as incorrect when the Recycle Fee order does not exist.', 'The case was considered rare; corrective measures will be considered if similar incidents recur.']
Root Cause: TOB did not provide the D21F file for C# 10360, so no Recycle Fee order was created or mapped to the Sales Order.
Resolution: Recovery was completed, allowing delivery approval and Sales Posting to complete without a recycling order. The incident was closed with monitoring for recurrence.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3672
Investigation Summary: A Payer Change Order retained the previous Closed Date after the user changed the Bill to Basic Account, causing bulk invoice data to be excluded from the expected closing-date processing and sent to KB at EOM instead. The issue was reproduced and fixed in FDP UAT-1, where Closed Date and Payment Term now update based on the newly selected payer. The fix was validated in UAT-1 and released to PROD on 12 June 2025.
Important Findings: ['For Account 0000205096, Change Order K000065493 retained an EOM closing date although the account closing date was 25.', 'In a Payer Change Order, Bill to Basic Account and Ship to Basic Account are initially retrieved from JCO.', 'Changing the payer in Bill to Basic Account did not refresh Closed Date or Payment Term; the prior values remained on the change order.', 'Because Closed Date remained EOM rather than 25, the change order was not sent to KB with the expected bulk invoice data; JC lines and change order lines were sent on 31 March.', 'The corrected behavior was verified in UAT-1 for Payer Change and Payer and Price Change scenarios.']
Root Cause: When the payer was changed in Bill to Basic Account on a Payer Change Order, the system did not update Closed Date and Payment Term from the newly selected payer, leaving the previous EOM Closed Date on the change order.
Resolution: Updated FDP so that changing the payer in Bill to Basic Account on a Service Change Order refreshes Closed Date and Payment Term according to the new payer. The fix was deployed to FDP UAT-1, validated, and released to PROD on 12 June 2025; recovery bulk invoice data was also shared with MDIS after approval.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3672
Timestamp: 2025-04-21T01:57:00
Author: Divyesh Ghiya
Comment: Thank you for your support.
We have investigated this issue thoroughly and below are our findings:
When user creates a Payer Change Order, values in Bill to Basic Account and Ship to basic account is fetched from JCO. Then user changes the payer in Bill to Basic Account and values in Closed Date and Payment term should be reflected according to new Payer entered. But when user enters the value in Bill to basic account, the closed date field value is not updated and old value remains in the change order. Because of this, closed date was not changed to 25 in the change order and hence not sent to KB. Since the date was EOM, all the JC lines and change order lines were sent to KB on EOM(31st March).
Fix Plan: We will fix this issue where closed date will be updated when user enters the new payer in Bill to basic account. We will share the fix on UAT1 by 24th April. 
Meanwhile, please let us know if you have any query or need any additional information.
Regards,
Divyesh Ghiya

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3672
Timestamp: 2025-04-21T05:35:00
Comment: Mr. Miyauchi,
Thank you for your continued support.
Problem summary:
When a user creates a payer change order, the "Bill to Basic Account" and "Ship to Basic Account" values are retrieved from the JCO. If the user subsequently enters a different payer in the Bill to Basic Account, the Closed Date and Payment Term must be updated based on the newly entered payer.
However, currently, when a user enters a new payer in the "Bill to Basic Account", the "Closed Date" value is not updated and the change order remains with the previous value.
As a result, in this case, the "Closed Date" was not updated to "25" and was not reflected in the change order, so the data was not sent to KB. All JC lines and change order lines were sent to KB on March 31st as the original closing date was the end of the month (EOM).
Modification plan:
We will correct this issue so that the "Closed Date" will be updated correctly when a new payer is entered in the "Bill to Basic Account".
This fix will be released to the UAT1 environment by April 24th.
If you have any questions or require additional information, please feel free to contact us.
Thank you very much for your support.

Resolution: Added the missing stock order creation logic, validated replenishment-order creation through a batch-job test in FDP UAT-1, and deployed the fix to production in an urgent release on March 27.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3650
Investigation Summary: The incident involved incorrect Credit and Debit Department Code assignment in PO GR JV for Trade-In purchase orders. The existing logic used the NV Sales Order Last Approver, but the required logic for NV Trade-In is to derive the Branch Code from the NV Sales Order Sales Rep. The fix was validated in UAT1, affected JVs were recovered, and the change was released to Production on April 24.
Important Findings: ['The original PO GR JV logic assigned Credit and Debit Department Code based on the NV Sales Order Last Approver/PO creator.', 'For NV Trade-In, both Credit and Debit Department Code must be set from the Branch Code of the NV Sales Order Sales Rep.', 'The fix was implemented in UAT1 and UAT passed with AR#H000046387 and PO# F001294580.', 'Alternate approver D0X20883 received the NV Sales Order approval request for Sales Rep D0X20897; approving the order created the Trade-In PO with D0X20883 as creator.', 'UV Trade-In does not require this fix because the department code on the JV Trade-In line is derived from the Assessment request, not the UV Sales Order final approval.', 'Affected JVs were recovered before the Production release.']
Root Cause: The NV Trade-In PO GR JV department-code logic incorrectly derived Credit and Debit Department Code from the NV Sales Order Last Approver instead of the NV Sales Order Sales Rep Branch Code.
Resolution: Updated the NV Trade-In PO GR JV logic to set Credit and Debit Department Code from the NV Sales Order Sales Rep Branch Code, validated the change in UAT1, recovered affected JVs, and released the fix to Production on April 24.
Technical Entities: ['Trade-In PO', 'PO GR JV', 'Credit Department Code', 'Debit Department Code', 'Department Code', 'NV Sales Order', 'NV Trade-In', 'UV Trade-In', 'UV Sales Order', 'UV Trade-In Purchase Order', 'Assessment request', 'Last Approver', 'Sales Rep', 'Branch Code', 'UAT1', 'Production', 'F000016673', 'D0X20897', 'D0X20883', 'A001294185', 'AR#H000046387', 'PO# F001294580', 'JV Trade-In line', 'PO - AP PostingUV Purchase Order', 'CSJS200', 'CSJS300']

Resolution: The recycle fee order was recovered, enabling the user to resend it to TOB. No permanent corrective change or preventive fix plan was documented.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3642
Investigation Summary: Sales Posting approval failed for Sales Orders whose associated account address lacked a city code, causing Falcon-side validation errors. The failure could leave approval history marked "Approved" and create a Planned Pool Cost - Shipment Order even though the final Inbox approval was not completed. Recovery removed the existing shipment order and required completion of customer address data; the MFTBCFFR-3641-equivalent fix was deployed to UAT and production on April 14.
Important Findings: ['The root cause matched MFTBCFFR-3641: the account used by the Sales Order had no city code in its address.', 'Error logs reported: "The following fields are required: Account, Account Code, Account Code, Account Code, Account Code, Account Code, Postal Code, Primary Postal Code Date (SBL-BPR-00131)".', 'During second Sales Posting approval in Inbox, a pop-up error prevented the Inbox item from becoming "Approved," while approval history could show "Approved" and the order could move to "Sales Posting Completed."', 'Rejecting and regenerating approval after the failure could create duplicate Planned Pool Cost - Shipment Orders.', 'Orders with null account address information error on the Falcon side; mandatory customer address fields, including "City County Name" and "OOAZA Name", must be populated before processing.', 'The existing Pool Cost Shipment was removed during recovery, and a reverse JV was created.']
Root Cause: Missing city code/address information in the customer account associated with the Sales Order caused Falcon-side mandatory-field validation errors during Sales Posting approval.
Resolution: Applied the MFTBCFFR-3641-equivalent fix in UAT and deployed it to production on April 14. The recovery removed the existing Pool Cost Shipment, created a reverse JV, and required the customer account address details to be completed before regenerating and approving Sales Posting.
Technical Entities: ['MFTBCFFR-3641', 'UAT 6', 'UAT', 'production environment', 'Falcon', 'Sales Order', 'Opportunity', 'quote', 'Sales Posting', 'Inbox', 'Generate Approval', 'Planned Pool Cost - Shipment Order', 'Pool Cost Shipment', 'Sales Posting Completed', 'Customer Account', 'Account', 'Account Code', 'Postal Code', 'Primary Postal Code Date', 'City County Name', 'OOAZA Name', 'SBL-BPR-00131', 'reverse JV', 'KB', 'A000026083', '0000032930']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3642
Timestamp: 2025-03-25T02:32:00
Author: Ujjwal Goel
Comment: Dear Tsunoda-san,
After analyzing the issue, we have determined that RCA of this jira is same as MFTBCFFR 3641 that there is no city code in the address associated with the account used in the Sales Order.
We have replicated the issue on UAT 6 (Sales Order: A000026083). Below are the steps to replicate the issue:
Step 1: Create an Opportunity with Account code: 0000032930.
Step 2: Create and approve the quote.
Step 3: Create a Sales Order for the respective quote and approve the Sales Order.
Step 4: During the approval process for the Sales Posting of the Sales Order, when you attempt to approve the second approval from the Inbox, you will encounter a pop-up error. As a result, you will not be able to change the status to "Approved."
Step 5: Despite the inability to approve the Inbox, the Sales Order’s approval status in the approval history will show as "Approved," a Planned Pool Cost - Shipment Order will be created, and the status of your Order will change to "Sales Posting Completed."
Step 6: In the Inbox, when you reject the approval, the order status will change to "Rejected." You can then generate approvals again. If you repeat the process from Step 4, you will notice multiple Planned Pool Cost - Shipment Orders being generated.
Error Message in error logs : The following fields are required: Account, Account Code, Account Code, Account Code, Account Code, Account Code, Postal Code, Primary Postal Code Date (SBL-BPR-00131)
Proposed Fix: To address this issue, we will ensure that the pop-up error currently encountered during the inbox approval process will be triggered when clicking "Generate Approval."
Please let us know if you need further clarification or assistance.
Best regards,
Ujjwal Goel
