investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3641
Investigation Summary: Incomplete address data on the account used by the NV Quote/Sales Order caused an approval-processing error while downstream processing still marked approval as completed and generated duplicate Planned Pool Cost - Shipment Orders and JVs. The affected account address is the account selected in the Contractor Name field, whose address is sent to Falcon. Duplicate JVs and Falcon records were recovered, and validation was implemented in NV Quote to prevent approval generation when the selected contractor account has incomplete address data. The validated fix was released to PROD on April 14.
Important Findings: ['The original failure was reproduced on UAT 6 with Sales Order A000026083 and customer code 0000032930.', 'During the second Sales Posting approval from Inbox, an error prevented Inbox approval, but approval history showed Approved, the order moved to Sales Posting Completed, and a Planned Pool Cost - Shipment Order was created.', 'Rejecting the Inbox approval and regenerating approvals could create multiple Planned Pool Cost - Shipment Orders and duplicate JVs.', 'The account address data used by the Sales Order was incomplete; missing city code/address fields, including Oaza/Common Name for account 0000029653, triggered the issue.', "Validation checks only the address of the account selected in the Contractor Name field because Falcon sends that account's address data.", 'Recovery included unmapping Pool Cost Shipment orders, creating reverse JVs for duplicate JVs, resolving a Data set separator-related JV error for KB transmission, and completing Falcon recovery after customer master updates.']
Root Cause: Incomplete or null address fields on the account selected in the Contractor Name field for the NV Quote/Sales Order, including missing city code and Oaza/Common Name, caused the approval-processing error.
Resolution: Implemented NV Quote validation on the Request Approval/Generate Approval action to block processing when the Contractor Name account has incomplete address information, with the message: "Please check the business partner master of the user selected in the business partner name. The customer address in the business partner master is a required field." The fix was validated in UAT and released to PROD on April 14; duplicate JVs were reversed and Falcon recovery was completed.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3639
Investigation Summary: Duplicate JVs were created for a JC linked to Sales Order#: Q050057080 because a spreadsheet could be approved, later manually changed to "Cancelled", and replaced with another approved spreadsheet. JV creation is triggered when "Spreadsheet Status" changes to "Spreadsheet Approved". A reverse JV was created for the JV generated from the cancelled spreadsheet, and the UI validation was deployed to production on April 14.
Important Findings: ['A JV for Liability Orders is created when "Spreadsheet Status" changes to "Spreadsheet Approved".', 'The "Spreadsheet Status" field remained editable after approval, allowing an approved spreadsheet to be manually changed to "Cancelled".', 'Spreadsheet 11SCS-17-24-00052-01 was approved and later cancelled; its approval had already created a JV.', 'Spreadsheet 11SCS-17-24-00052-02 was subsequently created and approved for the same JC, creating another JV.', 'A reverse JV was created for the JV generated by spreadsheet 11SCS-17-24-00052-01.', 'The fix restricts editing of "Spreadsheet Status" to records whose status is "Spreadsheet Created".']
Root Cause: The "Spreadsheet Status" field was editable after "Spreadsheet Approved", allowing an approved spreadsheet to be cancelled and replaced with another approved spreadsheet, which triggered duplicate JV creation.
Resolution: Created a reverse JV for the JV generated by cancelled spreadsheet 11SCS-17-24-00052-01 and changed the UI so "Spreadsheet Status" is editable only when its value is "Spreadsheet Created". The fix was validated in UAT and deployed to the production environment on April 14.
Technical Entities: ['JV', 'Liability Orders', 'Spreadsheet Status', 'Spreadsheet Approved', 'Spreadsheet Created', 'Cancelled', 'JC', 'Sales Order#: Q050057080', '11SCS-17-24-00052-01', '11SCS-17-24-00052-02', 'reverse JV', 'UAT', 'production environment']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3633
Investigation Summary: A Body Building Order could be manually transitioned without required vendor information, resulting in a blank Vendor Finance Account Code on the Journal Voucher (JV). Initial UAT1 validation covered the "Pending" to "Ordered" transition, but testing identified that "Order changed" could still be selected without a bodybuilder/Vendor Name. Validation for both required vendor details was corrected, verified, and deployed to production in the April 14 urgent release.
Important Findings: ['The affected Body Building Order had a blank Vendor Finance Account Code, which caused the corresponding Journal Voucher (JV) value to be blank.', 'The issue was reproduced in UAT by manually changing a Body Building Order status from "Pending" to "Ordered" while "Vendor Finance Account Code" was null.', 'The initial UAT1 fix added a pop-up validation when changing status from "Pending" to "Ordered" with a blank "Vendor Finance Account Code".', 'Validation testing found that status "Order changed" could still be selected without a bodybuilder/Vendor Name for both Non-IBOS and IBOS workflows.', 'The final fix added Vendor Name validation equivalent to the validation used when executing "Generate Approvals" without Vendor Code.']
Root Cause: Manual status changes for Body Building Orders lacked validation for required vendor information, allowing transitions with blank Vendor Finance Account Code and, in the "Order changed" path, missing Vendor Name.
Resolution: Recovered the affected order and deployed validation preventing status changes when required Vendor Finance Account Code or Vendor Name is missing. The corrected validation was verified and applied to production in the April 14 urgent release.
Technical Entities: ['Body Building Order', 'Journal Voucher', 'JV', 'Vendor Finance Account Code', 'Vendor Name', 'Vendor Code', 'UAT', 'UAT1', 'PROD', 'production environment', 'Pending', 'Ordered', 'Order changed', 'Generate Approvals', 'Non-IBOS', 'IBOS', 'Acceptance inspection completed', 'Shipped', 'B001199127']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3629
Investigation Summary: On 19/March/2025, a D2S-side network failure caused affected Parts Purchase order allocations to be received in reverse, reverting Confirmed Qty to null and leaving D2S Shipments in Allocation Pending. The root cause was identified as an outbound idoc failure caused by an Internet communication error. All affected records were retriggered, including reprocessing the latest D2S allocations and pending shipments.
Important Findings: ['Affected Parts Purchase order responses from D2S for 19/March/2025 were delayed.', 'A D2S-side network failure caused allocations to be received in reverse order.', 'Reverse allocation processing caused Confirmed Qty to revert to null.', 'The outbound idoc failed due to an Internet communication error.', 'Affected records were retriggered; latest D2S allocations and D2S Shipments with Allocation Pending were reprocessed.']
Root Cause: The outbound idoc failed due to an Internet communication error.
Resolution: All affected records were retriggered, including reprocessing the latest D2S allocations to update Confirmed Qty and reprocessing D2S Shipments with Allocation Pending.
Technical Entities: ['D2S', 'Parts Purchase orders', 'Confirmed Qty', 'D2S Shipment', 'Allocation Pending', 'outbound idoc', 'Internet communication error', 'Okayama Prod', 'Aomori Prod', 'Iwate Pord', 'Shikoku Pord', 'Wakayama Prod', 'Chugoku Prod']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3622
Investigation Summary: Parts Internal Order list prices became null when parts were added through Sub Quote in NV Quote. Investigation reproduced the issue on UAT1 and established that the related NV Sales Order Start Price was set to null during Sub Quote completion. A fix was validated on UAT1 and deployed to PROD in the April 14 release.
Important Findings: ['Parts Internal Order list price is fetched from NV Sales Order.', 'Adding a part through Sub Quote in NV Quote caused the NV Sales Order Start Price to be set to null.', 'The issue was reproduced on UAT1 with NV Sales Order A001293389, part ###600SILVER, resulting in null list price on Parts Internal Order M001293390.', 'When parts are added through Parts and Intenal Work in an NV Quote line item, the list price is displayed; the issue occurred when creating the part order through Sub Quote.', 'The fix was verified on UAT1 using NV Sales Order A001293480 with parts ###600BLACK-5K and ###1003, creating Parts Internal Order M001293481.', 'The fix was applied to PROD in the April 14 release.']
Root Cause: During Sub Quote completion in NV Quote, the Start Price for the added part in NV Sales Order was set to null. Since Parts Internal Order list price is sourced from NV Sales Order, its list price also became null.
Resolution: Fixed the Sub Quote processing issue that set NV Sales Order Start Price to null; the fix was validated on UAT1 and deployed to PROD in the April 14 release.
Technical Entities: ['Parts Internal Order', 'NV Sales Order', 'NV Quote', 'Sub Quote', 'Start Price', 'List Price', 'UAT1', 'PROD', 'A001293389', 'M001293390', '###600SILVER', 'A001293480', 'M001293481', '###600BLACK-5K', '###1003', 'Parts and Intenal Work']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3622
Timestamp: 2025-03-26T12:13:00
Author: Divyesh Ghiya
Comment: Thank you for your support.
We have analyzed this issue thoroughly and below are our findings:
 The list price in Parts Internal Order is fetched from NV Sales Order. In NV Sales Order Start Price is set as null when user adds Part through sub quote in NV quote.
 We have replicated this issue on UAT1. For NV Sales Order A001293389, we added part ###600SILVER through sub quote in NV quote. When sub quote is completed , part is added in NV Quote, during this process Start price of the part is set as null which leads to null list price in Parts Internal Order (M001293390). 
We are working on the fix of this issue and will provide the fix on UAT1 by 31st March. Meanwhile, please let us know if you have any query.
Regards,
 Divyesh Ghiya

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3622
Timestamp: 2025-03-26T12:51:00
Comment: Mr. Tsunoda,
Thank you for your continued support.
As a result of detailed analysis of this problem, the following findings were obtained.
The list price for internal parts orders is taken from the new vehicle sales order (NV Sales Order). When you add a part using Sub Quote in a new car quote (NV Quote), the Start Price for the new car order is set to null.
I reproduced this problem in a UAT1 environment. Added part "###600SILVER" to NV Sales Order "A001293389" using sub-quote. After the subquote was completed, when the part was added to the NV quote, the starting price was set to null, which caused the list price for the part internal order (M001293390) to also be null.
We are currently working on a fix for this issue and plan to apply the fix to the UAT1 environment by March 31st. 
If you have any questions, please let us know.
Thank you very much for your support.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3617
Investigation Summary: A JV was created for Sales Order # Q050020683 but was not linked to KB because its Credit Department Code was set to "INTERNAL" from the Insurance Order. Investigation found that the Ejibai-created order inherited incorrect Sales Rep, Position, and Organization details from its linked existing order because it was created before Sales Rep recovery for migrated orders completed. Recovery JVs were created with Credit and Debit Department Code 3011 and sent to KB, and the affected order was recovered.
Important Findings: ['The JV was not linked to KB because its Credit Department Code was "INTERNAL", sourced from the Insurance Order.', 'Sales Rep recovery for all migrated orders was completed on February 17, 2025.', 'Sales Order # Q050020683 was created through Ejibai on February 13, 2025, before the Sales Rep recovery completed.', 'Ejibai order-creation logic retrieves Sales Rep details from the linked existing order, causing incorrect Sales Rep, Position, and Organization details to be inherited.', 'Recovery JV processing used Credit Department Code 3011 and Debit Department Code 3011.']
Root Cause: Sales Order # Q050020683 was created through Ejibai before Sales Rep recovery for migrated orders completed, so it inherited incorrect Sales Rep, Position, and Organization details from its linked existing order; the resulting JV had Credit Department Code "INTERNAL" from the Insurance Order and could not link to KB.
Resolution: Created recovery JVs using Credit Department Code 3011 and Debit Department Code 3011, sent them to KB, and recovered the affected order.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3616
Investigation Summary: The affected record was recovered, but the incident was rare and could not be reproduced in UAT. Investigation identified that the Billing Status Code on sales order items associated with an invoice was not updated to "Invoiced," preventing Registration Request completion. A preventive workflow-based correction was deployed to Production on 24 April 2025, with increased logging and ongoing monitoring.
Important Findings: ['When an invoice is created, the associated sales order items are normally updated with Billing Status Code "Invoiced."', 'For the incident, the Billing Status Code update did not occur, which blocked completion of the Registration Request.', 'The issue could not be reproduced in UAT, so error handling was added to the invoice creation workflow and monitored.', 'The preventive correction checks order line items associated with completed invoices and updates unprocessed Billing Status Code values to "Invoiced" during Registration Request completion.', 'The intended business flow remains that a Registration Request can be completed only after invoice completion; canceled invoices and subsequently created replacement invoices are handled based on invoice status.', 'The correction was implemented in Production on 24 April 2025, with log levels increased for continued monitoring.']
Root Cause: The Billing Status Code on sales order items associated with an invoice was not updated to "Invoiced," preventing the Registration Request from being completed.
Resolution: A temporary preventive workflow-based correction was deployed to Production to identify order line items linked to completed invoices whose Billing Status Code was not updated and set the status to "Invoiced" during Registration Request completion. Error logging and monitoring were also increased.

Comment: Dear Tsunoda-san,

After analyzing the issue, we have determined the root cause as follows:
 
Typically, when an invoice is created, the "Billing Status Code" field in the sales order items related to the invoice is updated to "Invoiced." However, in this case, this update did not occur, which is preventing the Registration Request from being completed.
 
As this problem is rare and difficult to replicate, we have considered a preventive measure.
 
The preventive measure we propose involves updating the order line items where the billing code status should have been invoiced but was not processed correctly. To address this, we will trigger a workflow when the "Create Registration Request" button is clicked. The workflow will check the sales order line items whose status should have been invoiced but is not, and will update their billing code status to "Invoiced."

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3590
Investigation Summary: The approval flow was incorrectly configured for profit ratio values between -1 and 0. An initial UAT-05 fix generated the correct Approval flow, but a missed test case left the approver invisible. The additional issue was corrected, validated with reference Quote 1-LI6DJ, and released to production on 2025-03-26.
Important Findings: ['Approval flow configuration failed for profit ratio values between -1 and 0.', 'The initial fix was deployed to UAT-05 and generated the correct Approval flow for reference NV Quote 1-LFOUR.', 'Post-fix validation found that the approver was not visible.', 'The missing approver issue resulted from a missed test case and was corrected using reference Quote 1-LI6DJ.', 'The completed fix was released to production on 2025-03-26.']
Root Cause: The approval flow was not configured correctly for profit ratio values between -1 and 0; an additional missed test case caused the approver to remain invisible after the initial fix.
Resolution: Corrected the approval-flow configuration and the missed test-case issue affecting approver visibility, validated in UAT-05, and released the fix to production on 2025-03-26.

Investigation Summary: Vehicles from the common TOB TCB-01 file were synchronized to SC and all FDP environments, causing vehicles outside the intended dealer scope to be registered in the China region. Investigation confirmed that TCB-01 processing has no dealer-code-based filtering in either SC or FDP. The incident was closed as an IT issue after discussion with the business; no implementation change was recorded.
Important Findings: ['TOB sends the same TCB01 file, containing all TOB-managed vehicles, to SC and all FDP environments.', 'Vehicles with dealer codes other than 7306 were registered as China-region vehicles, although dealer code 7306 was the intended update scope.', 'TCB-01 processing in SC and FDP has no record filter based on dealer code; all file data is synchronized.', 'No dealer-code filter was configured during FDP initial setup, and no related business change request had been received.', 'Applying a filter to TCB-01 processing requires a change request (CR).', 'The case was considered a rare occurrence and closed following discussion with the business.']
Root Cause: TCB-01 processing in both SC and FDP environments was configured without dealer-code-based record filtering, so all vehicles in the common TOB file were synchronized to all environments.
Technical Entities: ['TOB', 'TCB01', 'TCB-01', 'SC', 'FDP', 'All FDP environments', 'dealer code', '7306', 'China region', 'CR', 'INC4637619', 'VM_VM data Issue', 'All VM']

Resolution: Automated replenishment jobs to stop on Sundays and released the fix to production on March 26, 2025.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3583
Investigation Summary: Stock IN processing was hindered for VINs used in UV purchase orders after migration from SC to FDP Chugoku. The affected VINs had Scrap Flag set to "Y" while Scrap Date was NULL. Recovery was completed through data patching and updates to affected records and related orders.
Important Findings: ['The affected VIN# was migrated from SC to FDP Chugoku.', 'Scrap Flag was set to "Y" while Scrap Date was NULL, which hindered Stock IN processing.', 'Multiple VIN#s with the same Scrap Flag and Scrap Date condition were identified.', 'Scrap Date was patched in the FDP Chugoku environment.', 'Assessment number, Purchase Type, Transmission Type, and Inspection Status were updated for affected records.', 'Recovery was completed for affected Stock IN requests, UV purchase orders, and UV pool cost procurement orders.']
Root Cause: During VIN# migration from SC to FDP Chugoku, affected VINs retained Scrap Flag = "Y" with Scrap Date = NULL, causing Stock IN processing to be hindered.
Resolution: Patched Scrap Date in the FDP Chugoku environment and updated affected record attributes, including Assessment number, Purchase Type, Transmission Type, and Inspection Status; recovered the affected Stock IN requests, UV purchase orders, and UV pool cost procurement orders.
Technical Entities: ['VIN#', 'UV purchase order', 'SC', 'FDP Chugoku', 'Scrap Flag', 'Scrap Date', 'Stock IN Operation', 'Stock IN requests', 'UV Pool cost Procurement Order', 'Assessment number', 'Purchase Type', 'Transmission Type', 'Inspection Status', 'Cubstion']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3574
Investigation Summary: Purchase orders were incorrectly visible in UV Inventory after vehicle restock, allowing users to change the associated Sales Order # and disrupting the sales process. Data migration had not set the FDP "Previous Assessment Flag" to Y for qualifying orders, and the editable "Sales Order #" field permitted the change without creating a KB Map/Unmap trigger. Recovery was completed for migrated orders, the field was changed to read-only, and the fix was released to production on March 26, 2025.
Important Findings: ['The affected PO was unmapped from UV Sales Order# E050064869 and mapped to Sales Order# E020841755 as recovery.', 'In FDP, "Previous Assessment Flag" must be set to Y when the parent UV Sales Order is Sales Posting Completed, preventing prior purchase orders from appearing after vehicle restock.', 'During data migration, "Previous Assessment Flag" was not set to Y, so previous purchase orders remained visible in UV Inventory.', '"MF UV Inventory Purchase Order View" was editable for 10 responsibilities, allowing authorized users to edit the UI "Sales Order #" field.', 'Editing "Sales Order #" for a purchase order associated with a stocked-in vehicle does not create a KB Map/Unmap trigger.', 'Recovery was completed for migrated orders, and no similar issue was found in NV.']
Root Cause: During data migration, FDP "Previous Assessment Flag" was not set to Y for qualifying orders, leaving prior purchase orders visible in UV Inventory. Users with access to the editable "MF UV Inventory Purchase Order View" could then change the editable "Sales Order #" field without generating a KB Map/Unmap trigger.
Resolution: Recovered migrated orders so prior purchase orders no longer appear in UV Inventory after restock, and changed the "Sales Order #" field to read-only in UV Inventory. The change passed UAT and was released to PROD on March 26, 2025.
Technical Entities: ['FDP', 'Previous Assessment Flag', 'UV Inventory', 'UV Inventory screen', 'MF UV Inventory Purchase Order View', 'Sales Order #', 'UV Sales Order', 'UV Sales Order# E050064869', 'Sales Order# E020841755', 'Sales Posting Completed', 'UV Pool Cost-Procurement', 'Job Card Order', 'UV Body Building Orders', 'KB Map/Unmap trigger', 'Data Migration', 'UAT', 'PROD', 'NV']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3574
Timestamp: 2025-03-18T09:47:00
Author: Shivam
Comment: *RCA:* The issue occurs due to data migration and editable Sales Order # field in UV Inventory screen.
In FDP a new flag “Previous Assessment Flag” was created which is set to Y for all the UV Pool Cost-Procurement, Job Card Order and UV Body Building Orders if the parent UV Sales Order is Sales Posting Completed. This flag ensures that purchase orders associated with old UV Sales Order are not visible on UI if the vehicle is stocked in again.
During data migration, this flag was not set to “Y” so user was able to see all the previous purchase orders on UI and was able to change the Sales Order #.
*Preventive Measures:* We will perform recovery for all the migrated order tonight so that they are not visible under UV Inventory screen after restock in.
Also, we suggest to make this field read only on UI because user can change the Sales Order # for any purchase order that is associated with stocked in vehicle and KB Map/Unmap trigger is not created in this user operation.
Please let us know if you have any further query.
Best Regards,
Shivam

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3574
Timestamp: 2025-03-18T10:36:00
Comment: Mr. Shiromoto,
Thank you for your continued support.
*RCA:*
 This issue is due to the Sales Order # field on the Data Migration and UV Inventory screens being editable.
 In FDP, a new flag called "Previous Assessment Flag" is created, and if the parent UV Sales Order is Sales Posting Completed, this flag is set to Y for all orders below.
 UV Pool Cost-Procurement
 Job Card Order
 UV Body Building Orders
 By setting this flag, purchase orders associated with past UV Sales Orders will not be displayed on the UI when the vehicle is re-stocked.
 However, because this flag was not set to "Y" during data migration, users were able to view past purchase orders and change the Sales Order # on the UI.
*Precautions:*
 This evening, we will perform recovery for all migrated orders and ensure that they do not appear on the UV inventory screen after being restocked.
 Additionally, users can change the Sales Order # of purchase orders associated with vehicles in stock.
 This operation does not create a KB Map/Unmap trigger, so we recommend making this field read-only on the UI.
Thank you very much for your support.
 Hirsch

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3573
Investigation Summary: The incident concerned self-approval behavior in the FDP version, where the requester and approver were the same person and no error message was displayed. Investigation confirmed that the Self-Approval Restriction CR exists in the SC version but is not implemented in FDP. The approval flow rules were reviewed and were functioning as expected; no system change was required.
Important Findings: ['In the SC version, the Self-Approval Restriction CR displays an error and prevents the approval email when the requester and approver are the same.', 'In the FDP version, approval email is expected to be sent to the approver even when the requester and approver are the same.', 'The FDP version does not implement the Self-Approval Restriction CR, so no self-approval error message is displayed.', 'The "JC Close Low Profit" (Manager) approval flow contains rules determined by "Quote Profit Ratio After Discount".', 'Reviewed approval flow rules were confirmed to be working as expected, and no additional modifications were required.']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3565
Investigation Summary: A UV Pool Cost Order remained incomplete although the related Stock-In verification was approved and the UV Purchase Order processing otherwise completed successfully. Recovery was completed by manually setting the affected PO status to "Completed" and creating a Journal Voucher, with Journal-to-KB batch linkage requested. investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3557
Investigation Summary: In FDP, Sales Posting was possible when no JCO existed because the Service Quote had not been progressed to "Customer Approved". The investigation confirmed that FDP had no Sales Posting validation for missing JCOs, while JCO creation after "Customer Approved" already required the corresponding Job Card to be closed before Sales Posting. A validation was implemented in UAT, approved for production, and released on March 26, 2025.
Important Findings: ['The issue was reproduced on UAT1: a Sales Order could be completed while the JCO activity was not completed.', 'In FDP, Sales Posting was allowed when no JCO was created because the Service Quote was not "Customer Approved".', 'Changing the Service Quote to "Customer Approved" creates a JCO; after that, Sales Posting is blocked until the corresponding Job Card is closed.', 'The existing FDP behavior resulted from a missing validation check, potentially triggered when the user did not progress the Service Quote to "Customer Approved".', 'SC includes a validation message when changing a Delivery Request status to "Completed" in the equivalent missing-JCO scenario.', 'A similar validation was implemented in FDP, validated in UAT, approved for Prod, and released on March 26, 2025.']
Root Cause: FDP did not validate the presence of a JCO during Sales Posting when the Service Quote was not "Customer Approved", allowing Sales Posting without JCO creation or Job Card closure.
Resolution: Implemented a validation in FDP to prevent the missing-JCO Sales Posting scenario; the change was deployed to UAT, approved for Prod, and released to production on March 26, 2025.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3557
Timestamp: 2025-03-11T12:47:00
Author: Shivam
Comment: Thanks for your continued support.
 We have investigated above issue and below are our findings.
 1. User is able to do the Sales Posting even if the JCO is not created(Service Quote is not "Customer Approved"). As per the current functionality in FDP, there is no check while doing sales positng if there is no JCO. 
 2. As soon as Service Quote status changes to "Customer Approved" JCO is created and now without closing the respective Job Card user will not be able to do the Sales Posting.
In above Sales Order, it seems there is a user mis operation. The user may not have progressed the Service Quote to "Customer Approved", which prevented the creation of JCO. As per FDP's functionality, Sales Posting is still allowed.
In SC version, there is a validation for the first point — when changing the status of a Delivery Request to "Completed", a validation message is displayed.
 Please let us know if we need to implement a similar validation in FDP as well.
Best Regards,
 Shivam

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3557
Timestamp: 2025-03-11T14:37:00
Comment: thank you always.
We investigated this matter and confirmed the following points.
1. Even if a JCO is not created (Service Quote is not "Customer Approved"), users can still perform Sales Posting. In the current FDP specifications, there is no mechanism to check the presence of JCO during Sales Posting. 
2. On the other hand, when the Service Quote status is changed to "Customer Approved", a JCO is created and Sales Posting cannot be performed after that unless the corresponding Job Card is closed.
This Sales Order may be due to a user operation error. Because the user did not advance the Service Quote to "Customer Approved," the JCO was not created, and Sales Posting was still allowed under the FDP specifications.
In addition, in the SC version, a verification message is displayed when changing the status of the Delivery Request to "Completed" for the first case.
Please check whether you need to implement similar validation in FDP as well.
Thank you very much for your support.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3549
Investigation Summary: Price master updates were missing in specific FDP environments for two separate groups of part numbers. In FDP Chugoku, the required morning-process file was not executed. investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3546
Investigation Summary: In the Chugoku Production environment, recycle fee orders were not created because the TOB D21F file was received and processed before the corresponding D21A file. D21A creates the chassis order, which is a prerequisite for D21F to create the recycle fee order. The initially reported D21E dependency was corrected: the relevant sequence is D21A and D21F. Affected records were recovered by re-executing D21F after D21A processing; monitoring was implemented to identify similar cases for recovery.
Important Findings: ['The root sequence issue was TOB processing D21F before the corresponding D21A file for the same order.', 'D21A creates the chassis order, while D21F creates the recycle fee order; without the chassis order, D21F cannot create the recycle fee order.', 'The initial reference to D21E in March 2025 was incorrect; the correct prerequisite file is D21A.', 'Re-executing D21F after successful D21A processing created the missing recycle fee orders.', 'The issue was identified as a TOB file sequencing issue rather than a Cubastion Siebel system defect.', 'Monitoring and email notifications were implemented to identify failed, unprocessed, or sequencing-related cases and enable recovery.']
Root Cause: The corresponding TOB D21F file was received and processed before the D21A file. Because D21A had not yet created the prerequisite chassis order, D21F could not create the recycle fee order.
Resolution: Recovered affected records by re-executing D21F after the corresponding D21A process completed, creating the recycle fee orders. Monitoring was implemented to detect similar cases and trigger recovery actions.

Please find below the analysis details for incident *MFTBCFFR: 3546* regarding the issue where the recycle order was not displayed in the Chugoku Production environment.
*Root Cause Analysis (RCA):*
The *D21F* file was received and processed before the *D21A* file. Since the chassis record had not yet been created during the D21A file execution, the recycle fee order could not be created during the D21F execution.
*Recovery Action:*
As part of the recovery, the *D21F* process was re-executed after the successful completion of the *D21A* process. This resulted in the successful creation of the recycle fee order.
*Countermeasure:*
As this issue was caused by the sequence of *TOB* file processing and is *not related to the Siebel system*, we are unable to provide a Siebel-side countermeasure for this scenario.
*Monitoring:*
To avoid such errors, Cubastion has configured email notifications to alert the team whenever any file execution fails. This enables us to promptly identify unprocessed or failed files and take timely recovery actions whenever required.
Since this issue was caused by the TOB file processing sequence and is not related to the Siebel system, we would like to proceed with closing this Jira ticket.
Best Regards,
Deepika Raheja

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3527
Investigation Summary: An intermittent Siebel issue caused Trade-in Consumption Tax not to be correctly reflected in the NV Quote header after entering a Trade-in Amount. Impacted records in the Okayama, Wakayama, and Chugoku environments were recovered. The code was corrected in UAT and released to production on March 26, 2025, with continued monitoring planned.
Important Findings: ['The issue occurred intermittently and had no specific reproducible steps.', 'The affected behavior occurred when entering a Trade-in Amount: Trade-in Consumption Tax should populate in both the Trade-in subtab and the Quote Header.', 'All impacted records in the Okayama, Wakayama, and Chugoku environments were recovered; no recovery was required for other FDP environments.', 'The code did not follow Siebel best practices because Link Specification was not set to TRUE.', 'The UAT validation was intended to confirm that NV quotation and trade-in functionality continued to operate normally after the code change.', 'The production release of the fix was completed on March 26, 2025.']
Root Cause: Link Specification was not set to TRUE in the Siebel code, contrary to Oracle-recommended Siebel best practices, causing intermittent failure to reflect Trade-in Consumption Tax in the NV Quote Header.
Resolution: Set Link Specification to TRUE in UAT, validated that existing NV quotation and trade-in functionality was not impacted, released the fix to production on March 26, 2025, and recovered affected records in the Okayama, Wakayama, and Chugoku environments.

Investigation Summary: A user revised a quote after creating an order, a Parts Internal Order, and Return order records for two part items. When the old part items were deleted and replacement part items were added, the replacement items received the same line numbers and synchronized to the existing part items instead of being created as new items. Recovery was completed for the affected record by removing the parent order ID from the affected part line items, allowing purchase-order creation to proceed.
Important Findings: ['The order was created from a quote containing two part items, followed by creation of a Parts Internal Order and Return order records for both items.', 'After the quote was revised, the original two part items were deleted and two new part items were added with the same line numbers.', 'Quote-to-order synchronization matched the new part items to existing part items rather than creating new items.', 'Existing part orders for the old items caused the operation to stop and prevented purchase-order creation.', 'The incident was identified as a rare scenario and future occurrences should be monitored.']
Root Cause: After quote revision, replacement part items were assigned the same line numbers as deleted part items. During quote and order synchronization, they matched existing part items that already had Parts Internal Order and Return order records, leaving the parent order ID unchanged and causing the operation to stop.
Resolution: Recovery was completed for the affected record by removing the parent order ID from the line items associated with the parts; the user was then instructed to create the purchase order.
Technical Entities: ['quote', 'order', 'line items', 'Part items', 'Parts Internal Order', 'Return order', 'parent order ID', 'purchase order', 'Jira']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3522
Timestamp: 2025-03-10T03:44:00
Comment: Thank you for your support.
 
*RCA*: In this case the sequence of events is as mentioned below: # 
User created order from quote with 2 Part items.
 # 
User created the Parts internal order and then the return order for both the items Part Items.
 # 
User revised the quote.
 # 
Deleted the old items (2 parts) and added the new Part items (2 parts).
The sequence of events happened in such a manner that the same line number was assigned to the new Part Items also. So, when the user synced the Quote and Order.
It got synced with existing part items rather creating new items.
And as the Part orders were already created for the older items. Therefore, the operation got stuck.
As this is a very rare scenario to occur, we request the business team to let us monitor if there is any further such any occurrence in the system to have a better and efficient solution to control this issue.
*Recovery*: Recovery is completed for the affected record.
 
In case of any further query, please let us know.
Regards
Ashutosh Dogra

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3522
Timestamp: 2025-03-10T08:10:00
Comment: Dear @Shiromoto, Hideaki (575) San,
Thank you very much for your continued support.
RCA: The events in this case are as follows.
A user creates an order from a quote that includes two parts items.
A user created a "Parts Internal Order" and then a "Return order" for both parts items.
The user has revised the quote.
I deleted the old item (2 parts) and added the new part item (2 parts).
Through this sequence, new part items were also assigned the same line number. As a result, when users synced quotes and orders, they were synced with existing part items and no new items were created. Additionally, the parts order was already created for the old item, which caused the operation to stop.
As this is a very rare occurrence, we ask that you please monitor your systems for similar occurrences in the future and check with our business team to find a better and more efficient solution to control this issue.
Recovery: Recovery is complete for the affected records.
If you have any questions, please let us know.
Thank you for your support.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3512

Comment: Thank you for your support.
We have analyzed this issue and found out that the issue arises due to *D21Z file* (Logistic Information).
File: *D21Z_03032025113216*
In this file the date is there for  Chassis Shipment Date, Actual Assembly Date for chassis and the date is there in format (*MMYY*) only as there is no year mentioned for the dates. 
The system takes the year from current year only (*i.e. in our case 2025*).
Therefore the date is updated to *04/12/2025*.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3505
Timestamp: 2025-03-11T01:04:00
Comment: Thank you for your support.
For this issue the probable fixes are as follows:
*Issue:* In D21Z file the date which is received from the TOB side does is in the format of *MMDD*  and not having the Year.
*Fix Plan-1*: Considering the Shipment date will be older than the  D21Z file execution data. We will compare the Shipment date received in the file to the file execution date and if the Shipment date is greater than the file execution date in the format of *MMDD* then we will take the previous year. Otherwise the current year. 
This change needs to be handled at the ODI side. So a project CR will be required for this.
*Fix Plan 2:* As the Shipment date is already updated by the D21N file. So, the Shipment date updating process from D21Z file will be stopped. This can be done by AMS-CR
*Fix Plan 3*: If TOB can send the year in the D21Z file then we can update the same in the Siebel system.
These are the probable fix plans to handle these types of issues.
In case a detailed discussion is required, we can also schedule a call for the same.
Regards
Ashutosh Dogra

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3505
Timestamp: 2025-03-11T01:17:00
Comment: Mr. Tsunoda,
Thank you for your continued support.
Regarding this issue, we are considering the following solutions.
■ Problems
In the D21Z file, the date received from the TOB side is in MMDD format and does not include Year information.
■ Countermeasure plan
① Amendment 1
It is assumed that the Shipment Date is a date in the past than the execution date of the D21Z file, and processing is performed according to the following rules. 
If the Shipment Date (MMDD format) is greater than the file execution date: apply the previous year
Otherwise: apply current year
Since this change requires action on the ODI side, a project CR application is required.
② Amendment 2
Since the Shipment Date has already been updated by the D21N file, this will stop the Shipment Date update process from the D21Z file.
In this case, AMS-CR can be used.
③ Amendment 3
If the TOB side can include Year information in the D21Z file, we can reflect it in the Siebel system.
The above is a solution to this problem.
If you have any questions or need detailed consultation, we can set up a separate meeting, so please contact us if necessary.

Regards
Ashutosh Dogra

Therefore, when processing D21Z files, the system reads this MMDD format date, automatically adds the current year and converts the date format from MMDD to YYYYMMDD based on the current system settings.

Resolution: The FDP logic was corrected in FDP UAT1, validated as working, and released to production in the August 27 regular release.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3489
Investigation Summary: INC4015844 addressed an incorrect UV Sales Order status behavior in the SC environment. A fix was implemented in FDP UAT-1 to prevent approval generation for rejected UV Sales Orders when the associated Delivery Request is completed. The change requires verification and approval before production deployment.
Important Findings: ["Users could click the 'Generate Approval' button when a UV Sales Order status was 'Rejected' and the Delivery Request was Completed.", "The fix disables the 'Generate Approval' button for UV Orders with a completed Delivery Request and a 'Rejected' Sales Order status.", 'The fix was implemented in the FDP UAT-1 environment.', 'Reference validation record: AR# H000051489, UV SO# E001300162.']
Root Cause: The 'Generate Approval' button was enabled for UV Sales Orders in 'Rejected' status when their associated Delivery Request was completed.
Resolution: Implemented a fix in FDP UAT-1 to disable the 'Generate Approval' button when the UV Sales Order status is 'Rejected' and the Delivery Request is completed.
Technical Entities: ['INC4015844', 'SC environment', 'FDP UAT-1', 'UV Sales Order', 'Sales Order', 'Delivery Request', 'Generate Approval', 'AR# H000051489', 'UV SO# E001300162']

This is to inform you that the incident INC4015844 raised in the SC environment, which involved a fix related to wrong UV Sales Order Status, has been addressed. The fix has been successfully implemented in the FDP UAT-1 environment.
With this update, users will no longer be able to click 'Generate Approval' button when UV Sales Order status is 'Rejected' but the Delivery Request has been Completed. The 'Generate Approval' button will now be disabled for UV Orders whose Delivery Request is completed but Sales Order status is 'Rejected'.
Kindly find the reference record on UAT-1 environment:
 AR#: H000051489, UV SO#: E001300162
Kindly verify the changes in the FDP UAT-1 environment and approve the fix for production deployment.
Please feel free to reach out if you have any questions or require further information.
Best regards,
Sunaina Gill

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3481
Investigation Summary: Customer-related fields were becoming null on UV Sales Order when users could manually clear the Customer Name field. The issue was fixed in the FDP UAT environment by making Customer Name read-only, preventing users from removing it. The fix was released to production in the regular release on July 24.
Important Findings: ['The Customer Name field on the UV Sales Order screen was not read-only.', 'Users could remove Customer Name manually on a UV Sales Order.', 'Clearing Customer Name also nullified Customer Name, Bill To Account, and Payer Account.', 'Making Customer Name read-only prevented customer-related fields from becoming null.', 'The fix was released to production on July 24 through the regular release.']
Root Cause: The Customer Name field on the UV Sales Order screen was editable, allowing users to clear it and thereby nullify Customer Name, Bill To Account, and Payer Account.
Resolution: Configured the Customer Name field on the UV Sales Order screen as read-only in FDP UAT and released the fix to production on July 24.
Technical Entities: ['FDP UAT environment', 'UV Sales Order', 'Customer Name', 'Bill To Account', 'Payer Account', 'production environment']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3481
Timestamp: 2025-07-02T05:49:00
Comment: Dear Shiromoto san
Thank you for your support.
We have fixed this issue in FDP UAT environment.
Issue: Field related to Customer were null on UV Sales Order.
This issue occured because the field 'Customer Name' was not Read-Only on UV Sales Order screen. Using this field user is able to Remove Customer Name from UV Sales Order. Upon nullifying this filed will also nullify Field "Customer Name", "Bill To Account" and "Payer Account".
To fix this issue, we have made the field 'Customer Name' as Read-Only.
Now user will not be able to remove customer name manually and hence Field related to Customer will not become null.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3465
Investigation Summary: Vehicle-to-business-object migration data in FDP was inconsistent because SC Prod vehicle identifiers did not reliably align. The investigation found duplicate VIN vehicles and mismatches between X_KEY and ASSET_NUM in SC Prod; migration used ASSET_NUM as the unique/user key. Recovery was completed in FDP according to the provided file, updating affected Chassis# (Key#) references.
Important Findings: ['Vehicle records in SC Prod contain X_KEY, SERIAL_NUM, and ASSET_NUM; these values should ideally match.', 'For ASSET_NUM "FK62F-605267", X_KEY and SERIAL_NUM were "FU74HZ-510966".', 'Migration used ASSET_NUM as the unique/user key, causing mismatches when X_KEY and ASSET_NUM differed.', 'When multiple SC Prod vehicles had the same VIN, the correct vehicle ID was not updated during migration.', 'Recovery scope included Chassis# (Key#) references for JC, WO, Quote, PO, JCO, Expense, and Change Order.', 'There was no Registration# gap; Power BI had no SC Version and no gap, so no Power BI recovery was required.']
Root Cause: SC Prod vehicle master data contained duplicate VIN records and mismatched X_KEY, SERIAL_NUM, and ASSET_NUM values; using ASSET_NUM as the unique key during migration prevented the correct vehicle ID from being updated.
Resolution: Completed FDP recovery based on the provided file by correcting affected Chassis# (Key#) references across JC, WO, Quote, PO, JCO, Expense, and Change Order.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3458
Investigation Summary: PBI profit values differed from Siebel because deleted Siebel line items remained in the Datamart database and were included in profit calculations. The fix added DELETE_FLG handling in ODI and filtered Power BI reports to display only active line items. The changes were validated in UAT and deployed to prod across all environments.
Important Findings: ["Deleted Siebel line items remain in the Datamart DB with DELETE_FLG = 'Y', while active line items use DELETE_FLG = 'N'.", 'The existing profit logic included records regardless of DELETE_FLG, causing PBI report profit discrepancies versus Siebel.', 'Impacted records for Iwate SO#: E000003241 and Chugoku SO#: E050024154 were recovered while the permanent fix was being developed.', "DELETE_FLG was added to WC_UV_SALES_F and ODI processing was updated to set DELETE_FLG = 'Y' for inactive records.", "Power BI UV reports 2_05 and 2_06 were updated with DELETE_FLG = 'N' filtering and verified by deleting a Siebel line item."]
Root Cause: PBI reports did not exclude Datamart line items marked DELETE_FLG = 'Y', so deleted Siebel line items were included in profit calculations.
Resolution: Added DELETE_FLG to WC_UV_SALES_F, updated ODI to set DELETE_FLG = 'Y' for inactive records, and applied DELETE_FLG = 'N' filtering in Power BI UV reports 2_05 and 2_06. The changes were validated in UAT and deployed to prod across all environments.
Technical Entities: ['Siebel', 'Datamart DB', 'PBI', 'Power BI', 'ODI', 'UAT', 'prod', 'DELETE_FLG', 'WC_UV_SALES_F', 'UV report', 'UV_205', 'UV_206', 'UV reports 2_05 and 2_06', 'UV Sales Quote', 'UV Sales Order', 'UV Trade-In', 'Sales Posting Completed', 'Iwate', 'Chugoku', 'SO#: E000003241', 'SO#: E050024154']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3458
Timestamp: 2025-03-05T11:19:00
Author: Sheetal
Comment: Dear Shiromoto-San,
Thank you for your support.
*RCA:*
Currently, our logic retrieves Profit (Sales Price - Cost Price) based on the formula: *Cost Price = Cost * Quantity*, regardless of the DELETE_FLG status in the Datamart database.
However, line items deleted from the Siebel side still exist in the Datamart DB, marked with *DELETE_FLG = 'Y'*, while active line items in Siebel are marked as *DELETE_FLG = 'N'* in Datamart.
Since the PBI report doesn't have a filter to separate deleted line items, causing the difference in Profit values between the PBI report and Siebel. 
*Fix Plan:* 
We are actively working on resolving this issue and expect to implement the fix by *14/03/2025* on UAT.In the meantime, we will proceed with the recovery of impacted records.
Regards,
Sheetal

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3458
Timestamp: 2025-03-05T11:21:00
Comment: Mr. Shiromoto,
Thank you for your continued support.
The following is a translation of Sheetal's email.
RCA:
The current logic is to obtain profit (sales price - cost) using the following formula, regardless of the status of DELETE_FLG.
Cost = Cost × Quantity
However, the lines deleted on the Siebel side remain in the Datamart DB with DELETE_FLG = 'Y', while the lines that are valid on Siebel are managed on the Datamart as DELETE_FLG = 'N'.
PBI reports did not have a filter to exclude deleted lines, resulting in discrepancies in profit values ​​between PBI reports and Siebel.
Fix plan:
We are currently working to resolve the issue and plan to apply the fix in UAT environments by March 14, 2025.
In the meantime, we will continue to recover the affected data.

Thank you for your support.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3451
Investigation Summary: The incident involved JV posting dates and manually editable Work Order dates. Investigation confirmed that JV posting-date logic matched MFTBCFFR-3348, MFTBCFFR-3347, MFTBCFFR-3337, and MFTBCFFR-3461, while users could set Work Start Date or Work Completion Date earlier than the Work Order creation date. The JV posting-date issue was addressed by MFTBCFFR-3348, and this incident added a control to make Work Completion Date read-only for external Work Orders, with the read-only timing changed to Acceptance Inspection.
Important Findings: ['JV posting dates use the same logic as MFTBCFFR-3348, MFTBCFFR-3347, MFTBCFFR-3337, and MFTBCFFR-3461.', 'Work Start Date and Work Completion Date were editable in Work Order, allowing dates earlier than the Work Order creation date.', 'The JV posting-date issue was fixed in UAT by MFTBCFFR-3348.', 'Work Completion Date was made read-only for External work orders in UAT1 under JC# I001292913.', 'The requested read-only timing was changed from Work Completed to Acceptance Inspection and validated in FDP UAT-1.']
Root Cause: Work Start Date and Work Completion Date were editable in Work Order, allowing users to manually set dates earlier than the Work Order creation date; JV posting dates used the related common posting-date logic.
Resolution: The JV posting-date fix from MFTBCFFR-3348 was applied, and Work Completion Date was configured as read-only for External work orders, with the lock applied at Acceptance Inspection. The change was validated in UAT-1/FDP UAT-1 and approved for PROD deployment.
Technical Entities: ['MFTBCFFR-3451', 'MFTBCFFR-3348', 'MFTBCFFR-3347', 'MFTBCFFR-3337', 'MFTBCFFR-3461', 'JV', 'Work Order', 'Work Start Date', 'Work Completion Date', 'External work orders', 'UAT', 'UAT1', 'UAT-1', 'FDP UAT-1', 'PROD', 'JC# I001292913', 'Work Completed', 'Acceptance Inspection']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3442
Timestamp: 2025-03-05T12:51:00
Comment: Mr. Tsunoda,
Thank you for your continued support.
After a detailed analysis of this issue, we have identified the root cause. It turns out that when a bodywork order has a negative cost and list price, the sales order's Quote ID is saved, which is causing the issue.
I reproduced the problem using the steps below.
**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Add a bodywork order item to the quote and enter both the list price and cost as negative values.
2. Approve the quote and create an order based on the quote.
3. Approve the order and click the "Create Purchase Order" button to create a purchase order for the bodywork order.
4. Approve the purchase order for the bodywork order and then revise the estimate. After modification, the quoted item is synchronized to the bodywork purchase order.
**Root Cause Analysis (RCA):**
Creating a purchase order for a bodywork order using the Create Purchase Order button triggers a workflow. However, negative price validation breaks this workflow. As a result, the sales order's Quote ID is saved in the bodywork purchase order.
Later, when you amend the quote, it will find all sales orders with the same Quote ID and sync the line items. As a result, bodywork purchase order line items with Quote IDs will also be synchronized with the sales order.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3438
Investigation Summary: Tax Finalization in Registration request failed when creating expense items after a UV Sales Quote was revised and synchronized with its UV Sales Order. The issue was reproduced in UAT-01 for reference order E001292965 and attributed to user changes that interchanged Additional Body and Liability insurance line-item product types before invoice creation. Recovery for the affected record was completed.
Important Findings: ['The user created a UV Sales Order from a UV Sales Quote.', 'The product type was changed from Additional Body to Liability insurance and then mistakenly changed back to Additional Body, interchanging the line items.', 'An Expense invoice was created from the Sales Order while the line items were interchanged.', 'Revising and syncing the UV Sales Quote restored the Additional Body and Liability Insurance line items to their original positions.', 'Because the invoice had been created from the interchanged line items, Tax Finalization in Registration request returned an error to create the expense for the items.', 'The issue was replicated in UAT-01 using reference order E001292965.']
Root Cause: User mis-operation caused Additional Body and Liability insurance line-item product types to be interchanged before Expense invoice creation; a subsequent UV Sales Quote revision and synchronization restored the original line-item positions, creating a mismatch that caused the Tax Finalization expense-creation error.
Resolution: Recovery was completed for the affected record.
Technical Entities: ['UV Sales Order', 'UV Sales Quote', 'Additional Body', 'Liability insurance', 'Expense invoice', 'Tax Finalization', 'Registration request', 'UAT-01', 'E001292965']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3437
Investigation Summary: Incorrect product IDs were assigned to migrated quote line items containing specific option codes, affecting NV Quotes and NV Sales Orders in the Chugoku environment. Investigation identified duplicate product-name records in the product master with different product types. All identified impacted records were recovered after business hours, and the issue was reported not to recur when processing migrated data or copying migrated NV Quotes.
Important Findings: ['Product master contained duplicate records for product names "AE", "AD", "AF", "4A", "FD", and "BB".', 'For each duplicate product name, one record had product type "Parts" and the other had product type "Options".', 'Migrated quote line items containing the affected option codes received incorrect product IDs.', 'The issue could also occur when a user copied a migrated NV Sales Quote and created a new record in Chugoku.', 'A list of impacted NV Quotes and NV Sales Orders was identified, and recovery for all impacted records was completed.']
Root Cause: Duplicate product-name records in the product master for "AE", "AD", "AF", "4A", "FD", and "BB", with conflicting product types "Parts" and "Options", caused incorrect product IDs to be populated on migrated quote line items containing those option codes.
Resolution: Recovery was completed for all identified impacted NV Quotes and NV Sales Orders. The issue was confirmed not to recur when users process migrated data or copy from migrated NV Quotes.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3429
Investigation Summary: The incident concerned FDP behavior for parts internal orders, including an error when creating a parts order and incorrect inventory name field editability. Investigation confirmed that FDP logic differed from SC. The corrected logic was validated in FDP UAT-1 and released to production on March 26, 2025.
Important Findings: ['FDP logic differed from SC for parts internal order inventory name field editability.', 'The inventory name field must be non-editable when Already Issued, Already Reserved, or Processed Qty is not 0.', 'The inventory name field must be editable only when Already Issued, Already Reserved, and Processed Qty are all 0.', 'Initial FDP UAT-1 fixes did not pass confirmation; additional feedback was addressed before the final UAT fix.', 'The final fix was applied to FDP UAT-1, approved for PROD deployment, and released to production on March 26, 2025.']
Root Cause: FDP logic for parts internal order inventory name field editability was not aligned with SC specifications based on Already Issued, Already Reserved, and Processed Qty values.
Resolution: Corrected the FDP logic in FDP UAT-1 to match SC behavior and released the approved fix to production on March 26, 2025.

Investigation Summary: Invoice data generation was affected when shipment O000126395 contained Part# MH000931 twice with the same Line # 14 in its shipment lines. The invoice-data query was improved and deployed to FDP Prod. The updated query handles monthly invoice creation on the 10th, 20th, and end of month, as well as Sales Return scenarios involving duplicate part numbers and shipment/return charges.

Root Cause: Part# MH000931 appeared twice with the same Line # 14 in the shipment lines for shipment O000126395, which the invoice-data query did not handle correctly.
Resolution: Improved the query used to provide invoice data to handle duplicate shipment lines, then deployed the change to FDP Prod.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3403
Investigation Summary: Duplicate Recycle Fee orders were mapped to a Sales order after two D21F files were received for the same VIN. The affected records were recovered in all FDP environments. Recurrence prevention is being handled under related issue MFTBCFFR-3357.
Important Findings: ['Two D21F files were received for the same VIN, creating duplicate records.', 'The duplicate records resulted in duplicate Recycle Fee orders mapped to the Sales order.', 'The duplicate files were D21F_10012025143156 and D21F_21022025093442.', 'Recovery of the affected records was completed in all FDP environments.', 'The issue is tracked as similar to MFTBCFFR-3357 for further handling and recurrence prevention.']
Root Cause: Duplicate D21F files received for the same VIN created duplicated data and duplicate Recycle Fee orders mapped to the Sales order.
Resolution: Recovered the affected records in all FDP environments; further recurrence-prevention work is tracked under MFTBCFFR-3357.
Technical Entities: ['Recycle Fee orders', 'Sales order', 'D21F files', 'VIN', 'D21F_10012025143156', 'D21F_21022025093442', 'FDP environments', 'MFTBCFFR-3357', 'TOB team']

Comment: Dear Tsunoda san,

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3399
Investigation Summary: An approval request was generated with a NULL approver after the user selected "Generate Approval" from the "Branch-CS-Staff" position. The spreadsheet status was reverted and the "Generate Approval" button was enabled on both affected spreadsheets. Users must generate approvals from the correct position.
Important Findings: ['The user pressed "Generate Approval" while in the "Branch-CS-Staff" position.', 'The resulting approval request had a NULL approver.', 'The spreadsheet status was reverted following the incorrect approval generation.', 'The "Generate Approval" button was enabled on both affected spreadsheets.', 'The incident was identified as user mis-operation.']
Root Cause: User generated the approval request from the "Branch-CS-Staff" position instead of the correct position, resulting in a NULL approver.
Resolution: Reverted the spreadsheet status and enabled the "Generate Approval" button on both affected spreadsheets; instructed the user to proceed from the correct position.
Technical Entities: ['Generate Approval', 'Branch-CS-Staff', 'approval request', 'NULL approver', 'spreadsheet']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3389
Investigation Summary: A bodywork purchase order incorrectly retained the originating sales order's Quote ID when created from a quote containing negative list price and cost. Negative price validation interrupted the workflow triggered by "Create Purchase Order", causing later quote amendments to synchronize sales-order line items to the bodywork purchase order. A fix was validated across FDP UAT environments and deployed to the production environment on March 12, 2025.
Important Findings: ['The issue was reproduced in UAT1 with Bodywork order B001292881 and Sales Order A001292880.', 'A bodywork order item with both negative list price and negative cost triggered the failure path.', 'The "Create Purchase Order" workflow was interrupted by negative price validation.', "The interrupted workflow saved the sales order's Quote ID on the bodywork purchase order.", 'When the quote was amended, line-item synchronization selected all sales orders sharing the Quote ID, including the bodywork purchase order.', 'The fix was applied to all FDP UAT environments and released to the production environment on March 12, 2025.']
Root Cause: Negative price validation broke the workflow triggered by "Create Purchase Order" for a bodywork order with negative cost and list price, causing the sales order's Quote ID to be saved on the bodywork purchase order. Subsequent quote amendments synchronized line items to that bodywork purchase order because it shared the Quote ID.
Resolution: A fix was deployed across all FDP UAT environments and then applied to the production environment in the March 12, 2025 release.
Technical Entities: ['Modification order', 'Sales order', 'Quote ID', 'bodywork order', 'bodywork purchase order', 'quote', 'Create Purchase Order', 'negative price validation', 'workflow', 'UAT1', 'UAT 1', 'B001292881', 'A001292880', 'FDP UAT environments', 'production environment']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3389
Timestamp: 2025-03-05T12:50:00
Comment: Mr. Tsunoda,
Thank you for your continued support. 
 
After a detailed analysis of this issue, we have identified the root cause. It turns out that when a bodywork order has a negative cost and list price, the sales order's Quote ID is saved, which is causing the issue. 
 
I reproduced the problem using the steps below. 
 
**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Add a bodywork order item to the quote and enter both the list price and cost as negative values. 
2. Approve the quote and create an order based on the quote. 
3. Approve the order and click the "Create Purchase Order" button to create a purchase order for the bodywork order. 
4. Approve the purchase order for the bodywork order and then revise the estimate. After modification, the quoted item is synchronized to the bodywork purchase order. 
 
**Root Cause Analysis (RCA):**
Creating a purchase order for a bodywork order using the Create Purchase Order button triggers a workflow. However, negative price validation breaks this workflow. As a result, the sales order's Quote ID is saved in the bodywork purchase order. 
Later, when you amend the quote, it will find all sales orders with the same Quote ID and sync the line items. As a result, bodywork purchase order line items with Quote IDs will also be synchronized with the sales order. 
 
**Reproduction on UAT:**
- **Bodywork order:** B001292881 (UAT 1)
- **Sales Order:** A001292880 (UAT 1)
 
The expected fix date for this issue in the UAT environment is **March 7**. 
 
If you have any questions or need additional support, please let us know.
Thank you very much for your support.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3374
Investigation Summary: Tax confirmation could not be completed for an affected order after data migration. Investigation found that completed invoices retained an old SC environment line number on PO lines of type "Tax" instead of the new China environment line number. The affected record was corrected, enabling the user to proceed with tax confirmation; no additional impacted records were found.
Important Findings: ['The issue affected tax confirmation for order code 0000U05007, with customer payment method Transfer and customer payment date 2025/02/14.', 'For invoices with status "Completed", the invoice line number in the China environment must be associated with the "Tax" type PO line.', 'Migrated invoices were registered as "Completed", but "Tax" type PO lines remained associated with the old line number from the SC environment.', 'The affected record was recovered by linking the "Tax" type PO line to the new China environment line number.', 'A review found no other records impacted; no additional recovery was required.']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3364
Investigation Summary: UV Quote and UV Sales Order showed differing Sales Profit values after quote creation or revision. Investigation identified inconsistent additional-cost calculation logic and rounding behavior in UV Quote, resulting in profit discrepancies, including 1-yen differences. The UV Quote calculation was aligned with UV Sales Order, validated in UAT-01 for AR#: H000045187, and deployed to production on April 14.
Important Findings: ['Initial UAT validation failed for AR#: H000037289, where Sales Quote# 1-5LHJS7 Rev.2 had Profit 526,340 and SO# E001281570 had Profit 552,740.', 'Data patches were completed in FDP environments except for two records in FDP Okayama; a remaining discrepancy was also reported for FDP Chugoku AR#: H000147553.', 'UV Quote rounded values during Sales Profit calculation, causing profit differences between UV Quote and UV Sales Order.', 'The fix aligned additional cost price calculation logic in UV Quote with UV Sales Order and removed rounding from the UV Quote Profit Amount calculation.', 'The fix is independent of Consumption Tax Rounding configured in Administration – Sales – Consumption Tax Master.', 'UAT passed for the rounding issue on AR#: H000045187 before production deployment.']
Root Cause: UV Quote used different rounding and additional cost price calculation logic than UV Sales Order when calculating Sales Profit, causing inconsistent Profit Amount values.
Resolution: Updated UV Quote Sales Profit calculation to use the same additional cost price logic and no-rounding behavior as UV Sales Order. The change passed UAT-01 validation for AR#: H000045187 and was deployed to production in the April 14 release.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3363
Investigation Summary: A Service Request created by USER: D8ISATAK generated an approval request with no approver. The approval flow requires a Branch-CS-Staff user's manager to have Branch-Parts-Mgr as the primary position; USER: D8YUJISA had Branch-Service-Mgr as the primary position. The issue can be resolved by correcting the manager primary position and staff parent position, deleting the existing approval request, and creating it again.
Important Findings: ['USER: D8ISATAK is a Branch-CS-Staff and created the Service Request.', 'USER: D8YUJISA had the Branch-Parts-Mgr role but its primary position was Branch-Service-Mgr.', 'The approval flow sends approval requests to Branch-Parts-Mgr, resulting in no approver when the manager primary position is Branch-Service-Mgr.', 'Only Branch-CS-Staff whose manager is Branch-Parts-Mgr can create an SR for approval under the current approval flow.', 'Existing approval requests must be deleted and recreated after updating the manager primary position and staff parent position.']
Root Cause: USER: D8YUJISA's primary position was Branch-Service-Mgr rather than Branch-Parts-Mgr, so the approval flow could not identify an approver for the Service Request created by USER: D8ISATAK.
Resolution: Change USER: D8YUJISA's primary position to Branch-Parts-Mgr and update the staff parent position, delete the current approval request, then create the approval request again.
Technical Entities: ['Service Request', 'SR', 'approval flow', 'approval request', 'USER: D8ISATAK', 'USER: D8YUJISA', 'Branch-CS-Staff', 'Branch-Service-Mgr', 'Branch-Parts-Mgr', 'Branch-Parts-Manger', 'Branch maintenance staff', 'Manager Primary', 'Staff Parent Position']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3362
Investigation Summary: Duplicate Premium Payment records with blank PPR# were identified for multiple orders in FDP and also in SC. Investigation found that SonpoWeb triggers IFIN011 (Settlement Confirmation) during daily settlement processing, and Siebel creates records from the decoded interface payload when the received Policy Number exists. The behavior was confirmed as functioning as expected; duplicate records were cancelled and the ticket was dismissed.
Important Findings: ['Duplicate Premium Payment records with blank PPR# were found for orders Q019496832, Q034399511, and Q036345352.', 'The duplicate records were created through SonpoWeb calls to IFIN011 (Settlement Confirmation).', 'Daily settlement processing triggers IFIN010 (Daily Settlement) from Siebel to SonpoWeb and IFIN011 (Settlement Confirmation) from SonpoWeb to Siebel.', 'Siebel decodes the IFIN011 payload, extracts settlement and premium values, and creates a record when the received Policy Number exists.', 'SC has the same functionality and contained 18 duplicate records; Chugoku had no new duplicate records since March 3, 2025.', 'The functionality was determined to be working as expected, with no interface-process change identified.']
Root Cause: SonpoWeb triggered IFIN011 (Settlement Confirmation) with additional clearance-data details, and Siebel created Premium Payment records from the decoded payload when the received Policy Number existed.
Resolution: Duplicate Premium Payment records were updated to "Cancelled". No functional change was made; the behavior was accepted as expected and the ticket was dismissed.

When the daily settlement process is performed through SonpoWeb, two interfaces are triggered:
IFIN010 (Daily Settlement) – From Siebel to SonpoWeb
IFIN011 (Settlement Confirmation) – From SonpoWeb to Siebel
In IFIN011, Siebel receives encoded data, which is then decoded within Siebel. An example of the encoded data is attached for your reference.
From this decoded data, Siebel extracts values for the following fields:
 * Policy Number
 * PPR Receive Date
 * PPR Confirm Date
 * PPR Gross Premium
 * PPR Collection Fee
 * Agent Commission Fee
 * PPR Net Premium
 * Insurance Company Code
 * Sales Rep
Siebel then checks whether the received *Policy Number* exists. If it does, a record is created in Siebel with the extracted values.

Comment: Mr. Miyauchi,

When daily payment processing is performed through SonpoWeb, the following two interfaces are triggered: 
- *IFIN010 (Daily Settlement)*: Send from Siebel to SonpoWeb
- *IFIN011 (Settlement Confirmation)*: Sent from SonpoWeb to Siebel
With IFIN011, Siebel receives encoded data and decodes it within Siebel. Please refer to the attached example of encoded data. After decoding, Siebel extracts the following items: 
- Policy number
- PPR receipt date
- PPR confirmation date
- PPR total premium
- PPR collection fee
- Agency fee
- PPR net premium
- Insurance company code
- Salesperson
Siebel then checks to see if the received policy number already exists, and if so, creates a record in Siebel with the above values.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3357
Investigation Summary: Duplicate Recycle Fee Orders were created for vehicles and affected delivery approval processing. Investigation identified duplicated D21F file processing and confirmed that users entering recycling confirmation in VOW triggered the issue. All affected duplicate orders were recovered across FDP environments; prevention requires users to stop entering recycling confirmation in VOW or a Change Request affecting Siebel and ODI.
Important Findings: ['Two D21F files were received for the same VIN, creating duplicate records: D21F_08012025113917 and D21F_10022025113525.', 'Under the current specification, receipt of a D21F file creates a Recycle Fee Order for the respective vehicle.', 'The issue was determined to occur when users entered recycling confirmation from VOW.', 'Duplicate Recycle Fee Orders were recovered in all FDP environments.', 'If VOW recycling confirmation cannot be discontinued, a Change Request is required for changes to both Siebel and ODI.']
Root Cause: Users entered recycling confirmation in VOW, resulting in duplicated D21F file processing and duplicate Recycle Fee Orders mapped to the Sales order.
Resolution: Recovered all affected duplicate Recycle Fee Orders in all FDP environments. Users were to be instructed to stop entering recycling confirmation in VOW; otherwise, a Change Request is required for Siebel and ODI changes.
Technical Entities: ['Recycle Fee Order', 'Sales order', 'D21F', 'D21F_08012025113917', 'D21F_10022025113525', 'VIN', 'VOW', 'Siebel', 'ODI', 'Change Request', 'FDP environments', 'delivery approval', 'recycling confirmation']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3352
Investigation Summary: During data migration, an unpopulated backend column on the Siebel side caused missing Trade-in Price Total values in the PBI report. Important Findings: ['A backend column on the Siebel side was not populated during data migration, causing missing Trade-in Price Total values in the PBI report.', 'Multiple impacted Sales Orders were recovered for the data-migration issue.', 'Sales Orders A003403571 and A017304950 remained at Trade-in Price Total 0 because they did not meet ODI logic conditions.', 'The issue can be reproduced when an NV Sales Order with a trade-in is posted, the related UV Purchase Order is stocked in, and the stocked-in UV Purchase Order is used for a new UV Sales Order; the NV sales order trade-in amount becomes 0 in PBI report NV_3-06.', 'The ODI behavior was common across FDPs and had been resolved in SC through Incident INC4242736.', 'Required FDP ODI code changes were applied across all UAT environments and UAT was approved.']
Root Cause: A backend column on the Siebel side was not populated during data migration, resulting in missing Trade-in Price Total values in the PBI report.
Resolution: All records impacted by the data-migration issue were recovered. The separate FDP ODI logic fix was applied in all UAT environments, approved for release to PROD, and tracked under MFTBCFFR-3470.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3348
Investigation Summary: A re-edited External WO caused the JV Posting Date for SPO J000192078 to remain at 2025/01/30 while the related work completed on 2025/02/19. Please note that in SPO Work Start Date/Time and Work completion date/time populated from JC Header.
For JC Header Work Start Date/Time is the Start time of WO in which work is started first (in this case 1-E6M77) and Work completion date/time is Completion time of the Last WO (in this case 1-E4SST, Work completion date/time :- 2025/01/30 06:46:45 PM).
As SPO status set to Completion of Acceptance Inspection JV is created and Posting date in JV has the value of Work completion date/time field of the SPO. 
posting date set to 30/01/2025 for JV of SPO J000188523.
 
2. Now, User created another External WO :- 1-F9HQT on 2025/02/19 01:57:28 PM and respective SPO :- J000192078 in Re-edit mode.
For this WO Work Start Date/Time is 2025/02/19 02:05:03 PM and Work completion date/time :- 2025/02/19 02:05:04 PM.
 
For JC Header Work Start Date/Time is the Start time of first WO (same as before 1-E6M77) and Work completion date/time is Completion time of the Last WO (in this case 1-F9HQT, Work completion date/time :- 2025/02/19 02:05:04 PM).
As SPO status set to Completion of Acceptance Inspection JV is created and Posting date in JV has the value of Work completion date/time field of the SPO. 
posting date still set to 30/01/2025 for JV of SPO J000192078 because Work completion date/time of last WO 1-F9HQT is not set to the JC Header.
 
Work completion date/time in JC Header is updated when user click the Generate Approval button on MF Job Card Detail Applet.
Once user clicked Generate Approval Work completion date/time set to 2025/02/19 02:05:04 PM in JC Header and same date is updated in both the SPO.
Posting Date in JV is correct but in SPO Screen Work Start Date/Time and Work completion date/time coming from from JC Header due to this there is a mismatch in JV and SPO dates.
