RCA
1. *First external WO creation*
 - User created *External WO (1-E6M77)* on *2025/01/29 15:54:31* and the corresponding *SPO (J000188523)* was generated.
 - The work start date and time of this WO is *2025/01/30 18:46:06, and the work completion date and time is **2025/01/30 18:46:08*.
 - SPO work start date and time and work completion date and time are obtained from *JC header*.
 - The work start date and time in the JC header is the start time of the WO (*1-E6M77* in this case) where work was first started.
 - The work completion date and time of the JC header is the completion time (2025/01/30 18:46:45*) of the last completed WO (*1-E4SST in this case).
 - *The JV will be created when the SPO status is set to "Completion of Acceptance Inspection", and the JV Posting Date will be set to the SPO work completion date and time. *
 - Therefore, the JV Posting Date for SPO *J000188523* is *2025/01/30*.
2. *Create new external WO (Re-edit mode)*
 - User created *External WO (1-F9HQT)* on *2025/02/19 13:57:28* and generated the corresponding *SPO (J000192078)* in *Re-edit mode*.
 - The work start date and time of this WO is *2025/02/19 14:05:03, and the work completion date and time is **2025/02/19 14:05:04*.
 - *The work start date and time in the JC header will continue to be the start time of the first WO (1-E6M77). *
 - *The work completion date and time of the JC header is the completion time (2025/02/19 14:05:04) of the last completed WO (1-F9HQT in this case). *
 - *JV is created when the SPO status is set to "Completion of Acceptance Inspection", and the Posting Date should be set to the SPO work completion date and time, but this time, the JV Posting Date of SPO J000192078 remained as 2025/01/30. *
 - This is because *1-F9HQT's work completion date and time was not set correctly in the JC header*.
3. *Impact of Approve Button*
 - The work completion date and time in the JC header was updated when the user *clicked the "Generate Approval" button in the MF Job Card Detail Applet*.
 - As a result, *2025/02/19 14:05:04* was set in the JC header and reflected in both SPOs.
 - However, on the *SPO screen, the work start date and time and work completion date and time are obtained from the JC header, so an inconsistency occurred between the JV and SPO dates and times. *
—

Root Cause: For Service Purchase Orders, the JV was created before the Job Card Work Completion Date was updated, so the SPO JV Posting Date retained the old Work Completion Date.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3346
Investigation Summary: The incident involved missing chassis and option asking prices and costs on the NV Quote. Initial investigation could not reproduce the one-time Production occurrence in UAT, but later testing in RT2 identified pricing issues when the RWD date was removed and re-entered while updating chassis and options. A validation requiring the Desired shipping date before chassis selection was implemented, the error-message wording was corrected, and the fix was released to Production on 12 August 2025.
Important Findings: ['The original Production occurrence was recovered, including the actual cost of options, but could not initially be reproduced in UAT.', 'When the RWD date was null, the selected chassis price was not displayed on the NV Quote.', 'In RT2, removing the RWD date and updating the chassis, then re-adding the date and updating the chassis, resulted in chassis pricing being displayed while option pricing became null.', 'The reported issue concerned missing asking price and cost for both chassis and option prices, not only blank chassis pricing.', 'Backend investigation attributed the zero-cost issue to the selected line options.', 'The validation message was corrected to use "Desired shipping date" rather than "scheduled shipping date".']
Root Cause: A null RWD date caused selected chassis pricing not to display; the zero-cost condition was attributed to the selected line options.
Resolution: Added validation requiring users to enter the Desired shipping date before selecting a chassis, corrected the validation-message wording, and released the changes to Production on 12 August 2025.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3343
Investigation Summary: Customer AR records in UAT8 and Chugoku Production had incorrect module open flags after AR data updates. The issue occurred when one NV/UV/Parts/Service responsible department code was blank while the remaining codes were "9999", preventing module flags from being updated. Recovery was completed in UAT8 and then in Chugoku Production.
Important Findings: ['Affected customers were identified in UAT8 and Chugoku Production.', 'During Customer AR data updates, module flags were not updated when one NV/UV/Parts/Service responsible department code was blank and the others were "9999".', 'If a module\'s responsible department is "9999", its corresponding module open flag must be removed; this applies to NV and the other modules.', 'Recovery was completed in UAT8 before being performed in Chugoku Production.', 'Recovery was completed in Chugoku Production.']
Root Cause: During Customer AR data updates, module flags were not updated when one of the NV/UV/Parts/Service responsible department codes was blank and the remaining codes were "9999".
Resolution: Corrected the affected Customer AR module open flags through recovery in UAT8 and subsequently in Chugoku Production, removing each module's open flag when its responsible department was "9999".
Technical Entities: ['UAT8', 'Chugoku Production', 'Customer AR data', 'AR records', 'NV', 'UV', 'Parts', 'Service', 'responsible department code', 'Module Open flag']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3336
Investigation Summary: TOB responses were not reflected in the UI because JMS connections were disconnected during response processing. JMS logs recorded a connection reset error, SBL-JCA-00303. The JMS connection pool size was increased from 60 to 90 and deployed to production on 26/02/2025; no Siebel changes were required.
Important Findings: ['Affected records were recovered before the root-cause investigation was completed.', 'TOB responses were not reflected in the UI.', 'JMS connections were lost during response processing.', 'JMS logs showed: "parseResponse\\{"Error":"Logon Request 18 was abandoned after 1739853464288 ms. Connection: e00080 due to connection shutdown request Connection reset(SBL-JCA-00303)"}"', 'The JMS connection pool was increased from 60 to 90 to accommodate requests from all FDPs.', 'The change was released to production on 26/02/2025 and required no Siebel changes.']
Root Cause: JMS connections were disconnected during TOB response processing, preventing TOB responses from being reflected in the UI.
Resolution: Increased the JMS connection pool size from 60 to 90 and deployed the JMS-level change to production on 26/02/2025.
Technical Entities: ['TOB', 'UI', 'JMS', 'JMS connection pool', 'FDPs', 'Siebel', 'production', 'SBL-JCA-00303', 'parseResponse', 'Connection reset', 'Logon Request 18', 'Connection: e00080']

RCA- In this case the TOB response was not getting reflected on the UI. The issue was the JMS connections was getting lost in middle of the response processing. 
The Error Code which we get in the JMS logs: "parseResponse\{"Error":"Logon Request 18 was abandoned after 1739853464288 ms. Connection: e00080 due to connection shutdown request Connection reset(SBL-JCA-00303)"}"
To fix this issue we will increase the JMS connection Pool Side (increased from 60-90) to accommodate the requests for all the FDPs altogether .
Please approve the following change so that fix will be applied on the production.
Note: Only JMS level changes are required. No Siebel level changes are required.
Regards
Ashutosh Dogra

Comment: Mr. Shiromoto,
Thank you for your continued support.
RCA:
In this case, an issue occurred where the TOB response was not reflected on the UI.
It turned out that the cause was that the JMS connection was disconnected during response processing.
Error code found in JMS log: "parseResponse\{"Error":"Logon Request 18 was abandoned after 1739853464288 ms. Connection: e00080 due to connection shutdown request Connection reset(SBL-JCA-00303)"}"
Countermeasures:
To resolve this issue, we will increase the JMS connection pool size from 60 to 90 and adjust it to handle all FDP requests.
Request for approval:
In order to apply this fix to the production environment, please approve the following changes.
Note:
This support only requires changes at the JMS level and does not require changes to Siebel.
Thank you for your support.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3324
Investigation Summary: Okinawa experienced spreadsheet creation failures caused by duplicate spreadsheet serial numbers, despite having only one agency. Investigation found that serial numbers were generated from 0001 for each Ejibai ID, which could collide with an existing spreadsheet having the same insurance company code, year, and serial number in Completed or Approved status. Tokyo Marine was requested to add codes individually so each branch can create spreadsheets separately.
Important Findings: ['The suspected extra-zero issue in the ID was ruled out; the Siebel configuration matched the provided Excel configuration.', 'Unlike Shikoku and Wakayama, where multiple agency codes caused serial-number overlap, Okinawa had one agency but received multiple requests with the same serial number.', 'For each Ejibai ID, the spreadsheet serial number was generated starting from 0001.', 'A new spreadsheet creation fails when a spreadsheet with the same insurance company code, year, and serial number already exists in Completed or Approved status.', 'The E column in the E-JiBAI Web ID Master file was blank for Okinawa; confirmation was requested regarding bulk-settlement authorization for registered users.']
Root Cause: Spreadsheet serial numbers were generated from 0001 per Ejibai ID, resulting in duplicate serial-number collisions with existing spreadsheets for the same insurance company code and year.
Resolution: Tokyo Marine was requested to add codes individually so that each branch can create spreadsheets separately.
Technical Entities: ['Siebel', 'Ejibai Location Code', 'E-JiBAI Web ID Master', 'E column', 'e-jibai', 'Hitachi GW', 'GW', 'FORCE', 'UAT', 'bulk settlement', 'spreadsheet', 'Ejibai ID', 'insurance company code', 'Completed status', 'Approved status', 'Tokyo Marine', 'FDP Okinawa', 'Shikoku', 'Wakayama', 'Okinawa']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3319
Investigation Summary: The response omitted data because the Planned Payment Date became null for the affected record. With Payment term "00", Payment term type "Month", and Payment date "01" earlier than the Job Card Delivery Date, no Planned Payment Date was generated. The Payment date was changed to "20".
Important Findings: ['Payment term was "00".', 'Payment term type was "Month".', 'Payment date "01" was less than the Delivery Date of the Job Card.', 'When the Payment date was earlier than the Job Card Delivery Date, Planned Payment Date became null and no data was sent in the response.', 'The affected record\'s Payment date was updated from "01" to "20".']
Root Cause: For Payment term "00" with Payment term type "Month", a Payment date earlier than the Job Card Delivery Date caused Planned Payment Date to become null, resulting in no response data.
Resolution: Updated the affected record's Payment date to "20".
Technical Entities: ['Payment term', 'Payment term type', 'Payment date', 'Delivery Date of Job Card', 'Planned Payment Date', 'Job Card']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3311
Investigation Summary: Report data was missing after the IKM was changed in ODI under MFTBCFFR-3269. The initial full load behavior deleted records from the DataMart table. The DataMart backup was used to recover affected data across environments, and reports now display the recovered records; Aomori remains empty because it has no records with qualifying report statuses.
Important Findings: ['The IKM in ODI was changed from IKM Insert Global to IKM Incremental Update under MFTBCFFR-3269.', 'After the IKM change, the IKM initially ran as a full load rather than an incremental load.', 'The full load deleted records from the DataMart table, causing missing report data.', 'A backup of the DataMart table containing the old records was available during recovery.', 'Recovery was completed for all environments and data became visible in reports.', 'The Aomori report has no records because it only includes records with status code "Internal Posted" or "Expired", and no Aomori records meet those conditions.']
Root Cause: Changing the ODI IKM from IKM Insert Global to IKM Incremental Update caused the IKM to initially run as a full load, deleting records from the DataMart table.
Resolution: Recovered the DataMart table records from the available backup and completed recovery across all environments.
Technical Entities: ['MFTBCFFR-3269', 'ODI', 'IKM Incremental Update', 'IKM Insert Global', 'DataMart table', 'Aomori environment', 'Siebel UI', 'Internal Posted', 'Expired']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3303
Investigation Summary: Journal vouchers were not sent to KB because required department-code mappings were missing. The missing mappings were added to the "KB Department Code Mapping Master" in the Chugoku production environment, and the dates of affected records were updated for transmission to KB in the nightly batch.
Important Findings: ['Affected journal vouchers had no corresponding records in the "KB Department Code Mapping Master".', 'The missing mappings were added based on the attached Excel in the Chugoku production environment.', 'All applicable affected records were extracted and their dates were updated for KB transmission during the nightly batch.', 'A list of journal entry slips subject to recovery was attached.']
Root Cause: No mapping records existed in the "KB Department Code Mapping Master" for the department-code values in the affected journal vouchers.
Resolution: Added the required mappings to the "KB Department Code Mapping Master" in Chugoku production and updated the affected record dates so they would be sent to KB in the nightly batch.
Technical Entities: ['KB', 'KB Department Code Mapping Master', 'Chugoku production environment', 'journal vouchers', 'journal entry slips', 'nightly batch']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3289
Investigation Summary: Job Cards created by users associated with SCHQ-CS-Service-Mgr had blank SV_Approver UID values on the Job Card approval screen. The approval flows referenced SCHQ-CS-Service Manager, which was not present in the user position hierarchy and was not configured as a primary position. SCHQ-CS-Service Manager was replaced with SCHQ-CS-SNR-MGR in the affected approval flows, and the changes were applied to Production.
Important Findings: ['Affected JCs had no UID displayed in the Job Card Approval Screen because the Primary Position field was not populated when the approval flow triggered.', 'The affected JCs were created by users holding position type SCHQ-CS-Service-Mgr.', 'SCHQ-CS-Service Manager was included in approval flows but was not present in the hierarchy of user positions.', 'A recovery list was prepared for JCs with null UIDs.', 'The approval-flow changes were applied to Production.']
Root Cause: Approval flows referenced SCHQ-CS-Service Manager, a position not present in the user position hierarchy and not configured as a primary position, preventing Primary Position and approver UID population.
Resolution: Replaced SCHQ-CS-Service Manager with SCHQ-CS-SNR-MGR in the affected approval flows and deployed the changes to Production.
Technical Entities: ['JCs', 'Job Card', 'SV_Approver UID', 'UID', 'Approval Screen', 'Primary Position', 'SCHQ-CS-Service-Mgr', 'SCHQ-CS-Service Manager', 'SCHQ-CS-SNR-MGR', 'Quote Over Discount Mgr 1', 'JC close Over Discount Manager 1', 'Quote Over Discount Manager', 'Quote Over Discount 2', 'JC close Over Discount Manager', 'JC close Over Discount 2', 'Production']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3269
Investigation Summary: An ODI package IKM issue caused updated records to be inserted into the fact table rather than updated, resulting in duplicate Security No.# values and incorrect commission fees. The fix was validated in FDP UAT and deployed to PROD in all environments, after which duplicates were removed and commission fees were corrected. A separate 6_10 report issue was traced to an ODI X_INS_TYPE filter that excluded records from insertion into the DataMart table.
Important Findings: ['The ODI package IKM processed record updates as inserts into the fact table.', 'This behavior created duplicate Security No.# records and affected commission fee values.', 'The ODI fix was validated in FDP UAT, where duplicate Security No.# records were no longer present.', 'Changes were deployed to PROD in all environments, correcting duplicate Security No.# records and commission fees.', 'Data was visible in the 6_02 report.', "The 6_10 report omitted records because the ODI X_INS_TYPE filter only included 'Voluntary Automobile', 'Voluntary Other', 'Voluntary Fire', and 'Life Insurance' values."]
Root Cause: The ODI package IKM inserted updated records into the fact table instead of updating existing records. Separately, the ODI X_INS_TYPE filter excluded non-matching records from the DataMart table, preventing them from appearing in the 6_10 report.
Resolution: The ODI changes were validated in FDP UAT and deployed to PROD in all environments, eliminating duplicate Security No.# records and correcting commission fees.
Technical Entities: ['ODI package', 'IKM', 'fact table', 'FDP UAT', 'PROD', 'Security No.#', 'commission fee', '6_02 report', '6_10 report', 'X_INS_TYPE', 'Voluntary Automobile', 'Voluntary Other', 'Voluntary Fire', 'Life Insurance', 'DataMart table']

Investigation Summary: Assessment-request approval behavior was caused by user D8TSAWAM being assigned the Branch NV/UV Sales Staff position rather than Branch Sales Staff. Root Cause: An incorrect position mapping/assignment in the Shikoku employee master file shikoku_Employee Master0110 assigned D8TSAWAM to Branch NV/UV Sales Staff instead of Branch Sales Staff, resulting in a different approval flow.
Resolution: The CMVM team completed an SR to correct the issue. A change to the Japanese role name was requested to prevent the same incorrect role selection from recurring.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3261
Investigation Summary: Duplicate UV Purchase Orders were created for Trade-in cases when a revised NV quote was approved, using the same assessment number. The defect was fixed and validated in UAT1 and UAT8, and the FDP production release was completed on February 18, 2025. Duplicate purchase orders identified during recovery were canceled after confirmation.
Important Findings: ['In Trade-in cases, approval of a revised NV quote incorrectly created a new UV Purchase Order with the same assessment number.', 'Multiple UV Purchase Orders with the same assessment number can also be valid when an NV quote contains multiple quantities or when an NV order is canceled.', 'The quote-revision duplicate-PO fix passed UAT using the flow: create Trade-In Quote and SO, approve SO, create revised quote, approve revised quote, and verify no duplicate UV Purchase Order is created.', 'The fix was deployed to UAT1 and UAT8 before release to the FDP production environment.', 'The multiple-quantity scenario required separate process changes and was not included in the completed quote-revision fix.', 'The SC version required a separate release planned for February 25, 2025 and SNOW incident tracking.']
Root Cause: A defect in the Trade-in quote-revision flow created an additional UV Purchase Order after approval of a revised NV quote, reusing the same assessment number.
Resolution: Canceled confirmed duplicate UV Purchase Orders and deployed a fix preventing duplicate UV Purchase Order creation after revised quote approval to the FDP production environment on February 18, 2025.

If the NV order is canceled in a trade-in case, a new UV purchase order can be created using the same appraisal number.
These processes have the same specifications for both SC and FDP.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3256
Investigation Summary: Sales orders appeared in the 'My' view for user 'D8AKIHIK' because that user was included in the 'Sales Rep' field on the affected records. Important Findings: ["All affected records had both 'D8AKIHIK' and 'D8KANEMT' in the 'Sales Rep' field.", "Siebel 'My' view displays a record for each user present in the 'Sales Rep' field.", "'D8AKIHIK' is a vehicle manager and should not have been assigned as a sales person.", "Removing 'D8AKIHIK' from the affected sales orders stopped the orders from appearing in that user's 'My' view."]
Root Cause: 'D8AKIHIK' was incorrectly included in the 'Sales Rep' field of the affected sales orders.
Resolution: Removed 'D8AKIHIK' from the 'Sales Rep' field for all affected sales orders.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3246
Investigation Summary: The Item Category Group field was editable across all FDPs for certain positions, including UID:D0X20883. The initial UAT change did not fully enforce read-only behavior, so the field was updated to be read-only for all positions on both the list applet and form applet of the affected View. The validated fix was released to production on February 26, 2025.
Important Findings: ['The issue existed across all FDPs.', 'Item Category Group remained editable for UID:D0X20883 after the initial UAT implementation.', 'The field was changed to always read-only for any position on the affected screen.', 'Read-only behavior was implemented on both the list applet and the form applet for the View.', 'The change was validated in UAT and released to production on February 26, 2025.']
Root Cause: Item Category Group read-only restrictions were not consistently applied for all positions and applets in the affected View.
Resolution: Configured Item Category Group as read-only for all positions on both the list applet and form applet; released the validated change to production on February 26, 2025.
Technical Entities: ['FDPs', 'UAT', 'Prod', 'production environment', 'Item Category Group', 'HQ-MasterMaint-Mgr', 'Branch-Sales-Staff', 'UID:D0X20883', 'list applet', 'form applet', 'View']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3237
Investigation Summary: The recycle-fee submission issue to TOB was caused by duplicate vehicle records with the same recycle fee ticket number. The duplication was reproduced in UAT and traced to a VIN# change occurring after the vehicle had already been migrated, causing the vehicle delta-data import program to create a new record because VIN# is its user key. All identified affected records were recovered under MFTBCFFR-3168.
Important Findings: ['The issue occurs when a vehicle is duplicated with the same recycle fee ticket number, preventing correct recycle-fee processing to TOB.', 'Vehicle "BE740G-400580" was initially created in SC Prod from a TCB01 file with both Fuso reception # and VIN# set to "046754".', 'The vehicle was migrated to FDP Chugoku before D21A from TOB updated its VIN# to "BE740G-400580".', 'During vehicle delta-data migration, the import program treated the updated VIN# as a user key and created a new vehicle record.', 'The user submitted the recycle fee to TOB before the duplicate-vehicle recovery was completed.', 'All impacted records, not only the reported order, were recovered as part of MFTBCFFR-3168.']
Root Cause: A vehicle was migrated while its VIN# was "046754", then D21A updated the VIN# to "BE740G-400580". During subsequent vehicle delta-data migration, the import program used VIN# as its user key and created a duplicate vehicle record.
Resolution: Recovered all identified impacted duplicate-vehicle records under MFTBCFFR-3168, including the reported order.
Technical Entities: ['MFTBCFFR-3237', 'MFTBCFFR-3168', 'UAT', 'SC Prod', 'TOB', 'FDP Chugoku', 'TCB01', 'D21A', 'DJ2A', 'VIN#', 'Fuso reception #', 'Recycle Fee Ticket #', 'recycle fee', 'vehicle delta data', 'import program', 'BE740G-400580', '046754']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3230
Investigation Summary: During recovery of Jira MFTBCFFR-3159, duplicate recycle fee orders existed for the affected vehicles. Because all duplicates were in Pending status with null TOB status and message, recovery selected orders based on Created date and unmapped older orders. An older recycle fee order was mapped to a Sales Order, so unmapping it from the vehicle also unmapped it from the Sales Order. The attached records were recovered, and the SOP will be updated to check Sales Order mappings when processing duplicate recycle fee orders.
Important Findings: ['Duplicate recycle fee orders existed for the affected vehicles during recovery of Jira MFTBCFFR-3159.', 'All duplicate recycle fee orders were in Pending status and had null TOB status and message.', 'The only observed difference between duplicate orders was the Created date; older orders were unmapped and latest orders retained for the chassis order.', 'The older recycle fee order was mapped to a Sales Order, which was overlooked during recovery.', 'Unmapping the older recycle fee order from the vehicle also unmapped it from the Sales Order.']
Root Cause: During duplicate recycle fee order recovery, an older order mapped to a Sales Order was unmapped based solely on its older Created date, causing it to be unmapped from the Sales Order.
Resolution: Recovered the records attached to this Jira and added a planned SOP check to verify whether duplicate recycle fee orders are mapped to any Sales Order before unmapping them.
Technical Entities: ['MFTBCFFR-3230', 'MFTBCFFR-3159', 'recycle fee order', 'chassis order', 'Chassis Order screen', 'UI', 'TOB status', 'TOB message', 'Pending', 'Created', 'Sales Order', 'vehicle', 'SOP']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3230
Timestamp: 2025-02-07T11:25:00
Author: Abhishek Singh.
Comment: We have analyzed this issue and we found that while performing recovery of Jira MFTBCFFR-3159, we had checked that duplicate recycle fee orders were existing for the attached vehicles.
 * When performing recovery for duplicate recycle fee orders, we check which recycle fee order is mapped to the chassis order and is visible on UI under the chassis order screen. 
 * Furthermore, we check if the TOB status and message is present in the recycle fee order and if so, we consider the one with TOB status and message as the final one and unmap the one that has null value for TOB status and message.
 * All the duplicate recycle fee orders were in 'Pending' status and their TOB status and message was null.
 * Only difference in the duplicate recycle fee orders was their 'Created' date.
 * So we unmapped the recycle fee orders with older 'Created' date and kept the latest 'Created' recycle fee orders that were mapped to the chassis order. 
 * While doing so, we missed the fact that the older 'Created' recycle fee order could be mapped to a sales order.
 * As a result, we updated the status of the latest 'Created' recycle fee order which was visible on UI and was visible under the chassis order screen and unmapped the older 'Created' recycle fee order from the vehicle, due to which it was also unmapped from the Sales order causing this issue.
As a precautionary measure to avoid such occurrence in the future, we will add one more step in our SOP while checking for duplicate recycle fee orders to check if they are mapped to any Sales order.
Kindly let us know if you have any further queries.
Regards,
Abhishek Singh.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3230
Timestamp: 2025-02-07T11:35:00
Comment: Mr. Tsunoda,
Thank you for your continued support.
As a result of investigating this issue, we have confirmed that when performing the recovery of Jira MFTBCFFR-3159, there was a duplicate recycling fee order for the target vehicle.
When recovering duplicate recycle fee orders, check which orders are mapped to chassis orders and displayed on the chassis orders screen on the UI.
Additionally, it checks if the TOB status and message exist on the recycling fee order, makes it final if it exists, and unmaps orders with null TOB status and message.
I checked and found that all duplicate recycling fee orders were in a "Pending" status with a null TOB status and message.
The only difference between these orders was the "Created" date, so we unmapped the orders with the older creation dates and kept the orders with the latest creation dates mapped to the chassis orders.
However, during this process, they overlooked the possibility that recycling fee orders with old creation dates were mapped to Sales Orders.
As a result, we updated the status of recycle fee orders with the most recent creation date displayed on the UI and displayed on the Chassis Order screen, and unmapped recycle fee orders with older creation dates from the vehicle.
As a result, it was also unmapped from the order, causing this issue.
To prevent similar issues in the future, we will add a step to our SOPs when reviewing duplicate recycling fee orders to ensure they are mapped to a sales order.
If you have any questions, please let us know.
Thank you for your support.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3213
Investigation Summary: Invoice C050006192 did not trigger the approval flow because it inherited a Dummy primary position from sales order A030793563. The sales order primary position was Dummy because position mapping for the primary position in the order's SC was not provided. The required corrective action is to change the missing position mapping through a service request.
Important Findings: ['Sales order A030793563 had a Dummy primary position.', "Position mapping was not provided for the primary position in the sales order's SC.", 'Invoice C050006192 copies its primary position from the sales order.', 'Invoice C050006192 had position type Dummy, which prevented the approval flow from being triggered.', 'The position mapping must be changed through a service request.']
Root Cause: Missing business-provided position mapping for the primary position in the sales order's SC caused sales order A030793563 to use a Dummy primary position, which was copied to invoice C050006192 and prevented approval-flow triggering.
Resolution: Raise a service request to change the missing position mapping.
Technical Entities: ['A030793563', 'C050006192', 'SC', 'Sales Order', 'Invoice', 'Primary Position', 'Dummy', 'Approval flow', 'position mapping']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3206
Investigation Summary: The incident involved a UV SO and Delivery Request requiring recovery of their statuses. Cubastion changed the UV SO status to 'Approved' and the Delivery Request status to 'Pending Delivery', after which the user was instructed to create a Registration Request and complete the Delivery Request. Resolution: Cubastion restored the UV SO to 'Approved' and the Delivery Request to 'Pending Delivery'; the user was instructed to create a Registration Request and complete the Delivery Request.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3193
Investigation Summary: A recycle fee order associated with a sales order was unintentionally unmapped during recovery of duplicate recycle fee orders for Jira MFTBCFFR-3159. All duplicate orders were Pending with null TOB status and message, so the recovery decision was based only on Created date. The affected record was recovered in Iwate Prod and remapped to the sales order; no product fix was required.
Important Findings: ['Duplicate recycle fee orders existed for the affected vehicle during recovery of Jira MFTBCFFR-3159.', 'All duplicate recycle fee orders had Pending status and null TOB status and message.', 'The duplicate orders differed only by Created date; older orders were unmapped while the latest-created order remained mapped to the chassis order.', 'The older recycle fee order was mapped to a sales order, but this relationship was not checked before unmapping it from the vehicle.', 'Recovery of the attached record was completed in Iwate Prod, and the recycle fee order was remapped to the sales order.', 'The SOP will be updated to verify whether duplicate recycle fee orders are mapped to Sales Orders before unmapping.']
Root Cause: During duplicate recycle fee order recovery, an older-created recycle fee order was unmapped based on Created date without checking that it was mapped to a Sales Order. Unmapping it from the vehicle also unmapped it from the sales order.
Resolution: Recovered the affected record in Iwate Prod and remapped the recycle fee order to the sales order. No product fix was required; the SOP will add a Sales Order mapping check for duplicate recycle fee orders.
Technical Entities: ['MFTBCFFR-3193', 'MFTBCFFR-3159', 'Iwate Prod', 'recycle fee order', 'Sales Order', 'chassis order', 'UI', 'TOB status', 'TOB message', 'Pending', 'Created', 'SOP']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3193
Timestamp: 2025-02-07T11:24:00
Author: Abhishek Singh.
Comment: We have analyzed this issue and we found that while performing recovery of Jira MFTBCFFR-3159, we had checked that duplicate recycle fee orders were existing for the attached vehicles.
 * When performing recovery for duplicate recycle fee orders, we check which recycle fee order is mapped to the chassis order and is visible on UI under the chassis order screen. 
 * Furthermore, we check if the TOB status and message is present in the recycle fee order and if so, we consider the one with TOB status and message as the final one and unmap the one that has null value for TOB status and message.
 * All the duplicate recycle fee orders were in 'Pending' status and their TOB status and message was null.
 * Only difference in the duplicate recycle fee orders was their 'Created' date.
 * So we unmapped the recycle fee orders with older 'Created' date and kept the latest 'Created' recycle fee orders that were mapped to the chassis order. 
 * While doing so, we missed the fact that the older 'Created' recycle fee order could be mapped to a sales order.
 * As a result, we updated the status of the latest 'Created' recycle fee order which was visible on UI and was visible under the chassis order screen and unmapped the older 'Created' recycle fee order from the vehicle, due to which it was also unmapped from the Sales order causing this issue.
As a precautionary measure to avoid such occurrence in the future, we will add one more step in our SOP while checking for duplicate recycle fee orders to check if they are mapped to any Sales order.
Kindly let us know if you have any further queries.
Regards,
Abhishek Singh.

After investigating this issue, we found that when performing the recovery of Jira MFTBCFFR-3159, there was a duplicate recycling fee order for the target vehicle.
When recovering duplicate recycle fee orders, check which orders are mapped to chassis orders and displayed on the chassis orders screen on the UI.
Additionally, it checks if the TOB status and message exist on the recycling fee order, makes it final if it exists, and unmaps orders with null TOB status and message.
I checked and found that all duplicate recycling fee orders were in a "Pending" status with a null TOB status and message.
The only difference between these orders was the "Created" date, so we unmapped the orders with the older creation dates and kept the orders with the latest creation dates mapped to the chassis orders.
However, during this process, they overlooked the possibility that recycling fee orders with old creation dates were mapped to Sales Orders.
As a result, we updated the status of recycle fee orders with the most recent creation date displayed on the UI and displayed on the Chassis Order screen, and unmapped recycle fee orders with older creation dates from the vehicle.
As a result, it was also unmapped from the order, causing this issue.
To prevent similar issues in the future, we will add a step to our SOPs when reviewing duplicate recycling fee orders to ensure they are mapped to a sales order.
If you have any questions, please let us know.
Thank you for your support.

Investigation Summary: The incident concerned inability to map PO# F000194343 and proceed with Sales Posting. Root Cause: PO# F000194343 was already mapped to NV SO# A000194337 and its Sales posting was completed, so the UV PO could only remain mapped to the NV SO under normal SC and FDP behavior.
Resolution: Unmapped PO# F000209715 from SO# E000210402 and completed recovery for the affected record; the remaining PO mapping behavior was confirmed as expected.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3184
Investigation Summary: On the morning of the 24th, D21N, D21R, and D21F file processing did not run because a database-related error stopped processing. Database memory usage became high while FDP Chugoku transaction data was being loaded concurrently. After IT approval, database parameters were adjusted; the affected Okinawa Prod Chassis order was recovered to "Shipment Instructed" with its pool cost order and recycle fee order created and mapped, and the issue did not recur.
Important Findings: ['D21N, D21R, and D21F files did not run on the morning of the 24th.', 'Logs showed that file processing stopped because of a database-related error.', 'Concurrent loading of FDP Chugoku transaction data caused database memory usage to reach a high state.', 'Database parameters were adjusted after IT approval to address the memory issue.', 'The Chassis order on Okinawa Prod was recovered to "Shipment Instructed", with pool cost order and recycle fee order created and mapped.', 'No recurrence was reported after the database parameter adjustment.']
Root Cause: High database memory usage caused by concurrent loading of FDP Chugoku transaction data, resulting in a database-related error that stopped D21N, D21R, and D21F file processing.
Resolution: Adjusted database parameters after IT approval and recovered the affected Okinawa Prod Chassis order, including creation and mapping of its pool cost order and recycle fee order.

Root Cause: Delayed release of 11,000 parts received from D2S allowed the replenishment order batch to run before the parts were released, resulting in purchase orders with no line items.
Resolution: Recovered the 184 affected orders by updating their status to "Cancelled".

Investigation Summary: Sales Order approval failed when the associated Recycle Fee Order had the status "Recycle Order Changed", which occurs after using "Change Order" in the Recycle Fee Order Applet. Root Cause: The Sales Order approval logic did not support approval when the associated Recycle Fee Order status was "Recycle Order Changed".
Resolution: Updated the approval logic to allow Sales Order approval for Recycle Fee Orders in "Recycle Order Changed" status, validated it in UAT1, and deployed it to PROD on March 12, 2025.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3133
Investigation Summary: A Sales Price mismatch between Siebel and FDP PBI reports was traced to ODI logic handling Billing Rate Type values. The logic did not correctly recognize the labor product 'FDP Rate' for FDP Shikoku order I00006001, causing the Sales Price to differ between Siebel and PBI. The ODI logic was corrected, validated in FDP UAT5 using order I000035271, and released to production in the FDP release on February 8, 2025.
Important Findings: ['The incident involved mismatched Sales Price values between Siebel and the FDP PBI report.', "For FDP Shikoku Order_num I00006001, line item 1-1A8DK0 had labor product 'FDP Rate', which did not satisfy the ODI Sales Price logic.", "The ODI logic was expected to include 'FDP Rate' and 'Warranty Rate', but incorrect values such as 'FDP???' and '?????????' were observed.", 'Recovery was completed for the affected mismatched values, after which Siebel sales prices matched the PBI report.', "The corrected logic was verified in FDP UAT5 with ORDER_NUM I000035271 and labor product 'FDP Rate'; values populated correctly in FDP PBI reports.", 'The ODI change was released to production with the FDP release on February 8, 2025.']
Root Cause: ODI Sales Price logic did not correctly match the Billing Rate Type value 'FDP Rate' due to incorrect expected values, so the labor product on FDP Shikoku Order_num I00006001 was excluded from Sales Price processing.
Resolution: Modified the ODI logic in FDP UAT to correctly handle 'FDP Rate' and 'Warranty Rate', validated the fix in FDP UAT5, recovered the affected mismatched data, and deployed the change to production on February 8, 2025.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3108
Investigation Summary: Parts Expense Return Orders displayed the parent order's "Expense Charge To" value in the UI while the return order backend value was based on the return creator's department. The agreed fix copies the original Parts Expense Order's "Expense Charge To" into the expense return order header and updates the UI to display the return order's own stored value. The fix was validated in UAT1 and deployed to Production on 12/02/2025.
Important Findings: ['For Parts Expense Order M000004280, creator D8MAEKAT had department code 8030, but "Expense Charge To" was manually changed to 8040.', 'Parts Expense Return Order M000004307 retained 8030 as its backend "Expense Charge To" based on the return-order creator, while the UI displayed 8040 from the parent order.', 'The same parent-order UI mapping existed in SC.', 'JV mapping used the Expense Return Order\'s "Expense Charge To" value in Department Code (CSJS300), creating a mismatch with the UI display.', 'In UAT1, Expense Order M001290336 was changed from department 1020 to 1030 before creating Expense Return Order M001290337; the return order and its Journal Voucher used 1030.', 'JV recovery was confirmed as not required.']
Root Cause: The Parts Expense Return Order UI mapped "Expense Charge To" from the parent order, while the return order header/backend value was independently set from the return creator's department, causing UI and Journal Voucher department-code inconsistency.
Resolution: Modified expense-return creation to copy the original expense order's "Expense Charge To" into the expense return order header and changed the Parts Expense Return Order UI to display the return order's own "Expense Charge To" value. The change was tested in UAT1, approved, and deployed to Production on 12/02/2025.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3108
Timestamp: 2025-01-28T11:24:00
Author: Divyesh Ghiya
Comment: Thank you for your support.
We have investigated this issue thoroughly and below are our findings:
 Expense charge to in Parts Expense Order and Parts expense order is set by Department code of the order creator. In the record mentioned above (Parts Expense Order : M000004280 and Parts Expense Return Order: M000004307), user D8MAEKAT created these records who have Department code 8030.
While creating Expense order, Department code of the creator is set as Expense charge to in Order. But user san changed the Expense charge to field as 8040 from Order screen. Hence, 8040 department code is set in Parts expense order.
When creating Parts expense return, department code of the creator was set in expense charge to field in parts expense return order which is 8030. On Parts Expense return screen the Expense charge to field shows value of the parent order, that is why 8040 is shown on UI but expense charge to field value in backend in 8030. 
Same mapping logic also exist in SC where Expense Return order shows Expense charge to value of parent order.
In JV, the correct mapping is done where Expense charge to field of the Expense return order is set in Department Code(CSJS300). 
To sum up, JV mapping is correct but on UI, parent order's Expense charge to field is shown in Expense return order. 
Fix Plan: Either we can change the Expense Charge to field mapping in Expense return order where we will show value of the return order rather than parent order expense charge value or we can change the mapping in JV where we will set Parent Order's expense charge to field value in Department Code(CSJS300) of Expense Return Order JV line. 
Kindly validate our analysis and let us know if you have any query.
Regards,
 Divyesh Ghiya

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3102
Investigation Summary: Recycle Fee Orders were not created because the D21F file received from TOB contained an incorrect Fuso Reception#. Initial checks showed no valid D21F file at the Siebel side for the affected VINs. The affected file was corrected with the proper Fuso Reception#, recovered, and the order was completed.
Important Findings: ['For the affected VINs, D21A_17012025171558, D21N_18012025214101, and D21R_18012025214104 were received, but Recycle Fee Orders were not created.', 'The D21F file was sent and received by TOB, but it contained an incorrect Fuso Reception#.', 'The invalid Fuso Reception# prevented Recycle Fee Order creation at the Siebel side.', 'The Fuso Reception# in the affected D21F file was replaced with the correct value and the order was completed.', 'The issue was identified as a TOB-side issue.']
Root Cause: TOB sent an incorrect Fuso Reception# in the D21F file, preventing creation of the Recycle Fee Orders.
Resolution: Corrected the Fuso Reception# in the affected D21F file, performed recovery, and completed the Recycle Fee Order.
Technical Entities: ['TOB', 'Shikoku FDP', 'Siebel', 'D21F', 'D21A_17012025171558', 'D21N_18012025214101', 'D21R_18012025214104', 'VIN', 'Recycle Fee Orders', 'Fuso Reception#']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3097
Investigation Summary: Pool Cost price was blank for Wakayama orders created at branch level because Pool Cost master lookup used only Dealer code values configured for HQ. The fix was implemented in UAT-7 and required validation through a newly created Stock-In Verification because Pool Cost Order creation occurs during Stock-In Verification approval. UAT passed, and the fix was released to the production environment on 29/01/2025.
Important Findings: ['Pool Cost price was fetched from the Pool Cost master using Dealer code only.', 'Dealer codes were configured for HQ, while Wakayama orders were created at branch level.', 'Pool Cost Order is created at the time of Stock-In Verification approval.', 'Testing with a vehicle Stocked-In before the fix could not validate the change; a new Stock-In Verification was required.', 'UAT passed after retesting, and the emergency release was deployed to production on 29/01/2025.']
Root Cause: The Pool Cost master lookup used only Dealer code values configured for HQ, causing Pool Cost price to be blank when Wakayama orders were created from branch level.
Resolution: A fix was implemented in UAT-7, validated through a new Stock-In Verification, and released to the production environment as an emergency release on 29/01/2025.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3089
Investigation Summary: The issue was reproduced on UAT-02 when a Sales Order was cancelled at specified workflow statuses, causing the Vehicle status and sub-status to change to "Sold", "Sold". The behavior originated from logic implemented under FDP CR UV 11/14 Sales Revision Without Change Order to be implemented. The logic was corrected for UV so that a Vehicle is set to "Sold" only after Sales Posting is complete; the change was deployed to Production on 12/02/2025.
Important Findings: ['On UAT-02, cancelling a Sales Order in Registration Completed, Sales Posting Completed, Delivery Completed, or Delivery Pending Approval updated the Vehicle status and sub-status to "Sold", "Sold".', 'The behavior was introduced after FDP CR UV 11/14 Sales Revision Without Change Order to be implemented.', 'The agreed rule for UV is that Vehicle status becomes "Sold" only after Sales Posting is complete.', 'A Sales Order cancelled before Sales Posting must retain its current Vehicle status.', 'The initial change was applied to both NV and UV tracks, but NV changes were reverted because NV has different requirements.', 'The UV fix passed UAT and was deployed to Production on 12/02/2025.']
Root Cause: Cancellation logic introduced after FDP CR UV 11/14 Sales Revision Without Change Order to be implemented incorrectly updated the Vehicle status and sub-status to "Sold", "Sold" when a UV Sales Order was cancelled before Sales Posting was complete.
Resolution: Updated the UV cancellation process so that Vehicle status is changed to "Sold" only after Sales Posting is complete; cancellations before Sales Posting retain the current Vehicle status. The NV change was reverted, and the UV fix was deployed to Production on 12/02/2025.
Technical Entities: ['Sales Order', 'SO', 'Vehicle', 'Purchase order', 'Unmap', 'Stocked In', 'Reserved', 'Approved', 'Cancelled', 'Sold', 'Registration Completed', 'Sales Posting Completed', 'Delivery Completed', 'Delivery Pending Approval', 'Sales Posting', 'FDP CR UV 11/14 Sales Revision Without Change Order to be implemented', 'UAT-02', 'UAT-01', 'UAT1', 'NV', 'UV', 'Production', 'E000002129', 'A001186632', 'E001212525']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3085
Investigation Summary: In UV Purchase Quote, the List Applet fetched Assessment number from Vehicle while the Form Applet fetched it from Assessment Request (AR). When a new Assessment Request was created for the same VIN#, the Vehicle Assessment number was updated and older Purchase Quotes displayed the newer number in the List Applet. The fix aligned both applets to fetch Assessment # from AR, was validated in UAT01, and released to production on February 12, 2025.
Important Findings: ['UV Purchase Quotes created from different Assessment numbers but linked to the same VIN# could display an updated Assessment number in the List Applet.', 'The List Applet sourced Assessment number from Vehicle, whereas the Form Applet sourced it from Assessment Request (AR).', 'Creating a new Assessment Request for the same Vehicle updated the Vehicle Assessment number, affecting older Purchase Quotes linked to that Vehicle.', 'The reported behavior initially matched the SC version existing functionality.', 'The fix was tested on UAT01 using UV Purchase Quote 1-5WJ1LD and UAT passed.', 'The change was released to production on February 12, 2025.']
Root Cause: Inconsistent Assessment number sourcing between the UV Purchase Quote List Applet (Vehicle) and Form Applet (Assessment Request); Vehicle Assessment number updates for the same VIN# changed the value shown for older Purchase Quotes.
Resolution: Changed the List Applet to fetch Assessment # from AR, matching the Form Applet; validated in UAT01 and deployed to production.
Technical Entities: ['UV Purchase Quote', 'Assessment number', 'Vehicle', 'Assessment Request', 'VIN#', 'SC version', 'List Applet', 'Form Applet', 'AR', 'UAT-01', 'UAT01', 'UAT1', '1-5WJ1LD', 'production']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3075
Investigation Summary: The incident affected Power BI reporting for Real Time Service and Real Time Branch. Investigation identified missing X_RPT_JC_TYPE values in SIEBEL DB for specific locations and a required x_5sc_desc_ filter condition for Real Time Branch. The fixes were validated in FDP UAT and deployed to FDP PROD after approval.
Important Findings: ['X_RPT_JC_TYPE existed in SIEBEL DB for Okayama, Iwate, Shikoku, and Wakayama, allowing the values to appear in the Power BI report for the selected period.', 'X_RPT_JC_TYPE did not exist in SIEBEL DB for Aomori, Hakodate, and Okinawa; clearing the period filter could display the value for Hakodate.', 'Real Time Branch required an x_5sc_desc_ filter for Iwate, Shikoku, Wakayama, and Okinawa.', 'The Real Time Branch filter and Real Time Service changes were validated in FDP UAT before PROD deployment.', 'After deployment to FDP PROD, JC Type was no longer displayed in the Power BI report for Real Time Service.']
Root Cause: Missing X_RPT_JC_TYPE values in SIEBEL DB for Aomori, Hakodate, and Okinawa, together with a missing x_5sc_desc_ filter condition for Real Time Branch.
Resolution: Added the x_5sc_desc_ filter for Real Time Branch, fixed the Real Time Service behavior in FDP UAT, obtained validation approval, and deployed the Real Time Service changes to FDP PROD.
Technical Entities: ['Real Time Service', 'Real Time Branch', 'Power BI', 'PBI report', 'SIEBEL DB', 'X_RPT_JC_TYPE', 'x_5sc_desc_', 'FDP UAT', 'FDP PROD', 'UAT', 'PROD', 'Okayama', 'Iwate', 'Shikoku', 'Wakayama', 'Aomori', 'Hakodate', 'Okinawa', 'JC Type']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3066
Investigation Summary: The incident was recovered successfully. Investigation determined that the user created multiple SRs without completing existing SRs and completed them in a non-chronological order, which led to a rare validation gap where a Module flag could be selected without entering the module's responsible shop code. No further corrective action was implemented under this Jira.
Important Findings: ['The user created multiple SRs before completing the existing SRs and completed the SRs in random order.', 'The SR created at 2025/01/20 06:39:44 PM was completed at 2025/01/21 09:22:17 AM, after the SR created at 2025/01/20 07:45:08 PM was completed at 2025/01/20 08:07:48 PM.', 'An existing SR creation validation requires responsible code details when a Module flag is selected.', "In this rare completion-order scenario, the user was able to select the Module flag without entering the module's responsible shop code.", 'A potential future AMS-CR would add validation on the Update AP button requiring existing SRs to be completed or rejected before creating another Update AP SR.']
Root Cause: User mis-operation: multiple SRs were created without completing existing SRs and then completed in a random, non-chronological order, exposing a rare validation gap.
Resolution: Recovery was completed. No additional action was taken in this Jira; a future AMS-CR may add Update AP button validation.
Technical Entities: ['SR', 'Module flag', 'responsible code details', 'responsible shop code', 'AMS-CR', 'Update AP button', 'Update AP SR']

Timestamp: 2025-01-23T10:32:00
Author: Divyesh Ghiya
Comment: Thank you for your support.
This is a case of user miss-operation where user created multiple SRs and completed the new SR first and then completed old SR later. 
User created multiple SRs without completing the existing SRs and then completed SRs in random order. Here SR created at 2025/01/20 06:39:44 PM was closed after SR created on 2025/01/20 07:45:08 PM.
Completion time of SR  created at  2025/01/20 07:45:08 PM.:  2025/01/20 08:07:48 PM
Completion time of SR  created at  2025/01/20 06:39:44 PM.: 2025/01/21 09:22:17 AM:
Also, there already exist a validation where if any module flag is selected, the responsible code details for that module are mandatory while creating SR:
  
This is a rare case issue where user tried completing SRs in a random manner and was able to check Module flag without filling module's responsible shop code. If any further case occur in the future we will add an additional validation through an AMS-CR on Update AP button where existing SRs must be completed(or Rejected) before creating another Update AP SR. 
Recovery is completed and no further action is due in this Jira. Hence, allow us to close this incident. 
Please let us know if you have any query.
Regards,
Divyesh Ghiya

Investigation Summary: The "PO - RecycleUV Purchase Order" order type JV line item had Taxable code set to 10 since the KB Process started. Root Cause: The "PO - RecycleUV Purchase Order" order type JV line item was configured with Taxable code 10 instead of the required fixed tax rate value of 0 for debit and credit tax rates.
Resolution: Set the debit and credit tax rates to 0 for the JV line item of the "PO - RecycleUV Purchase Order" order type, including "Tax rate (CSJS320)" and "Tax rate (CSJS220)", and released the change to production on February 26, 2025.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3055
Investigation Summary: The incident affected synchronization of 'Body Building Name' in FDP when revising Sales Quotes and when creating Sales Orders after Quote Approval. The implementation was aligned with SC behavior, validated for existing UAT1 data, and released to the production environment on January 29, 2025.
Important Findings: ["Upon Sales Quote revision, 'Body Building Name' was not synced to the newly revised quote.", 'Body Building synchronization functionality differed between SC and FDP, causing inconsistent Sales Order synchronization after Quote Approval.', 'SC had no issue in either synchronization scenario.', 'The initial UAT1 fix failed; subsequent testing passed for existing data because UAT could not be performed on newly created data.', 'Testing on newly created data was blocked by the Approval WF on UAT1.', 'The fix was deployed through an emergency release scheduled for 29-01-2025.']
Root Cause: FDP used Body Building synchronization logic that differed from SC, resulting in missing 'Body Building Name' synchronization for revised Sales Quotes and Sales Orders after Quote Approval.
Resolution: Updated FDP to synchronize 'Body Building Name' according to SC behavior for revised quotes and Sales Orders after Quote Approval, then released the fix to production on January 29, 2025.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3045
Investigation Summary: An invoice upsert failed in Siebel with an EAI Siebel Adapter error, and no invoice number was generated. Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3043
Investigation Summary: The Address field in Service Quote BIP was not updated when the corresponding AR address was updated because the two components used different backend Siebel field mappings. The required BIP mapping changes, previously implemented in Wave 1 and Wave 2 production under MFTBCFFR-2575, were applied to FDP UAT-5 and then released to Wave 3 production on January 24. Branch verification was completed and the incident was closed.
Important Findings: ['Service Quote BIP and AR used different backend Siebel field mappings for the Address field.', 'Because of the mapping discrepancy, Address in Quote BIP was not updated when AR was updated.', 'The same BIP mapping changes had already been deployed to Wave 1 and Wave 2 production through MFTBCFFR-2575.', 'The MFTBCFFR-2575 BIP changes were applied on FDP UAT-5 and deployed to Wave 3 production on January 24.', 'Branch verification was completed after the production release.']
Root Cause: Different backend Siebel field mappings for the Address field between Service Quote BIP and AR prevented Quote BIP Address updates when AR was updated.
Resolution: Applied the BIP mapping changes from MFTBCFFR-2575 to FDP UAT-5 and deployed them to Wave 3 production on January 24.

Root Cause: Incorrect or problematic settings in KB caused the Bank Info/account-name value; the value was not supplied by SIEBEL.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3034
Investigation Summary: Duplicate Recycle fee order records caused TOB responses to update a duplicate order rather than the original, leaving the correct recycling order/TOB status unupdated. The incident was initially attributed to duplicate D21F files, but CIH server logs showed no evidence that the file was sent twice and the reason duplicate files existed on the ODI server remained unknown. A VOW-related explanation was later confirmed to apply to a separate Iwate incident, not this Okinawa incident. Affected records were recovered, and the ticket was ultimately closed as a rare case without a confirmed recurrence-prevention change.
Important Findings: ['Duplicate recycling fee orders caused TOB response data to be reflected on duplicate records instead of the original submitted order.', 'The same D21F file was observed twice in the system, resulting in duplicate Recycle fee order records.', 'CIH server logs did not show a history of the D21F file being sent twice.', 'The cause of two identical files being created on the ODI server was not determined.', 'The VOW recycling-confirmation input cause applied to a separate Iwate incident and was not applicable to this incident.', 'Recovery was completed for affected VINs, including updating affected recycling order statuses to Completed.']
Resolution: Recovered the affected recycling order records, including updating their status to Completed. The ticket was placed on HOLD pending recurrence and later closed as a rare case; no preventive system change was documented.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3033
Investigation Summary: An order-related invoice integration failure was investigated despite the spreadsheet being in Spreadsheet Approved status. Important Findings: ['Order Q000010091 was initially associated with a database error and referenced Jira 2964, but it was considered a different problem.', 'System configuration was rechecked and reported as correctly configured.', 'The failure occurred at the "Upsert - Invoice" step through EAI Siebel Adapter: "No user key can be used for the Integration Component instance \'MF Ejibai Invoice\'."', 'No Invoice number was generated following the integration error.', 'Further analysis required the request XML sent from Ejibai to Siebel and revalidation of Ejibai Codes.', 'The incident was determined to be the same as MFTBCFFR-3045 and tracking continued there.']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3006
Investigation Summary: Sales Posting JV amounts and creation behavior for outsourcing orders were inconsistent with the required IBOS and Non-IBOS pricing logic. The existing logic depended on Net Price, causing JV creation to fail when Net Price was absent despite bodywork and other billing amounts being present. The UAT1 fix changed Sales Posting JV creation to evaluate Net Price and Total Selling Price, with the Base Amount set to their sum; the change was validated and released to Prod on 14 May 2025.
Important Findings: ['Initially, JV contained Agency Fee, PO, and CT pricing, while the invoice sent Agency Price plus Total Selling and did not send PO price, causing a JV-to-invoice price difference.', 'For Non-IBOS cases, Total Selling Price was mapped to JV in UAT1; subsequent changes addressed both IBOS and Non-IBOS logic.', 'Outsourcing Order A001292536 did not create a Sales Posting JV because Net Price was not set in Taxes & Expenses and the existing creation condition required Net Price to be non-zero.', 'The required behavior was to create a JV when bodywork and other billing amounts were present, regardless of whether Net Price was set.', 'The corrected Sales Posting JV Base Amount is Net Price plus Total Selling Price.', 'JV tax calculation subtracts License Plate Number Fee and Illuminated License Plate Number Fee from the taxable amount; the validated example calculated tax of 5200 from a taxable amount of 52000 at a 10% Consumption Tax Rate.']
Root Cause: Sales Posting JV creation and Base Amount logic relied on Net Price being non-zero, so no JV was created when Net Price was absent even when Total Selling Price or bodywork and other billing amounts required a JV.
Resolution: Updated the Sales Posting JV condition to check Net Price and Total Selling Price, and set the JV Base Amount to the sum of Net Price and Total Selling Price. The fix was validated in UAT1 and released to Prod in the 14 May 2025 release.
Technical Entities: ['JV', 'Sales Posting JV', 'UAT1', 'Prod', 'IBOS', 'Non-IBOS', 'Outsourcing Order', 'A001290748', 'A001291772', 'A001292536', 'Agency Fee', 'Agency Price', 'PO', 'CT', 'Net Price', 'Total Selling Price', 'Taxes & Expenses', 'Base Amount(CSJ213)', 'Base Amount(CSJ313)', 'License Plate Number Fee', 'Illuminated License Plate Number Fee', 'Consumption Tax Rate', 'FDPs', 'Sielbel']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-3001
Investigation Summary: A mismatch between Actual Expense and Journal Voucher was reproduced on UAT-4 using two browser sessions. Completing the Shaken Expense in one browser created a Journal Voucher using the original Actual Amount, while a stale second browser session could subsequently overwrite the Actual Expense amount. The fix prevents updates to Actual Amount after the Actual Expense is Completed, and the Journal Voucher difference was recovered.
Important Findings: ['The issue was reproduced on UAT-4 with JC# I000031108 and Expense ID 1-JCL44.', 'Clicking Done in Browser 1 marked the Shaken Expense as Completed and created a Journal Voucher with Actual Amount 17,400.', 'Without refreshing Browser 2, changing Weight Tax Actual Amount to 16,800 overwrote the Actual Expense but did not update the existing Journal Voucher.', 'The resulting discrepancy between Actual Expense and Journal Voucher was ▲600.', 'After the fix, users cannot update Actual Amount from another browser once the Actual Expense is Completed.']
Root Cause: A stale multi-browser session allowed the Actual Expense Actual Amount to be updated after the record was marked Completed and its Journal Voucher had already been created, causing the Journal Voucher and Actual Expense amounts to diverge.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2994
Investigation Summary: In the Map/Unmap process for UV Purchase Orders, Journal Vouchers were created when Net Price was zero because the required zero-price condition was missing from the DataMap search specification. The condition was added and validated in UATs, preventing JV creation for zero-price Map/Unmap cases while retaining JV creation when Cost fields contain a non-zero value. The fix was released to FDP on 23 January 2025.
Important Findings: ['MAP/UNMAP scenarios in UV Purchase Orders lacked a DataMap search specification condition for Net Price equal to zero.', 'The missing condition caused Journal Vouchers to be created for zero-price cases.', 'After the fix, zero-amount Journal Vouchers are not created for Map/Unmap cases.', 'A Journal Voucher is still created when any Cost field contains a value other than zero, even if the total amount is not zero yen.', 'The fix was deployed to UATs, passed UAT, and was released in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.']
Root Cause: The DataMap search specification for MAP/UNMAP scenarios in UV Purchase Orders did not handle cases where Net Price equals zero.
Resolution: Added a Net Price equals zero condition to the DataMap search specification for MAP/UNMAP scenarios, preventing Journal Voucher creation for zero-price cases; released to FDP on 23 January 2025.
Technical Entities: ['Map/Unmap', 'MAP/UNMAP', 'Journal Vouchers', 'JV', 'DataMap', 'DataMap search specification', 'Net Price', 'Cost fields', 'UV Purchase Orders', 'UATs', 'PROD', 'FDP', '23rd January 2025 FDP release']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2980
Investigation Summary: The issue was replicated on FDP UAT-4 using JC# I000032336 and Invoice# 1-32491254. A Planned expense created in a Job card defaults to Type "Service Expense", but changing the invoice type to "Expense" from the Service Invoice screen caused the Service invoice to disappear from that screen and appear under Customer Invoice. The Type and Code fields were made read-only in the Service Invoice screen, verified in FDP UAT-1, and released to PROD in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.
Important Findings: ['Planned expenses created under a Job card have a predefined Type value of "Service Expense".', 'Changing the invoice Type from "Service Expense" to "Expense" in the Service Invoice screen moved the created Service invoice from the Service Invoice screen to the Customer Invoice screen.', 'The issue was replicated on FDP UAT-4 with JC# I000032336 and Invoice# 1-32491254.', 'Type and Code were changed to read-only fields in the Service Invoice screen and verified in FDP UAT-1.', 'The fix was released to PROD in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.']
Root Cause: Users could change the predefined invoice Type from "Service Expense" to "Expense" in the Service Invoice screen, causing the Service invoice to be displayed under Customer Invoice instead.
Resolution: Made the Type and Code fields read-only in the Service Invoice screen and deployed the fix to PROD in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.
Technical Entities: ['Planned expense', 'Job card', 'Customer Invoice', 'Service Invoice screen', 'Service invoice', 'Service Expense', 'Expense', 'FDP UAT-4', 'JC# I000032336', 'Invoice# 1-32491254', 'FDP UAT-1', 'PROD', 'FDP release']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2978
Investigation Summary: In the Okinawa production environment, the Self-Contract flag was read-only for Quote# 1-8KE7V because its Contractant Code, 0000001163, was not included in the configured Own-Company codes. The required Own-Company codes were provided for multiple FDPs and configured in production, including Okinawa code 0000001163. An Own-Company code for Chugoku Fuso remained requested but was not provided in the discussion.
Important Findings: ['The Self-Contract flag can be checked only when the Contractant Code is configured as an Own-Company code.', 'Quote# 1-8KE7V used Contractant Code 0000001163, which was initially not among the configured codes and therefore showed the Self-Contract flag as read-only.', 'The existing configuration listed 0000H00031 and 0000GZ6000 for SC use, and 0000108561 for Okayama use.', 'Production configuration was updated with Own-Company codes for Aomori, Hakodate, Iwate, Wakayama, Shikoku, and Okinawa, including 0000001163 for Okinawa.', 'The Own-Company code for Chugoku Fuso was still requested after the production configuration update.']
Root Cause: Contractant Code 0000001163 for Okinawa was not configured as an Own-Company code, causing the Self-Contract flag to remain read-only.
Resolution: Configured the provided Own-Company codes in production, including Okinawa Contractant Code 0000001163.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2962
Investigation Summary: The user could not map or create a Purchase Order for a line item. Investigation found the target Purchase Order was in Pending status, which disables the OK button, and a Purchase Order already existed for the line item. The incident was rejected as expected functionality rather than a product defect.
Important Findings: ['The OK button is inactive when the Purchase Order status is Pending, Pending Approval, Rejected, or Cancelled.', 'The Purchase Order being mapped had Pending status.', 'A new Purchase Order could not be created because a Purchase Order already existed for the line item.', 'To create a new Purchase Order, the existing order must be cancelled or completed.']
Root Cause: The existing Purchase Order for the line item was in Pending status, which prevented mapping, and its existence prevented creation of another Purchase Order for the same line item.
Resolution: Cancel or complete the existing Purchase Order before creating a new Purchase Order; mapping is only available when the Purchase Order is not in Pending, Pending Approval, Rejected, or Cancelled status.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2960
Investigation Summary: Parts Sales return creation failed when the editable Already Returned Qty field in the shipment screen was set to a value equal to the ordered quantity. The failure was reproduced in UAT-5 and caused the Parts Sales Order screen to update its Already Returned Qty with the shipment-screen value, resulting in the validation "Please enter Return Qty." The field was changed to read-only in the shipment screen, verified in FDP UAT-1, and released to production in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.
Important Findings: ['For SO M000034005 in UAT-5, setting Already Returned Qty in the shipment screen equal to the ordered quantity caused return-order creation to fail.', 'The displayed validation was "Please enter Return Qty."', 'After the validation, the Already Returned Qty on the Parts Sales Order screen was updated with the value entered in the shipment screen.', 'The issue was also reproduced for M000031415 in UAT5, while testing with several other orders did not reproduce it.', 'Previously affected shipment-line Already Returned Qty values were reset to 0 for SO M000003330 and M000007642 to allow Parts Sales return recreation.', 'The corrective change made Already Returned Qty read-only in the shipment screen.']
Root Cause: Already Returned Qty was editable in the shipment screen; entering a value equal to the ordered quantity propagated that value to the Parts Sales Order screen and prevented Parts Sales return creation.
Resolution: Made the Already Returned Qty field read-only in the shipment screen, verified the fix in FDP UAT-1, and released it in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.
Technical Entities: ['Parts Sales return', 'Parts Sales Order', 'shipment screen', 'shipment lines', 'Already Returned Qty', 'Return Qty', 'UAT5', 'UAT-5', 'FDP UAT-1', 'FDP release', 'SO M000003330', 'SO M000007642', 'O000003786', 'SO M000031415', 'SO M000034005', 'Please enter Return Qty']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2954
Investigation Summary: FDP users in Shikoku and Wakayama could not create Liability Insurance policies or select the 11SC Agency code because the Production Pick Applet search specification did not include 11SC. UAT was configured for "= 26SC OR =11SC", while Production was configured only for "=26SC" after CR-820 changes had been migrated in FDP but not yet to Production. The Production configuration was released on 9 January 2025, and a subsequent Pick Applet search-spec data issue was corrected so both agency options became available.
Important Findings: ['UAT search spec was "= 26SC OR =11SC", while Production search spec was "=26SC".', 'The configuration difference resulted from CR-820 changes being migrated in FDP while the CR had not yet been migrated to Production.', 'The issue affected FDPs using the 11SC agency, specifically Shikoku and Wakayama.', 'Users could not select the 11SC Agency code on the Insurance order screen.', 'A data issue in the Pick Applet search spec was corrected, after which both agency options were available.']
Root Cause: Production Pick Applet search-spec configuration/data restricted agency selection to 26SC and did not include 11SC. The discrepancy existed because CR-820 changes were present in FDP but had not yet been migrated to Production.
Resolution: Released the required search-spec configuration to Production for Shikoku and Wakayama on 9 January 2025, then corrected the Pick Applet search-spec data so users could select both 26SC and 11SC.
Technical Entities: ['FDP', 'UAT', 'Production', 'Prod', 'Liability Insurance policy', 'Insurance order screen', 'Pick Applet', 'search spec', '11SC', '26SC', 'Shikoku', 'Wakayama', 'CR-820', 'Wave 3', 'Agency code']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2926
Investigation Summary: Sales Posting records required recovery after the process failed to complete. Root Cause: A code issue in the UV Sales Posting process caused rare/random failures to update the sales order status correctly, leaving Sales Posting incomplete at Delivery Pending Approval.
Resolution: The UV Sales Posting code was fixed in UAT1, approved for production, and deployed to PROD in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2916
Investigation Summary: Delivery Request Approval failed because vehicle information was inconsistent between related orders. The inconsistency was traced to recovery for MFTBCFFR-2834, where the Sales Order vehicle was updated but the corresponding Body Building Order was not updated for Trailer and Forklift cases. Recovery procedures were updated, and a later validation confirmed consistent Vehicle IDs across associated orders in all production environments.
Important Findings: ['The incident occurred during Delivery Request Approval.', 'The Body Building Order and Sales Order had different vehicle information for Trailer and Forklift cases.', 'During recovery for MFTBCFFR-2834, the vehicle was updated in the Sales Order but not in the Body Building Order.', 'The issue was identified as a manual recovery error rather than a system defect.', 'Validation across all production environments confirmed that Sales Order, Chassis Order, NV Pool Cost Order, Recycle Fee Order, and NV Body Building Order had the same Vehicle ID.', 'The Recovery Manual was updated to require vehicle-information updates for all related orders during recovery.']
Root Cause: Manual recovery for MFTBCFFR-2834 updated vehicle information in the Sales Order but omitted the related Body Building Order, causing inconsistent vehicle information and the Delivery Request Approval error.
Resolution: Updated the Recovery Manual so vehicle information is updated for all related orders during recovery; associated orders were subsequently validated to have consistent Vehicle IDs across all production environments.
Technical Entities: ['Delivery Request Approval', 'Sales Order', 'Body Building Order', 'Trailer', 'Forklift', 'MFTBCFFR-2834', 'MFTBCFFR-3807', 'Recovery Manual', 'Chassis Order', 'NV Pool Cost Order', 'Recycle Fee Order', 'NV Body Building Order', 'Vehicle ID', 'Vehicle Information', 'production environments']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2913
Investigation Summary: The incident involved incorrect accounting configuration for Trade-In Loss transactions in NV and UV Trade In processes. The configuration was corrected in UAT1, but UAT8 initially failed for SO# E050016909 and Trade-In PO# F050016910, requiring additional changes. After validation, the fix was released to PROD in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.
Important Findings: ['For NV and UV Trade In processes, the Trade in Loss Fuso account code must be configured as the debit account code.', 'For NV and UV Trade In processes, the Bill to account code must be configured as the credit account code.', 'The initial UAT1 fix passed UAT approval, but UAT8 failed for SO# E050016909 and Trade-In PO# F050016910.', 'Additional changes were applied in UAT8 before the PROD release.', 'The incident was released to PROD on 23 January 2025 through the FDP release.']
Root Cause: Incorrect debit and credit account-code configuration for Trade-In Loss in NV and UV Trade In processes.
Resolution: Configured the Trade in Loss Fuso account code as the debit account code and the Bill to account code as the credit account code, applied additional UAT8 changes, and released the fix to PROD in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2906
Investigation Summary: The KB Department code was blank in JV (SV). Investigation confirmed that the Department code was null because the JCO Branch ID was null when the JCO was created by SADMIN for SR MFTBCFFR-2899. Recovery was completed by correcting the JV data sent to KB, and a countermeasure was planned to populate the Department code for backend-created JCOs for SRs.
Important Findings: ['KB Department code was blank in JV (SV).', 'The Department code was null because the JCO Branch ID was null.', 'The JCO was created by SADMIN for SR MFTBCFFR-2899, and SADMIN does not have a branch.', 'Correct JV data was sent to KB after recovery.', 'A countermeasure will update the Department code when a JCO is created from the backend for an SR.']
Root Cause: A JCO created by SADMIN for SR MFTBCFFR-2899 had a null Branch ID because SADMIN does not have a branch, resulting in a null Department code in JV (SV).
Resolution: Recovered the data and sent corrected JV data to KB; implement Department code updating for JCOs created from the backend for SRs.
Technical Entities: ['KB', 'Department code', 'JV (SV)', 'JCO', 'Branch ID', 'SADMIN', 'SR MFTBCFFR-2899', 'JV']
