investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2246
Investigation Summary: A Service Request selected an incorrect Responsible shop code from employee details. The employee master initially contained an incorrect Location code from the first employee-code file, resulting in shop code 7203 for the Default organization instead of 00. A corrected business file updated the employee data, and a newly created SR reflected the correct values and would populate the correct Responsible shop code in account master.
Important Findings: ['The incorrect Responsible shop code was sourced from employee details during Service Request creation.', 'The employee record had shop code 7203 for the Default organization; the expected shop code was 00.', 'The initial employee-code file contained an incorrect Location code.', 'A second file received from the business corrected the employee master data.', 'A newly created SR reflected the correct values and, upon completion, would update account master with the correct Responsible shop code.', 'Employee master reruns will be monitored, with validation of the Location code.']
Root Cause: Incorrect Location code in the initial employee-code file caused an erroneous employee master update, resulting in Responsible shop code 7203 being selected instead of 00.
Resolution: The business provided a corrected employee-code file that corrected the employee master data. A new Service Request was created with correct values and would populate the correct Responsible shop code in account master upon completion; future employee master reruns will be monitored for Location code accuracy.
Technical Entities: ['Service Request', 'Responsible shop code', 'employee details', 'employee master', 'Default organization', '7203', '00', 'Location code', 'account master']

comments.comment:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2246
Timestamp: 2024-04-09T07:47:00
Author: Divyesh Ghiya
Comment: Thank you for your support.
We investigated this issue thoroughly and below are our findings:
When user created Service Request, the Responsible shop code was wrongly selected from the employee details. The Value of shop code corresponding to that employee was for Default organization, which is 7203. The correct value of the shop code should be 00, the wrong value was reflected because of the error in employee master update. The data in the initial file of the employee code was wrong for Location code, which was then corrected by second file received from the business.
As a countermeasure, we will monitor the Employee master records which re run. We will check the location code. 
Recovery: The user created another SR in which correct values are being reflected, the completion of this SR will populate correct responsible shop code in account master.

Divyesh Ghiya

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2243
Investigation Summary: No employee was assigned to the Branch-CS-Head position in Division 10, causing no user to appear for that role in approval flow history. Analysis of the April 1, 2024 employee master execution on Prod found that Position Type Mapping mapped Branch-CS-Head to Branch-Service-Mgr, so D8TMASAA received the Branch-Service-Mgr role instead. The position mapping was corrected and the employee master file was re-executed, assigning D8TMASAA to Branch-CS-Head in Division 10.
Important Findings: ['D8ISHDA1 was assigned to the Branch-Head position, not the Branch-CS-Head position, in Okayama Higashi Branch with 10 Dealer Code.', 'The April 1, 2024 employee master file execution removed D8TOTAKE from the Branch-CS-Head position and intended to assign D8TMASAA.', 'The employee master file operation for D8TMASAA was specified as "Assign" although the investigation stated it should have been "Change".', 'Position Type Mapping mapped Branch-CS-Head to Branch-Service-Mgr, resulting in D8TMASAA being assigned Branch-Service-Mgr rather than Branch-CS-Head.', 'Because no employee held Branch-CS-Head in Division 10, no user appeared for that role in approval flow history.']
Root Cause: Position Type Mapping incorrectly mapped Branch-CS-Head to Branch-Service-Mgr during employee master processing, leaving no employee assigned to Branch-CS-Head in Division 10.
Resolution: Corrected the position mapping on Prod and re-executed the employee master file for D8TMASAA, which correctly assigned the user to Branch-CS-Head in Division 10.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2243
Timestamp: 2024-04-09T14:16:00
Author: Abhishek Singh
Comment: We have analysed this issue and we have found that on 1st April,2024, an employee master file was executed on Prod. 
As per that file, the user initially assigned to Branch-CS-Head position, D8TOTAKE, was deleted and after that operation, same position was to be assigned to D8TMASAA.
But in that step, the operation to be performed on D8TMASAA was given as 'Assign' in the file provided to us. It should have been 'Change' for that step to be executed correctly. 
Hence, the user that was initially assigned the role of Branch-CS-Head position was deleted and no new user was assigned that position. And therefore, no user appeared in the approval flow history for Branch-CS-Head role.
PFA the screenshot from the file that was run on 1st April,2024 for your reference.
Kindly let us know if you have any queries.
Regards,
Abhishek Singh

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2243
Timestamp: 2024-04-10T04:40:00
Comment: Mr. Ikezawa,
When we investigated this issue, we found that the April 1, 2024 employee master file was being executed in the production environment. 
Looking at the file, the user initially held the position of factory manager at the branch. D8TOTAKE, was deleted and then manipulated. The same position was being assigned to D8TMASAA.
However, during that process, the operations performed by D8TMASAA were "assigned" in the file we received. The correct step to take should have been "change". 
As a result, the user who was initially assigned the role of Branch Factory Manager was deleted, and no one was newly assigned to that position. Therefore, none of the users were displayed for the branch factory manager in the approval flow history.
Please refer to the screen copy of the file executed on April 1st.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2243
Timestamp: 2024-04-16T10:27:00
Author: Abhishek Singh.
Comment: We have analyzed this issue and we have found that in the employee master file that we receive, there's a column for position of the employee. When this file is executed, a script is run in which we look for the position type mapped to the position that we receive in the file. Currently in Position Type Mapping, Branch-CS-Head was mapped to Branch-Service-Mgr. So when employee master was executed on 1st April, 2024, the user, D8TMASAA was assigned the role of Branch-Service-Mgr. 
Thus, there was no employee that was assigned the role of Branch-CS-Head, in Division 10.
We have corrected the mapping and executed the employee master file for that user, after which, it was correctly assigned the role of Branch-CS-Head in Division 10.
Kindly let us know if you have any queries.
Thanks,
Abhishek Singh.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2243
Timestamp: 2024-04-17T00:48:00
Comment: Mr. Ikezawa,
(The following is a Japanese translation of Abhishek's comment)
We investigated this issue and found that there was a position column for employees in the employee master file we received. Executing this file will run a script that checks whether the position type is mapped in the received file. Currently, branch factory manager was mapped to branch service manager in position type mapping. Therefore, when the employee master was executed on April 1, 2024, the user D8TMASAA was assigned to the role of Branch Service Manager. 
Thus, there were no employees assigned to the role of Branch Plant Manager in Division 10.
We corrected the mapping for that user, ran the employee master, and then the user was correctly assigned to the role of Branch Factory Manager in Division 10.
If you have any questions, please let us know.
Abhishek Singh.

Investigation found that the SC Siebel changes under AMS CR 610008113 were not reflected in FDP Siebel, requiring an AMS CR on the FDP Okayama Siebel side and a corresponding FDP PBI mapping update. The fix was validated in FDP UAT and deployed to FDP PROD on July 20, 2024.
Important Findings: ['SC SIEBEL changes for "Change Order Completion Date/Time" under AMS CR 610008113 were not reflected in FDP Siebel.', 'FDP PBI Settlement Date for change orders needed to source the "Change Order Completion date" column from Siebel.', 'An AMS CR was required for FDP Okayama Siebel in addition to the PBI change.', 'The PROD release added a new column to the ODI mapping and required a full load of Daily Load Plan.', 'The fix was verified in FDP UAT for reports SV_101, 1_10A, 1_12A, and 1_15A, and the issue could not be reproduced in UAT after the change.']
Root Cause: The "Change Order Completion Date/Time" changes made in SC SIEBEL were not reflected in FDP Siebel, so FDP PBI could not source the correct Settlement Date for change orders.
Resolution: Applied the required FDP Okayama Siebel AMS CR and updated the FDP PBI ODI mapping to source change-order Settlement Date from the Siebel "Change Order Completion date" column; performed a full Daily Load Plan load and deployed the fix to FDP PROD.
Technical Entities: ['FDP PBI', 'Settlement Date', 'change order', 'SC SIEBEL', 'AMS CR: 610008113', 'Change Order Completion Date/Time', 'FDP Siebel', 'FDP Okayama Siebel', 'FDP UAT', 'FDP PROD', 'ODI mapping', 'Daily Load Plan', 'SV_101', '1_10A', '1_12A', '1_15A', 'SC PBI', 'CR:610008406', 'SV_CR_CO Completion Date_Time']

Root Cause: The editable Line Number field in the Chassis Tab of the Quote was changed during Quote revision and Model Code change, preventing the Quote from syncing to the Sales Order.
Resolution: Set the Line Number field to read-only in UAT1, obtained approval, and released the change to PROD on 19th April.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2218

UAT1 validation identified that the Create Return Order button could be pressed when return quantity and return reason were blank, but no return order was created. Resolution: Updated the return-order behavior in UAT1, obtained validation and PROD approval, and released the fix to PROD on 19 April. Related NV Sales Orders were temporarily reverted to "Registration Completed" for return processing and restored to "Sales Posting Completed" afterward.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2206
Investigation Summary: PBI 1_10A Report populated Settlement Date from the Service Change Order LAST_UPD date, causing dates to appear for Change Orders that were still in progress. Analysis confirmed that the PBI logic differs from Siebel, where the relevant field is Change Order Completion date and only approved Change Orders should have a settlement date. A change to PBI SV_1_10A was identified as necessary, and an AMS-CR was requested.
Important Findings: ['The settlement date in PBI was populated using the Service Change Order LAST_UPD date.', 'For JC# I000097002 / Change Order# K000121869, LAST_UPD changed from March 18 to March 19 after an update, and PBI reflected March 19.', 'Using LAST_UPD causes in-progress Change Orders, including recently created and unapproved Change Orders, to receive a settlement date in PBI.', 'Siebel uses Change Order Completion date for the settlement date requirement.', 'Only approved Change Orders should have a settlement date and be displayed in PBI reports.', 'PBI SV_1_10A requires logic changes to align with Siebel.']
Root Cause: PBI 1_10A mapped Settlement Date to the Service Change Order LAST_UPD date instead of the Siebel Change Order Completion date, resulting in settlement dates for in-progress, unapproved Change Orders.
Resolution: An AMS-CR was requested to implement Settlement Date logic changes in PBI SV_1_10A to align with Siebel and populate settlement dates only for approved Change Orders.
Technical Entities: ['PBI', 'LAST_UPD', 'Service Change Order', 'JC# I000097002', 'Change Order# K000121869', 'Siebel', 'Change Order Completion date', 'PBI 1_10A Report', 'Power BI', 'PBI SV_1_10A', 'AMS-CR']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2202
Investigation Summary: The incident concerned changing Adjustment Amount values in Siebel. Directly changing and saving the Adjustment Amount on an existing record was identified as an incorrect operation. Users must end-date the old record and create a new record with the revised amount and corresponding effective dates.
Important Findings: ['Directly changing and saving Adjustment Amount on an existing Siebel record is an incorrect operation.', 'The old record must have its Effective To date populated before the Adjustment Amount is changed.', 'A new record must be created for the revised Adjustment Amount.', 'The new record must have the appropriate Effective From date populated.', 'The required handling was classified as an operation rule rather than a system issue.']
Root Cause: Users attempted to directly change and save Adjustment Amount on an existing Siebel record instead of end-dating the old record and creating a new effective-dated record.
Resolution: Users were instructed to populate Effective To on the old record, then create a new record with the updated Adjustment Amount and an appropriate Effective From date.
Technical Entities: ['Siebel', 'Adjustment Amount', 'Effective To', 'Effective From']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2196
Investigation Summary: The NV Outsourcing Order (KB) API response structure was initially verified as correct, but a subsequent investigation identified that an Expense Item line item had been changed to Penalty Charges by a user. This caused the line item to disappear and resulted in an invalid API structure. The affected order was recovered, and fields contributing to the issue were made read-only and released to production on 8 May.
Important Findings: ['The API Response structure of NV Outsourcing Order (KB) was verified as correct before identifying the data-change issue.', 'A user updated an Expense Item line item to Penalty Charges, causing the line item to disappear and the API to show an invalid structure.', 'Recovery for the related order was completed and confirmed by MDIS.', 'The Type field was changed to read-only in UAT1.', 'The Line# field was subsequently changed to read-only after validation feedback.', 'The changes were validated and released to Prod on 8 May.']
Root Cause: A user changed an Expense Item line item to Penalty Charges, causing the line item to disappear and producing an invalid NV Outsourcing Order (KB) API structure.
Resolution: Recovered the affected order and made the Type and Line# fields read-only; the validated changes were released to Prod on 8 May.
Technical Entities: ['NV Outsourcing Order (KB)', 'API Response', 'Expense Item', 'Penalty Charges', 'MDIS', 'UAT1', 'Prod', 'Type', 'Line#', 'Detail number']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2117
Investigation Summary: Journal Voucher creation failed in Sales Posting and for Individual Purchase Order B000060944 because the IBOS shipment workflow did not meet the existing trigger conditions. The change was developed and tested in UAT, approved after UAT validation, and released to Prod on 8 March 2024.
Important Findings: ['Sales Posting did not trigger a Journal Voucher when Body Building Order-IBOS was not Shipped, even though the related Sales Order status was Acceptance Verification done.', 'Individual Purchase Order B000060944 did not create a Journal Voucher because the Inbound Process of IBOS-Shipment could not trigger the JV.', 'The revised Sales Posting logic triggers a Journal Voucher when Body Building Order-IBOS is either Shipped or Acceptance Verification done.', 'The GR case was handled so that the Journal Voucher is triggered when the status is Shipped.', 'The change was tested in UAT, UAT passed, and the release was deployed to Prod on 8 March 2024.']
Root Cause: Journal Voucher trigger logic required Body Building Order-IBOS to be Shipped and did not handle the Acceptance Verification done status or the IBOS-Shipment inbound process scenario.
Resolution: Updated Journal Voucher trigger logic so Sales Posting triggers for Body Building Order-IBOS statuses Shipped or Acceptance Verification done, and handled the GR case to trigger the Journal Voucher when status is Shipped; released to Prod on 8 March 2024.
Technical Entities: ['Journal Voucher', 'Sales Posting', 'Body Building Order-IBOS', 'Sales Order', 'Acceptance Verification done', 'Shipped', 'Individual Purchase Order', 'B000060944', 'Inbound Process of IBOS-Shipment', 'GR', 'UAT', 'Prod']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2107
Investigation Summary: Purchase type values were incorrect or null in PBI reports because of both report LOV inconsistencies and a Siebel assessment update defect. In Siebel, Assessment purpose remained editable after an assessment reached "Assessment Completed"; cancelling a purpose change with Esc could leave the associated purchase type as null. The fix was validated in UAT1, released to Prod, and affected Prod records were recovered; the Purchase Type filter LOV issue was subsequently rectified.
Important Findings: ['UV_2B had different LOVs between PBI and SIEBEL, causing purchase-type discrepancies for records H000000801, H000002802, and H000003406.', 'UV_2_01_2_02 did not display a value in the SIEBEL UI, so the value was not reflected in the PBI report.', 'Assessment purpose was editable when assessment status was "Assessment Completed".', 'If a user began changing Assessment purpose and pressed Esc to restore the prior value, the UI restored the purpose but set the assessment purchase type to null.', 'UAT initially showed "UV Trade-in" for purchase classifications in 2-01, 2-02, 2-05, 2-06, and 2-01(History), rather than "Magotori".', 'After the Prod release, the Purchase Type filter in 2-01 and 2-02 incorrectly included "SV reception category" LOV values; this was rectified.']
Root Cause: In Siebel, Assessment purpose could be edited after an assessment was "Assessment Completed". Cancelling an in-progress Assessment purpose change with Esc restored the displayed purpose but left the associated purchase type set to null. Separate PBI and SIEBEL LOV differences also caused UV_2B purchase-type discrepancies.
Resolution: The issue was fixed and validated in UAT1, then released to Prod. Affected Prod records were recovered, PBI reports were refreshed, and the Purchase Type filter LOV issue was rectified.
Technical Entities: ['UV_2B', 'UV_2_01_2_02', 'PBI', 'SIEBEL', 'SIEBEL UI', 'Siebel UV Inventory', 'Assessment purpose', 'Assessment Completed', 'purchase type', 'UAT', 'UAT1', 'Prod', '2-01', '2-02', '2-05', '2-06', '2-01(History)', '2B', '2-01 Used car inventory details', 'UV Trade-in', 'Magotori', 'Purchase Type filter', 'SV reception category', 'H000000801', 'H000002802', 'H000003406']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2107
Timestamp: 2024-02-07T07:41:00
Author: Abhishek Singh.
Comment: Dear Shiromoto san,
We have analyzed this issue and we've found that Assessment purpose is editable even when the status of the assessment is 'Assessment Completed'. Since it is editable, user can change the assessment purpose, and in that process, if we set the assessment purpose to null, although it will not be saved, but its purchase type will be set to null. And then as soon as we press Esc, the assessment purpose will be set back to its previous value, but now, its purchase type has been set to null. Thus, causing this issue.
User steps would be:
 # Create an assessment and approve it
 # Since assessment purpose is editable, trying to change it.
 # Changing the assessment purpose mid process back to its previous value(Pressing Esc)
 # Now, on UI, Assessment purpose is set back to its original value. But in that process, the purchase type for that assessment is set to null.
Let us know if you have any queries.
Regards,
Abhishek Singh.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2088
Investigation Summary: A deleted line item in UV Sales Quote (Revision 1) caused a line-number mismatch between the quote and the UV Sales Order created through the auto order button. During synchronization of UV Sales Quote (Revision 3), the mismatch deleted order line items and child records, causing the sync to fail when updating Line Item# 5. The corrective change disabled deletion from the Line Items tab while retaining deletion of Liability Insurance through the Taxes and Expenses tab; the change was validated in UAT1 and deployed to PROD.
Important Findings: ['Deleting Line Item# 4, Expense (S07), from UV Sales Quote (Revision 1) removed Line Item# 4 from the Backend Column.', 'The UV Sales Order created through the auto order button still contained Line Item# 4 for Recycle Fee(YN5Z).', 'During synchronization of UV Sales Quote (Revision 3), Line Item# 4 and its child records were deleted from the order, which also deleted Line Item# 5.', 'The sync failed when UV Sales Quote Line Item# 5 attempted to update the already deleted UV Sales Order Line Item# 5.', 'The FDP fix disables the Delete button on the Line Items tab; Liability Insurance can only be deleted from the Taxes and Expenses tab.', 'The change passed UAT1 validation and was implemented on PROD.']
Root Cause: Deletion of Line Item# 4 from UV Sales Quote (Revision 1) created a Backend Column line-number mismatch with the UV Sales Order, which retained Line Item# 4 after auto-order creation. Synchronization of UV Sales Quote (Revision 3) then deleted order lines and child records, including Line Item# 5, causing the subsequent Line Item# 5 update to fail.
Resolution: Disabled the Delete button on the Line Items tab and restricted deletion of Liability Insurance to the Taxes and Expenses tab. The change was implemented in UAT1, passed UAT, and was deployed to PROD.
Technical Entities: ['UV Sales Quote', 'UV Sales Order', 'FDP UAT1', 'UAT1', 'PROD', 'FDP version', 'SC version', 'FDP-Okayama release', 'UV Sales Quote (Revision 1)', 'UV Sales Quote (Revision 2)', 'UV Sales Quote (Revision 3)', 'Line Item# 4', 'Line Item# 5', 'Expense (S07)', 'Recycle Fee(YN5Z)', 'Backend Column', 'auto order button', 'Sync', 'Order Intake', 'Line Items tab', 'Taxes and Expenses tab', 'Liability Insurance', 'E001241833', '1-48EACR', 'E000069250', '1-N9KHP']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2083
Investigation Summary: Rejected and incomplete used-car sales orders appeared in reports because users manually populated date fields used by report filters. UV SO# E000087121 appeared in the Order Report despite Rejected status because Approval Date was manually entered; UV SO# E000037797 appeared in the sales report because Delivery Completion Approved Date was manually entered. The incident was classified as user misoperation and closed with no system fix required.
Important Findings: ['Approval Date is normally auto-populated when an approver approves a Sales Order, but it was manually entered for UV SO# E000087121 before approval was requested.', 'The Order Report filters approved orders based on Approval Date, so UV SO# E000087121 appeared even after rejection by the Branch Head.', 'Delivery Completion Approved Date is normally populated when the Delivery Request is completed, but it was manually entered for UV SO# E000037797.', 'The Sales Order Reporting screen filters sales-posting-completed orders based on Delivery Completion Approved Date, causing UV SO# E000037797 to appear in the sales report.', 'Making the two date fields Read Only was confirmed as possible and not expected to affect functionality, but no change was implemented because the issue was handled through user operation.']
Root Cause: User misoperation: manual entry of Approval Date and Delivery Completion Approved Date caused orders to satisfy date-based report filters regardless of their actual approval or delivery-completion status.
Resolution: No system fix was implemented. The incident was handled through user operation and the Jira was rejected/closed.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2082
Investigation Summary: Parts Sales Orders created from the Part dealer sale order screen did not populate fixed tax rates because a Parts Quote is not required in that flow. Root Cause: The Part dealer sale order screen creates Part Sales Orders without requiring a Parts Quote, but the fixed tax rate population depended on the Parts Quote.
Resolution: Updated the logic to store the fixed tax rate based on the tax type of the added part number, including detail lines; resolved the shipment drilldown issue; validated on UAT-1 and released to Production.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2069
Investigation Summary: PO Creation Outbound interface processing experienced duplicate triggers after CPI system timeouts caused Siebel to retry. Recovery was completed by updating affected POs with D2S SO numbers and PO dates, reprocessing allocation and shipment where required, and setting the header status to Ordered. The timeout parameter was increased from 180 to 300 seconds, after which the issue was reported resolved and monitoring was performed.
Important Findings: ['CPI system timeouts triggered the retry mechanism in Siebel, resulting in multiple triggers despite evidence that only one trigger was initially sent from the Siebel side.', 'The retry mechanism was configured for other Outbound Interfaces and was reported to be operating without issues.', 'The PO Creation Outbound interface timeout parameter was increased from 180 to 300 seconds.', 'Affected POs required D2S SO number and PO date updates, allocation reprocessing, shipment creation for BANS, and header status changes to Ordered.', 'All recoveries were completed before the incident was closed.']
Root Cause: A timeout from the CPI system caused the Siebel retry mechanism to send multiple triggers for the PO Creation Outbound interface.
Resolution: Increased the PO Creation Outbound interface timeout from 180 to 300 seconds and completed recovery of affected POs by reprocessing allocation and shipment as needed, then setting header status to Ordered.
Technical Entities: ['CPI system', 'Siebel', 'SIEBEL', 'Network team', 'Outbound Interfaces', 'PO Creation Outbound interface', 'D2S', 'PI team', 'D2S SO number', 'PO date', 'allocation', 'shipment', 'BANS', 'header status', 'Ordered', 'timeout parameter']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2066
Investigation Summary: Profit values differed between PBI Report UV_2_05 and UV_2_06 because repair fee cost was sourced from UV Inventory under the recorded transaction sequence. Root Cause: The UV Body Building PO was created from UV Inventory before sales posting status, causing PBI Report UV_2_05 and UV_2_06 to use the repair fee cost from UV Inventory while the Sales quote value was zero.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2065
Investigation Summary: UV Sales Order Reporting had not been updated to match the Sales Order logic introduced by CR "FDP CR UV Inventory_01 Individual Cost for Inventory Repair". Repair fees were not deducted from the sales price, causing 70,000 to be reported instead of 64,300, and UAT also identified missing cost-field calculation in Sales Report and Order Interk Rerpot. The logic and PBI were corrected on UAT1, passed UAT, and were released to PROD without reported issues.
Important Findings: ['UV Sales Order Reporting did not deduct the 5,700 repair fee from the 70,000 sales price.', 'The expected reported value after repair-fee deduction was 64,300.', 'Initial UAT showed profit was correct, but cost was not included in the Cost field calculation in Sales Report and Order Interk Rerpot.', 'PBI initially had no data and was corrected on UAT1.', 'UAT passed after the fixes, and the PROD check reported no problem.']
Root Cause: UV Sales Order Reporting logic was not updated to align with the Sales Order changes from CR "FDP CR UV Inventory_01 Individual Cost for Inventory Repair", resulting in repair fees not being deducted and incomplete cost-field calculation.
Resolution: Corrected the UV Sales Order Reporting and PBI logic on UAT1 to deduct repair fees and include cost-field calculation; after UAT approval, the changes were released to PROD.
Technical Entities: ['Sales Order', 'FDP CR UV Inventory_01 Individual Cost for Inventory Repair', 'UV Sales Order Reporting', 'Repair fees', 'Sales Report', 'Order Interk Rerpot', 'Cost field', 'UAT1', 'SO:E001235374', 'PBI', 'PROD']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2045
Investigation Summary: BIP generation failed because the Tax Rate column in NV Sales Order was set to null. The Generate Approval logic queried Consumption Tax Master using the Sales Order Last Contract Date for FDP-Okayama orders with an acknowledgment date earlier than the current date; no matching tax-master record was found. The Consumption Tax Master start date was changed in FDP-Okayama Prod to match the SC version, allowing tax percent to be set correctly.
Important Findings: ['Tax percent in Sales Order originates from the sales quote but is recalculated by logic behind the Generate Approval button.', 'For acknowledgment dates earlier than today, the logic queries Consumption Tax Master using Start Date <= Last Contract Date <= End Date.', 'In FDP-Okayama, the acknowledgment date was 2020/11/30 and affected orders had a Last Contract Date earlier than the Consumption Tax Master start date of 2023/07/29.', 'The Consumption Tax Master query returned zero records, causing tax percent and the NV Sales Order Tax Rate column to be set to null.', 'The same behavior was reproduced in SC UAT1 using Order A025013709 with Last Contract Date 2018/01/31 earlier than Start Date 2020/11/30, resulting in Order Sheet BIP failure.', 'The logic was confirmed to be the same as in SC.']
Root Cause: The Consumption Tax Master start date in FDP-Okayama was later than the affected Sales Order Last Contract Date. For acknowledgment dates earlier than today, the Generate Approval logic queried tax records by Last Contract Date and returned no result, setting tax percent to null and causing BIP generation failure.
Resolution: Changed the Consumption Tax Master start date in FDP-Okayama Prod to match the SC version: 2019/10/01.
Technical Entities: ['BIP', 'NV Sales Order', 'Sales Order', 'Tax Rate', 'tax percent', 'sales quote', 'Generate Approval', 'Consumption Tax Master', 'Acknowledgment Date', 'Last Contract Date', 'Planned Delivery Date', 'Start Date', 'End Date', 'FDP-Okayama', 'FDP-Okayama Prod', 'SC', 'SC UAT1', 'Order A025013709', 'Order Sheet BIP']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2045
Timestamp: 2024-01-10T12:33:00
Author: Divyesh Ghiya
Comment: We investigated this issue thorughly and below are our findings:
In Sales Order, tax percent comes from the sales quote but there is a logic written behind Generate Approval button. In this logic, Whenever user clicks generate approval, tax rate is being searched in Consumption Tax Master in following manner:
First, query by acknowledgment date in consumption master, 
if acknowledgment date is >= Today then:
Condition 1: Last Contract Date <= Acknowledgment Date
Condition 2: Last Contract Date >= Acknowledgment Date
else,
Condition 3: acknowledgment date < Today
For condition 1 and 3, we then query start date <= Last Contract Date <= End Date
For condition 2, we query start date <= Planned Delivery Date <= End Date
In FDP-Okayama, Acknowledgment date is 2020/11/30(which is less then today), so condition 3 will be followed and query will be done on the basis of Last Contract Date in Sales Order. In all the orders we shared with you, you can find that last contract date was less then start date(2023/07/29), hence there were 0 results of the query and tax percent was set to null.
*This logic is same as in SC.*
We replicated the same test case in SC UAT1 where se set Last Contract Date(2018/01/31) less then Start Date (2020/11/30) in Order A025013709. In this case also, tax percent was set to null and order sheet bip was failed.
one solution to avoid this in FDP is to set Start Date same as SC so that query will not give null result and tax percent is set properly.
Kindly, confirm this RCA and let us know if you have any query.
Regards,
Divyesh Ghiya

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2019
Investigation Summary: For PO - Body Building Order - Non IBOS, the Journal Voucher account item code was determined using the Vehicle product class derived from VIN. When VIN was null, the product class defaulted to Others and selected the class-Others account item code. The logic was changed to fetch the Vehicle Product Class from the Sales Order Screen, validated in Uat, and released to Prod.
Important Findings: ['The original logic fetched the Vehicle product class from VIN.', 'When VIN was null, the product class was set to Others.', 'The Others product class caused the Journal Voucher for PO - Body Building Order - Non IBOS to use the class-Others account item code.', 'The corrected logic fetches the Vehicle Product Class from the Sales Order Screen.', 'The fix was tested in Uat, approved after validation, and released to Prod.']
Root Cause: The Vehicle product class was derived from VIN; when VIN was null, it defaulted to Others, resulting in selection of the class-Others account item code in the Journal Voucher.
Resolution: Updated the logic to fetch the Vehicle Product Class from the Sales Order Screen instead of VIN, then tested it in Uat and released it to Prod.
Technical Entities: ['VIN', 'Vehicle', 'Product Class', 'Others', 'Journal Voucher', 'PO - Body Building Order - Non IBOS', 'class-Others', 'Sales Order Screen', 'Uat', 'Prod']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2016
Investigation Summary: Debit department code was missing for certain Journal Voucher entries because the Responsible Service Shop Code was null for account 1000004435. The mapping behavior differed by journal line type: Parts Sales Consumption Excl and Parts Sales Consumption Tax used the Responsible Service Shop Code, while Parts Sales Cost used the Inventory Name. Sales Order M000067949 was recovered, the fix was tested in UAT, and released to Prod.
Important Findings: ['For account 1000004435, Responsible Service Shop Code was null on the Account Receivable Screen of Accounts.', 'Journal Voucher debit department code for Parts Sales Consumption Excl and Parts Sales Consumption Tax is mapped from Responsible Service Shop Code.', 'Journal Voucher debit department code for Parts Sales Cost is mapped from Inventory Name on the Parts Sales Order Screen, so this entry retained a debit department code.', 'Recovery of Sales Order M000067949 was completed.', 'The change was tested successfully in UAT and released to Prod.']
Root Cause: Responsible Service Shop Code was null for account 1000004435, causing the mapped debit department code to be null for Parts Sales Consumption Excl and Parts Sales Consumption Tax in Journal Voucher.
Resolution: Sales Order M000067949 was recovered and the corrective change was tested in UAT and released to Prod.
Technical Entities: ['Journal Voucher', 'Debit department code', 'Parts Sales Consumption Excl', 'Parts Sales Consumption Tax', 'Responsible Service Shop Code', 'Account Receivable Screen', 'Accounts', 'account-1000004435', 'Parts Sales Cost', 'Inventory Name', 'Parts Sales Order Screen', 'Sales Order M000067949', 'AMS CR', 'uat', 'Prod']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2016
Timestamp: 2023-12-18T07:15:00
Comment: Dear Miyauchi San,
We have investigated the issue and due to the below reasons debit department code was not set in Journal Voucher
 
1. In Journal Voucher ,the Debit department code of Parts Sales Consumption Excl and Parts Sales Consumption Tax is mapped from Responsible Service Shop Code from Account Receivable Screen of Accounts. In this case, the Responsible Service Shop Code is null for this account-1000004435 and due to which debit department code was set to null.
 
2. In Journal Voucher ,the Debit department code of Parts Sales Cost is mapped from Inventory Name of Parts Sales Order Screen.
Due to which it had debit department code in the Journal Voucher Screen.
Thanks 
Amit

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2013
Investigation Summary: The Parts Quote estimation action failed because the user set the record Active flag to N before attempting estimation. An inactive record cannot be updated, so the status could not change and the system displayed "The record in not editable". The behavior was confirmed in UAT1 and is existing functionality consistent with SC; the incident was rejected as no product defect was identified.
Important Findings: ['Parts sub-quotes created from the NV sub-quotes screen have a null branch Id, so no branch name is displayed on the Parts Quote screen.', 'Setting the Active flag to N makes the Parts Quote record inactive and non-editable.', 'The Estimate button cannot update an inactive record; therefore, the Parts Quote status does not change.', 'With the Active flag set to Y, the estimation process works correctly.', 'The behavior was replicated and confirmed in UAT1 and is consistent with SC.']
Root Cause: The user set the Parts Quote Active flag to N before estimation, making the record inactive and preventing the Estimate action from updating its status.
Resolution: Set the Active flag to Y before clicking the Estimate button. No system change was required; the incident was rejected as expected business functionality.
Technical Entities: ['Parts Quote', 'parts sub-quote', 'NV sub-quotes screen', 'branch Id', 'branch name', 'Active flag', 'Estimate button', 'status', 'UAT1', 'SC', 'The record in not editable']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-2000
Investigation Summary: UV Body Building Purchase Orders existed for the affected Additionaly body line items but were not mapped to the UV Sales order and therefore were not visible in the UI. Investigation found that the purchase order IDs were present on the line items, but their parent sales order IDs had been set to null, consistent with a user unmapping the POs through the UI. The user manually recovered the records and the business process was confirmed to be functioning normally.
Important Findings: ['UV Body Building Purchase Orders were created for the affected line items but were not mapped in the UV Sales order.', 'Both affected Additionaly body line items had purchase order IDs mapped to them.', 'When a user unmaps a PO through the UI, the PO parent sales order ID is set to null.', 'A null parent sales order ID causes the PO to not be visible in the UI.', 'The user manually recovered the incident.']
Root Cause: User mis-operation: the Purchase Orders were unmapped through the UI, which set their parent sales order IDs to null.
Resolution: The user manually recovered the affected Purchase Order mappings; no business-process defect was identified.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1983
Investigation Summary: Approval routing for Quote and Job Card was using the total of all Non-chargeable costs when a Free Cost line item was present, causing approval escalation up to HQ for JC I000049866 / Quote 1-MDQ71. The required logic was to evaluate only the Non Chargeable Cost Total for the applicable line item type: 42 (Free Cost) or 45 (Reworking). Separate total fields were created, validated in FDP UAT-1, and deployed to PROD on 9th April.
Important Findings: ['For JC I000049866 / Quote 1-MDQ71, the presence of a Free Cost line item caused all Non-chargable values to be summed to 19190, exceeding the 10000 approval threshold.', 'The approval flow must use Non Chargeable Cost Total for Line Item Type 42 only when Line Item Type 42 (Free Cost) exists.', 'The same line-item-specific calculation logic is required for Line Item Type 45 (Reworking).', 'The existing configuration behaved the same in UAT and required both Siebel configuration and approval flow changes.', 'New Total of Non-chargeable Cost fields were created for Line Item Type 42 and Line Item Type 45 and used for Quote and Job Card approver selection.', 'FDP UAT-1 confirmed that approvers were judged using only the Free Cost total before PROD deployment.']
Root Cause: The approval rule summed all Non-chargable costs whenever a Free Cost line item was present, rather than calculating and using the Non Chargeable Cost Total for the relevant line item type only.
Resolution: Created separate Total of Non-chargeable Cost fields for Line Item Type 42 (Free Cost) and Line Item Type 45 (Reworking), updated Quote and Job Card approver selection to use the applicable line-item-specific total, validated in FDP UAT-1, and deployed to PROD on 9th April.
Technical Entities: ['JC I000049866', 'Quote 1-MDQ71', 'Free Cost', 'Non-chargable', 'Non Chargeable Cost Total', 'HQ', 'Line Item Type 42', 'Line Item Type 45', 'Reworking', 'Siebel', 'approval flow', 'Quote', 'Job Card', 'FDP UAT-1', 'UAT', 'PROD']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1978
Investigation Summary: Employee records were being interfaced to KB despite the relevant data having been last updated in August. Investigation confirmed that records with the same employee code could include active and inactive entries, with HMCP004 identifying the active/inactive status in the outbound file. The interface logic was changed so records are sent to KB only when the employee master is updated, and duplicate employee-code records use the latest updated record. The fix was tested in UAT and released to Prod on December 15.
Important Findings: ['The reported records were not duplicate records in the initial assessment: one employee record was inactive and another was active.', 'HMCP004 identifies whether an employee record is active or inactive and was sent in the file accordingly.', 'The incident required clarification of why data last updated in August was sent to the accounting magistrate on the prior day.', 'The interface to KB was changed to send affected records only when the employee master is updated.', 'For duplicate employee code records, the most recently updated record is interfaced to KB.', 'The fix was validated in UAT before release to Prod.']
Root Cause: The KB interface logic did not restrict outbound records to employee-master updates and did not select the latest updated record when employee codes were duplicated.
Resolution: Updated the KB interface so it sends affected records only when the employee master is updated and selects the latest updated record for duplicate employee codes; tested in UAT and deployed to Prod on December 15.
Technical Entities: ['HMCP004', 'Siebel UI', 'employee master', 'KB', 'UAT', 'Prod', 'accounting magistrate', 'employee code']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1974
Investigation Summary: VIN selection in the vehicle-search pick applet was blocked when the Quote vehicle allocation flag was set to 'Y'. The implemented vehicle-search validation excluded assessments with this flag value, including Stocked Vehicles that needed to be related to Opportunity. The fix sets the Vehicle Assessment Allocation Flag to 'N' when a vehicle status becomes 'Stocked-In' with sub-status 'Available'; it passed UAT and was released to Prod on 5 Dec.
Important Findings: ["Vehicle search displayed only assessments whose Quote vehicle allocation flag was not 'Y', preventing the VIN from appearing in the pick applet.", 'The validation affected the function to relate an already Stocked Vehicle to Opportunity and was identified as not being a stated Opportunity BRD requirement.', 'The affected record was recovered through SR MFTBCFFR-1975.', "The implemented fix automatically sets the Vehicle Assessment Allocation Flag to 'N' when vehicle status is 'Stocked-In' and sub-status is 'Available'.", 'The fix was validated in UAT using Assessment#H000024836, approved, and released to Prod.']
Root Cause: Vehicle-search validation excluded assessments with the Quote vehicle allocation flag set to 'Y', blocking selection of Stocked Vehicle VINs for Opportunity.
Resolution: Modified the logic so the Vehicle Assessment Allocation Flag is set to 'N' when a vehicle is set to status 'Stocked-In' and sub-status 'Available'; the change passed UAT and was deployed to Prod.
Technical Entities: ['Quote vehicle allocation flag', 'Vehicle Assessment Allocation Flag', 'vehicle search', 'pick applet', 'VIN', 'Opportunity', 'Stocked Vehicle', 'Assessment', 'H000002102', 'SR MFTBCFFR-1975', 'CR UV - 05(Sprint A)', 'UV-05 BRD', 'UAT', 'UAT1', 'Assessment#H000024836', 'Prod', 'Stocked-In', 'Available']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1971
Investigation Summary: The issue was investigated in relation to vehicle and account details used in the Job Card (JC) during quote creation. The implemented fix populates missing finance account codes from JC fields. The change was validated in UAT-1, approved for production, and released in the 5th Dec FDP Release.
Important Findings: ['Quote creation from JC required validation of Bill To Finance Account Code and Sold To Finance Account Code.', 'When Bill To Finance Account Code is null, it is populated using the Bill To Basic Account Code from the JC.', 'When Sold To Finance Account Code is null, it is populated using the Customer Code from the JC.', 'The change was deployed to UAT-1 before production approval.', 'The fix is available in Prod following the 5th Dec FDP Release.']
Root Cause: Bill To Finance Account Code and Sold To Finance Account Code could be null during quote creation from a Job Card (JC).
Resolution: Updated quote creation from JC to populate Bill To Finance Account Code from the JC Bill To Basic Account Code and Sold To Finance Account Code from the JC Customer Code when the respective finance account code is null; deployed to Prod.
Technical Entities: ['Job Card (JC)', 'Quote', 'Bill To Finance Account Code', 'Sold To Finance Account Code', 'Bill To Basic Account Code', 'Customer Code', 'UAT-1', 'PROD', 'FDP Release']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1947
Investigation Summary: Recovery data for September and October required correction before release to Prod. Validation found that BZDO008 was generated using D/N price * Qty for price revision, while KB processes price revision and cycle count with the same logic. The UAT fix changed BZDO008 generation for both workflows and was validated before release to Prod.
Important Findings: ['BZDO008 initially showed D/N price * Qty for price revision data.', 'KB processes cycle count and price revision using the same logic.', 'BZDO008 must contain D/N price only for both cycle count and price revision.', 'Records must not be created when D/N price is 0, because they cause an error on the KB side.', 'Price revision recovery data must use the same Posting date for all records; September 30 data must not include an October 1 Posting date.', 'The fix was completed and tested in UAT, approved, and released to Prod.']
Root Cause: BZDO008 generation for price revision used D/N price * Qty and allowed records with D/N price of 0, which was incompatible with the shared KB processing logic used for cycle count and price revision.
Resolution: Updated the UAT and Prod program for both cycle count and price revision so BZDO008 is created with D/N price only, records with D/N price of 0 are not created, and recovery-data Posting dates are consistent across records. The change was tested in UAT and released to Prod.
Technical Entities: ['BZDO008', 'D/N price', 'Qty', 'KB', 'MDIS', 'Cycle count', 'Price Revision', 'Parts Cycle Count', 'Posting date', 'UAT', 'Prod', 'recovery data']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1935
Investigation Summary: The Expense Invoice BIP stamp/logo changed from a square shape to a rectangle shape, likely during BIP report parameter changes performed in Production on 20 August. The issue was corrected in UAT1, including stamp synchronization and resizing to 15mm length and width. After approval from Okayama Business and MFTBC, the change was deployed to PROD.
Important Findings: ['The affected output was the Expense Invoice BIP.', 'The stamp/logo shape change was traced to BIP report parameter changes performed on PROD on 20 August.', 'MFTBCFFR-1613 included changes to the Expense Invoice BIP and approval of a rectangular stamp.', 'UAT1 validation confirmed correct vertical and horizontal synchronization.', 'Okayama Business requested the stamp size be changed to 15mm length and width.', 'The corrected and approved change was released to PROD.']
Root Cause: The stamp/logo was likely changed from square to rectangular during BIP report parameter changes performed in PROD on 20 August.
Resolution: Corrected the stamp configuration in UAT1, adjusted the stamp size to 15mm by 15mm, obtained approval from Okayama Business and MFTBC, and deployed the change to PROD.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1934
Investigation Summary: The issue was replicated in UAT1 using Quote 1-40NT88 and Job Card I001236399. The investigation found that the user changed the editable Print Order value in quote line items after selecting Generate Approval, causing the approval status to become Approved while the Quote itself was not Approved. The incident was classified as an operational/user error rather than a system defect.
Important Findings: ['The issue was replicated in UAT1.', 'After Generate Approval was selected, the user changed Print Order in the quote line items.', 'The Approval Tab status became Approved, but the Quote was not Approved.', 'Quote data must not be changed after Generate Approval; required changes must be made before submitting the approval request.', 'The incident was approved for denial because it was an operational error, not a system issue.']
Root Cause: A user changed the editable Print Order value in quote line items after clicking Generate Approval.
Resolution: Make all required quote changes before clicking Generate Approval and do not modify the Quote during the approval request.
Technical Entities: ['UAT1', 'Quote', '1-40NT88', 'Job Card', 'I001236399', 'Generate Approval', 'Print Order', 'Approval Tab']

comments.comment:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1934
Timestamp: 2023-11-07T09:57:00
Author: kartik chanana
Comment: We have replicated the same process on UAT1 and have observed the RCA for the error that occurred.
 The RCA for error caused was user mistake only.
 The steps performed by the user were:
 After creating the quote and clicking the Generate Approval button, the user changed the value of Print Order in the line items, which was editable, which is why the error occurred.
 The Status is set Approved in Approval Tab but Quote is not Approved. 
 The correct way to perform these steps was:
 After creating the quote, the user should make the changes he wants to make before clicking on the Generate Approval Button.
 No change in Quote should be made after Generate Approval. The process will run smoothly and no errors will occur.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1923
Investigation Summary: Creating a "Payer Change" Change Order in FDP failed at Generate Approval with "Please Enter the Value For Payer Finance Account Code". The failure was caused by backend validations migrated from SC, where more account values existed than in FDP. The implemented fix copies Bill To Customer into the Payer field when creating the Service Quote; it was validated in UAT1 and deployed to Prod.
Important Findings: ['FDP contained only "Ship To Account" and "Bill To Account", while the migrated SC backend configuration contained validations for additional accounts.', 'Generate Approval applied the same account validations as SC and raised "Please Enter the Value For Payer Finance Account Code".', 'In SC, changing Payer in the JC header had no effective meaning because the Bill To Customer value was always entered.', 'The agreed mitigation was to populate Payer by copying Bill To Customer during Service Quote creation.', 'The change was tested successfully in UAT1 and then deployed to Prod.']
Root Cause: Backend account validation configuration migrated from SC required a Payer Finance Account Code during Generate Approval, although FDP did not have the corresponding Payer account configuration/value.
Resolution: Updated Service Quote creation to copy the Bill To Customer field into the Payer field. The change was tested in UAT1, approved, and deployed to Prod.
Technical Entities: ['FDP', 'Change Order', 'Payer Change', 'Generate Approval', 'Payer Finance Account Code', 'SC', 'Ship To Account', 'Bill To Account', 'Payer', 'JC', 'Bill To Customer', 'Service Quote', 'UAT1', 'Prod']

Investigation Summary: After final Sales Order approval, Shipment PoolCost Order creation completed, but the Sales Order status was not updated and the Journal Voucher (JV) was not generated. Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1917

Root Cause: Bulk Invoice did not round Sales Price before multiplying by Qty, unlike the calculation performed in Siebel.
Resolution: Updated Bulk Invoice calculation logic to round Sales Price before quantity multiplication; the fix was validated and released to Production.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1908
Investigation Summary: When a quote was revised with a planned delivery date earlier than the current date, trade-in consumption tax was set to null. The configuration was changed in UAT so the value is set to 0 instead of null, validated using Quote# 1-3Z5VZN rev.2, and released to PROD. Impacted records were extracted and recovered after the production release.
Important Findings: ['The existing revised-quote functionality set trade-in consumption tax to null when the planned delivery date was less than today.', 'The UAT configuration was changed so trade-in consumption tax is set to 0 rather than null for planned delivery dates less than today.', 'The UAT change was validated with Quote# 1-3Z5VZN rev.2.', 'The change was released to PROD on 2023-11-06.', 'Affected production records were extracted and recovery was completed.']
Root Cause: Existing revised-quote configuration set trade-in consumption tax to null when the planned delivery date was less than today.
Resolution: Changed the configuration to set trade-in consumption tax to 0 instead of null for revised quotes with planned delivery dates earlier than today, released the change to PROD, and recovered affected records.
Technical Entities: ['UAT', 'PROD', 'trade-in consumption tax', 'planned delivery date', 'revised quote', 'Quote# 1-3ZRQBB', 'Quote# 1-3Z5VZN rev.2']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1901
Investigation Summary: The "Ordered SO revised conditions" report initially returned Sales Orders based on the revised Quote last Approval Date, as defined in BRD of CR NV-08. A requirement clarification established that Sales Orders in "Pending" and "Pending Approval" status must not be returned by this filter. The required change was implemented and validated in UAT, then released to PROD.
Important Findings: ['The existing functionality selected Sales Orders based on the revised Quote last Approval Date.', 'For the "Ordered SO revised conditions" report, Sales Orders with status "Pending" or "Pending Approval" must be excluded from the filter results.', 'The change was implemented in UAT and confirmed under reference A001235943.', 'The validated change was released to PROD.']
Root Cause: The report filter did not exclude Sales Orders in "Pending" and "Pending Approval" status.
Resolution: Updated the "Ordered SO revised conditions" report filtering logic in UAT to exclude "Pending" and "Pending Approval" Sales Orders, validated the change, and released it to PROD.
Technical Entities: ['Ordered SO revised conditions', 'BRD of CR NV-08', 'SO', 'Revised Quote', 'last Approval Date', 'Pending', 'Pending Approval', 'UAT', 'PROD', 'A001235943']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1895
Investigation Summary: Service consumption-tax rounding in UAT-1 was not covered by the existing BRD rounding logic, which applied only to Parts and NV/UV. A temporary Siebel change was implemented to hard-code the calculated Round Type to round down. The change was validated in UAT1, approved, and released to PROD on 31 October.

Root Cause: Service was excluded from the existing consumption-tax rounding requirements and logic; its functionality did not reference the consumption tax master, while rounding was configured only for Parts and NV/UV.
Resolution: Hard-coded the Siebel Round Type calculation for Service to round down, validated the change in UAT1, and deployed it to PROD in the 31 October release.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1874
Investigation Summary: Parts Purchase Order transactions were created but not visible on the Inventory Transaction Screen after migration from SC. The issue was caused by a hardcoded SC transaction type id being used instead of the FDP value. The FDP transaction type id was corrected in UAT and released to PROD, and recovery was completed for 5,467 affected records.
Important Findings: ['Parts Purchase Order transactions were created successfully but were not visible on the Inventory Transaction Screen.', 'A hardcoded transaction type id from SC remained in use after migration.', 'The transaction type id value for FDP was updated and validated in UAT.', 'The fix was released to PROD.', 'Recovery was completed for 5,467 records related to the issue.']
Root Cause: A hardcoded SC transaction type id was used after migration, causing Parts Purchase Order transactions to be created but not displayed on the Inventory Transaction Screen.
Resolution: Updated the transaction type id to the FDP value in UAT, released the fix to PROD, and completed recovery for 5,467 affected records.
Technical Entities: ['Parts Purchase Order', 'Inventory Transaction Screen', 'transaction type id', 'SC', 'FDP', 'UAT', 'PROD']

Investigation Summary: A posting-date mismatch occurred for Job Card I000011402 after the job card was re-edited without any amount changes and closed again on a later date. No new journal voucher was created during re-edit because the Job Card amount was unchanged, while the existing journal voucher retained the first closure date. Recovery was completed under SR MFTBCFFR-1887, and the incident was closed.
Important Findings: ['Re-editing the Job Card without changing its amount did not create a new journal voucher.', 'The journal voucher had been created when the Job Card was first closed, so its posting date remained the first completion date.', 'Closing the re-edited Job Card on a later date changed the Job Card settlement date.', 'The differing journal voucher posting date and Job Card settlement date caused the mismatch.', 'Re-edit functionality was disabled.', 'Recovery for Job Card I000011402 was completed in SR MFTBCFFR-1887.']
Root Cause: The Job Card was re-edited without an amount change and closed on a later date. Because no new journal voucher was created for an unchanged Job Card amount, the existing journal voucher retained the first completion date while the Job Card settlement date changed.
Resolution: Recovery of Job Card I000011402 was completed in SR MFTBCFFR-1887.
Technical Entities: ['Job Card', 'I000011402', 'journal voucher', 'posting date', 'JC settlement date', 're-edit functionality', 'MFTBCFFR-1887']

Investigation Summary: The D2S Invoice Mismatch process incorrectly set the match flag to N when comparing "Sales Order Item" with "D2S Sales Order Line#". Root Cause: "Sales Order Item" and "D2S Sales Order Line#" were configured as Text, causing improper comparison in D2S Invoice Mismatch.
Resolution: Changed the data type of "Sales Order Item" and "D2S Sales Order Line#" to NUMBER, validated the fix in UAT, and released it to Prod.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1860
Investigation Summary: The Activity for JC# I000008899 in Prod was created from a Service Effort Line Item of a UV Quote. The Service Quote remained In Progress because the user selected the Job Card from the Activity after creating it, rather than creating the Job Card from the Internal Work Request. The workflow was confirmed to operate correctly in UAT and Prod according to UV-16 CR, and the issue was rejected as user-miss operation.
Important Findings: ['Activities created from UV Inventory support internal approval of SV-Quote through Process #2, implemented under FDP CR UV-15.', 'Activities created from UV Quote follow Process #1 from the start of FDP.', 'JC# I000008899 Activity in Prod was created from a Service Effort Line Item of a UV Quote.', 'The Service Quote stayed In Progress because the Job Card was selected from the Activity instead of being created from the Internal Work Request.', 'The UV-16 CR business process was verified as working correctly in both UAT and Prod environments.']
Root Cause: User-miss operation: the Job Card was created separately and then mapped to the Activity, instead of creating the Job Card from the Activity/Internal Work Request workflow.
Resolution: No product change was required. The issue was rejected after confirming that the UV-16 CR workflow operates correctly in UAT and Prod; users must create the Job Card through the intended Internal Work Request/Activity process.
Technical Entities: ['SV-Quote', 'UV Inventory', 'FDP CR UV-15', 'UV Quote', 'Process #1', 'Process #2', 'FDP', 'JC# I000008899', 'Prod', 'Service Effort Line Item', 'Service Quote', 'In Progress', 'Internal Work Request', 'UV-16 CR', 'UAT']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1858
Investigation Summary: Actual Labour Hour values in Power BI were initially discrepant because the column was aggregated differently from the SC (1-10 report). After removing the aggregation, a further issue was identified: cancelled work order labour hours were included in the 1-10A report. An ODI Package filter was implemented and validated in UAT and PROD to exclude cancelled work order status; historical JC values were provided in an Excel recovery file.
Important Findings: ['Actual Labour Hour was incorrectly summarized in Power BI, while the corresponding SC (1-10 report) column was not summarized.', 'Removing the Power BI aggregation corrected the initial discrepancy and did not require data recovery because values were recalculated using the revised logic.', 'The 1-10A report and SC PBI included labour hours from cancelled work orders, including JC I000013477 and JC I022120457.', 'An ODI Package filter was added to exclude work orders with cancelled status.', 'The ODI filter affected JCs updated after implementation; earlier JCs required corresponding DB_LAST_UPD updates for recalculation.', 'UAT validation using JCs I001235533 and I001235538 confirmed that cancelled work order labour hours were excluded from PBI.']
Root Cause: The ODI Package did not filter out cancelled work order status, causing cancelled work order labour hours to be included in Actual Labour Hour calculations. The initial discrepancy was additionally caused by aggregation of the Actual Labour Hour column in Power BI.
Resolution: Removed aggregation from the Actual Labour Hour column in Power BI and deployed an ODI Package filter in PROD on 13-OCT-2023 to exclude cancelled work orders. An Excel file was provided with updated and previous Actual Labor Hour values for earlier JCs.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1853
Investigation Summary: In the affected service quote, External WO line item ML254826 was included in Service Quote Header Chargeable Cost(Excl. Tax). Investigation determined that the user changed the outsourcing carry in Flag from 'N' to 'Y' after customer approval and created a PO without running the Update Quote Header Process. This was classified as a user operation issue rather than a system bug.
Important Findings: ['The External WO line item ML254826 was calculated in Chargeable Cost(Excl. Tax) on the Service Quote Header.', "The External WO was initially created with outsourcing carry in Flag value 'N'; a Parts Internal order would have been required to complete the WO after customer approval.", "After the quote was customer approved, the user changed the Outsourcing flag to 'Y' and created the PO.", 'The Update Quote Header Process was not run after the flag change, leaving Total Chargeable Cost(Excl. Tax) unchanged.', 'Calculated fields caused Chargeable Cost on the quote line items to change to 0.', 'The scenario was replicated in UAT1 using Quote# 1-3Y0ZUP and JC# I001235319.']
Root Cause: The Outsourcing flag was changed from 'N' to 'Y' after customer approval and PO creation without running the Update Quote Header Process, leaving the Service Quote Header Total Chargeable Cost(Excl. Tax) unchanged.
Resolution: No system fix was required; the issue was rejected as a user operation error. The Update Quote Header Process must be followed after changing the Outsourcing flag.
Technical Entities: ['External WO', 'ML254826', 'Chargeable Cost(Excl. Tax)', 'Service Quote Header', 'outsourcing carry in Flag', 'Parts Internal order', 'Outsourcing flag', 'PO', 'Update Quote Header Process', 'Total Chargeable Cost(Excl. Tax)', 'UAT1', 'Quote# 1-3Y0ZUP', 'JC# I001235319']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1849
Investigation Summary: PBI Report SV 1_01 and 1_10A showed inflated Sales Price for affected JCs because Warranty Claim data introduced multiple claim records per work order through a report join. Canceled historical claims and newly generated Submitted claims were both associated with the same JC. Okayama Fuso agreed to remove the FALCON column, and an AMS-CR would be submitted before closing the incident.
Important Findings: ['A change associated with MFTBCFFR-1524 added Warranty Claim fields, including CLAIM_PAID_DATE, CLAIM_STATUS, ACCEPTED_TOTAL_AMOUNT, Claim Status, and Claim Number, to the FDP SV PBI report through a join.', 'For JC I000011334, multiple claims existed for a work order because initial claims were canceled and new claims were generated with Claim Status "Submitted."', 'The Warranty Claim-derived "FALCON Status" field produced multiple PBI records for a JC, resulting in multiple Sales Price values and inflated Sales Price.', 'The issue affected JCs beyond the initially reported cases, including I000018287.', 'Filtering Field Fix Status to exclude "Canceled" was considered, but could remove JCs such as I000018287 and was not confirmed as a suitable general solution.', 'Okayama Fuso agreed to remove the FALCON column rather than apply an alternative filtering solution.']
Root Cause: The join introduced for Warranty Claim/FALCON fields returned multiple claim records for the same work order and JC, including canceled and Submitted claims, causing duplicate PBI records and inflated Sales Price.
Resolution: Remove the FALCON column via an AMS-CR.
Technical Entities: ['FDP SV PBI report', 'CLAIM_PAID_DATE', 'CLAIM_STATUS', 'ACCEPTED_TOTAL_AMOUNT', 'MFTBCFFR-1524', 'Claim Status', 'Claim Number', 'JC', 'I000018287', 'I000011334', 'PBI Report SV 1_01', '1_10A', 'Warranty Claim', 'FALCON Status', 'FALCON column', 'Field Fix Status', 'Canceled', 'Submitted', 'Sales Price', 'Okayama Fuso', 'AMS-CR']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1837
Investigation Summary: The NV Quote to NV Sales Order Sync excluded cases where a revised quote was created before Sales Posting, allowing quote changes to remain linked to a Sales Order with Sales Posting Completed. An AMS-CR was implemented for NV and UV to handle revised quotes created before Sales Posting, including cancellation, active/sub-quote reassignment, and validation for pending approvals. The change was validated on UAT1, including a corrected UV rejection-status case, and released to PROD on 5 December.
Important Findings: ['The original sync logic ignored Sales Order sync when the 3rd revised quote was created before NV SO Sales Order.', 'Revised quotes created before Sales Posting could allow edits to Model Code, option, color, and tire while linked to a Sales Order with Sales Posting Completed.', 'For In Progress or Rejected quotes created before Sales Posting, Delivery Completion approval must cancel the quote and move the active flag and only sub quotes created in the previous revision to the Sales Posting-synced quote revision.', 'For Pending Approval quotes created before Sales Posting, approval generation or Delivery Completion Approval must show: "There is a correction request request for approval for this order, please check."', 'During UAT1 validation, UV Quote 1-431G92 rev.5 remained Rejected after Sales Posting; this was resolved and retested with SO E001239841 and Quote 1-43BOUX.', 'Impacted NV and UV data was extracted after the PROD release for recovery through SRs where applicable.']
Root Cause: NV Quote to NV Sales Order Sync was conditioned on whether a revised quote was created before or after Sales Posting, causing sync processing to be skipped for revised quotes created before Sales Posting.
Resolution: Released an AMS-CR for NV and UV that syncs all NV SO Sales Posting Completed cases regardless of revised-quote creation timing; it cancels applicable In Progress/Rejected quotes, updates active flags and prior-revision sub quotes, and blocks Pending Approval quotes with a validation error. The UV UAT1 status-handling defect was corrected before PROD release.
Technical Entities: ['NV', 'UV', 'NV Quote', 'NV Sales Order Sync', 'NV SO Sales Order', 'Sales Order', 'Sales Posting', 'Sales Posting Completed', 'Delivery Completion approval', 'In Progress', 'Rejected', 'Pending Approval', 'Cancelled', 'active flag', 'sub quote', 'Model Code', 'option', 'color', 'tire', 'UAT1', 'PROD', 'UVSO#E001239812', '1-431G92 rev.4', '1-431G92 rev.5', 'SO# E001239841', 'Quote# 1-43BOUX', 'AMS-CR', 'SR']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1830
Investigation Summary: The incident occurred when a JCO mapped to an NV sales order had multiple SV-Quotes in "Customer Approved" status, causing an error during quote synchronization. Affected records were recovered by linking the correct SV-Quote to each NV Order. The preventive change was handled under MFTBCFFR-1822, validated in UAT, approved, and implemented in PROD.
Important Findings: ['Two quotes in "Customer Approved" status within the same JCO caused the error.', 'The duplicate SV-Quotes were attributed to user mis-operation.', 'Recovery required identifying and synchronizing the correct SV-Quote to the affected NV Order.', 'The requested preventive control restricts multiple quote creation for Internal Order (Charge To) - NV / UV unless the existing quote is "Cancelled".', 'The required changes were implemented in the Prod Environment after UAT confirmation and release approval.']
Root Cause: Multiple SV-Quotes in "Customer Approved" status were created in the same JCO due to user mis-operation.
Resolution: Recovered affected sales orders by synchronizing the correct SV-Quote, and implemented the MFTBCFFR-1822 change in PROD to restrict multiple quote creation for Internal Order (Charge To) - NV / UV except when the existing quote is "Cancelled".

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1829
Investigation Summary: For Child Sales Order cases, the record creator is the final approver of the Parent NV Sales Order. When the final approver was position "HQ-TAJ-Fleet-SnrMgr", Dealer Code was not set and therefore was not interfaced correctly to DJ2L. The logic was corrected in UAT and, after confirmation, deployed to the Prod Environment; recovery was also completed for FBA20-602730.
Important Findings: ['Child Sales Order records are created upon final approval of the Parent NV Sales Order.', 'The Child Sales Order creator is the Parent NV Sales Order final approver.', 'Dealer Code was not set when the final approver position was "HQ-TAJ-Fleet-SnrMgr".', 'For Child SO HQ user cases, Dealer Code was not interfaced correctly to DJ2L.', 'The corrected logic interfaces Dealer Code to TOB using the same value as the Chassis order in the Purchase Order tab of the Sales Order.', 'Recovery for FBA20-602730 was completed and confirmed before the production deployment.']
Root Cause: Dealer Code was not set for Child Sales Orders when the Parent NV Sales Order final approver was in position "HQ-TAJ-Fleet-SnrMgr", causing an incorrect Dealer Code interface to DJ2L.
Resolution: Updated the Child SO HQ user logic so that Dealer Code interfaced to TOB matches the Chassis order value in the Sales Order Purchase Order tab. The fix was validated in UAT and implemented in the Prod Environment; recovery was completed for FBA20-602730.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1828
Investigation Summary: NV Sales Orders created by Headquarter users failed during Falcon interfacing and appeared in the Inbox after sales posting had completed. Investigation identified that the Branch 4 Digit dealer Code was blank for the affected records, causing Falcon null-field validation failures. The production fix sets the Branch 4 Digit dealer Code from the Headquarter 4 Digit Code for HQ users, and the affected records were interfaced to Falcon.
Important Findings: ['Affected NV Sales Orders had already completed sales posting and required Inbox Recovery.', 'The Branch 4 Digit dealer Code was blank in all provided affected records.', 'The affected records were created by Headquarter users.', 'Falcon interface null-field validation caused the records to error and appear in the Inbox.', 'The production fix derives the Branch 4 Digit dealer Code from the Headquarter 4 Digit Code for HQ users.', 'Falcon interface processing was performed for the provided impacted records after the fix.']
Root Cause: Records created by Headquarter users had a blank Branch 4 Digit dealer Code, which triggered null-field validation failures in the Falcon interface.
Resolution: Implemented the production change to set Branch 4 Digit dealer Code from Headquarter 4 Digit Code for HQ users, recovered the affected orders from the Inbox, and interfaced the impacted records to Falcon.
Technical Entities: ['NV Sales Order', 'Inbox Recovery', 'Sales Posting', 'Branch 4 Digit dealer Code', 'Headquarter users', 'Headquarter 4 Digit Code', 'Falcon', 'Falcon interface', 'PROD', 'Prod Environment', 'request response xml']

Root Cause: A "Latest_flg" filter added for validation purposes was unintentionally left applied in the PBI FDP 3_06 Report.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1801
Investigation Summary: Duplicate SO#s were reported in the 3-06C and 3-06 reports in UAT. A missing package filter for incremental approval-history data caused duplicates in 3-06C and was corrected. Root Cause: A missing incremental approval-history filter in the 3-06C package caused duplicate SO#s; separate residual duplicates in 3-06 were caused by old Change Order error records in UAT after the Change Order Process was removed.
Resolution: Added the missing filter condition to the 3-06C package and removed the old Change Order error records in UAT.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1792
Investigation Summary: The incident involved incorrect or ambiguous part-number handling for Parts PO#: N000013519 when allocations changed. Monitoring alone could not determine the correct part number after a change, and CPI had no alternate solution. An AMS CR introduced a D2S Allocation creation timestamp tag so allocations are processed according to the D2S Timestamp; the change was released to Okayama Prod. on 25th June.
Important Findings: ['Recovery was completed for Parts PO#: N000013519.', 'A 2 sec time delay was considered for D2S, matching the implementation on the SC side, but D2S/CPI could not implement an alternate solution.', 'Cubastion monitoring could not reliably identify the correct part number when a part number changed.', 'SQL monitoring was prepared and used to monitor the case.', 'The AMS CR added a tag carrying the Allocation creation timestamp from D2S, enabling processing based on the D2S Timestamp.', 'The change was released to Okayama Prod. on 25th June.']
Root Cause: D2S allocations did not provide an Allocation creation timestamp for reliable processing order, leaving Cubastion unable to determine the correct part number when part-number changes occurred; CPI had no alternate solution.
Resolution: Implemented an AMS CR that adds a D2S Allocation creation timestamp tag and processes allocations according to the D2S Timestamp; released to Okayama Prod. on 25th June.
Technical Entities: ['Parts PO#: N000013519', 'D2S', 'SC', 'CPI', 'Cubastion', 'SQL', 'AMS CR', 'Allocation creation timestamp', 'D2S Timestamp', 'Okayama Prod.']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1748
Investigation Summary: PO Allocation requests received while the material master and Siebel production version creation job was executing failed because the required product version was not yet available. The issue was related to MFTBCFFR-1690; after EIM table cleanup on 5-Sep-2023 reduced job timing, the issue did not recur.
Important Findings: ['PO Allocation requests conflicted with the Product creation job.', 'The allocation failed when it arrived while the material master and Siebel production version creation job was running.', 'The product version was unavailable at the time the PO Allocation request was processed.', 'EIM table cleanup on 5-Sep-2023 reduced job timing and prevented recurrence.']
Root Cause: A timing conflict between PO Allocation processing and the material master and Siebel production version creation job caused allocation requests to be processed before the product version was available.
Resolution: Performed EIM table cleanup on 5-Sep-2023, reducing job timing; the issue did not occur again afterward.
Technical Entities: ['D2S', 'PO Allocation', 'Product creation job', 'material master', 'Siebel production version creation job', 'product version', 'EIM table', 'MFTBCFFR-1690']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1741
Investigation Summary: Dealer code was not sent because supplier code was not configured for the 11SC (Dummy Record) in UAT2 (RT2), while UAT1 worked correctly. Important Findings: ['UAT1 processed the data correctly, while UAT2 (RT2) had no supplier code configured for 11SC (Dummy Record).', 'Setting the supplier code in RT2 enabled Dealer Code to be sent correctly.', 'FDP PROD received garbage characters from TOB when data containing Dealer Code was sent.', 'TOB was corrected and confirmed in the test environment.', 'UAT1 testing used D21A, D21N, and D21F chassis; D21F recycling status was set to “under construction”.', 'DJ2L receipt confirmation was successful after the TOB correction.']
Root Cause: Supplier code was not set for 11SC (Dummy Record) in UAT2 (RT2), preventing Dealer Code from being sent. A separate TOB issue caused FDP PROD to receive garbage characters; the specific technical cause was not documented.
Resolution: Set the supplier code in RT2, correct TOB, and validate TOB transmission/reception in UAT1. DJ2L receipt was confirmed successfully.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1733
Investigation Summary: PO creation succeeded in Siebel and Azure gateway logs showed a successful response from D2S CPI, but concurrent order requests caused an issue in D2S. Root Cause: D2S could not handle concurrent requests for different order numbers through the file based interface from CPI to D2S.
Resolution: D2S applied a solution on FDP PROD; no new problems were reported afterward.

Root Cause: The shipment-creation logic depended on the Pending Approval status, which Auto Approval bypassed by directly setting the status to Approved.
Resolution: Updated the Part Return Order PO to Supplier logic to create shipments when the status is updated to Approved; the change was validated in UAT1 and implemented in Production Environment.
