investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1727
Investigation Summary: A UV Sales Order could map a Purchase Order that was already associated with a Parts Sales Order when the same VIN was used. The mapping logic did not exclude Parts Sales Orders, causing Parts Sales Order M000006663 to be mapped with UV Sales Order E000007349 for VIN FG508BD-430572. The mapping condition was updated, recovery was completed, and the change passed UAT before deployment to Production Environment.
Important Findings: ['Parts Staff processed Purchase Quote and Parts Sales Order M000006663 using VIN FG508BD-430572, which mapped the Purchase Order to that VIN.', 'Branch Sales created UV Sales Order E000007349 with the same VIN and used the map button to select the UV Purchase Order.', 'The existing mapping logic also mapped the Parts Sales Order associated with the Purchase Order to the UV Sales Order.', 'The scenario was not handled in the application and also existed in FDP UAT.', 'The fix was implemented in UAT, passed UAT, and was subsequently deployed to Production Environment.', 'Recovery of the affected data was completed.']
Root Cause: The UV Sales Order map-button logic did not exclude Parts Sales Orders already mapped to the selected Purchase Order, allowing a Parts Sales Order to be mapped to a UV Sales Order when both used the same VIN.
Resolution: Updated the UV Sales Order mapping condition to omit Parts Sales Orders associated with the selected Purchase Order, completed data recovery, validated the change in UAT, and deployed it to Production Environment.
Technical Entities: ['Purchase Quote', 'Parts Sales Order', 'M000006663', 'Purchase Order', 'VIN', 'FG508BD-430572', 'UV Sales Order', 'E000007349', 'map button', 'FDP UAT', 'UAT', 'Production Environment']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1724
Investigation Summary: The investigation confirmed that the amount sent from Siebel was correct because records with "Missing" status are not interfaced to KB. MDIS reported that Inventory ID 1-3URB0G was missing; it was not sent because its Counted date was 2023/09/11 07:45:22 PM and cycle count data is sent daily based on Counted date. A change request, MFTBCFFR-1743, was created to address the date-mapping issue.
Important Findings: ['Only records with Availability and Status of On Hand/Good are interfaced to KB.', 'Records with "Missing" status are excluded from the Siebel-to-KB interface amount calculation.', 'Cycle count data is sent daily using the Counted date as the selection logic.', 'Inventory ID 1-3URB0G was not sent because its Counted date was 2023/09/11 07:45:22 PM.', 'Multiple cycle counts for the same Part# on the same day can create ambiguity for "Before Cycle Count" and "After Cycle Count" quantities.']
Root Cause: The daily cycle count interface selects records based on Counted date, causing Inventory ID 1-3URB0G to be excluded from the expected transmission/reporting period.
Technical Entities: ['Siebel', 'KB', 'MDIS', 'Inventory ID 1-3URB0G', 'Counted date', 'Cycle count', 'On Hand/Good', 'Missing', 'Before Cycle Count', 'After Cycle Count', 'Part#', 'MFTBCFFR-1743']

Resolution: Corrected the D21A, D21C, and D21E configuration so Vin Number, Serial Number, and Key are populated with VIN#, validated the change in UAT1, and implemented it in Production. Impacted records were recovered until the Production fix was applied.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1713
Investigation Summary: The Real Time Invoice API returned incorrect invoice delivery and registration dates because date mappings did not account for whether registration and delivery were completed or pending. The initial UAT logic was partially implemented and migrated to production. A fix was validated in UAT1 for NV and UV sample requests and then deployed to the production environment.
Important Findings: ['During initial Real Time Invoice API development, Planned Delivery Date and Requested Registration Date were mapped to the Invoice.', 'The initial mapping failed for orders where Registration and Delivery were completed, for which Actual Delivery/Registration Date should have been displayed in the Invoice.', 'Mapping Actual Delivery/Registration Date unconditionally was also incorrect; the logic needed to distinguish completed versus pending registration and delivery.', 'The partially implemented UAT logic was migrated to production, causing the incident.', 'UAT1 validation for NV order A001233104 and UV order E001233107 returned "Invoice details returned successfully." with DeliveryDate and RegisteredDate values.']
Root Cause: Invoice date-mapping logic in the Real Time Invoice API was partially implemented and did not conditionally select Planned/Requested dates versus Actual Delivery/Registration dates based on registration and delivery completion status.
Resolution: The fix was implemented in UAT1, validated by UAT testing, approved for release, and deployed to the production environment.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1704
Investigation Summary: BIP reports for Quote 34 omitted expected line items when cancelled items occupied the page-2 positions. The existing BIP template logic paginated 22 line items per page before excluding cancelled lines, resulting in an empty page. The filtering logic was moved from the BIP template to Siebel so that only non-cancelled line items are sent to BI Publisher. The change was tested in UAT1 and deployed to Prod after validation.
Important Findings: ['Quote 34 had cancelled line items from line 15 through line 53.', 'The BIP Report logic printed 22 line items per page and ignored line items with Cancelled status.', 'All line items allocated to page 2 were cancelled, so no line items were printed on that page.', 'Filtering of cancelled line items was moved from the BIP template to Siebel.', 'Siebel now sends only non-cancelled line items to BI Publisher.', 'The change was tested in UAT1 and implemented in Prod Environment.']
Root Cause: The BIP template paginated line items before excluding Cancelled items; because all items assigned to page 2 were cancelled, the page printed no line items.
Resolution: Moved cancelled-line filtering from the BIP template to Siebel, so Siebel sends only non-cancelled line items to BI Publisher; the change was tested in UAT1 and deployed to Prod Environment.
Technical Entities: ['RT2', 'Quote 34', 'BIP Report', 'BIP template', 'Siebel', 'BI Publisher', 'UAT1', 'Prod Environment']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1697

Root Cause: PO to D2S stock orders were created by the Replenishment Batch Job using SADMIN, and SADMIN had no branch code assigned; therefore Department Code was populated as blank.
Resolution: Implemented and released changes to the Production Environment to populate Department Code from Inventory Name for Parts Purchase Orders and use Received Date as Posting Date.

Resolution: Added reject reason codes FJ, ZF, and FN to UAT1 and Production, then completed recovery of the affected Purchase Orders.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1685
Investigation Summary: NV Quote allowed a Closing date value of 30 in the Approval Information tab, while NV Sales Order accepted only 10, 20, or EOM. Auto Order failed when creating an NV SO with the unsupported value. The logic was corrected in UAT, validated, and deployed to Production.
Important Findings: ['The Finance Tab of NV Quote and NV Sales Order restricted Closing date values to 10, 20, and EOM.', 'The Approval Information tab of NV Quote allowed additional Closing date values, including 30.', 'Selecting 30 in Approval Information caused an error during Auto Order because 30 could not be entered in the NV SO Closing date field.', 'The initial UAT implementation failed because Baseline type behavior did not match SC incident#520320920 requirements.', 'The corrected logic makes Closing Date non-editable when Baseline type is "Closing" and clears Closing Date when Baseline type changes from "Closing" to "On Delivery".']
Root Cause: Inconsistent Closing date validation between the NV Quote Approval Information tab and NV Sales Order allowed an unsupported value (30) to be selected, causing Auto Order to fail during NV SO creation.
Resolution: Updated the Closing date and Baseline type logic in UAT, validated the changes, and deployed the required changes to Production.

Ticket Description: By analyzed the print solution logs, I almost know where to investigate when it's not printing.

I discussed this with Mr. Mayank along with the following documents.

check list

 ### pktmon start -c --comp 8

 # then we can analyze how many packet will be captured for 1 print job
 # after above information re-enable pktmon

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1673
Investigation Summary: A cancelled Assessment record required recovery after the vehicle was restocked. The Assessment Request vehicle-value update depends on a change to the UV Inventory vehicle value. Because UV Inventory already contained the same value, 1,034,500, no inventory update occurred and the downstream Assessment Request update was not triggered. Assessment Number H000000037 was recovered, and the proposed recovery approach was to null the UV Inventory vehicle value before recovery.
Important Findings: ['The issue could not be replicated in UAT1 or RT2, and other Assessment Requests worked correctly in PROD.', 'Vehicle H000000001 was restocked and cancelled through SR#MFTBCFFR-1637.', 'The workflow is: Assessment Request Stock in Verification Completed; UV Inventory vehicle value updated from UV Purchase Order; Assessment Request vehicle value updated from the UV Inventory update.', 'UV Inventory already held vehicle value 1,034,500 after Assessment #H000000001 completed a re-evaluation request with the same value.', 'Because the UV Inventory value did not change, the downstream Assessment Request update trigger did not execute.', 'Assessment Number H000000037 was recovered with Vehicle Value 1,034,500.']
Root Cause: UV Inventory already contained vehicle value 1,034,500, so the update from UV Purchase Order produced no value change and did not trigger the downstream Assessment Request vehicle-value update during recovery of a cancelled Assessment.
Resolution: Recovered Assessment Number H000000037 with Vehicle Value 1,034,500. For cancelled-Assessment recovery cases, add a recovery step to set the UV Inventory vehicle value to null so the subsequent update triggers the Assessment Request update.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1671
Investigation Summary: PO Creation outbound calls to D2S intermittently failed with an internal error and affected PO records were initially recovered by repushing. D2S identified DNS anycast route instability caused by flapping of the track associated with the IP route. D2S removed the track from the static route, after which the DNS anycast route stabilized; no further D2S failures were recorded during one-day monitoring.
Important Findings: ['The DMS_PO_CREATION outbound call failed at DMS_PO_CREATIONPort with an internal error referencing MPL ID AGTuzXKF0wh4rvW5ufoSPGKUIqtU.', 'Repushing failed PO Creation requests processed successfully, and all records through 31 August were recovered.', 'D2S initially reported a timeout and increased the read timeout in CPI.', 'D2S later identified DNS anycast route flapping caused by flapping of the track associated with the IP route.', 'Removing the track from the static route stabilized the DNS anycast route; the reconfigured track remained under monitoring and was not yet reattached to the static route.']
Root Cause: Flapping of the track associated with the IP route caused DNS anycast route flapping on the D2S side, resulting in intermittent D2S PO Creation failures.
Resolution: D2S removed the track from the static route, stabilizing the DNS anycast route. Failed requests were repushed and recovered, and the incident was closed after one day without further D2S failures.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1661
Investigation Summary: PFB Export returned blank Vehicle Name values for all model codes because the Model Master lacked model-code-to-vehicle-name mappings. The Model Master was initially created from a TCH01 file generated from SC PROD data, but the initial FDP PROD setup did not receive the mapping data. Business provided the missing file, which was uploaded to PROD, and the mapping requirement was added to the initial setup plan for future FDPs.
Important Findings: ['Vehicle Name was blank in PFB Export for all model codes.', 'Model Master was created from a TCH01 file generated from SC PROD data.', 'The TCH01 file contained no logic to update Vehicle Name in Model Master.', 'The model-code-to-Vehicle-Name mapping was not received during FDP PROD initial setup.', 'Business-provided mapping data was uploaded to PROD.', 'Vehicle Name mapping was added to the initial setup plan for future FDPs.']
Root Cause: The model-code-to-Vehicle-Name mapping was not received during the FDP PROD initial setup, leaving Vehicle Name values missing from Model Master.
Resolution: The Business-provided mapping file was uploaded to PROD to populate Vehicle Name in Model Master; the mapping requirement was added to the initial setup plan for future FDPs.
Technical Entities: ['PFB Export', 'Vehicle Name', 'model code', 'Model Master', 'TCH01 file', 'SC PROD', 'FDP PROD', 'PROD', 'SR#MFTBCFFR-1664']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1653
Investigation Summary: The required-field validation for BB Work Planned Start Date and Requested Registration Date was found to differ based on the chassis-order creation source. The initial proposed order-classification logic was corrected after confirmation that FORCE1.0 applies to order classification "J" (=BTO). UAT initially failed because selecting "M" still displayed a required-item error; the feedback was implemented, UAT was approved, and the changes were deployed to PROD.
Important Findings: ['The existing validation required BB Work Planned Start Date and Requested Registration Date for Chassis Orders created from TOB files, but not for orders created in Siebel UI through the Create Purchase Order Button.', 'The behavior was confirmed in SC PROD and replicated in SC UAT.', 'FORCE1.0 scope was confirmed as order classification "J" (=BTO), requiring correction of the proposed validation approach.', 'Initial UAT validation failed because selecting order classification "M" still displayed a required-item error.', 'After implementing UAT feedback, UAT confirmation was completed and approved for PROD deployment.']
Root Cause: A bug in the required-field validation logic for BB Work Planned Start Date and Requested Registration Date, which did not align with the intended FORCE1.0 order-classification scope.
Resolution: The validation changes were corrected in UAT following failed UAT feedback, approved after retesting, and deployed to the Production environment.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1639
Investigation Summary: Order Allocation and Shipment notification issues were attributed to a technical issue in the CPI Middleware configuration (#520341066). Root Cause: Technical issue with configuring the CPI Middleware configuration (#520341066), which delayed Order Allocation relative to Shipment notification processing.
Resolution: The CPI Middleware configuration fix was applied and fully implemented. Follow-up work to apply the SC countermeasure to FDP Force was raised as MFTBCFFR-1656.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1636
Investigation Summary: Chassis Orders created from TOB files had Chassis Order Line Items with blank status, reproduced in UAT1 and SC UAT and observed in SC PROD. When a DJ2B Change Order was sent to TOB, line items with null status were not processed, so Product Code and Model Code were omitted from the request. The handling was changed in UAT1 and deployed to Production to include blank-status line items in Change Orders; existing chassis orders were recovered.
Important Findings: ['Chassis Orders created from TOB files could have Chassis Order Line Items with blank status.', 'The issue existed in both SC and FDP and was reproduced in UAT1 and SC UAT; blank status was also observed in SC PROD.', 'When sending a DJ2B Change Order to TOB, Product Code and Model Code were not sent for line items with null status.', 'The corrective change handles null Line Item status and includes Product Code and Model Code in the TOB request string.', 'Existing Chassis Orders raised up to the prior day were recovered; production verification was pending the next PO change.']
Root Cause: Change Order processing did not handle Chassis Order Line Items with blank/null status, causing Product Code and Model Code to be omitted when sending the Change Order to TOB.
Resolution: Implemented and deployed a change that allows Change Orders for blank-status line items and includes their Product Code and Model Code in the TOB request; recovered affected existing Chassis Orders.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1627
Investigation Summary: The vehicle inspection expiration date was not updated correctly when an uploaded vehicle inspection certificate had an issuance date older than the existing certificate and a blank expiration date. Certificates with a newer issuance date did not cause the issue even when the expiration date was blank. The agreed approach was to prioritize a data patch for Okayama Fuso and raise an AMS CR for a code change to ignore certificates with blank expiration dates.
Important Findings: ['The issue occurs when an uploaded vehicle inspection certificate has an issuance date older than the existing certificate and a blank expiration date.', 'Certificates with an issuance date greater than the existing certificate do not cause an issue when the expiration date is blank.', 'The file field used for the expiration date is ON_EXPIRTN_DT_VBALIDITY_PERIOD.', 'Solution 1, a data patch for Okayama Fuso, was prioritized.', 'Solution 2 requires a code change to ignore vehicle inspection certificates with blank expiration dates.']
Root Cause: A vehicle inspection certificate with a blank expiration date was processed when its issuance date was older than the existing certificate, causing the vehicle inspection expiration date to be updated incorrectly.
Resolution: Prioritize a data patch for Okayama Fuso (Solution 1) and raise an AMS CR for a code change to ignore vehicle inspection certificates with blank expiration dates (Solution 2).

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1620
Investigation Summary: The "Manager Position" and "Position Type JPN" fields displayed SC-version position names instead of FDP-version position names. Their LOV values were sourced from database views migrated from SC FORCE with a hardcoded workspace ID and SC-to-FDP position mappings. The LOV condition was updated to remove the hardcoded condition and retrieve values using the correct workspace ID; the fix was validated in UAT1 and UAT2 (RT2), then deployed and verified in Production.
Important Findings: ['"Manager Position" and "Position Type JPN" values were sourced from a database view used by the LOV.', 'The database view was migrated from SC FORCE, carrying a hardcoded workspace ID into all FDP environments.', 'UAT1 validation initially showed SC-version position names in both affected fields rather than FDP-version names.', '"Position Type JPN" and "Manager Name" used Position Type values retained from SC and mapped to FDP positions.', 'The LOV condition was changed to remove the hardcoded workspace-ID condition and fetch values for the correct workspace ID.', 'The change was validated in UAT1 and UAT2 (RT2), deployed to Production, and confirmed operational.']
Root Cause: Database views migrated from SC FORCE contained a hardcoded LOV workspace ID, causing the affected fields to retrieve SC-version position values rather than the correct FDP workspace values.
Resolution: Updated the LOV condition to remove the hardcoded workspace-ID condition and retrieve values using the correct workspace ID; deployed the validated change to Production.
Technical Entities: ['Manager Position', 'Position Type JPN', 'Manager Name', 'LOV', 'Database View', 'Workspace ID', 'SC FORCE', 'FDP', 'UAT1', 'UAT2 (RT2)', 'FDP Okayama PROD', 'Production Environment']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1619
Investigation Summary: The scheduled TCB01 package incorrectly changed Chassis Orders from "Shipment Instructed" to "Ordered". The package behavior was based on SC Force/SC Force 2.0 logic involving RF status, which was not appropriate for FDP where RF is disconnected. The corrected TCB01 behavior was validated in UAT1 and deployed to PROD; the package was scheduled and the latest file was processed successfully.
Important Findings: ['TCB01 selected Chassis Orders with status "Shipment Instructed" and RF status "Send Shipment to RF", then changed the order status to "Ordered".', 'In FDP, RF is disconnected, and Chassis Order status must not be updated by the TCB01 file.', 'The agreed TCB01 scope was to update Planned Completion Date and K1_1_OK_Actual_Date, while preventing status updates.', 'Some UAT1 records were not updated because update_date in column 127 was not today or yesterday; updating update_date to the current date allowed the changes to be reflected.', 'The PROD fix was deployed, the package was scheduled, and the latest TCB01 file was processed successfully after update_date was updated.']
Root Cause: The TCB01 package retained SC Force/SC Force 2.0 logic that updated Chassis Order status from "Shipment Instructed" to "Ordered" based on RF status, although this status update was not valid for FDP.
Resolution: Modified TCB01 processing so that it does not update Chassis Order status and only updates Planned Completion Date and K1_1_OK_Actual_Date. The fix was validated in UAT1, deployed to PROD, and the TCB01 update_date column was set to the current date before processing the latest file.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1618
Investigation Summary: Printing to OKYF_10_P03 failed and was investigated through DIS printer and printer-object re-registration. The printer object was recreated on dms-0 and dms-1, and an incorrectly configured DIS port on dms-1 was subsequently corrected. After the recreated object was reflected on August 24, business testing confirmed successful printing; Canon RCA investigation remained ongoing.
Important Findings: ['OKYF_10_P03 was deleted from and re-registered to DISU using del_OKYF_10_P03.txt and add_OKYF_10_P03.txt through web monitor.', 'The printer object was deleted and recreated on dms-0 and dms-1 using prnmngr.vbs with the Canon Generic Plus LIPSLX driver and LPT1: port.', 'The DIS port on dms-1 was found to be incorrectly configured and was corrected.', 'The recreated printer object was not reflected immediately on the night of August 23; reflection was confirmed on August 24.', 'Business testing confirmed that printing to OKYF_10_P03 was successful after the object recreation and port configuration correction.']
Resolution: Recreated and re-registered the OKYF_10_P03 printer object in DISU, recreated the printer object on dms-0 and dms-1, and corrected the DIS port configuration on dms-1. Printing was then confirmed successful.
Technical Entities: ['Print Solution', 'OKYF_10_P03', 'DISU', 'web monitor', 'del_OKYF_10_P03.txt', 'add_OKYF_10_P03.txt', 'dms-0', 'dms-1', 'Windows', 'Printing_Admin_Scripts', 'prnmngr.vbs', 'Canon Generic Plus LIPSLX', 'LPT1:', 'DIS port', 'Canon']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1611
Investigation Summary: D21E data displayed incorrect values in the TOB Receiving Data Screen/D21E one click Print because the configured file-position-to-field mapping did not match the mapping provided by TOB. The mapping was corrected through an AMS CR, validated using the D21E BIP Report in UAT, approved for production, and deployed with data patching for affected TOB files.
Important Findings: ['The D21E mapping had a column shift between the business requirement Excel and the actual file-position-to-field mapping received from TOB.', 'The mapping mismatch caused different values to appear in D21E one click Print from the TOB Receiving Data Screen.', 'Changes were implemented according to the provided D21E Excel and tested in the UAT Environment using a D21E file and D21E BIP Report.', 'UAT confirmation was completed and the corrected mapping was approved for PROD release.', 'The change was deployed to production and data was patched for D21E TOB files dated 8/22/2023, 8/23/2023, and 8/25/2023.']
Root Cause: A column shift in the D21E file-position-to-field mapping caused the configured mapping to differ from the TOB-provided mapping.
Resolution: Corrected the D21E mapping through an AMS CR, validated it in UAT, deployed it to PROD, and patched data for affected TOB D21E files.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1574
Investigation Summary: Employee master records were initially received with userId identical to Employee code, and the account master was imported using those values. After the Employee master was updated with the actual new employee userId, the corresponding account master records were not updated, preventing details from displaying for affected records. Data recovery was completed.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1529
Investigation Summary: The batch job process differed from the SC version. The Interface data extraction was changed to run after the Siebel-side job completes and the Annual Cycle count status is updated to "Completed". The Interface now includes data updated in the previous 24 hours with Cycle count status "Completed".

Root Cause: Interface data extraction timing and selection criteria did not align with the required post-Siebel job execution and completed Annual Cycle count status.
Resolution: Updated the Interface extraction process to run after the Siebel-side job and include only previous-24-hour data where the Annual Cycle count status is "Completed".

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1455
Investigation Summary: Trade-in consumption tax could remain blank when a Trade-In Vehicle line item was added before entering Expected Sales Posting Date. The identified workaround was to enter Expected Sales Posting Date before adding the trade-in line. A temporary validation was implemented on UAT1 to require the date before adding a trade-in line item, and UAT passed; the broader handling was planned under the Invoice tax CR.
Important Findings: ['Adding a Trade-In Vehicle before Expected Sales Posting Date caused the trade-in consumption tax to be blank.', 'Entering or refreshing Expected Sales Posting Date after the trade-in line was added did not populate the blank consumption tax.', 'The original error message did not indicate that the trade-in consumption tax was blank.', 'A temporary validation was added when clicking the + button in trade-in to require Expected Sales Posting Date before adding a trade-in line item.', 'The temporary solution was implemented on UAT1 and passed UAT.']
Root Cause: The Trade-In Vehicle line item was added before Expected Sales Posting Date, preventing trade-in consumption tax calculation from being populated.
Resolution: Implemented a temporary validation on the trade-in + button requiring Expected Sales Posting Date before a trade-in line item can be added; the solution passed UAT. Permanent handling was planned in the Invoice tax CR.
Technical Entities: ['Trade-In Vehicle', 'Expected Sales Posting Date', 'Trade-In Consumption Tax', 'Ongoing Invoice Tax CR', 'Invoice tax CR', 'QA', 'UAT1', 'UAT', 'trade-in + button', '消費税の計算の為、事前にをご入力ください。']

Ticket key: MFTBCFFR-1337
Ticket type: Bug
Ticket Summary: Journal data with a tax rate of 0% is displayed on the screen as a tax rate of 10%.
Ticket Description: ・Confirm with OBC regarding workarounds.
⇒4/21 We will consider measures based on the response from OBC.
===OBC answer===
[1: If it is a tax-exempt transaction]
The cause is that the "tax classification" is not specified.
As a result, the journal entry is likely to be registered under the tax category "Taxable Purchase", which is the initial value of the account.
First of all, in Account Bugyo, you cannot register a journal entry slip with a tax rate of 0% for taxable transactions.
If this is a tax-free transaction, no tax calculation is required, so the tax rate in this case can be said to be 0%.
Therefore, although the account items such as "Parts" attached in this journal entry example are normally taxable transactions,
If you want to register a journal entry as a tax-exempt transaction (=0%) only this time,
Please explicitly set the debit tax classification (CSJS203) to "1", which is the tax classification code for non-taxable purchases.
[2: If the consumption tax amount is recorded separately]
The example journal entry you received is a taxable transaction, but the consumption tax amount is recorded in a separate statement.
If the amount is 0% if the consumption tax amount is not included, then the answer is that there is no problem with the journal entry received.
Even if the consumption tax amount is not included in the statement, the main item will be subject to 10% tax when calculating consumption tax.
The correct state is to display 10%.
============

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1273
Investigation Summary: Re-test showed that consumption tax journal entries were still being created for MFTBC PO. Resolution: Updated the journal creation logic so that Modification Orders with MFTBC Account create no journal, while Non MFTBC Account Modification Orders create a journal; tax lines remain in journals for Body Building Order Non IBOS and IBOS.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1251
Investigation Summary: The recycling confirmation message was sent using the SC name DJ2NA1TG instead of the required FDP name DJ2NA1TB, causing replies to be routed to the SC version of FORCE. The issue had also occurred in Pre SIT because a prior modification had been reverted. After correction and retesting, receipt of the recycling confirmation was confirmed.
Important Findings: ['Recycling confirmation messages must use FDP name DJ2NA1TB.', 'The message was incorrectly sent using SC name DJ2NA1TG.', 'Using DJ2NA1TG caused the reply destination to be the SC version of FORCE.', 'A similar issue occurred in Pre SIT after previously modified content was reverted.', 'Retesting confirmed receipt of the recycling confirmation.']
Root Cause: The recycling confirmation message configuration was reverted and used SC name DJ2NA1TG instead of FDP name DJ2NA1TB, routing replies to the SC version of FORCE.
Resolution: Corrected the recycling confirmation message to use FDP name DJ2NA1TB and confirmed successful receipt through retesting.
Technical Entities: ['DJ2NA1TB', 'DJ2NA1TG', 'FDP', 'SC', 'FORCE', 'Pre SIT', 'recycling confirmation message']

comments.comment:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1251
Timestamp: 2023-04-13T08:52:00
Comment: It was necessary to send the recycling confirmation message using DJ2NA1TB with the FDP name, but since it was sent with the SC name DJ2NA1TG, the reply destination was the SC version of FORCE.
A similar error occurred in Pre SIT, and the modified contents have been reverted to the original, so I have requested a check to see if there are other versions for SC.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1251
Timestamp: 2023-04-14T05:11:00
Comment: As a result of the retest, confirmation of receipt of recycling confirmation was confirmed.

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1173
Investigation Summary: Tax Journal entries were created, but account code mappings were incorrectly configured and some required account codes were missing from journal lines. The account code master initially stored concatenated values such as 25580 instead of separating account and sub-account codes as 255-80. After correcting the master configuration and addressing the remaining missing-code and zero-value journal issues, the incident was confirmed fixed.
Important Findings: ['Tax Journal can be searched using the Job card# in Project code.', 'All expense items require accounting codes if they must be journalized.', 'Account code and Sub-account code must be maintained separately; for example, 255 and 80 must produce 255-80 rather than 25580.', 'For JC# I001215124, account codes 255-80 and 255-03 were initially absent from the required credit and debit journal lines.', 'A 0-yen journal entry was created for recycling fee even though no recycling fee existed.', 'The account code master was corrected and the issue was subsequently fixed.']
Root Cause: Incorrect and incomplete account-code master configuration: account and sub-account codes were stored as concatenated values instead of separated hyphenated values, causing incorrect or missing journal account-code mappings.
Resolution: Corrected the account codes in the master so account and sub-account codes are separated with a hyphen, and fixed the remaining missing account-code and 0-yen journal-entry behavior.
Technical Entities: ['Tax Journal', 'Job card#', 'Project code', 'accounting code', 'Journal', 'Account code', 'Sub-account code', 'account code list', 'account code master', '25580', '255-80', '25504', '255-04', '255-03', 'JC# I001215124', 'automobile tax (environmental performance percentage)', 'automobile tax (classification)', 'recycling fee']

investigation_report:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-1112
Investigation Summary: The issue affected journal creation for purchase-order flows to Supplier and Inventory Cancellation. Reported UAT orders covered direct purchase goods receipt, split goods receipt, and GR cancellation scenarios. A code change was implemented so journals are created by tax category, and the requester was asked to validate the fix.
Important Findings: ['Affected UAT orders were N001213019, N001213021, and N001213022.', 'The reported scenarios were PT-P03 Directly purchased product in stock, PT-P06 Direct purchase goods receipt_split, and PT-P07 GR cancel.', 'The issue required a code change.', 'After the fix, journals for Purchase orders from PO to Supplier and Inventory Cancellation are created tax category wise.']
Root Cause: The existing implementation did not create journals tax category wise for Purchase orders from PO to Supplier and Inventory Cancellation.
Resolution: Implemented a code change to create journals tax category wise for the affected purchase-order and inventory-cancellation flows.
Technical Entities: ['PT-P03', 'PT-P06', 'PT-P07', 'N001213019', 'N001213021', 'N001213022', 'Purchase orders from PO to Supplier', 'Inventory Cancellation', 'Journals', 'Tax category']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-766
Investigation Summary: The affected fields were initially populated from the chassis PO, but the intended source was the Sales Order. The issue resulted from an unclear requirement regarding the source system. Changes were implemented, and the option and retrofit option batch runs daily at 4:00 PM JST. A subsequent incorrect "User name" display was reported, but the comments do not document its specific cause or fix.
Important Findings: ['The affected fields were originally sourced from the chassis PO.', 'The fields were intended to be populated from the Sales Order.', 'The source-system mismatch was caused by an understanding gap because the Sales Order requirement was not clearly specified.', 'The option and retrofit option batch runs once daily at 4:00 PM JST.', 'An incorrect "User name" display was reported after the changes.']
Root Cause: The requirement did not clearly specify that the fields must be populated from the Sales Order, resulting in them being sourced from the chassis PO.
Resolution: Changes were implemented to populate the affected fields from the Sales Order; the option and retrofit option batch processes the updates daily at 4:00 PM JST.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-733
Investigation Summary: The issue was reclassified as an additional change request to support configurable approval thresholds based on delta amount total. The requested behavior is to create an approval flow when the delta amount total exceeds 100,000 and automatically approve when the absolute delta amount total is below 100,000. The change request was planned for Sprint D and placed on hold.
Important Findings: ['Approval behavior must be configurable for FDPs that require approval setup.', 'Approval flow should be created when the delta amount total exceeds 100,000.', 'Automatic approval should occur when the Absolute delta amount total is less than 100,000.', 'For Okayama, setting the threshold to 99,999,999 results in automatic approval unless the threshold is exceeded.', 'When the Okayama threshold is exceeded, SCHQ-CS-Parts-Mgr should be included in the approval flow.']
Technical Entities: ['FDPs', 'Okayama', 'SCHQ-CS-Parts-Mgr', 'Sprint D']

comments.comment:
Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-733
Timestamp: 2023-02-08T06:38:00
Comment: As discussed with you, I will change this issue to an additional CR.
other FDPs may be approval set up, so we need to be flexible and set a new threshold based on delta amount total.
For example, if the delta amount total is over 100,000, the approval flow should be created, and if the Absolute delta amount total is less than 100,000, the approval should be automatic.
In the case of Okayama, which does not set approval flow, I think that setting this threshold to 99,999,999 will always result in automatic approval.
In the case of Okayama, if the threshold is exceeded, set the SCHQ-CS-Parts-Mgr to be set to the approval flow.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-588
Investigation Summary: Chassis Purchase Orders created from NV Sales Orders displayed operating costs, although PO cost fields must display actual costs. Root Cause: Incorrect cost mapping between NV Sales Order and Chassis Purchase Order caused operating costs to be populated in the PO cost field instead of actual costs.
Resolution: Corrected the Chassis Purchase Order cost mapping to populate actual cost rather than operating cost; validated using Sales Order A001195181 and Chassis PO B001195191.

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-587
Investigation Summary: UV Trade-In Purchase Contract Received Date remained blank when creating a UV Trade-in PO. Investigation confirmed that NV Trade-In populates the UVPO field from the NVSO Last Contract Date, and the same behavior was required for UV Trade-In without a Payer Account. The issue was resolved by correcting a configuration miss, after which the UV PO Purchase Contract Received Date populated successfully.
Important Findings: ['UV Trade-In PO creation did not populate Purchase Contract Received Date.', 'For NV Trade-In, the NVSO Last Contract Date populates Purchase Contract Received Date on the UVPO.', 'The required UV Trade-In behavior is the same as NV Trade-In: using the final/last contract date is acceptable.', 'A Payer Account must not be required for UV Trade-In or NV Trade-In processing.', 'The initial fix was incomplete, as the field was still blank and the incident was reopened.', 'After the final correction, UV PO Purchase Contract Received Date was populated.']
Root Cause: Configuration miss prevented Purchase Contract Received Date from being populated for UV Trade-In PO creation.
Resolution: Corrected the configuration so UV PO Purchase Contract Received Date is populated without requiring a Payer Account.
Technical Entities: ['UAT', 'UV Trade-In', 'NV Trade-In', 'UV Trade-in PO', 'UVPO', 'NVSO', 'Purchase Contract Received Date', 'Last Contract Date', 'Order Date', 'Payer Account', 'NV Sales Order', 'A001194866', 'F001194868', 'H000011786', 'FDP02TS-20230112', 'E001194768']

Issue Key: MFTBCFFR-221
Investigation Summary: The BIP report generation issue affected BB PO created by the Branch-Head position because the relevant hierarchy in FDP differed from the hierarchy used during initial testing. Root Cause: Different hierarchy data in FDP for BB PO created by the Branch-Head position.
Resolution: Updated the relevant hierarchy data in FDP; BIP report generation was then successful for Branch-Head-created BB PO.
Technical Entities: ['FDP', 'BB PO', 'Branch-Head position', 'Branch Sales staff', 'BIP report']
